```{r m9-budget}
    dWD <- dS %*% t(In) + t(dIn) %*% Ei + Dl %*% dP              # S ; In = Ei WD' ; P = Dl' WD
    dw  <- diag(dU) + rowSums(dWD * Dl)
    out[[k]] <- list(w = dw, WD = dWD, P = dP, In = dIn, S = dS, U = dU, M = dM)
  }
  out
}

## The budget: one run's first-order error bound for (Tr M, Tr M^2), each route.
gg_beta_noU <- function(Gm, Dl, c_ch = 6 * (ncol(Dl) + 1)) {
  p <- nrow(Dl); q <- ncol(Dl)
  w <- 1 / diag(Gm); WD <- w * Dl; P <- crossprod(Dl, WD); Ei <- solve(P)
  G <- Gm %*% WD; B <- crossprod(WD, G); C <- crossprod(G, w * G); EB <- Ei %*% B
  dX <- list(w = gg_u * w, WD = gg_u * abs(WD),
             P = gg_ip(p, crossprod(abs(Dl), abs(WD))) + c_ch * gg_u * sqrt(outer(diag(P), diag(P))),
             G = gg_ip(p, abs(Gm) %*% abs(WD)), B = gg_ip(p, crossprod(abs(WD), abs(G))),
             C = gg_ip(p, crossprod(abs(G), w * abs(G))), EB = gg_ip(q, abs(Ei) %*% abs(B)),
             GG = gg_u * Gm * Gm)
  gr <- gg_grad_noU(Gm, Dl)
  a1 <- sum(w * diag(Gm)); s1 <- sum(diag(EB))
  a2 <- drop(crossprod(w, (Gm * Gm) %*% w)); s2 <- sum(diag(Ei %*% C)); s3 <- sum(diag(EB %*% EB))
  fin1 <- gg_ip(p, sum(abs(w * diag(Gm)))) + gg_g(q) * sum(abs(diag(EB))) + gg_u * (abs(a1) + abs(s1))
  fin2 <- gg_ip(p * p, sum(abs(outer(w, w) * Gm * Gm))) +
          2 * (gg_ip(q, sum(abs(Ei) * abs(t(C)))) + gg_g(q) * abs(s2)) +
          gg_ip(q, sum(abs(EB) * abs(t(EB)))) + gg_g(q) * abs(s3) + 2 * gg_u * (abs(a2) + 2 * abs(s2) + abs(s3))
  b <- sapply(1:2, function(k) sum(sapply(names(dX), function(nm) sum(abs(gr[[k]][[nm]]) * dX[[nm]]))))
  c(trM = b[1] + fin1, trM2 = b[2] + fin2,
    kappa2 = (abs(a2) + 2 * abs(s2) + abs(s3)) / abs(a2 - 2 * s2 + s3))
}
gg_beta_U <- function(Gm, Dl, c_ch = 6 * (ncol(Dl) + 1)) {
  p <- nrow(Dl); q <- ncol(Dl)
  w <- 1 / diag(Gm); WD <- w * Dl; P <- crossprod(Dl, WD); Ei <- solve(P)
  In <- Ei %*% t(WD); S <- WD %*% In; U <- diag(w) - S; M <- U %*% Gm
  dX <- list(w = gg_u * w, WD = gg_u * abs(WD),
             P = gg_ip(p, crossprod(abs(Dl), abs(WD))) + c_ch * gg_u * sqrt(outer(diag(P), diag(P))),
             In = gg_ip(q, abs(Ei) %*% t(abs(WD))), S = gg_ip(q, abs(WD) %*% abs(In)),
             U = gg_u * abs(U), M = gg_ip(p, abs(U) %*% abs(Gm)))
  gr <- gg_grad_U(Gm, Dl)
  fin <- c(gg_g(p) * sum(abs(diag(M))), gg_ip(p * p, sum(abs(M * t(M)))))
  sapply(1:2, function(k) sum(sapply(names(dX), function(nm) sum(abs(gr[[k]][[nm]]) * dX[[nm]]))) + fin[k])
}

## V1: every hand derivative against a central difference of the instrumented forward computation.
gg_fdcheck <- function(Gm, Dl) {
  set.seed(7); h <- 1e-6; res <- c()
  for (route in c("noU", "U")) {
    fwd <- if (route == "noU") gg_fwd_noU else gg_fwd_U
    gr  <- if (route == "noU") gg_grad_noU(Gm, Dl) else gg_grad_U(Gm, Dl)
    for (nm in names(gr[[1]])) {
      E <- array(rnorm(length(gr[[1]][[nm]])), dim = dim(as.matrix(gr[[1]][[nm]])))
      if (is.null(dim(gr[[1]][[nm]]))) E <- as.vector(E)
      fd <- (fwd(Gm, Dl, setNames(list(h * E), nm)) - fwd(Gm, Dl, setNames(list(-h * E), nm))) / (2 * h)
      an <- c(sum(gr[[1]][[nm]] * E), sum(gr[[2]][[nm]] * E))
      res[paste(route, nm)] <- max(abs(fd - an) / pmax(abs(an), 1e-300))
    }
  }
  res
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(Rmpfr))
gb_solve_mp <- function(A, B) {                                      # Gauss-Jordan, partial pivoting, in mpfr
  q <- nrow(A); X <- cbind(A, B)
  for (k in seq_len(q)) {
    piv <- k - 1 + which.max(abs(as.numeric(X[k:q, k])))
    if (piv != k) { tmp <- X[k, ]; X[k, ] <- X[piv, ]; X[piv, ] <- tmp }
    X[k, ] <- X[k, ] / X[k, k]
    for (i in seq_len(q)[-k]) X[i, ] <- X[i, ] - X[i, k] * X[k, ]
  }
  X[, (q + 1):ncol(X), drop = FALSE]
}
gb_exact <- function(Gm, Dl, bits = 256) {                           # exact traces by definition, Rmpfr
  G  <- Rmpfr::mpfrArray(as.vector(Gm), bits, dim = dim(Gm))
  Dm <- Rmpfr::mpfrArray(as.vector(Dl), bits, dim = dim(Dl))
  p  <- nrow(Gm); ii <- cbind(seq_len(p), seq_len(p))
  w  <- 1 / G[ii]
  WD <- Dm * w
  P  <- t(Dm) %*% WD
  U  <- -(WD %*% gb_solve_mp(P, t(WD)))
  for (i in seq_len(p)) U[i, i] <- U[i, i] + w[i]
  M  <- U %*% G
  c(trM = as.numeric(sum(M[ii])), trM2 = as.numeric(sum(M * t(M))))
}

## m9-budget verification (draft). Needs gg.R and gx.R (gb_exact) loaded.
set.seed(20261028)
gg_eqcor <- function(p, q, rho) {                                    # strong correlations: large cancellation
  G <- matrix(rho, p, p); diag(G) <- 1; A <- matrix(rnorm(p * q), p, q)
  list(G = G * outer(1 + (1:p) / p, 1 + (1:p) / p), D = A) }
gg_designs <- list(
  "Gate 5 synthetic (p* 16, q 6)"     = list(G = Gsyn, D = Dsyn),
  "near-saturated (p* 16, q 14)"      = local({ p <- 16; q <- 14; A <- matrix(rnorm(p^2), p)
                                          list(G = crossprod(A) / p + diag(p), D = matrix(rnorm(p * q), p, q)) }),
  "equicorrelated 0.9 (p* 16, q 14)"  = gg_eqcor(16, 14, 0.9),
  "equicorrelated 0.97 (p* 16, q 14)" = gg_eqcor(16, 14, 0.97),
  "larger synthetic (p* 300, q 40)"   = list(G = Gbig, D = Dbig))

cat("V1: hand derivatives against central differences (max relative gap per intermediate)\n")
v1 <- gg_fdcheck(gg_designs[[2]]$G, gg_designs[[2]]$D); print(signif(v1, 3))
stopifnot(all(v1 < 1e-5))

cat("V2: one run's actual error (R against exact) within the gradient budget\n")
gg_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(gg_designs)[1:4], function(nm) {
  d <- gg_designs[[nm]]; ex <- gb_exact(d$G, d$D)
  tn <- trace_noU(d$G, d$D); tu <- trace_U(d$G, d$D)
  bn <- gg_beta_noU(d$G, d$D); bu <- gg_beta_U(d$G, d$D)
  data.frame(design = nm, kappa2 = signif(bn[["kappa2"]], 3),
    noU_err_over_beta = signif(max(abs(tn - ex) / bn[c("trM", "trM2")]), 3),

stopifnot(all(gg_tab$noU_err_over_beta <= 1), all(gg_tab$U_err_over_beta <= 1))

    signif((gg_beta_noU(big$G, big$D)[["trM2"]] + gg_beta_U(big$G, big$D)[2]) / abs(trace_U(big$G, big$D)[2]), 3), "\n")

cat("V3: a structural error is not hidden: the expansion with Tr(E^-1 C) counted once, not twice\n")

  bad <- trace_noU(d$G, d$D)[["trM2"]] + sum(diag(solve(crossprod(d$D, d$D / diag(d$G))) %*%
           crossprod(d$G %*% (d$D / diag(d$G)), (1 / diag(d$G)) * (d$G %*% (d$D / diag(d$G))))))
  abs(bad - trace_U(d$G, d$D)[["trM2"]]) / (gg_beta_noU(d$G, d$D)[["trM2"]] + gg_beta_U(d$G, d$D)[2])
```

**What these show.** Executed 2026-10-28 under R 4.6.0 (Rmpfr at 256 bits for the exact traces), by
extracting `gate5-setup`, `m9-traces` and `m9-budget`. The document was not re-rendered.

- **V1.** Every hand derivative agrees with a central difference of the instrumented route, to within
  8.6e-8 relative, on all 15 intermediates.
- **V2.** One run's actual error against the exact traces is at most 0.0062 of $\beta^{\rm exp}$ and
  2.6e-4 of $\beta^{U}$. That holds on four designs, with $\kappa_2$ from 3.6 to 736; case D's measured
  208 lies inside that range. The budget, relative to $\operatorname{Tr}(M^2)$, is 1.3e-13 on the Gate 5
  synthetic design and 1.0e-11 to 1.7e-10 on the near-saturated ones.
- **V3.** Counting $\operatorname{Tr}(E^{-1}C)$ once instead of twice produces a gap of $3\times10^{11}$ to
  $5\times10^{12}$ budgets.
- **Not shown:** that Stata's measured gaps lie within the budget. That needs the budget computed in
  Mata at the test's own fits (owed with the test change).

### What Module 9 needs

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| $\Gamma$ | Module 4 (Gates 3, 4) |
| $\Delta$ at the canonical $\hat\theta$ | `fit.Delta` (Module 7) |
| $W_D = \operatorname{diag}(\Gamma)^{-1}$ | re-formed as a vector, as in Module 8; never stored |
| $T = (N-1) F(\hat\theta)$ | Module 7 (`T_raw`) |
| $D$ | Module 3's parameter count |

Then the two traces by @sec-gate5-traces's expansion — never $U$, never $M$ — and
$(a,b)$. Three implementation notes: report the degrees of freedom actually used,
since $T_2$ and $T_3$ target different chi-square distributions; assert $b$ with an
absolute tolerance, for the cancellation above; and the expansion supersedes this
section's earlier advice to compute $\operatorname{Tr}(M^2)$ as
$\sum_{ij}M_{ij}M_{ji}$. That advice was right about the trace step and silent
about the $O(p^{*3})$ of forming $M = U\Gamma$ in the first place, which is the
cost that actually matters once $p^*$ is in the hundreds.

### The nested difference test, DIFFTEST {#sec-difftest}

*Added 2026-10-08, for spec Module 12 (target 0.3.0).* Drafted in a Cloud session from
`794cd4a`, corrected and executed by the main session. The evaluation point is the
user's decision of 2026-10-08 (E-003); this section derives the statistic
and shows that the decided form is the one lavaan and Mplus compute. Still open, and not
settled here: what persists between the two fits, whether $V_1$ is used as is or rescaled
(spec Module 12), and $N$ against $N-1$ in the statistic.

**Setting.** One Stage 1, so $\hat s$, $\Gamma$ and $W = \operatorname{diag}(\Gamma)^{-1}$
are shared. Model $j$ has $\sigma_j(\theta_j)$, $\theta_j \in \mathbb R^{q_j}$, and
$T_j = (N-1)F_j(\hat\theta_j)$. $H_0$ is nested in $H_1$ by $\theta_1 = h(\theta_0)$ with
$\sigma_0(\theta_0) = \sigma_1(h(\theta_0))$; in the v1a grammar
$h(\theta_0) = H\theta_0 + c$, $H$ a $q_1\times q_0$ selection matrix. $d = q_1 - q_0$.
Nothing below uses the selection property: for a smooth $h$ (the invariance levels,
@sec-invariance-id Result I6) read $H=\partial h/\partial\theta_0$ at the true $\theta_0$, of full
column rank (added 2026-10-13).

**Step 1 (the quadratic form).** Under $H_0$, with $e = \sqrt N(\hat s - \sigma^*) \to
N(0,\Gamma)$ and $\Delta_0 = \Delta_1 H$ at the truth, the minimum-distance expansion behind
@sec-gate5 gives $N F_j(\hat\theta_j) = e'U_je + o_p(1)$,
$U_j = W - W\Delta_j(\Delta_j'W\Delta_j)^{-1}\Delta_j'W$. With $P_1 = \Delta_1'W\Delta_1$,

$$U_0 - U_1 = W\Delta_1 K \Delta_1'W, \qquad K = P_1^{-1} - H(H'P_1H)^{-1}H',$$

and $K = P_1^{-1/2}(I-\Pi)P_1^{-1/2}$ with $\Pi$ the projector onto
$\operatorname{col}(P_1^{1/2}H)$: PSD, rank $d$. So $T_0 - T_1$ is asymptotically
$\sum_{i=1}^d \lambda_i\chi^2_1$, the $\lambda_i$ the nonzero eigenvalues of
$(U_0-U_1)\Gamma$, real and non-negative.

**Step 2 (reduction to $q_1\times q_1$).** $AB$ and $BA$ share nonzero eigenvalues, twice:
with $V_1 = P_1^{-1}\Delta_1'W\Gamma W\Delta_1P_1^{-1}$ (Section 4.10's ACOV on the
$\sqrt N$ scale, as `dwlsmv_acov()` computes it), $\Delta_1'W\Gamma W\Delta_1 = P_1V_1P_1$
and the $\lambda_i$ are those of

$$M_1 = \big(P_1 - P_1H(H'P_1H)^{-1}H'P_1\big)V_1,$$

the spec's $M_1$. Then $T_3$'s rule at $D = d$:
$a_d = \sqrt{d/\operatorname{Tr}(M_1^2)}$, $b_d = d - a_d\operatorname{Tr}(M_1)$,
$T_{d3} = a_d(T_0 - T_1) + b_d$ on $d$ degrees of freedom. $b_d \ge 0$ by Cauchy–Schwarz on
$d$ non-negative eigenvalues; at $d = 1$, $b_d = 0$ and $T_{d3} = (T_0-T_1)/\lambda$;
at $W = \Gamma^{-1}$, $M_1$ is idempotent and $a_d = 1$, $b_d = 0$. $T3_0 - T3_1$ is not a
valid statistic: each marginal matches its own $\chi^2$, the difference matches nothing.

**Step 3 (the evaluation point, decided).** Steps 1–2 hold at the truth, where
$\Delta_0 = \Delta_1H$. A sample needs a point. Every $H_1$ quantity — $\Delta_1$, $W$,
$\Gamma$, $P_1$, $V_1$ — is taken at $\hat\theta_1$, and $H$ is replaced by

$$\hat h = \Delta_1(\hat\theta_1)^{+}\,\Delta_0(\hat\theta_0),$$

the least-squares coefficients of $H_0$'s Jacobian on $H_1$'s. Under $H_0$ both estimates
converge to points related by $h$, $\Delta_0(\theta_0) = \Delta_1(h(\theta_0))H$, and
$\Delta_1$ has full column rank, so $\hat h \to H$: the two forms are asymptotically
equivalent. For a non-affine $h$, $H$ here is $\partial h/\partial\theta_0$ at the limit of
$\hat\theta_0$, not a constant (`inv-nesting` asserts the identity at a point). Under an alternative $\hat\theta_1 \not\to h(\hat\theta_0)$ and they differ —
on the `beta0` pair below by a factor of two. Only $\hat h$ reproduces lavaan and Mplus.
For $\hat h$ of full column rank, lavaan's written form
$P_1^{-1}A'(AP_1^{-1}A')^{-1}AP_1^{-1}$, with $A$ spanning the orthocomplement of
$\operatorname{col}(\hat h)$, equals $P_1^{-1} - \hat h(\hat h'P_1\hat h)^{-1}\hat h'$:
`difftest-synth` asserts it.

```{r difftest-synth}
trc  <- function(A) sum(diag(A))
quad <- function(r, W) drop(crossprod(r, W %*% r))
Uof  <- function(W, Dl) W - W %*% Dl %*% solve(crossprod(Dl, W %*% Dl)) %*% t(Dl) %*% W
M1of <- function(P, H, V) (P - P %*% H %*% solve(t(H) %*% P %*% H) %*% t(H) %*% P) %*% V
ortho <- function(h) { q <- qr(h); t(qr.Q(q, complete = TRUE)[, -seq_len(ncol(h)), drop = FALSE]) }

set.seed(2026)
pstar <- 24; q1 <- 9; q0 <- 6; d <- q1 - q0
Gam  <- crossprod(matrix(rnorm(pstar^2), pstar)) / pstar + diag(pstar)
W    <- diag(1 / diag(Gam))
D1   <- matrix(rnorm(pstar * q1), pstar, q1)
H    <- diag(q1)[, c(1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9)]
cfix <- numeric(q1); cfix[c(3, 6, 8)] <- c(0, 0.3, 0)
sig0 <- rnorm(pstar); D0 <- D1 %*% H
P1   <- crossprod(D1, W %*% D1); Pinv <- solve(P1)
V1   <- Pinv %*% crossprod(D1, W %*% Gam %*% W %*% D1) %*% Pinv
K    <- Pinv - H %*% solve(t(H) %*% P1 %*% H) %*% t(H)
Ad   <- Uof(W, D0) - Uof(W, D1)
M1   <- M1of(P1, H, V1)

# Step 1, exact in a linear model sigma = sig0 + D1 theta with H0 true
e   <- drop(t(chol(Gam)) %*% rnorm(pstar))
s   <- sig0 + D1 %*% (H %*% rnorm(q0) + cfix) + e
F1  <- quad(s - sig0 - D1 %*% solve(P1, crossprod(D1, W %*% (s - sig0))), W)
y0  <- s - sig0 - D1 %*% cfix
F0  <- quad(y0 - D0 %*% solve(crossprod(D0, W %*% D0), crossprod(D0, W %*% y0)), W)
evK <- eigen((K + t(K)) / 2, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
stopifnot(abs((F0 - F1) / quad(e, Ad) - 1) < 1e-10,
          max(abs(Ad - W %*% D1 %*% K %*% t(D1) %*% W)) < 1e-10,
          min(evK) > -1e-12, sum(evK > 1e-8 * max(evK)) == d)

# Step 2: M1 carries the nonzero spectrum and both traces of (U0 - U1) Gamma
MG <- Ad %*% Gam
eb <- sort(Re(eigen(MG, only.values = TRUE)$values), decreasing = TRUE)
es <- sort(Re(eigen(M1, only.values = TRUE)$values), decreasing = TRUE)
trM <- trc(M1); trM2 <- sum(M1 * t(M1)); b_d <- d - sqrt(d / trM2) * trM
stopifnot(max(abs(eb[1:d] - es[1:d])) / es[1] < 1e-10,
          max(abs(c(eb[-(1:d)], es[-(1:d)]))) / es[1] < 1e-10, min(es[1:d]) > 0,
          abs(trM / trc(MG) - 1) < 1e-10, abs(trM2 / sum(MG * t(MG)) - 1) < 1e-10,
          b_d >= 0)

# Step 2's special cases: W = Gamma^-1 (idempotent) and d = 1 (b = 0)
Wf  <- solve(Gam); P1f <- crossprod(D1, Wf %*% D1)
M1f <- M1of(P1f, H, solve(P1f) %*% crossprod(D1, Wf %*% Gam %*% Wf %*% D1) %*% solve(P1f))
af  <- sqrt(d / sum(M1f * t(M1f)))
M1d <- M1of(P1, diag(q1)[, -q1], V1); lam <- trc(M1d)
stopifnot(max(abs(M1f %*% M1f - M1f)) < 1e-10, abs(af - 1) < 1e-10,
          abs(d - af * trc(M1f)) < 1e-10,
          abs(sum(M1d * t(M1d)) / lam^2 - 1) < 1e-10)      # rank 1: Tr(M^2) = Tr(M)^2

# Step 3: in a linear model Delta does not move, so h-hat is H exactly
hh_lin <- MASS::ginv(D1) %*% D0
stopifnot(max(abs(hh_lin - H)) < 1e-12)
# lavaan's A-form equals the K-form, for H and for an arbitrary full-rank h
hr <- H + matrix(rnorm(q1 * q0, sd = 0.3), q1, q0)
for (hx in list(H, hr)) {
  A  <- ortho(hx)
  KA <- Pinv %*% t(A) %*% solve(A %*% Pinv %*% t(A)) %*% A %*% Pinv
  stopifnot(max(abs(KA - (Pinv - hx %*% solve(t(hx) %*% P1 %*% hx) %*% t(hx)))) < 1e-10)
}
# negative control: an h that is not H moves the statistic
stopifnot(abs(trc(M1of(P1, hr, V1)) / trM - 1) > 1e-3)
c(trM = trM, trM2 = trM2, b_d = b_d)
```

The three corrections under @sec-gate5's compound-symmetry sweep, as there a property of
the approximations and not pass/fail, except that at $\rho = 0$ ($W = \Gamma^{-1}$) all
three must coincide:

```{r difftest-sweep}
#| cache: true
set.seed(303); Rrep <- 100000
row1 <- function(x, df, lbl, rho) data.frame(rho = rho, stat = lbl, df = df,
  mean = round(mean(x), 3), var = round(var(x), 2),
  reject_pct = round(100 * mean(x > qchisq(.95, df)), 2))
sweep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0, 0.5, 0.85), function(rr) {
  Gm <- matrix(rr, pstar, pstar); diag(Gm) <- 1
  Wm <- diag(1 / diag(Gm)); Adm <- Uof(Wm, D0) - Uof(Wm, D1); Mm <- Adm %*% Gm
  t1 <- trc(Mm); t2 <- sum(Mm * t(Mm)); a <- sqrt(d / t2); b <- d - a * t1
  Dh <- max(1, round(t1^2 / t2))
  E  <- matrix(rnorm(Rrep * pstar), Rrep) %*% chol(Gm)
  Td <- rowSums((E %*% Adm) * E)
  rbind(row1(Td * d / t1, d, "mean-only", rr),
        row1(Td * Dh / t1, Dh, "Satterthwaite", rr),
        row1(a * Td + b, d, "T3 form", rr))
}))
stopifnot(length(unique(sweep$reject_pct[sweep$rho == 0])) == 1)
sweep
```

Measured (main session, R 4.6.0): at $\rho = 0.5$ and $0.85$ the $T_3$ form rejects 4.84%
and 5.12%, mean-only 6.29% and 9.17%, Satterthwaite 4.29% and 3.87% (its $\hat D$ rounds to
2, then 1). Monte Carlo SE about 0.07%. The same pattern as @sec-gate5's sweep for $T$.

**Against lavaan.** lavaan 0.7.2's `lav_test_diff_satorra2000()` takes $\Delta$, $W$,
$\Gamma$ and $P$ from the $H_1$ fit; with `A.method = "delta"`, `lav_test_diff_a()` forms
$\hat h$ = `ginv(delta1) %*% delta0` and $A$ its orthocomplement. `"exact"` uses the
selection constraint instead. Case E, two nested pairs: `beta0` ($H_1$ `f2 ~ f1` against
`f2 ~ 0*f1`, $d = 1$, $H_0$ false) and `xload2` (two cross-loadings, $d = 2$, $H_0$ true).

```{r difftest-lavaan}
#| cache: true
library(lavaan)
root <- file.path("..", "..")
datE <- read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "data", "case_E.csv")); datE[] <- lapply(datE, ordered)
fitE <- function(m) sem(m, data = datE, ordered = names(datE), estimator = "WLSMV",
  parameterization = "delta", test = "scaled.shifted", zero.add = c(0.5, 0.0),
  zero.keep.margins = TRUE, bad.marker.crit = 0)
BASE <- "f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3\n f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6"
pairs_dt <- list(
  beta0  = list(h1 = paste(BASE, "f2 ~ f1", sep = "\n"), h0 = paste(BASE, "f2 ~ 0*f1", sep = "\n")),
  xload2 = list(h1 = "f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4\n f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6 + y3\n f1 ~~ f2",
                h0 = paste(BASE, "f1 ~~ f2", sep = "\n")))
flab <- function(f) { pt <- parTable(f); pt <- pt[pt$free > 0, ]; pt <- pt[order(pt$free), ]
                      paste0(pt$lhs, pt$op, pt$rhs) }
T3of <- function(D1, w, Gm, h, Td, d) {
  WD <- w * D1; P <- crossprod(D1, WD); Pi <- solve(P)
  M <- M1of(P, h, Pi %*% crossprod(WD, Gm %*% WD) %*% Pi)
  a <- sqrt(d / sum(M * t(M))); a * Td + d - a * trc(M)
}
lrt <- function(f0, f1, am) {
  o <- suppressWarnings(lavTestLRT(f0, f1, method = "satorra.2000", A.method = am,
                                   scaled.shifted = TRUE))
  o[["Chisq diff"]][which(!is.na(o[["Df diff"]]))]
}
res_dt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pairs_dt), function(tag) {
  f1 <- fitE(pairs_dt[[tag]]$h1); f0 <- fitE(pairs_dt[[tag]]$h0)
  l1 <- flab(f1); l0 <- flab(f0); d <- length(l1) - length(l0)
  H  <- matrix(0, length(l1), length(l0)); H[cbind(match(l0, l1), seq_along(l0))] <- 1
  Gm <- lavTech(f1, "gamma")[[1]]; w <- 1 / diag(Gm)
  stopifnot(max(abs(diag(lavTech(f1, "wls.v")[[1]]) - w)) == 0)   # lavaan's W is diag(Gamma)^-1
  D1 <- lavTech(f1, "delta")[[1]]; D0 <- lavTech(f0, "delta")[[1]]
  Td <- f0@test$standard$stat - f1@test$standard$stat
  data.frame(pair = tag, d = d, Td = Td,
             lav_delta = lrt(f0, f1, "delta"),
             hhat      = T3of(D1, w, Gm, MASS::ginv(D1) %*% D0, Td, d),
             selection = T3of(D1, w, Gm, H, Td, d),
             lav_exact = if (tag == "beta0") lrt(f0, f1, "exact") else NA_real_,
             h_gap     = max(abs(MASS::ginv(D1) %*% D0 - H)))
}))
rel <- function(x, y) abs(x / y - 1)
stopifnot(all(rel(res_dt$hhat, res_dt$lav_delta) < 1e-9),               # h-hat is lavaan
          rel(res_dt$selection[1], res_dt$lav_exact[1]) < 1e-9,          # selection is "exact"
          rel(res_dt$selection[1], res_dt$lav_delta[1]) > 0.5,           # negative control, H0 false
          rel(res_dt$selection[2], res_dt$lav_delta[2]) < 1e-2)          # H0 true: close, not equal
res_dt
```

Measured (main session, lavaan 0.7.2): $\hat h$ reproduces `"delta"` to $6\times10^{-14}$
(`beta0`) and $3\times10^{-11}$ (`xload2`); the selection form reproduces `"exact"` to
$10^{-14}$. On `beta0` $\hat h$ gives 506.935 and the selection form 1040.297, with
$\max|\hat h - H| = 0.95$; on `xload2` they differ by $2\times10^{-3}$ relative. The
$10^{-9}$ tolerances and the $10^{-2}$ bound were **chosen after measuring**.

**Against Mplus (a one-off scratch run, not executed here).** Mplus 8.10's DIFFTEST file
holds $F_1$ (Mplus's $F$, half lavaan's $T/(N-1)$), the number of groups, $p^*$, $q_1$, then
$\Delta_1$ row-major, $P_1$ and $V_1$ as packed upper triangles. Its blocks match lavaan's
$\hat\theta_1$ quantities to $2\times10^{-6}$–$6\times10^{-5}$ by spectrum, and it holds no
$\hat\theta_1$ and no parameter labels, so its $H_0$ run can only form $\hat h$. Computed on
Mplus's own saved $\Delta_1$, $P_1$, $V_1$ and $\Delta_0$, $\hat h$ gives 507.036068 and
0.049942 with $T = 2N\cdot F$; Mplus prints 507.036 and 0.050. The whole Mplus–lavaan gap is
$N$ against $N-1$. Scripts: a scratch run, discarded.

#### The precision band $\varepsilon$ (validation check 10)

*Added 2026-10-08.* Spec Module 12's check 10 aborts when $T_0 - T_1 < -\varepsilon$ and
reports 0 when $|T_0 - T_1| \le \varepsilon$. $\varepsilon$ must come from the fits' stopping
rule, not from results.

`dwlsmv_minimize()` minimizes $F(\theta) = r'Wr$, $r = s - \sigma(\theta)$ (no factor
$\tfrac12$), with the Gauss–Newton Hessian $H_{GN} = 2\Delta'W\Delta$, and declares
convergence only with the Newton decrement $\nu = g'H_{GN}^{-1}g \le \mathrm{nrtol} =
10^{-12}$. Near the minimum, with $\delta = \theta - \hat\theta$ and the true Hessian
$H_t$, $F(\theta) - F(\hat\theta) = \tfrac12\delta'H_t\delta$ and $g = H_t\delta$, so

$$\frac{F(\theta) - F(\hat\theta)}{\tfrac12\nu}
  = \frac{\delta'H_t\delta}{\delta'H_tH_{GN}^{-1}H_t\delta} \le \kappa,
\qquad \kappa = \lambda_{\max}\big(H_t^{-1}H_{GN}\big).$$

With zero residuals $H_t = H_{GN}$ and $\kappa = 1$. Each fit's $T_j$ therefore exceeds
its minimum by at most $\tfrac12\kappa(N-1)\,\mathrm{nrtol}$. A true difference
$T_0^* - T_1^* \ge 0$ can be observed as low as $-\tfrac12\kappa(N-1)\,\mathrm{nrtol}$
(only $T_1$'s excess lowers it), which is the derived band:

$$\varepsilon = \tfrac12\,\kappa\,(N-1)\,\mathrm{nrtol}.$$

The argument needs $\nu \le \mathrm{nrtol}$ *at the returned* $\hat\theta$, not only at
optimize()'s last internal evaluation. `tests/unit/test_decrement.do` asserts it (main
session, StataMP 18, 2026-10-08): on seven fits, including all four DIFFTEST models
(`str_marker` and `cor_marker` are `beta0`'s H₁ and `xload2`'s H₀), $\nu \le 2.0\times10^{-18}$
at `fit.theta`.
In practice the band is therefore conservative by about six orders of magnitude.

Production has $\Delta$ but not $\sigma$'s second derivatives, so $\kappa$ is not computed
there. `difftest-kappa` measures it on the four Case E fits, building $F$ from lavaan's own
$\sigma(\theta)$ (internal functions, so tied to lavaan 0.7.2) and its Hessian by central
differences at two step sizes.

```{r difftest-kappa}
#| cache: true
Fof <- function(fit) {
  s <- lavTech(fit, "wls.obs")[[1]]; w <- 1 / diag(lavTech(fit, "gamma")[[1]]); M <- fit@Model
  function(x) { Mx <- lavaan:::lav_model_set_parameters(M, x = x)
                r <- s - lavaan:::lav_model_wls_est(Mx)[[1]]; sum(w * r^2) }
}
hess_num <- function(f, x, h) {
  q <- length(x); H <- matrix(0, q, q); E <- diag(h, q)
  for (i in 1:q) for (j in i:q)
    H[i, j] <- H[j, i] <- (f(x + E[, i] + E[, j]) - f(x + E[, i] - E[, j]) -
                           f(x - E[, i] + E[, j]) + f(x - E[, i] - E[, j])) / (4 * h^2)
  H
}
kap <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pairs_dt), function(tag) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("h1", "h0"),
  function(role) {
    fit <- fitE(pairs_dt[[tag]][[role]]); f <- Fof(fit); x <- lav_model_get_parameters(fit@Model)
    D <- lavTech(fit, "delta")[[1]]; w <- 1 / diag(lavTech(fit, "gamma")[[1]])
    HG <- 2 * crossprod(D, w * D)
    k <- sapply(c(1e-3, 1e-4), function(h)
      max(Re(eigen(solve(hess_num(f, x, h), HG), only.values = TRUE)$values)))
    stopifnot(abs(f(x) - fit@test$standard$stat / (lavInspect(fit, "ntotal") - 1)) < 1e-12)
    data.frame(pair = tag, role = role, F = f(x), kappa_h3 = k[1], kappa_h4 = k[2])
  }))))
stopifnot(all(abs(kap$kappa_h3 / kap$kappa_h4 - 1) < 1e-4))   # the Hessian is resolved
kap
```

Measured (main session, lavaan 0.7.2): $\kappa$ = 1.0215 and 1.0000 for `beta0`'s $H_1$ and
$H_0$ (the latter at $F = 0.31$, heavy misfit), 1.0367 and 1.0215 for `xload2`'s. Stable to
$10^{-6}$ between the two step sizes. The step-size agreement tolerance $10^{-4}$ was
**chosen after measuring**.

**Not established here:** a bound on $\kappa$ for every model, and that `optimize()`
evaluates $\nu$ at the parameters it returns rather than at the previous iterate. The second
is to be asserted in the Stata test that builds check 10 (compute $\nu$ at $\hat\theta$ and
require $\nu \le \mathrm{nrtol}$). **Decided 2026-10-08 (user):** the allowance is
$\kappa \le 2$, so $\varepsilon = (N-1)\,\mathrm{nrtol}$, **chosen after measuring** the
values above.


### Binary and mixed-item invariance: identification and degrees of freedom {#sec-invariance-id}

*Added 2026-10-08, for 0.3.0 (E-003, the 2026-10-08 invariance boundary).
Drafted in a Cloud session from `742a368` (no R there); executed by the main session (R 4.6.0,
lavaan 0.7.2): every assertion holds after two corrections, both recorded in the verification
below. W&E's propositions are cited as E-035 records them; the
main session compared the levels with W&E's Conditions 19 and 27 in the paper's text: the
loadings level for polytomous items is Condition 19 and the intercepts level is Condition 27.*

**Scope.** Delta parameterization; four levels (configural, thresholds, loadings, intercepts);
no means level and no strict level. The results are stated for one factor per item set (simple
structure) and **conditionally on the configural model being locally identified**. That
condition is the ordinary single-group CFA question and is not re-derived here.

#### Notation

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $g=1..G$ | groups; group 1 is the reference |
| $j=1..p$ | items; $K_j$ categories, $C_j=K_j-1$ thresholds; $\mathcal P=\{j:C_j\ge2\}$ the *polytomous* items |
| $\tau_{jc}$ | latent-response threshold (the invariant quantity, unscaled) |
| $\nu_{gj}$ | latent-response intercept |
| $\lambda_{gj}$ | unscaled loading |
| $\omega_{gj}$ | scale factor $=\operatorname{Var}(y^*_{gj})^{-1/2}$ ("delta"). Not $\Delta$, the Jacobian |
| $\phi_g,\ \kappa_g$ | factor variance and mean. $\psi_g$ if the factor is exogenous |
| $s_{gjc}$ | the standardized threshold statistic ($=\hat s_\tau$ at Stage 1) |
| $u_{gj}$ | $\omega_{gj}\lambda_{gj}\sqrt{\phi_g}$, the standardized loading |

Reference group (delta): $\omega_{1j}=1,\ \nu_{1j}=0,\ \phi_1=1,\ \kappa_1=0$. The model-implied statistics are

$$ s_{gjc}=\omega_{gj}\big(\tau_{gjc}-\nu_{gj}-\lambda_{gj}\kappa_g\big),\qquad
\rho_{g,ij}=u_{gi}u_{gj}\ (i\ne j),\qquad
\Theta^*_{g,jj}=1-u_{gj}^2 \text{ (derived)}. $$

Under delta $\Theta$ stays derived. $\omega_{gj}$ is the scale and $\Theta^*$ follows from it, so
the "$\Theta$ is derived, never free" rule is not reopened. Strict invariance (equal residual
variances) would need $\omega$ fixed and is not expressible, which matches the 2026-10-08
boundary.

#### The four levels as parameter classes (groups $g\ge2$)

| Level | $\tau$ | $\lambda$ | $\omega_g$ | $\nu_g$ | $\phi_g$ | $\kappa_g$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| configural | own | own | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| thresholds | tied | own ($=u_g$) | free iff $j\in\mathcal P$, else 1 | free | 1 | 0 |
| loadings | tied | tied | free (all $j$) | free | free iff $\mathcal P_f\neq\emptyset$ | 0 |
| intercepts | tied | tied | free | 0 | free | free |

"Own" means group-specific and free. At the configural and thresholds levels, $u_{gj}$ is the free
loading itself.

#### Results

**Result I0 (reduction).** A level is identified exactly when its parameter-to-statistics map has
full column rank $q$ at generic parameter values, and its degrees of freedom are $D-q$, where
$D=\sum_g(T+\binom p2)$. This is the same rank notion as Module 3's. Chunks `inv-algebra` and
`inv-lavaan` compute $D-q$ two independent ways and compare them.

**Result I1 (thresholds level is item-local).** Given the configural $s_{gjc}$:
- $C_j\ge2$: the equations $s_{gjc}=\omega_{gj}(\tau_{jc}-\nu_{gj})$, $c=1,2$, solve to
  $\omega_{gj}=(s_{gj2}-s_{gj1})/(\tau_{j2}-\tau_{j1})$, which is positive because both pairs are
  ordered, and then $\nu_{gj}$. They leave $C_j-2$ restrictions.
- $C_j=1$: $(\omega,\nu)$ are not separately identified. Fix $\omega_{gj}=1$ and let $\nu_{gj}$ be
  free. The item is then saturated and contributes no restriction.

No factor-level parameter is involved, so mixing binary and polytomous items needs no new
condition at this level. This reproduces the note's finding 2 ($K=3$: $\Delta df=0$; $K\ge4$:
$K-3$ per item) and finding 3 (binary $\equiv$ configural). The latter is W&E's Proposition 4
note and §5.2 as the note records them.

**Result I2 (loadings level is factor-level, not item-level).** Given the configural $u_{gj}$ and
$\lambda_j$: if $j\in\mathcal P$, then $(\omega_{gj},\nu_{gj})$ are known from its thresholds
(Result I1), so
$$\sqrt{\phi_g}=u_{gj}/(\omega_{gj}\lambda_j)$$
is identified. Every binary item $j'$ then gets $\omega_{gj'}=u_{gj'}/(\lambda_{j'}\sqrt{\phi_g})$,
and $\nu_{gj'}$ from its one threshold. **So $\phi_g$ is identified iff the factor has at least
one polytomous item.**
- **Counterexample to "each item's level holds item by item".** Take an all-binary factor and free
  $\phi_g$, as the polytomous rule prescribes. Then $u_{gj}=\omega_{gj}\lambda_j\sqrt{\phi_g}$
  depends on $(\omega_{gj})_j$ and $\phi_g$ only through $\omega_{gj}\sqrt{\phi_g}$. The family
  $\phi_g\to t\phi_g,\ \omega_{gj}\to\omega_{gj}t^{-1/2}$ leaves $\sigma$ unchanged, with $\nu$
  untouched. The deficiency is exactly 1 per later group and holds at every parameter value, as
  the $\psi_{12}$ rank deficiency in spec §4.8 does. Fixing $\phi_g=1$ gives the model equivalent
  to the configural one (W&E Proposition 6, per the note).
- A direct consequence: in a mixed factor the loadings step can be **empty**. Its $\Delta df$ is
  $|\mathcal P|-\mathbf 1[\mathcal P\ne\emptyset]$, which is 0 when exactly one item is
  polytomous. Design D below is such a case.

**Result I3 (intercepts level; the ratio lemma).** With $\nu=0$ and $u_{gj}$ identified, write
$r_{jc}=\tau_{jc}/\lambda_j$, a group-1 quantity. Then for every threshold
$$ \frac{s_{gjc}}{u_{gj}}=\frac{\omega_{gj}(\tau_{jc}-\lambda_j\kappa_g)}{\omega_{gj}\lambda_j\sqrt{\phi_g}}
=\frac{r_{jc}-\kappa_g}{\sqrt{\phi_g}} . $$
This is linear in $r_{jc}$ with slope $1/\sqrt{\phi_g}$ and intercept $-\kappa_g/\sqrt{\phi_g}$.
**So $(\phi_g,\kappa_g)$, and then every $\omega_{gj}$, are identified iff the set
$\{r_{jc}\}$ over the factor's thresholds has at least two distinct values.**
- A polytomous item contributes $\tau_{j1}<\tau_{j2}$, hence two distinct $r$ for $\lambda_j>0$, so
  a factor with any polytomous item is always identified.
- An all-binary factor is identified iff the $\tau_j/\lambda_j$ are not all equal. That is
  exactly W&E's exceptional set for Proposition 11, as the note states it, so it is a
  consistency check on this derivation.

**Result I4 (degrees of freedom).** With $T=\sum_jC_j$, $F$ the number of factors, $G$ groups and
$p^*=\binom p2$, for simple structure with one free loading per item and unit-variance metric in
group 1:
$$ df_{\rm conf}=G\big(p^*-p\big),\qquad
df_{\rm thr}=df_{\rm conf}+(G-1)\!\!\sum_j\max(C_j-2,0), $$
$$ df_{\rm load}=df_{\rm thr}+(G-1)\big(|\mathcal P|-F_+\big),\qquad
df_{\rm int}=df_{\rm conf}+(G-1)\big(T-2F\big), $$
with $F_+$ the number of factors that have a polytomous item. The increment from loadings to
intercepts is $(G-1)(p-2F+F_+)$.
- *Binary.* $df_{\rm conf}=G(p^*-p)$, thresholds and loadings add 0, and intercepts add
  $(G-1)(p-2)$ for $F=1$. $p=5,G=2$: 10, 10, 10, 13.
- *All $K\ge3$.* Increments: thresholds $p(K-3)$, loadings $p-1$, intercepts $p-1$. These are
  the note's measured $\Delta df$ for $p=3,5$ and $K=3,4,5$.

*Not established:* the $G$ dependence beyond $G=2$ and multi-factor models with cross-loadings.
For those, Module 3's rank check at run time is the authority and these formulas are an upper
bound.

**Result I5 (the singular case).** On an all-binary factor with $r_j\equiv c$ for all $j$, the
intercepts-level map depends on $(\omega_{gj},\phi_g,\kappa_g)$ only through
$$a_{gj}=\omega_{gj}\lambda_j\sqrt{\phi_g}\quad\text{and}\quad m_g=(c-\kappa_g)/\sqrt{\phi_g},$$
which is $p+1$ combinations of $p+2$ parameters.
- The null direction in $(\omega_{gj},\phi_g,\kappa_g)$ is
  $$ n=(\omega_{g1},\dots,\omega_{gp},\ -2\phi_g,\ c-\kappa_g). $$
  Check: $d\ln\rho=2\,\mathrm da-\mathrm d\ln\phi\cdot(-1)$, and $\mathrm ds_j=\lambda_j[\omega_j(c-\kappa)-\omega_j(c-\kappa)]=0$.
  The chunk `inv-algebra` asserts $\|Jn\|<10^{-8}$.
- The rank deficiency is $G-1$, so the nominal df overstates the true df by $G-1$. For
  $p=5,G=2$: nominal 13, true 14. Both H₁ and H₀ in a DIFFTEST built on this model would carry
  the wrong $d$.
- *Detection.* This is a structured Δ deficiency on a measure-zero set, so exact detection is a
  rank test at an exact point. Three consequences:
  1. At sample estimates $\hat r_j$ are never exactly equal, so Δ(θ̂) is full rank but ill
     conditioned, with a small $\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}$ above the $10^{-8}$ criterion. The
     symptom is large SEs on $\phi_g,\kappa_g$, not an abort.
  2. At the *start*, thresholds start at $s_\tau$. Balanced binary items (all $\tau=0$) give
     $r\equiv0$ **exactly**, whatever the loadings. Spec §4.8's second-point perturbation moves
     $\lambda,\beta,\psi$ and leaves thresholds unchanged, so it **does not leave the singular
     set** in that case. The rank check aborts correctly there, but only because it cannot escape.
     With nonzero equal $\tau/\lambda$, perturbing $\lambda$ does leave the set.
  3. An invariance-specific diagnostic is needed: the spread of $\hat r_{jc}$ within each factor,
     relative to its sampling variability, or equivalently the conditioning of the
     $(\phi_g,\kappa_g)$ block of the information. **I do not choose a cutoff** (project rule:
     anything chosen after seeing data must be labelled).

**Result I6 (consecutive levels are nested through a smooth map).** For the pair (restricted
$\theta_0$, less restricted $\theta_1$), each step is $\sigma_0(\theta_0)=\sigma_1(h(\theta_0))$:

| Step | $h$ |
|---|---|
| configural $\leftarrow$ thresholds | $s_{g}\mapsto\omega(\tau-\nu)$ |
| thresholds $\leftarrow$ loadings | $u'_{gj}:=\omega_{gj}\lambda_j\sqrt{\phi_g}$; $\omega'_{gj}:=\omega_{gj}$ for $j\in\mathcal P$; for a binary $j$ (whose $\omega'$ is fixed at 1 at the thresholds level) $\nu'_{gj}:=\tau_j-\omega_{gj}(\tau_j-\nu_{gj})$ |
| loadings $\leftarrow$ intercepts | $\nu':=\lambda\kappa$ (if $\phi$ is free there); for an all-binary factor $\omega':=\omega\sqrt\phi,\ \nu':=\tau-(\tau-\lambda\kappa)/\sqrt\phi$ |

*Corrected 2026-10-13 (main session):* the thresholds $\leftarrow$ loadings row first gave only
$u'$. Without the binary items' $\nu'$ the map misses $\sigma$ by 0.57–0.88 on every design with a
binary item in the scratch run (0.56–1.14 in the document run; `inv-nesting`, kept there as a
negative control); the nesting claim itself was right.

- $h$ is smooth and **not** a selection matrix, unlike the v1a case in `@sec-difftest`'s Setting
  ($h=H\theta_0+c$).
- `@sec-difftest`'s Steps 1–3 use $h$ only through $\Delta_0=\Delta_1H$ with
  $H=\partial h/\partial\theta_0$ at the truth of full column rank, which the chain rule gives and
  which holds iff $\theta_0$ is locally identified (given $\Delta_1$ of full column rank). Re-read
  2026-10-13 (main session; the earlier text referred to "Steps 2–7", which do not exist): Step 2
  is algebra in any full-rank $H$; Step 3's $\hat h\to H$ needs only the chain rule, with $H$
  evaluated at the limit point because $h$ is not affine. Nothing uses the selection property.
  `inv-nesting` asserts $\hat h=\partial h/\partial\theta_0$ at a point with $\theta_1=h(\theta_0)$.
- Non-adjacent pairs (e.g. configural $\leftarrow$ intercepts) are nested through the composition
  of the maps, smooth wherever each is; `inv-nesting` asserts one composition.
- **The nesting is local, not global.** Every map from the loadings level on takes
  $\sqrt{\phi_g}$, so $h$ is defined only where $\phi_g>0$. The estimator does not bound $\phi_g$
  (a Heywood case is reported, not prevented). At $\phi_g<0$ a factor with three or more items
  has all-negative group-$g$ correlations, which no real $u$ reproduces, since
  $\rho_{12}\rho_{13}\rho_{23}=(u_1u_2u_3)^2\ge0$: there $\sigma_0(\theta_0)$ lies outside
  $\sigma_1$'s image. Steps 1–3 are unaffected (the truth is interior). The precision band's
  premise, "$H_0$'s optimum is feasible in $H_1$, so $T_0\ge T_1$", is **not** guaranteed at an
  $H_0$ estimate with $\hat\phi_g\le0$. What the validation contract does then is not settled here.
- A step with $d=0$ (binary thresholds and loadings; design D's loadings) is an *equivalent
  model*, not a test.

#### Verification

Two independent computations agree in every cell. The first is an own-σ(θ) Jacobian in base R
(`inv_model`), independent of lavaan. The second is lavaan's `df` and `Delta` from fitted
models: lavaan's df equals Result I4 in all 16 design × level cells.

**Two corrections made on the first run.** (1) `lavTech(fit, "delta")` has a column for every
free parameter *before* equality constraints (lavaan ties by labels and `==` constraints), so
the draft's `ncol(delta) == npar` failed; Δ is now post-multiplied by
`lav_con_eq_basis()`, as `lavTestLRT` does, so the rank checks see the constrained Δ lavaan
estimates with. (2) A threshold restriction *adds* df, so design D's check is
`thresholds$df > configural$df`; the draft had the inequality reversed. The rank tolerance
1e-7, the misfit bound 5 and the conditioning factor 10 were set before measuring and held
(measured: misfit 51.3; conditioning 9.3e-5 singular against 0.0156 generic). The χ²-equality
tolerance, provisional at 1e-3, is **1e-6, chosen after measuring** gaps of at most
1.2e-9.

```{r inv-setup}
#| eval: true
library(lavaan)
cat("lavaan", as.character(packageVersion("lavaan")), "\n")        # provenance, not a check
INV_TOL <- 1e-7                                                    # provisional rank ratio

inv_lam <- c(.60, .65, .70, .75, .80)
inv_tau <- function(K, shift = .1)
  lapply(seq_along(K), function(j) qnorm(seq_len(K[j] - 1L) / K[j]) + shift * j)

inv_sim <- function(K, tau, lam, N = 2000L, kappa2 = .3, phi2 = 1.44,
                    th2 = seq(.4, .8, length.out = length(K)), seed = 1L) {
  set.seed(seed); p <- length(K)
  one <- function(n, kap, phi, th) {
    eta <- rnorm(n, kap, sqrt(phi))
    sapply(seq_len(p), function(j) findInterval(lam[j] * eta + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(th[j])), tau[[j]]))
  }
  # group 1 has total latent-response variance 1 (delta reference); group 2 is
  # nu = 0, same lambda and tau, free factor mean/variance and residuals
  d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:2, each = N),
                  rbind(one(N, 0, 1, 1 - lam^2), one(N, kappa2, phi2, th2)))
  names(d)[-1] <- paste0("y", seq_len(p))
  for (g in 1:2) for (j in seq_len(p))
    stopifnot(length(unique(d[d$g == g, j + 1L])) == K[j])   # no empty category (O6 is not under test)
  attr(d, "K") <- K
  d
}

# ---- the level table as code (group 2 status of each class) --------------------
inv_spec <- function(K, level) {
  p <- length(K); poly <- K > 2L
  list(tied_tau = level != "configural",
       tied_lam = level %in% c("loadings", "intercepts", "naive_loadings", "semtools_loadings"),
       om  = switch(level, configural = rep("fix", p), thresholds = ifelse(poly, "free", "fix"),
                    semtools_loadings = rep("fix", p), rep("free", p)),
       nu  = if (level %in% c("configural", "intercepts")) rep("fix", p) else rep("free", p),
       phi = level %in% c("intercepts", "naive_loadings", "semtools_loadings") ||
             (level == "loadings" && any(poly)),
       kap = level == "intercepts")
}

# ---- lavaan syntax, explicit (nothing relies on lavaan's automatic freeing) ----
inv_syntax <- function(K, level) {
  sp <- inv_spec(K, level); p <- length(K); y <- paste0("y", seq_len(p))
  ld <- if (sp$tied_lam) sprintf("c(l%d,l%d)*%s", seq_len(p), seq_len(p), y)
        else sprintf("c(NA,NA)*%s", y)
  out <- paste("f =~", paste(ld, collapse = " + "))
  if (sp$tied_tau) for (j in seq_len(p)) {
    cc <- seq_len(K[j] - 1L)
    out <- c(out, sprintf("%s | %s", y[j],
             paste(sprintf("c(t%d_%d,t%d_%d)*t%d", j, cc, j, cc, cc), collapse = " + ")))
  }
  c(out,
    sprintf("%s ~*~ c(1,%s)*%s", y, ifelse(sp$om == "free", "NA", "1"), y),
    sprintf("%s ~ c(0,%s)*1",    y, ifelse(sp$nu == "free", "NA", "0")),
    sprintf("f ~~ c(1,%s)*f", if (sp$phi) "NA" else "1"),
    sprintf("f ~ c(0,%s)*1",  if (sp$kap) "NA" else "0")) |> paste(collapse = "\n")
}

inv_fit <- function(dat, level) {
  K <- attr(dat, "K"); p <- length(K); warns <- character()
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    cfa(inv_syntax(K, level), data = dat, group = "g", ordered = paste0("y", seq_len(p)),
        estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta", std.lv = TRUE),
    warning = function(w) { warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") })
  list(fit = fit, warns = warns, conv = lavInspect(fit, "converged"),
       df = unname(fitMeasures(fit, "df")), chisq = unname(fitMeasures(fit, "chisq")),
       npar = unname(fitMeasures(fit, "npar")),
       delta = {                         # constrained Delta: free columns times lavaan's equality basis
         B <- lavaan:::lav_con_eq_basis(fit@Model); D <- do.call(rbind, lavTech(fit, "delta"))
         if (is.null(B)) D else D %*% B })
}

# ---- own sigma(theta), G = 2: thresholds then vech-offdiagonal R, per group -----
inv_model <- function(K, level) {
  sp <- inv_spec(K, level); p <- length(K); C <- K - 1L; nT <- sum(C); poly <- K > 2L
  itm <- rep(seq_len(p), C)
  off <- function(u) { R <- tcrossprod(u); R[lower.tri(R)] }     # column-major lower triangle
  lay <- switch(level,
    configural        = c(tau = nT, lam = p, tau2 = nT, lam2 = p),
    thresholds        = c(tau = nT, lam = p, lam2 = p, om = sum(poly), nu = p),
    loadings          = ,
    naive_loadings    = c(tau = nT, lam = p, om = p, nu = p, phi = as.integer(sp$phi)),
    intercepts        = c(tau = nT, lam = p, om = p, phi = 1L, kap = 1L),
    semtools_loadings = c(tau = nT, lam = p, nu = p, phi = 1L))
  sigma <- function(x) {
    z <- split(x, rep(names(lay), lay))
    phi <- if (is.null(z$phi)) 1 else z$phi
    kap <- if (is.null(z$kap)) 0 else z$kap
    om <- rep(1, p); nu <- rep(0, p)
    if (!is.null(z$om)) { if (level == "thresholds") om[poly] <- z$om else om <- z$om }
    if (!is.null(z$nu)) nu <- z$nu
    s1 <- c(z$tau, off(z$lam))
    s2 <- if (level == "configural") c(z$tau2, off(z$lam2)) else {
      lam2 <- if (level == "thresholds") z$lam2 else om * z$lam * sqrt(phi)
      c(om[itm] * (z$tau - nu[itm] - z$lam[itm] * kap), off(lam2))
    }
    c(s1, s2)
  }
  list(sigma = sigma, lay = lay)
}
inv_point <- function(m, tau, lam) {          # a generic, deterministic parameter point
  p <- length(lam)
  gen <- list(tau = unlist(tau), lam = lam, tau2 = unlist(tau) + .05, lam2 = lam + .05,
              om = seq(.8, 1.3, length.out = p), nu = seq(-.2, .2, length.out = p),
              phi = 1.3, kap = .35)
  unlist(lapply(names(m$lay), function(n) gen[[n]][seq_len(m$lay[[n]])]), use.names = FALSE)
}
inv_jac  <- function(f, x, h = 1e-5)
  sapply(seq_along(x), function(i) { e <- replace(numeric(length(x)), i, h); (f(x + e) - f(x - e)) / (2 * h) })
inv_rank <- function(J, tol = INV_TOL) { s <- svd(J, nu = 0, nv = 0)$d; sum(s > tol * s[1]) }

# ---- Result I4 as code ------------------------------------------------------------
inv_df <- function(K, level, G = 2L) {
  p <- length(K); C <- K - 1L; P2 <- sum(C >= 2L); Fp <- as.integer(P2 >= 1L)   # F = 1
  d0 <- G * (p * (p - 1) / 2 - p)
  d0 + (G - 1L) * switch(level, configural = 0, thresholds = sum(pmax(C - 2L, 0L)),
                         loadings = sum(pmax(C - 2L, 0L)) + P2 - Fp, intercepts = sum(C) - 2L)
}
inv_designs <- list(A = rep(2L, 5), B = rep(3L, 5), C = c(3L, 3L, 2L, 2L, 2L), D = c(4L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L),
                    E = c(4L, 4L, 4L, 2L, 2L))   # E: the §4.8 worked example (2026-10-08)
inv_levels  <- c("configural", "thresholds", "loadings", "intercepts")
```

```{r inv-note}
  stopifnot(unname(d["thresholds"] - d["configural"]) == p * (K - 3),     # K = 3: 0; K = 4: 3, 5; K = 5: 6, 10
            unname(d["loadings"]   - d["thresholds"])  == p - 1,
            unname(d["intercepts"] - d["loadings"])    == p - 1)
}
```

```{r inv-algebra}
# (a) own-sigma Jacobian: rank = npar and D - rank = the formula, every design x level
for (nm in names(inv_designs)) for (l in inv_levels) {
  K <- inv_designs[[nm]]; m <- inv_model(K, l); x <- inv_point(m, inv_tau(K), inv_lam)
  J <- inv_jac(m$sigma, x)
  stopifnot(inv_rank(J) == length(x), nrow(J) - inv_rank(J) == inv_df(K, l))
}
KA <- inv_designs$A

# (b) negative control 1: free phi_g on an all-binary factor at the loadings level
mN <- inv_model(KA, "naive_loadings"); xN <- inv_point(mN, inv_tau(KA), inv_lam); JN <- inv_jac(mN$sigma, xN)
stopifnot(length(xN) == 21, inv_rank(JN) == 20, nrow(JN) - length(xN) == 9, nrow(JN) - inv_rank(JN) == 10)

# (c) negative control 2: semTools' binary "loadings" model is over-restricted (df 14 vs 10)
mS <- inv_model(KA, "semtools_loadings"); xS <- inv_point(mS, inv_tau(KA), inv_lam)
stopifnot(nrow(inv_jac(mS$sigma, xS)) - length(xS) == 14)

# (d) Result I5: exact singular set (tau_j / lambda_j = c for all j) and its null vector
mI <- inv_model(KA, "intercepts")
for (cc in c(.4, 0)) {                                   # cc = 0 is the balanced-items case
  x <- inv_point(mI, as.list(cc * inv_lam), inv_lam); J <- inv_jac(mI$sigma, x)
  stopifnot(inv_rank(J) == length(x) - 1L)
  n <- numeric(length(x)); n[11:15] <- x[11:15]; n[16] <- -2 * x[16]; n[17] <- cc - x[17]   # tau|lam|om|phi|kap
  stopifnot(max(abs(J %*% n)) < 1e-8)
}
# a polytomous item removes the exception even when every binary ratio is equal
KD <- inv_designs$D; mD <- inv_model(KD, "intercepts")
xD <- inv_point(mD, c(list(qnorm(1:3 / 4)), as.list(.4 * inv_lam[-1])), inv_lam)
stopifnot(inv_rank(inv_jac(mD$sigma, xD)) == length(xD))

# (e) Result I3's ratio lemma, and identification by regression on r = tau / lambda
x <- inv_point(mI, inv_tau(KA), inv_lam)
tau <- x[1:5]; lam <- x[6:10]; om <- x[11:15]; phi <- x[16]; kap <- x[17]
s2 <- om * (tau - lam * kap); u <- om * lam * sqrt(phi); r <- tau / lam
stopifnot(max(abs(s2 / u - (r - kap) / sqrt(phi))) < 1e-12)
cf <- unname(coef(lm(s2 / u ~ r)))
stopifnot(abs(1 / cf[2]^2 - phi) < 1e-9, abs(-cf[1] / cf[2] - kap) < 1e-9)
stopifnot(qr(cbind(1, rep(.4, 5)))$rank == 1)            # equal r: slope and intercept collinear
```

**The rank at the starting values (2026-10-08).** Module 3 checks Δ's rank at θ⁽⁰⁾ only, so the
level models must be full rank at the starts dwlsmv would use: every λ at 0.7, τ at the sample
thresholds (a tied τ at group 1's; its start is open, E-036), ω = 1, ν = 0,
α = κ = 0 and a later group's free φ at 1. The chunk evaluates the own-σ Jacobian there for every
design and level. Result I5 predicts the one exception: an all-binary factor at the intercepts
level whose τ_j/λ_j are all equal, which equal λ starts turn into equal *sample* thresholds; the
chunk shows it on design A with every threshold at 0, and that a polytomous item (design E)
removes it.

*Executed by the main session from the repository file, 2026-10-08 (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2),
with design E added to every chunk:* every assertion held. Design E's df are 10, 13, 15, 19
in lavaan, Result I4 and the hand count alike, with 32, 29, 27, 23 free parameters. At the
starts every design × level is full rank; the smallest σ_min/σ_max is 0.021 (A, intercepts),
printed, not asserted. So the binary intercepts-level start can fail Module 3's rank check
exactly on I5's singular set, which the open singular-case guards must meet before the fit.

```{r inv-start}
inv_start <- function(m, tau) {               # Module 3's starts, in inv_model's layout
  gen <- list(tau = unlist(tau), lam = rep(.7, 5), tau2 = unlist(tau) + .05, lam2 = rep(.7, 5),
              om = rep(1, 5), nu = rep(0, 5), phi = 1, kap = 0)
  unlist(lapply(names(m$lay), function(n) gen[[n]][seq_len(m$lay[[n]])]), use.names = FALSE)
}
for (nm in names(inv_designs)) for (l in inv_levels) {
  K <- inv_designs[[nm]]; m <- inv_model(K, l); x0 <- inv_start(m, inv_tau(K))
  J0 <- inv_jac(m$sigma, x0)
  cat(sprintf("start rank %s %-10s %2d of %2d, sv ratio %.3g\n", nm, l, inv_rank(J0), length(x0),
              { s <- svd(J0, nu = 0, nv = 0)$d; min(s) / max(s) }))
  stopifnot(inv_rank(J0) == length(x0))
}
# Result I5 at the start: balanced binary thresholds (all 0) with equal lambda starts
mI <- inv_model(KA, "intercepts")
stopifnot(inv_rank(inv_jac(mI$sigma, inv_start(mI, as.list(rep(0, 5))))) == length(inv_start(mI, as.list(rep(0, 5)))) - 1L)
# ... and design E's polytomous items keep it full rank with all binary thresholds at 0
mE <- inv_model(inv_designs$E, "intercepts")
tE <- c(lapply(1:3, function(j) qnorm(1:3 / 4)), list(0, 0))
stopifnot(inv_rank(inv_jac(mE$sigma, inv_start(mE, tE))) == length(inv_start(mE, tE)))
```

#### Result I6's maps, executed {#sec-inv-nesting}

*Added 2026-10-13 (main session), for the generated-chain exemption gate (spec Module 12 check
8).* Each of Result I6's maps is applied to random points of the restricted level and
$\sigma_0(\theta_0)=\sigma_1(h(\theta_0))$ is asserted with `inv_model`'s own $\sigma$, on all five
designs, 20 points each. The chunk also asserts one composition, the I6-as-first-printed negative
control, $\hat h=\partial h/\partial\theta_0$, and the $\phi_g<0$ non-representability. Tolerances,
**chosen after measuring** on a scratch run of the same code (discarded):
$10^{-12}$ for the map identities (measured at most $4.4\times10^{-16}$), $> 0.1$ for the negative
control (measured 0.57–0.88), $10^{-8}$ for $\hat h$ against central differences of step
$10^{-5}$ (measured $8.4\times10^{-12}$). In the full document run (2026-10-13, R 4.6.0, lavaan
0.7.2, 174 chunks, its own random stream) the identities stayed at most $6.7\times10^{-16}$, the
negative control 0.56–1.14 on designs A, C, D, E (0 on B), and $\hat h$ at $2.7\times10^{-11}$.

```{r inv-nesting}
nz_split <- function(m, x) split(x, factor(rep(names(m$lay), m$lay), levels = names(m$lay)))
nz_pack  <- function(m, z) unlist(z[names(m$lay)], use.names = FALSE)
nz_itm   <- function(K) rep(seq_along(K), K - 1L)
nz_first <- function(K) match(seq_along(K), nz_itm(K))           # each item's first threshold
# h: thresholds -> configural (binary items: omega = 1 at the thresholds level)
nz_thr_conf <- function(K, z) {
  om <- replace(rep(1, length(K)), K > 2L, z$om)
  list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, tau2 = om[nz_itm(K)] * (z$tau - z$nu[nz_itm(K)]), lam2 = z$lam2)
}
# h: loadings -> thresholds; full = FALSE is the map as I6 first printed it (no binary nu')
nz_load_thr <- function(K, z, full = TRUE) {
  poly <- K > 2L; phi <- if (length(z$phi)) z$phi else 1; nu <- z$nu
  if (full) { b <- which(!poly); t1 <- z$tau[nz_first(K)][b]; nu[b] <- t1 - z$om[b] * (t1 - z$nu[b]) }
  list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, lam2 = z$om * z$lam * sqrt(phi), om = z$om[poly], nu = nu)
}
# h: intercepts -> loadings (phi free at loadings, or the all-binary form)
nz_int_load <- function(K, z, m1) {
  if (m1$lay[["phi"]] == 1L)
    return(list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, om = z$om, nu = z$lam * z$kap, phi = z$phi))
  t1 <- z$tau[nz_first(K)]; r <- sqrt(z$phi)
  list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, om = z$om * r, nu = t1 - (t1 - z$lam * z$kap) / r)
}
nz_point <- function(m, K) {
  p <- length(K); tau <- unlist(lapply(K - 1L, function(c) sort(rnorm(c))))
  z <- list(tau = tau, lam = runif(p, .4, .9), tau2 = tau + rnorm(length(tau), 0, .1),
            lam2 = runif(p, .3, .9), om = runif(p, .6, 1.5), nu = rnorm(p, 0, .3),
            phi = runif(1, .5, 2), kap = rnorm(1, 0, .5))
  out <- lapply(names(m$lay), function(n) z[[n]][seq_len(m$lay[[n]])]); names(out) <- names(m$lay); out
}
set.seed(20261013)
nz_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(inv_designs), function(nm) {
  K <- inv_designs[[nm]]; m <- setNames(lapply(inv_levels, function(l) inv_model(K, l)), inv_levels)
  gap <- function(m0, x0, m1, z1) max(abs(m0$sigma(x0) - m1$sigma(nz_pack(m1, z1))))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(1:20, function(r) {
    zt <- nz_point(m$thresholds, K); zl <- nz_point(m$loadings, K); zi <- nz_point(m$intercepts, K)
    data.frame(design = nm,
      thr_conf = gap(m$thresholds, nz_pack(m$thresholds, zt), m$configural, nz_thr_conf(K, zt)),
      load_thr = gap(m$loadings, nz_pack(m$loadings, zl), m$thresholds, nz_load_thr(K, zl)),
      load_thr_first = gap(m$loadings, nz_pack(m$loadings, zl), m$thresholds, nz_load_thr(K, zl, FALSE)),
      int_load = gap(m$intercepts, nz_pack(m$intercepts, zi), m$loadings, nz_int_load(K, zi, m$loadings)),
      int_conf = gap(m$intercepts, nz_pack(m$intercepts, zi), m$configural,
                     nz_thr_conf(K, nz_load_thr(K, nz_int_load(K, zi, m$loadings)))))
  }))
}))
nz_max <- aggregate(. ~ design, nz_res, max)
stopifnot(all(nz_res[, c("thr_conf", "load_thr", "int_load", "int_conf")] < 1e-12),
          all(nz_max$load_thr_first[nz_max$design != "B"] > 0.1),   # every design with a binary item
          nz_max$load_thr_first[nz_max$design == "B"] < 1e-12)      # B: all three-category, no binary item

# h-hat = dh/dtheta0 at a point with theta1 = h(theta0) (design E, loadings -> thresholds)
K <- inv_designs$E; mT <- inv_model(K, "thresholds"); mL <- inv_model(K, "loadings")
x0 <- nz_pack(mL, nz_point(mL, K)); hx <- function(x) nz_pack(mT, nz_load_thr(K, nz_split(mL, x)))
Hn <- inv_jac(hx, x0)
nz_hgap <- max(abs(MASS::ginv(inv_jac(mT$sigma, hx(x0))) %*% inv_jac(mL$sigma, x0) - Hn))
stopifnot(nz_hgap < 1e-8, qr(Hn)$rank == ncol(Hn))

# phi_g < 0 at the loadings level: all group-g correlations of a 3+-item factor are negative,
# and no real u gives rho12 rho13 rho23 < 0
zL <- nz_point(mL, K); v <- zL$om * zL$lam; Rn <- tcrossprod(v) * -0.3
stopifnot(all(Rn[lower.tri(Rn)] < 0), Rn[1, 2] * Rn[1, 3] * Rn[2, 3] < 0)
list(max_by_design = nz_max, hhat_gap = nz_hgap)
```

**Several factors** (added 2026-10-13, main session; a precondition the user set for admitting
non-adjacent generated pairs). Result I6's maps act factor by factor; with two factors the only
new element is the factor covariance, which the generator copies into each later group as that
group's own free parameter (§4.8 Q-5). Moving from the metric to the thresholds level it must
rescale with both variances, $r'_{g}=\psi_{g,12}/\sqrt{\phi_{g1}\phi_{g2}}$, again needing
$\phi_{g1},\phi_{g2}>0$. `inv-nesting-mf` writes $\sigma$ for two factors directly from the
model equations of the notation table. It is anchored to `inv_model`: with one factor it
reproduces `inv_model`'s $\sigma$ at every level. It then asserts every map and the configural
$\leftarrow$ scalar composition on two two-factor designs, each factor having a polytomous item,
and the configural and metric maps on a third whose second factor is all binary (φ fixed at
the metric level; that design's scalar level is refused in 0.3.0). The negative control leaves
the covariance unrescaled. Tolerances **chosen after measuring** on a scratch run of the same
code (discarded): $10^{-12}$ for identities and the anchor (measured at most
$4.4\times10^{-16}$), $> 0.05$ for the control (measured 0.108 and 0.110 on F2a and F2b in
scratch; 0.072 on F2c, first seen in the full document run). The scratch run first
failed its own anchor at the thresholds level (0.099): the scratch σ multiplied the
thresholds-level loading by ω, though that loading is already the standardized $u$. The anchor
caught it; the derivation was not involved.

```{r inv-nesting-mf}
mf_sig <- function(K, fac, g1, g2) {        # sigma: thresholds then lower-triangle rho, per group
  itm <- rep(seq_along(K), K - 1L); off <- function(M) M[lower.tri(M)]; p <- length(K)
  c(g1$tau, off(g1$lam * g1$R[fac, fac, drop = FALSE] * rep(g1$lam, each = p)),
    g2$om[itm] * (g2$tau - g2$nu[itm] - g2$lam[itm] * g2$kap[fac[itm]]),
    off(g2$u * g2$Psi[fac, fac, drop = FALSE] * rep(g2$u, each = p)))
}
mf_corr <- function(r) { R <- diag(2); R[1, 2] <- R[2, 1] <- r; R }
mf_cov  <- function(phi, c12) { P <- diag(phi); P[1, 2] <- P[2, 1] <- c12; P }
# group 2's structure at each level from that level's free parameters (shared: tau, lam, r1)
mf_g2 <- function(K, fac, level, z) {
  p <- length(K); poly <- K > 2L; one <- rep(1, p); zero <- rep(0, p)
  phi <- function() { f <- rep(1, 2); has <- tapply(poly, fac, any); f[has] <- z$phi[has]; f }
  switch(level,
    configural = list(tau = z$tau2, lam = z$lam2, u = z$lam2, om = one, nu = zero, Psi = mf_corr(z$r2), kap = c(0, 0)),
    thresholds = list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam2, u = z$lam2, om = replace(one, poly, z$om), nu = z$nu,
                      Psi = mf_corr(z$r2), kap = c(0, 0)),
    metric     = list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, u = z$om * z$lam, om = z$om, nu = z$nu,
                      Psi = mf_cov(phi(), z$c12), kap = c(0, 0)),
    scalar     = list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, u = z$om * z$lam, om = z$om, nu = zero,
                      Psi = mf_cov(z$phi, z$c12), kap = z$kap))
}
mf_sigma <- function(K, fac, level, z)
  mf_sig(K, fac, list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, R = mf_corr(z$r1)), mf_g2(K, fac, level, z))
mf_itm <- function(K) rep(seq_along(K), K - 1L)
mf_thr_conf <- function(K, fac, z) {
  om <- replace(rep(1, length(K)), K > 2L, z$om)
  modifyList(z, list(tau2 = om[mf_itm(K)] * (z$tau - z$nu[mf_itm(K)])))
}
mf_met_thr <- function(K, fac, z, rescale = TRUE) {
  poly <- K > 2L; f <- diag(mf_g2(K, fac, "metric", z)$Psi); nu <- z$nu
  b <- which(!poly); t1 <- z$tau[match(seq_along(K), mf_itm(K))][b]; nu[b] <- t1 - z$om[b] * (t1 - z$nu[b])
  modifyList(z, list(lam2 = z$om * z$lam * sqrt(f[fac]),
                     r2 = if (rescale) z$c12 / sqrt(f[1] * f[2]) else z$c12, om = z$om[poly], nu = nu))
}
mf_sca_met <- function(K, fac, z) modifyList(z, list(nu = z$lam * z$kap[fac]))  # each factor has a polytomous item
mf_point <- function(K) {
  p <- length(K); tau <- unlist(lapply(K - 1L, function(c) sort(rnorm(c))))
  list(tau = tau, lam = runif(p, .4, .9), r1 = runif(1, -.5, .5), tau2 = tau + rnorm(length(tau), 0, .1),
       lam2 = runif(p, .3, .9), r2 = runif(1, -.5, .5), om = runif(p, .6, 1.5), nu = rnorm(p, 0, .3),
       phi = runif(2, .5, 2), c12 = runif(1, -.4, .4), kap = rnorm(2, 0, .5))
}
mf_thr_pt <- function(K, z) { z$om <- z$om[K > 2L]; z }    # thresholds level: omega for polytomous items only
set.seed(20261014)

# anchor: one factor (design E), mf_sigma against inv_model at every level
mf_anchor <- sapply(inv_levels, function(l) {
  K <- inv_designs$E; m <- inv_model(K, l); z <- mf_point(K); z$phi <- c(z$phi[1], 1)
  zl <- switch(l, configural = list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, tau2 = z$tau2, lam2 = z$lam2),
    thresholds = list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, lam2 = z$lam2, om = z$om[K > 2L], nu = z$nu),
    loadings   = list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, om = z$om, nu = z$nu, phi = z$phi[1]),
    intercepts = list(tau = z$tau, lam = z$lam, om = z$om, phi = z$phi[1], kap = z$kap[1]))
  lv <- c(configural = "configural", thresholds = "thresholds", loadings = "metric", intercepts = "scalar")[[l]]
  max(abs(m$sigma(unlist(zl[names(m$lay)], use.names = FALSE)) -
          mf_sigma(K, rep(1L, 5), lv, if (l == "thresholds") mf_thr_pt(K, z) else z)))
})
stopifnot(all(mf_anchor < 1e-12))

mf_designs <- list(F2a = list(K = c(4L, 4L, 2L, 3L, 2L, 2L), fac = rep(1:2, each = 3)),
                   F2b = list(K = c(3L, 2L, 2L, 4L, 3L, 2L), fac = rep(1:2, each = 3)),
                   F2c = list(K = c(4L, 3L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), fac = rep(1:2, each = 3)))  # factor 2 all binary
mf_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(mf_designs), function(nm) {
  K <- mf_designs[[nm]]$K; fac <- mf_designs[[nm]]$fac; scal <- nm != "F2c"
  do.call(rbind, lapply(1:20, function(r) {
    z <- mf_point(K); zt <- mf_thr_pt(K, z)
    g <- function(l0, z0, l1, z1) max(abs(mf_sigma(K, fac, l0, z0) - mf_sigma(K, fac, l1, z1)))
    data.frame(design = nm,
      thr_conf = g("thresholds", zt, "configural", mf_thr_conf(K, fac, zt)),
      met_thr  = g("metric", z, "thresholds", mf_met_thr(K, fac, z)),
      sca_met  = if (scal) g("scalar", z, "metric", mf_sca_met(K, fac, z)) else NA_real_,
      sca_conf = if (scal) g("scalar", z, "configural",
                             mf_thr_conf(K, fac, mf_met_thr(K, fac, mf_sca_met(K, fac, z)))) else NA_real_,
      met_thr_norescale = g("metric", z, "thresholds", mf_met_thr(K, fac, z, rescale = FALSE)))
  }))
}))
mf_max <- aggregate(cbind(thr_conf, met_thr, sca_met, sca_conf, met_thr_norescale) ~ design, mf_res,
                    max, na.action = na.pass)
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(mf_max[, c("thr_conf", "met_thr")]) < 1e-12),
          all(as.matrix(mf_max[mf_max$design != "F2c", c("sca_met", "sca_conf")]) < 1e-12),
          all(mf_max$met_thr_norescale > 0.05))
list(anchor = mf_anchor, max_by_design = mf_max)
```

#### Check 11 for $G$ groups {#sec-inv-check11}

*Added 2026-10-08. Drafted in a Cloud session from `ddcd1d9`; every chunk below was run by the
main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2), green on the first run with no corrections. Three
mutants (ω never scaling the loading, ω always scaling it, `<` for `<=` in rule (b)) each
turned it red.*

Spec Module 12 check 11 refuses an $H_0$ whose **fixed values force** the boundary of the
parameter space: (a) a maximal all-fixed block of $\Psi$ that is not positive definite, or (b) a
$\Theta_{jj}$ that is a function of fixed values only and is $\le 0$; exact, structural, on
$H_0$'s table, an absent row counting as fixed at 0. `dwlsmv_dtboundary()` implements it for
$G=1$ (ptypes 1–3). This section extends the rule to $G$ groups under the delta
parameterization of this section, and asks whether anything the generated levels fix can trip
it. The pooled multiple-group scaling is not touched: check 11 reads parameter tables only.

**Setting.** Group $g$ has loadings $\Lambda_g$, structural paths $B_g$ and disturbance
covariance $\Psi_g$, with $\Phi_g=(I-B_g)^{-1}\Psi_g(I-B_g)^{-\top}$, scales $\omega_{gj}$,
intercepts $\nu_{gj}$, factor intercepts $\alpha_g$ and thresholds $\tau$. Group 1 has
$\omega_{1j}=1$, $\nu_{1j}=0$, $\phi_1=1$, $\kappa_1=0$, all fixed. In dwlsmv's table (spec
§4.8, **Multiple groups**) ν, ω, α are ptypes 5, 6, 7, a later group's factor variance is a ψ
row, and a tie is a shared θ index whose operands §4.8 G2 requires to be free, so **a tied
element is free**. Generated chains use the unit-variance metric and refuse $B\ne0$ (§4.8 G5),
so $\Phi_g=\Psi_g$ there; the formulas keep $B$ because check 11 also judges tables that are not
generated.

##### Result C11-1 (what enters $\Theta_{gjj}$)

The implied statistics of group $g$ are $s_{gjc}=\omega_{gj}(\tau_{jc}-\nu_{gj}-\lambda_{gj}\kappa_g)$
and $\rho_{g,ij}=u_{gi}u_{gj}$, with $\Theta^*_{g,jj}=1-u_{gj}^2$. For a general table,
$$ \Theta_{g,jj}=1-m_{gj}^{2}\,\big(\Lambda_g\Phi_g\Lambda_g'\big)_{jj}, $$
where $m_{gj}=\omega_{gj}$ when ω multiplies the loading and $m_{gj}=1$ otherwise. In
`inv_model` this is a property of the level: at the loadings and intercepts levels the loading
is the tied, unscaled $\lambda_j$ and $u_{gj}=\omega_{gj}\lambda_j\sqrt{\phi_g}$, so
$m_{gj}=\omega_{gj}$; at the configural and thresholds levels $u_{gj}$ is the free loading
itself, $m_{gj}=1$, and ω scales thresholds only. Whether dwlsmv's own table carries ω as a
multiplier at every level was Q-2, below (decided 2026-10-09: it does, spec §4.8 G4).

So $\Theta_{g,jj}$ depends on row $j$ of $\Lambda_g$, on $\Psi_g$ among the factors row $j$
reaches, on $B_g$ into those factors and their ancestors, and on $\omega_{gj}$ only where it
multiplies. It **cannot** depend on $\nu_g$, $\alpha_g/\kappa_g$ or τ: they enter the threshold
block, not $R_g$. Chunk `c11-theta` checks both halves on every design and level: $\Theta_{gjj}$
from the parameterization equals the value read off `inv_model`'s implied correlations, and
perturbing τ, ν, κ leaves the correlation entries unchanged while λ, φ and (at loadings and
intercepts) ω change them.

##### Result C11-2 (when $\Theta_{gjj}$ is determined by fixed values alone)

As in the $G=1$ rule, $\Theta_{g,jj}$ is determined by fixed values iff, in group $g$'s own
table, (1) every loading in row $j$ is fixed (absent = fixed at 0); (2) every β into
$\mathrm{Anc}_j$ and every ψ within $\mathrm{Anc}_j$ is fixed, $\mathrm{Anc}_j$ being the factors
with a nonzero loading in row $j$ and their ancestors through nonzero or free β; (3) $m_{gj}$
is fixed. Consequences:

- **A tied element is free, so never "fixed"**: a tied loading in row $j$ leaves
  $\Theta_{gjj}$ undetermined. §4.8 G2 refuses a tie on a fixed element (rc 3498), so no other
  case arises.
- **Group 1's reference values are ordinary fixed values**: group 1 is the single-group case
  verbatim.
- **A free multiplying ω is a free parameter inside the product**: $\Theta_{gjj}=1-\omega_{gj}^2v$
  is $\le 0$ only on an interior set, a boundary forced *through* a free parameter, which the
  rule does not refuse. If $v=0$ the row is $\Theta=1$ and skipped, as at $G=1$.

##### Result C11-3 (rule (a), per group)

Rule (a) for $G$ groups is rule (a) on each $\Psi_g$. The maximal-block argument of
`dwlsmv_dtboundary()` carries over unchanged: a PD matrix has only PD principal submatrices,
every all-fixed block lies in a maximal one, and the parameter space is the product over
groups, so refuse if any group fails. What changes with the group is which factors have a fixed
diagonal:

| Level | $\phi_g$ (group $g\ge2$) | factors with fixed diagonal, group $g$ |
|---|---|---|
| configural | fixed 1 | all |
| thresholds | fixed 1 | all |
| loadings | free iff the factor has a polytomous item | those with none |
| intercepts | free for every factor | none |

Group 1 has them all fixed, so a later group's vertex set is a subset of group 1's at every
level; a block with a free diagonal is not all-fixed, whatever its fixed covariance.

##### Result C11-4 (generated levels add no refusal of their own)

Let $C$ be a configural table and let the generator emit each level per §4.8 G8. Assume
**(G1)** the generator copies $C$'s user-written loading, ψ and β rows, free or fixed with the
same values, into every group. (G2), that a tie is a shared free index, is §4.8 G2. Then:

- **(a)** group $g$'s fixed-pair graph is an induced subgraph of group 1's, so rule (a) fires on
  group $g$ only if it fires on group 1;
- **(b)** a row with a free or tied loading is never determined; a user-fixed row is fixed in
  every group by (G1). At configural and thresholds ($m=1$, $\phi_g=1$ fixed) $\Theta_{gjj}$ is
  the same number as $\Theta_{1jj}$; at loadings and intercepts the free multiplying ω leaves it
  undetermined. Rule (b) fires on group $g\ge2$ only if it fires on group 1;
- the values the generator introduces (ω = 1, ν = 0, κ = 0, $\phi_g=1$) never create a
  refusal.

So a refusal of a generated $H_0$ always comes from $C$'s own fixed values, and group 1
refuses first. Chunk `c11-generated` verifies this on designs A–E at all four levels, including
a user loading fixed at 1, refused at every level by group 1 and additionally by group 2 exactly
where ω does not multiply (the `inv_model` reading of Q-2; the headline holds under either).

Hence, for a generated chain, the configural preflight (spec Module 12, check 11; user,
2026-10-08) removes every refusal C11-4 can produce: under (G1) and either reading of Q-2,
check 11 on a generated level fires only if the generator itself introduces a forcing value.
The per-level check stays as a backstop because (G1) and Q-2 are not settled. A user-written
pair gets check 11 unchanged, group by group.

**ω's own domain.** A *fixed* ω ≤ 0 never reaches check 11: §4.8 G7 refuses it at rc 3498. A
free ω leaving $(0,\infty)$ is §4.8's open O12; check 11 does not cover it.

**Open here.** Q-2: does dwlsmv's table make ω multiply the loading at every level, or only at
loadings and intercepts? (Decided 2026-10-09: at every level. Under it, a user-fixed loading
at the thresholds level is refused by group 1 only, not also by group 2.) Q-5 = (G1): what the generator copies into later groups, namely
user-fixed loadings (which cannot be tied) and later-group factor covariances, which §4.8 G8
does not list. (Decided 2026-10-09: (G1) as stated, every λ and ψ row copied with its status,
value and start; spec §4.8 G8.) §4.8 O1 (decided 2026-10-09: no row at the reference value): an absent ω row is read as 1 here. $G>2$: `inv_model` is $G=2$; the
argument is group-local and does not use $G$. The 1e-12 tolerances below are for exact algebra
and were chosen before measuring.

```{r c11-defs}
# Reference implementation of check 11, rules (a) and (b), for G groups.
# It mirrors dwlsmv_dtboundary() (LDL' with a strict pivot > 0; maximal all-fixed blocks;
# structural "determined by fixed values alone"), and adds omega as a multiplier of lambda.
# A group is a list: Lam/Lfree (p x F), Psi/Pfree (F x F, symmetric), B/Bfree (F x F),
# om/omfree (p), omscales (does omega multiply lambda in R_g?). A free entry's value is never read.

c11_pd <- function(M) {                      # LDL' with a strict pivot test, as dwlsmv_dtb_pd
  n <- nrow(M); L <- diag(n); dv <- numeric(n)
  for (k in seq_len(n)) {
    d <- M[k, k]
    for (t in seq_len(k - 1L)) d <- d - L[k, t] * L[k, t] * dv[t]
    if (is.na(d) || d <= 0) return(FALSE)
    dv[k] <- d
    for (i in seq_len(n)[seq_len(n) > k]) {
      L[i, k] <- M[i, k]
      for (t in seq_len(k - 1L)) L[i, k] <- L[i, k] - L[i, t] * L[k, t] * dv[t]
      L[i, k] <- L[i, k] / d
    }
  }
  TRUE
}

c11_blocks <- function(Pfree) {              # maximal all-fixed index sets of Psi
  fixd <- which(!diag(Pfree))                # factors whose variance is fixed
  if (!length(fixd)) return(list())
  cl <- list()
  for (mask in seq_len(2L^length(fixd) - 1L)) {
    S <- fixd[bitwAnd(mask, as.integer(2L^(seq_along(fixd) - 1L))) > 0L]
    ok <- TRUE
    if (length(S) > 1L) for (a in S) for (b in S) if (a != b && Pfree[a, b]) ok <- FALSE
    if (ok) cl[[length(cl) + 1L]] <- S
  }
  Filter(function(S) !any(vapply(cl, function(T) length(T) > length(S) && all(S %in% T), TRUE)), cl)
}

c11_rule_a <- function(g)
  Filter(function(S) !c11_pd(g$Psi[S, S, drop = FALSE]), c11_blocks(g$Pfree))

c11_rule_b <- function(g) {
  p <- nrow(g$Lam); nf <- ncol(g$Lam)
  Lam <- g$Lam; Psi <- g$Psi; B <- g$B
  Lam[g$Lfree] <- 0; Psi[g$Pfree] <- 0; B[g$Bfree] <- 0          # free entries are zeroed, as the Mata does
  E <- g$Bfree | (B != 0)                                          # E[to, from]: a free or nonzero path
  for (k in seq_len(nf)) for (i in seq_len(nf)) for (j in seq_len(nf))
    if (E[i, k] && E[k, j]) E[i, j] <- TRUE
  A <- diag(nf); Bk <- diag(nf)                                    # (I - B)^-1 as a finite series (B nilpotent)
  for (k in seq_len(nf - 1L)) { Bk <- Bk %*% B; A <- A + Bk }
  out <- list()
  for (j in seq_len(p)) {
    if (any(g$Lfree[j, ])) next                                    # a free loading in the row
    nz <- Lam[j, ] != 0
    if (!any(nz)) next                                             # Theta_jj = 1
    anc <- nz | (as.vector((nz + 0) %*% (E + 0)) > 0)
    det <- TRUE
    for (r in which(anc)) {
      if (any(g$Bfree[r, ])) det <- FALSE                          # a free beta into Anc
      for (cc in which(anc)) if (g$Pfree[r, cc]) det <- FALSE      # a free psi inside Anc
    }
    scl <- 1
    if (isTRUE(g$omscales)) { if (g$omfree[j]) det <- FALSE else scl <- g$om[j] }
    if (!det) next
    a  <- matrix(Lam[j, ], 1) %*% A
    th <- 1 - scl^2 * drop(a %*% Psi %*% t(a))
    if (th <= 0) out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- list(item = j, theta = th)
  }
  out
}

c11_check <- function(tab) {                 # tab = list of groups; "refused" iff any group fires
  res <- list()
  for (g in seq_along(tab)) {
    ba <- c11_rule_a(tab[[g]]); bb <- c11_rule_b(tab[[g]])
    if (length(ba)) res[[length(res) + 1L]] <- list(group = g, rule = "a", detail = ba)
    if (length(bb)) res[[length(res) + 1L]] <- list(group = g, rule = "b", detail = bb)
  }
  list(refused = length(res) > 0L, hits = res,
       groups = vapply(res, function(h) h$group, 1L), rules = vapply(res, function(h) h$rule, ""))
}

c11_group <- function(Lam, Lfree, Psi, Pfree,
                      B = matrix(0, ncol(Lam), ncol(Lam)), Bfree = matrix(FALSE, ncol(Lam), ncol(Lam)),
                      om = rep(1, nrow(Lam)), omfree = rep(FALSE, nrow(Lam)), omscales = FALSE) {
  Psi[upper.tri(Psi)]     <- t(Psi)[upper.tri(Psi)]               # symmetric: the lower triangle rules
  Pfree[upper.tri(Pfree)] <- t(Pfree)[upper.tri(Pfree)]
  list(Lam = Lam, Lfree = Lfree, Psi = Psi, Pfree = Pfree, B = B, Bfree = Bfree,
       om = om, omfree = omfree, omscales = omscales)
}

# Two factors, three items each (loading .7 free), unit variances fixed unless v1free / v2free;
# covariance cov, fixed unless covfree; item 1's loading fixed at lam1 if given; item 1's omega
# free if omfree1, multiplying the loading if omscales.
c11_std <- function(cov, covfree, v1free = FALSE, v2free = FALSE, lam1 = NA_real_,
                    omfree1 = FALSE, omscales = FALSE) {
  Lam <- matrix(0, 6, 2); Lam[1:3, 1] <- .7; Lam[4:6, 2] <- .7
  Lfree <- Lam != 0                                                # absent entries are fixed at 0
  if (!is.na(lam1)) { Lam[1, 1] <- lam1; Lfree[1, 1] <- FALSE }
  omfree <- rep(FALSE, 6); omfree[1] <- omfree1
  c11_group(Lam, Lfree, Psi = matrix(c(1, cov, cov, 1), 2),
            Pfree = matrix(c(v1free, covfree, covfree, v2free), 2),
            omfree = omfree, omscales = omscales)
}
```

```{r c11-oracle}
# The R reference reproduces the verdicts of the executed Mata test
# (tests/unit/test_dtboundary.do: g3, g4, g5, g8 accepted; r1, r4, r5, r6, r8, r11 refused),
# so the G-group extension below is built on a reference known to agree at G = 1.
local({
  one <- function(g) c11_check(list(g))
  two_fac <- function(lam4, Bto, Bfree21 = FALSE, psi21 = NA_real_) {        # test_dtboundary's case E shapes
    Lam <- matrix(0, 6, 2); Lam[1:3, 1] <- .7; Lam[4:6, 2] <- .7
    Lfree <- Lam != 0; Lam[4, 2] <- lam4; Lfree[4, 2] <- FALSE
    B <- matrix(0, 2, 2); B[2, 1] <- Bto; Bfree <- matrix(FALSE, 2, 2); Bfree[2, 1] <- Bfree21
    Psi <- diag(2); if (!is.na(psi21)) Psi[2, 1] <- Psi[1, 2] <- psi21
    c11_group(Lam, Lfree, Psi, Pfree = matrix(FALSE, 2, 2), B = B, Bfree = Bfree)
  }
  r8 <- one(two_fac(.9, .5)); g4 <- one(two_fac(.9, .3)); g5 <- one(two_fac(1.05, 0, TRUE, -.5))
  stopifnot(r8$refused, identical(r8$rules, "b"), abs(r8$hits[[1]]$detail[[1]]$theta - (-0.0125)) < 1e-12,
            !g4$refused, !g5$refused)
  # the matrix formula for Theta, with an endogenous factor: Phi22 = beta^2 + psi22 (spec 4.8)
  c11_theta <- function(Lam, Psi, B = matrix(0, ncol(Lam), ncol(Lam)), m = rep(1, nrow(Lam))) {
    A <- solve(diag(ncol(Lam)) - B); Phi <- A %*% Psi %*% t(A)
    1 - m^2 * diag(Lam %*% Phi %*% t(Lam))
  }
  Lam <- matrix(0, 6, 2); Lam[1:3, 1] <- .7; Lam[4, 2] <- .9; Lam[5:6, 2] <- .7
  B <- matrix(0, 2, 2); B[2, 1] <- .5
  stopifnot(abs(c11_theta(Lam, diag(2), B)[4] - (1 - .81 * 1.25)) < 1e-14,
            abs(c11_theta(Lam, diag(2), matrix(0, 2, 2))[4] - (1 - .81)) < 1e-14)
  stopifnot(!one(c11_std(.999, FALSE, lam1 = .999))$refused,                  # g3: legal near the boundary
            one(c11_std(1, FALSE))$refused, one(c11_std(1.2, FALSE))$refused, # r1, r11
            one(c11_std(1, FALSE))$rules == "a")
  Lam4 <- matrix(0, 4, 2); Lam4[1:3, 1] <- .7; Lam4[4, 2] <- 1                 # r4: marker F2 on y4,
  Lfree4 <- Lam4 != 0; Lfree4[4, 2] <- FALSE                                     #     psi22 fixed 0, cov .3
  r4 <- c11_group(Lam4, Lfree4, Psi = matrix(c(1, .3, .3, 0), 2), Pfree = matrix(FALSE, 2, 2))
  stopifnot(one(r4)$refused)
  P3 <- function(c21, c31, c32) {                                              # three factors, all psi fixed
    Lam <- matrix(0, 9, 3); for (f in 1:3) Lam[(3 * f - 2):(3 * f), f] <- .7
    c11_group(Lam, Lam != 0, Psi = matrix(c(1, c21, c31, c21, 1, c32, c31, c32, 1), 3),
              Pfree = matrix(FALSE, 3, 3))
  }
  stopifnot(!one(P3(.5, .5, .4))$refused,                                      # g8
            one(P3(.5, .5, -.5))$refused)                                      # r5: singular PSD, no singular 2 x 2 block
  one1 <- c11_group(matrix(c(1, .7, .7), 3), matrix(c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE), 3), Psi = matrix(1, 1, 1),
                    Pfree = matrix(FALSE, 1, 1))
  stopifnot(one(one1)$refused, one(one1)$rules == "b")                         # r6: unit variance, loading 1
})
```

```{r c11-theta}
# Result C11-1, numerically. Reuses inv_designs, inv_levels, inv_model,
# inv_point, inv_tau, inv_lam, inv_spec from inv-setup (G = 2 only: that is inv_model's scope;
# the argument itself is group-local and does not depend on G).
c11_unpack <- function(m, x) split(x, rep(names(m$lay), m$lay))     # as inv_model's sigma does

c11_theta <- function(Lam, Psi, B = matrix(0, ncol(Lam), ncol(Lam)), m = rep(1, nrow(Lam))) {
  A <- solve(diag(ncol(Lam)) - B); Phi <- A %*% Psi %*% t(A)        # Phi = (I-B)^-1 Psi (I-B)^-T
  1 - m^2 * diag(Lam %*% Phi %*% t(Lam))                            # Theta_jj = 1 - m_j^2 (Lam Phi Lam')_jj
}

# Theta_gjj from the PARAMETERIZATION, per the level table (one factor, so Lam is a column).
c11_param <- function(K, level, x) {
  m <- inv_model(K, level); sp <- inv_spec(K, level); p <- length(K); z <- c11_unpack(m, x)
  phi2 <- if (is.null(z$phi)) 1 else z$phi
  om <- rep(1, p)
  if (!is.null(z$om)) { if (level == "thresholds") om[K > 2L] <- z$om else om <- z$om }
  scales <- sp$tied_lam                                              # omega multiplies lambda: loadings, intercepts
  list(g1 = c11_theta(matrix(z$lam, ncol = 1), matrix(1, 1, 1)),
       g2 = c11_theta(matrix(if (scales) z$lam else z$lam2, ncol = 1), matrix(phi2, 1, 1),
                      m = if (scales) om else rep(1, p)))
}

# Theta_gjj read off the IMPLIED CORRELATION MATRIX of inv_model's sigma (one-factor triads).
c11_theta_from_R <- function(K, level, x) {
  m <- inv_model(K, level); p <- length(K); nT <- sum(K - 1L); P <- p * (p - 1) / 2
  s <- m$sigma(x); stopifnot(length(s) == 2 * (nT + P))
  tri <- function(r) { R <- matrix(0, p, p); R[lower.tri(R)] <- r; R + t(R) }
  u2  <- function(R) vapply(seq_len(p), function(j) {
    o <- setdiff(seq_len(p), j)[1:2]; R[j, o[1]] * R[j, o[2]] / R[o[1], o[2]] }, 0)   # R_jk R_jl / R_kl = u_j^2
  list(g1 = 1 - u2(tri(s[nT + seq_len(P)])), g2 = 1 - u2(tri(s[2 * nT + P + seq_len(P)])))
}

# Which parameter blocks change the correlation entries of sigma when perturbed?
c11_enter <- function(K, level) {
  m <- inv_model(K, level); x <- inv_point(m, inv_tau(K), inv_lam); p <- length(K)
  nT <- sum(K - 1L); P <- p * (p - 1) / 2
  cid  <- c(nT + seq_len(P), 2 * nT + P + seq_len(P))
  base <- m$sigma(x)[cid]; blk <- rep(names(m$lay), m$lay)
  vapply(unique(blk), function(b) {
    x2 <- x; i <- which(blk == b); x2[i] <- x2[i] * 1.1 + 0.01
    max(abs(m$sigma(x2)[cid] - base)) > 1e-8 }, TRUE)
}

local({
  for (nm in names(inv_designs)) for (l in inv_levels) {
    K <- inv_designs[[nm]]; m <- inv_model(K, l); x <- inv_point(m, inv_tau(K), inv_lam)
    a <- c11_param(K, l, x); b <- c11_theta_from_R(K, l, x)
```
