```{r c11-theta}
    stopifnot(max(abs(a$g1 - b$g1)) < 1e-12, max(abs(a$g2 - b$g2)) < 1e-12)     # (i): the parameterization = the implied R
    ent <- c11_enter(K, l)
    for (nme in intersect(c("tau", "tau2", "nu", "kap"), names(ent))) stopifnot(!ent[[nme]])  # tau, nu, kappa never enter
    stopifnot(ent[["lam"]])
    for (nme in intersect(c("lam2", "phi"), names(ent))) stopifnot(ent[[nme]])
    if ("om" %in% names(ent)) stopifnot(identical(unname(ent[["om"]]), l %in% c("loadings", "intercepts")))
  }
  # omega enters Theta at loadings/intercepts and NOT at thresholds (design B: all items polytomous)
  KB <- inv_designs$B
  stopifnot(c11_enter(KB, "loadings")[["om"]], !c11_enter(KB, "thresholds")[["om"]])
})
```

```{r c11-tables}
# One refused and one accepted two-group table for each of (a) and (b),
# plus attribution to the right group (and G = 3, a refusal in group 1 only, in group 3 only).
local({
  g_free <- c11_std(cov = .3, covfree = TRUE)                    # unit variances fixed, covariance free
  chk <- function(tab) c11_check(tab)

  # (a) refused: group 2 fixes the correlation of two unit-variance factors at 1
  ra <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(cov = 1, covfree = FALSE)))
  stopifnot(ra$refused, identical(ra$groups, 2L), identical(ra$rules, "a"))
  # (a) accepted: the same group with the correlation fixed at .9 (positive definite)
  aa <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(cov = .9, covfree = FALSE)))
  stopifnot(!aa$refused)
  # (a) accepted for a level-table reason: covariance 1.2 beside a FREE variance is not an all-fixed block
  aa2 <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(cov = 1.2, covfree = FALSE, v2free = TRUE)))
  stopifnot(!aa2$refused)

  # (b) refused: group 2's item 1 has its only loading fixed at 1 under a fixed unit variance (Theta = 0)
  rb <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(cov = .3, covfree = TRUE, lam1 = 1)))
  stopifnot(rb$refused, identical(rb$groups, 2L), identical(rb$rules, "b"),
            rb$hits[[1]]$detail[[1]]$item == 1L, abs(rb$hits[[1]]$detail[[1]]$theta) < 1e-14)
  # (b) accepted: omega free and multiplying (loadings level): the scale is not determined
  ab <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(cov = .3, covfree = TRUE, lam1 = 1, omfree1 = TRUE, omscales = TRUE)))
  stopifnot(!ab$refused)
  # (b) accepted: a legal fixed loading
  ab2 <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(cov = .3, covfree = TRUE, lam1 = .8)))
  stopifnot(!ab2$refused)
  # (b) refused: omega FIXED at 1 does not rescue it, even where it multiplies
  rb2 <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(cov = .3, covfree = TRUE, lam1 = 1, omfree1 = FALSE, omscales = TRUE)))
  stopifnot(rb2$refused, identical(rb2$groups, 2L))

  # attribution: group 1 only, group 3 only (G = 3)
  stopifnot(identical(chk(list(c11_std(1, FALSE), g_free, g_free))$groups, 1L),
            identical(chk(list(g_free, g_free, c11_std(1, FALSE)))$groups, 3L))
  # refusals add up over groups
  both <- chk(list(g_free, c11_std(1, FALSE), c11_std(cov = .3, covfree = TRUE, lam1 = 1)))
  stopifnot(identical(both$groups, c(2L, 3L)), identical(both$rules, c("a", "b")))
})
```

```{r c11-generated}
# Result C11-4: tables generated from the level table cannot trip check 11
# beyond what the configural table already does. Group 1: reference values fixed
# (phi = 1, omega = 1); group 2: the level table's statuses for phi and omega
# (inv_spec(K, level)$phi, $om), a tied loading being free (G2).
c11_from_level <- function(K, level, lam1 = NA_real_) {
  sp <- inv_spec(K, level); p <- length(K)
  Lam <- matrix(.7, p, 1); Lfree <- matrix(TRUE, p, 1)
  if (!is.na(lam1)) { Lam[1, 1] <- lam1; Lfree[1, 1] <- FALSE }     # (G1): a user-fixed loading is copied to every group
  list(c11_group(Lam, Lfree, Psi = matrix(1, 1, 1), Pfree = matrix(FALSE, 1, 1)),
       c11_group(Lam, Lfree, Psi = matrix(1, 1, 1), Pfree = matrix(isTRUE(sp$phi), 1, 1),
                 om = rep(1, p), omfree = sp$om == "free", omscales = sp$tied_lam))
}

local({
  for (nm in names(inv_designs)) for (l in inv_levels) {
    K <- inv_designs[[nm]]
    # defaults (every loading free) and a legal fixed loading: never refused
    stopifnot(!c11_check(c11_from_level(K, l))$refused,
              !c11_check(c11_from_level(K, l, lam1 = .8))$refused)
    # a loading fixed at 1: the configural table is itself refused (group 1) and every level inherits it
    r1 <- c11_check(c11_from_level(K, l, lam1 = 1))
    stopifnot(r1$refused, 1L %in% r1$groups)
    # group 2 adds its own refusal exactly where omega does not multiply the loading
    stopifnot(identical(2L %in% r1$groups, l %in% c("configural", "thresholds")))
  }

  # (a), per group: group g's refusal implies group 1's, and a free diagonal can only remove it
  for (cv in c(0, .3, .999, 1, -1, 1.2)) for (v1 in c(FALSE, TRUE)) for (v2 in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
    g1 <- c11_std(cov = cv, covfree = FALSE)                       # group 1: both variances fixed at 1
    g2 <- c11_std(cov = cv, covfree = FALSE, v1free = v1, v2free = v2)
    fires2 <- length(c11_rule_a(g2)) > 0L; fires1 <- length(c11_rule_a(g1)) > 0L
    stopifnot(!fires2 || fires1)                                    # inherited
    stopifnot(identical(fires2, fires1 && !v1 && !v2))              # lost as soon as a variance is free
    stopifnot(identical(fires1, cv %in% c(1, -1, 1.2)))             # near-boundary .999 and 0, .3 are fine
  }
})
```


#### What this section does not establish

- Multi-factor models, cross-loadings, endogenous factors ($\alpha_g$ versus $\kappa_g$,
  $\psi_g$ versus total variance), $G>2$ and marker-metric models are not covered. (0.3.0
  refuses structural paths with invariance and uses the unit-variance metric only.) See
  `@sec-inv-check11` for what check 11 needs of them. Endogenous factors with simple structure,
  recursive B and G = 2 are now covered by @sec-mg-beta (Results B1–B9; B9 for check 11).
- *Resolved by the main session:* `@sec-difftest` holds for a smooth $h$. Its Steps use only
  $\Delta_0 = \Delta_1H$ at the truth with $H = \partial h/\partial\theta_0$, and the sample
  construction uses $\hat h = \Delta_1^{+}\Delta_0$, never a selection matrix, so W&E chains need
  no change to the statistic.
- The scaling of the pooled multi-group $F$, $\Gamma$ and $T$ is not derived here; it is
  `@sec-multigroup-scaling`'s, and was decided there on 2026-10-09 ($T=(N-G)F$,
  `e(V)` $=\mathrm{ACOV}/(N-G)$, check 10's $\varepsilon=(N-G)\,\mathrm{nrtol}$). (Corrected
  2026-10-09: this bullet said the scaling was open.)


### Singular-case guards {#sec-singular-guards}

*Drafted by a read-only agent (task G) from `e439022`; executed by the main session 2026-10-09 from this
file (purled, in document order after `setup`, `inv-setup`, `inv-algebra`, `inv-start`; R 4.6.0,
lavaan 0.7.2): every chunk green on the first run, no correction. The `grd-regime` bounds 8 and 4 were
chosen after the drafting agent's scratch run measured them, and are labelled so in the chunk; the
chunks' "set before measuring" labels are the drafting agent's own statement.*

**Scope.** The intercepts level of `@sec-invariance-id`, an all-binary factor, two groups, delta
parameterization, group 1 the reference. This is the derivation behind the pre-fit warning frozen in
E-037 (warn iff $S_{1w,1}\le$ cut). It sets no cutoff; the post-fit guard's
role is left open.

Throughout, $r_j=\tau_j/\lambda_j$ is group 1's ratio: the item's normal-ogive *difficulty*, the factor
value (in group-1 factor-SD units) at which $E(y^*_j\mid\eta)=\tau_j$. Result I5's singular set is "every
item equally difficult". The preregistered path is $r=c+\delta d$, $d$ = `grd_zpat(p)` (mean 0,
population SD 1), $\lambda$ = `grd_lam(p)`, $\kappa_2=0.3$, $\phi_2=1.44$.

#### Result G1 (the geometry of $S_{1w}$)

For $\lambda\ne0$,
$$S_{1w}(\tau,\lambda)=\min_c\frac{\|\tau-c\lambda\|}{\|\lambda\|}=\frac{\|P_\lambda^\perp\tau\|}{\|\lambda\|}
=\Big(\tfrac{\sum_j\lambda_j^2(r_j-\bar r_w)^2}{\sum_j\lambda_j^2}\Big)^{1/2},\qquad
\bar r_w=\tfrac{\sum\lambda_j^2r_j}{\sum\lambda_j^2}.$$
(i) $S_{1w}=0$ iff $\operatorname{rank}[\lambda,\tau]=1$, I5's set. (ii) $\sigma_1\sigma_2([\lambda,\tau])=\|\lambda\|^2S_{1w}$.
(iii) $S_{1w}$ is unchanged by reverse-coding any item ($(\tau_j,\lambda_j)\to-(\tau_j,\lambda_j)$), by the
factor sign ($\lambda\to-\lambda$) and by $r\to r+b$; it scales as $|a|$ under $r\to ar$, so it is in the
units of $r$, group-1 factor SD. (iv) Along $r=c+\delta d$, $S_{1w}=\delta\,S_{1w}(d\circ\lambda,\lambda)$ exactly,
for every $c$.

*Proof.* The minimum over $c$ is a least-squares projection whose residual is $\lambda\circ(r-\bar r_w)$,
which gives the weighted-variance form and (iv). (ii) is $\sigma_1\sigma_2=|\det|^{1/2}$ of the Gram matrix of
two columns, $\|\lambda\|^2\|P^\perp_\lambda\tau\|^2$. (iii): $r_j$ and $\lambda_j^2$ are invariant under the
first two maps, and the weighted variance is location-free. $\square$

**Why not S1, S2, S3, S4** (recorded, not used, by the preregistration):
$S_1=\operatorname{sd}(r)$ divides by each $\hat\lambda_j$ separately, so one small loading can make it large
while $S_{1w}$ stays small (chunk). $S_3$, the equilibrated ratio of $[1,r]$, is 1 whenever $\sum r_j=0$,
whatever the spread, which is every $c=0$ cell, and $0/0$ at $r=0$. $S_4=\sigma_2/\sigma_1$ is linear in
$\delta$ only to first order ($\sigma_1$ moves with $\delta$, by (ii)). $S_2$, the Wald $Q$ for equal $r$, is a
signal-to-noise statistic: at fixed $\delta$ it grows as $N_1\delta^2$ ($N_1$ group 1's size), so a constant
$S_2$ cutoff is a $\delta$-threshold shrinking as $N_1^{-1/2}$, while Result G2's first-order harm boundary
does not move with $N$.

#### Result G2 (first-order harm is free of N; its conditions)

*Setting.* The pooled DWLS estimator of `@sec-multigroup-scaling` (weighting (a)):
$W=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\pi_gW_g)$, $\Omega=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\Gamma_g/\pi_g)$, $H=\Delta'W\Delta$,
$$\operatorname{ACOV}(\hat\theta)=\tfrac1N A(\vartheta,\pi),\qquad A=H^{-1}\Delta'W\Omega W\Delta H^{-1},$$
with $\vartheta$ the population ($c,\delta,d,\lambda$ and group 2's parameters). Let
$R(\delta)=\mathrm{SE}(\hat\kappa_2;\delta)/\mathrm{SE}(\hat\kappa_2;\delta_{ok})$ at the same $(c,N,p)$, the
preregistration's harm ratio.

**Result.** $R(\delta)=\big(A_{\kappa\kappa}(\delta)/A_{\kappa\kappa}(\delta_{ok})\big)^{1/2}$ is free of $N$. It depends on
$\pi$, on $c-\kappa_2$, $d$, $\lambda$ and group 2's parameters. ($A_{\kappa\kappa}^{-1}$ is the sandwich
precision, not a Fisher information: DWLS is not efficient.)

*Proof.* $A$ is a function of the population and $\pi$ alone ($\Gamma_g$ its limit, $\Delta$ and $W$ at
$\theta^*$); the common $1/N$ cancels. $\square$

**Conditions.** Independent groups, $\pi_g$ fixed, $\theta^*$ interior, $\delta>0$ (local identification, I3),
and above all that the first-order expansion holds at the sample size in use. Near the set
$\hat\theta$ depends on the estimated spread through a near-singular $H$, so the linearization needs the
spread to be large against its own sampling error,
$$z=\sqrt{N_1}\,S_{1w}/\operatorname{ASE}(\hat S_{1w})\gg1 .$$
In the grid $z\ge8.9$ at $\delta\ge\delta_{ok}$ for every $N$, and $1.3\le z\le3.7$ at $\delta=0.05$ (chunk
`grd-regime`). So the first-order argument holds in the safe cells, where the reference SE is N-free
relative to its own $N$ and the geometric $S_{1w}$ is the right axis; at $\delta=\delta_{harm}$ it does not,
and there harm (non-convergence, the tail of the reported SE) is governed by $z^2$, of the order of $Q$,
and depends on $N$. The preregistration classifies $\delta\le0.05$ as harmful by derivation ($\delta=0$) and
from the pilot ($\delta=0.05$, labelled pilot-informed), not by $R$; this Result does not alter that.

#### Result G3 (the leading term, and when $\hat\kappa_2$ is blind)

Let $M(\delta)=W^{1/2}\Delta$, with $M(0)n=0$ for I5's null vector $n=(0_\tau,0_\lambda,\omega_2,-2\phi_2,c-\kappa_2)$,
normalized to $\|n\|=1$. Let $M_1=\partial M/\partial\delta|_0$, $P$ the projector off $\operatorname{col}M(0)$,
$v=PM_1n$, $a=\|v\|^2$, $b=v'W^{1/2}\Omega W^{1/2}v$. If $v\ne0$,
$$\delta^2A(\delta)\to nn'\,b/a^2,\qquad
\frac{\mathrm{SE}(\hat\kappa_2)}{\mathrm{SE}(\hat\phi_2)}\to\frac{|c-\kappa_2|}{2\phi_2},\qquad
\frac{\sigma_{\min}}{\sigma_{\max}}\big(W^{1/2}\Delta\big)=O(\delta).$$
*Proof.* $M(\delta)(n-\delta K)=\delta v+O(\delta^2)$ for $K$ with $M(0)K=(I-P)M_1n$. So $H$ has one eigenvalue
$\delta^2a+O(\delta^3)$ with eigenvector $n+O(\delta)$ and the others are $O(1)$; hence
$H^{-1}=nn'/(\delta^2a)+O(\delta^{-1})$, $n'Bn=\delta^2b+O(\delta^3)$, and $A=H^{-1}BH^{-1}$ gives the leading term.
The $\sigma_{\min}$ statement is that eigenvalue's square root. $\square$

**Corollary.** If $c=\kappa_2$ then $n_\kappa=0$: $\kappa_2$ stays identified on the singular set,
$\mathrm{SE}(\hat\kappa_2)$ stays bounded as $\delta\to0$, and $\mathrm{SE}(\hat\phi_2)\sim1/\delta$. **A harm criterion on
$\hat\kappa_2$ alone is blind near $c=\kappa_2$.** In the grid $c=0.4$ has $c-\kappa_2=0.1$, and the first-order
$R(0.05)$ is 1.56 ($p=4$) and 1.44 ($p=6$), below $m=2$; at $c=0$ it is 3.27 and 2.92. Harm in the
$c=0.4$, $\delta=0.05$ cells therefore comes from outside first order (Result G2's condition): in the
confirmatory run it was 0.30–0.57, largely non-convergence. Recorded, not acted on: the preregistration
is frozen.

*Remark (heuristic, not a Result).* The SE reported at $\hat\theta$ is evaluated at the estimated spread, so
by G3 it behaves roughly as $|\hat c-\hat\kappa_2|/\hat S_{1w}$, one reason a statistic in $\hat S_{1w}$ can track
the SE leg of harm even where $z$ is small.

#### Result G4 (the start, and Module 3's second point)

Module 3's starts are λ = 0.7 throughout, τ at group 1's sample thresholds $s_\tau$ (the tied-τ start;
group 1's, as `inv-start` assumed, decided 2026-10-09, §4.8 O5), ω = 1, κ = 0, φ = 1. So $r^{(0)}=s_\tau/0.7$, and:
(i) θ⁽⁰⁾ is on I5's set iff the sample thresholds are all equal, to some $t$, not iff the true $r_j$
are. (ii) θ⁽²⁾ leaves the set iff $t\ne0$: at $t=0$, $r\equiv0$ for every λ, so no perturbation that keeps
thresholds fixed can leave it (λ only; λ and φ, the literal "every free ψ"; λ, φ, ω and κ all fail), and
the rank check aborts, correctly, since it has no way out. (iii) A population on the set with unequal λ
($\tau\propto\lambda$) has unequal $s_\tau$, so θ⁽⁰⁾ is full rank and the start check passes while the
population point is deficient; conversely equal thresholds with unequal λ are identified but start
deficient. The start check is neither necessary nor sufficient for I5's set; the pre-fit guard on
$\hat S_{1w,1}$ is the check that sees the population. Whether thresholds join the perturbation is not
decided here (O7; decided 2026-10-09 in spec §4.8: they do not, nor ν, ω, α).

#### Results P1–P4 (the post-fit statistics near the set)

*Drafted by a read-only agent (task I) from `45c03c9`; its runs (a Python port of the helpers, then the
chunks once in R 4.3.3) are not evidence. Executed by the main session from the repository file,
2026-10-09 (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2), after every earlier chunk in document order: every assertion held on
the first run with no chunk changed, and the printed figures match those quoted here (seeded Monte Carlo
to the third digit or better). Every numeric bound in those chunks was chosen after the drafter's scratch
run measured it, and is labelled so; none was set before measuring.*

**Scope.** The setting of Results G1–G4 (intercepts level, all-binary factor, $G=2$, delta parameterization,
weighting (a), $\pi=(\pi_1,\pi_2)$). It derives the first-order sampling behaviour of the four post-fit
candidates listed under "Open" item 1, their relation to Module 10's rank criterion, and their relation to
the preregistered harm. **It gives the post-fit guard no role and proposes no cutoff. It uses no result of the
confirmatory run.** Everything is first order in $N^{-1/2}$ at a fixed population; no estimate was computed.

**Notation.** $\theta=(\eta,\zeta)$ with $\eta=(\tau,\lambda)\in\mathbb R^{2p}$ and
$\zeta=(\omega,\phi_2,\kappa_2)\in\mathbb R^{p+2}$, $q=3p+2$ (`inv_model`'s layout $\tau|\lambda|\omega|\phi|\kappa$).
$M(\theta)=W^{1/2}\Delta(\theta)$ is $D\times q$, $D=p(p+1)$, with $W=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\pi_gW_g)$ held at the
population value in first-order statements (justified in Result P2). $\mathcal S={\tau\propto\lambda}$ is I5's set.
**Every** $\theta$ decomposes exactly as $\theta=\theta_0+(\varepsilon,0)$ with
$\theta_0=(\hat c\lambda,\lambda,\zeta)\in\mathcal S$, $\hat c=\lambda'\tau/\lambda'\lambda$ (the
$\lambda^2$-weighted mean of $\tau/\lambda$) and $\varepsilon=P_\lambda^\perp\tau\perp\lambda$, so
$|\varepsilon|=|\lambda|,S_{1w}(\tau,\lambda)$ (G1): the spread is the distance from $\mathcal S$, and
$\mathcal S$ has no extent in $\zeta$. Write $n$ for the unit vector proportional to
$(0_\tau,0_\lambda,\omega,-2\phi_2,\hat c-\kappa_2)$, I5's null vector of $M(\theta_0)$, and $n_f$ for its two entries on $(\phi_2,\kappa_2)$.

The candidates, at $\hat\theta$ of the intercepts fit ($M=\hat W^{1/2}\Delta(\hat\theta)$):

| | definition | note |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | $\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}$ of $M$ | **the same number as Module 10's** `e(bread_ratio)` (Result P3) |
| P1e | the same after scaling each column of $M$ to unit norm | removes the units of $\omega,\phi,\kappa$ |
| P2 | $\lvert n(\theta_0)'v_{\min}\rvert$, $v_{\min}$ the right singular vector of $\sigma_{\min}$ | $n$ needs a $c$; none exists in a sample, so $\hat c$ above; in $\theta$-units, so not invariant to reparameterizing $\zeta$. Reported as $1-$P2 |
| P3 | $\lambda_{\min}(S)/\lambda_{\max}(S)$, $S$ the Schur complement of $M'M$ for $(\phi_2,\kappa_2)$ given the other $q-2$ parameters | squared units ($H=M'M$, not $M$); $S^{-1}=[H^{-1}]_{ff}$; for $G>2$ the block is $2(G-1)$ |
| $\hat S_{1w}$ | $S_{1w}(\hat\tau,\hat\lambda)$ of the **intercepts** fit | *not* the preregistered pre-fit statistic (group 1's configural estimates) |

#### Result P1 (the leading term of each candidate)

Let $\theta_0\in\mathcal S$ be interior with $\phi_2>0$, $M_0=M(\theta_0)$ of rank $q-1$ (I5) with
$M_0n=0$ and $\sigma_{q-1}(M_0)>0$, $P=I-M_0M_0^+$, $s_1=\sigma_{\max}(M_0)$. For $\varepsilon\in\lambda^\perp$ let
$M_1[\varepsilon]$ be the derivative of $M$ in the direction $(\varepsilon,0)$, and define on $\lambda^\perp$ the
linear maps
$$V\varepsilon=P,M_1[\varepsilon],n,\qquad Y\varepsilon=M_0^+M_1[\varepsilon],n ,$$
the parts of $M_1[\varepsilon]n$ orthogonal to and inside $\operatorname{col}M_0$. **Condition:** $V$ has full column
rank $p-1$ (so $|V\varepsilon|\ge c|\varepsilon|$). Then for $\theta=\theta_0+(\varepsilon,0)$, as $\varepsilon\to0$:

1. $\sigma_{\min}(M)=|V\varepsilon|(1+O(|\varepsilon|))$, so $\mathrm{P1}=|V\varepsilon|/s_1+O(|\varepsilon|^2)$;
2. $\mathrm{P1e}=\rho_e(\theta_0),\mathrm{P1}$, $\rho_e=s_1/(|D_cn|,s_1^{e})$, $D_c=\operatorname{diag}$ of the column norms of $M_0$, $s_1^e=\sigma_{\max}(M_0D_c^{-1})$;
3. $\mathrm{P3}=\gamma(\theta_0),\mathrm{P1}^2,(1+O(|\varepsilon|))$, $\gamma=s_1^2/(|n_f|^2\lambda_2(S_0))$, $S_0$ the Schur complement at $\theta_0$ (rank 1: $S_0n_f=0$; $\lambda_2$ its other eigenvalue);
4. $1-\mathrm{P2}=\tfrac12|Y\varepsilon|^2+O(|\varepsilon|^3)$.

*Proof.* Put $H=M'M=H_0+H_1+H_2+\dots$ in powers of $\varepsilon$, $H_0n=0$, $H_1=M_0'M_1+M_1'M_0$. $H_0$ has the
simple zero eigenvalue with eigenvector $n$ and gap $\sigma_{q-1}^2$, so (Rayleigh–Schrödinger) the smallest eigenvalue is
$\lambda_{\min}=n'H_2n-n'H_1H_0^+H_1n+O(\varepsilon^3)$. With $M_0n=0$: $n'H_2n=|M_1n|^2$ and
$n'H_1H_0^+H_1n=|M_0M_0^+M_1n|^2$, since $H_0^+M_0'=M_0^+$. Hence $\lambda_{\min}=|PM_1n|^2+O(\varepsilon^3)$,
which is (1) after the square root (this is G3's $M(n-\delta K)=\delta v$ with the lower bound supplied by the
eigenvalue expansion). (2): $MD_c^{-1}$ has the same column space, so the same $P$, and the unit null vector $D_cn/|D_cn|$;
apply (1) to it, $D_c(\theta)=D_c(\theta_0)(1+O(\varepsilon))$. (3): $H^{-1}=\nu\nu'/\lambda_{\min}+O(1)$ with $\nu$
the near-null unit eigenvector, so $S^{-1}=[H^{-1}]_{ff}$ has the one large eigenvalue
$|\nu_f|^2/\lambda_{\min}(1+O(\lambda_{\min}))$, i.e. $\lambda_{\min}(S)=\lambda_{\min}/|n_f|^2$ to relative
$O(\varepsilon)$; $S(\theta)\to S_0$ continuously, and $H_{rr}$ is invertible at $\theta_0$ because the only column
dependency is $n$, whose $\phi_2$ entry is non-zero; so $\lambda_{\max}(S)=\lambda_2(S_0)+O(\varepsilon)$. (The unprofiled block $H_{ff}$ is well conditioned on $\mathcal S$: eigenvalue ratio 0.59–0.99 on the grid, chunk `pst-first-order`; only the profile sees the set, so "the conditioning of the $(\phi_g,\kappa_g)$ block" must mean $S$, not $H_{ff}$.) (4): the
first-order eigenvector is $\nu=n-H_0^+H_1n=n-M_0^+M_1n$, orthogonal to $n$ because $\operatorname{ran}M_0^+\perp\ker M_0$,
and $\hat n$ is exactly the null vector at $\theta_0(\theta)$, so $\lvert\hat n'v_{\min}\rvert=(1+|Y\varepsilon|^2)^{-1/2}$ to this order. $\square$

*Checked in chunk `pst-first-order`* (assertions at $10^{-2}$, $10^{-3}$, $5\times10^{-2}$; the R scratch run measured (4) to $10^{-3}$ at $|\varepsilon|=10^{-3}$, and a numpy run measured (1) to $1.3\times10^{-3}$ at $|\varepsilon|=10^{-2}$, $\rho_e$ and
$\gamma$ to $5\times10^{-5}$): $\rho_e\approx1.29$–$1.46$, $\gamma\approx15$–$20$ at the grid population.

**Corollary P1a (population values).** Along the preregistered path $\tau=(c+\delta d)\lambda$,
$\varepsilon=\delta,P_\lambda^\perp(d\circ\lambda)$ and the base point has $\hat c=c+\delta\bar r_w(d)$, so
$\mathrm{P1}=\delta,k_1+O(\delta^2)$ with $k_1=|VP_\lambda^\perp(d\circ\lambda)|/s_1$: linear in $\delta$ (G3's
$O(\delta)$, now with its coefficient), and likewise P1e; P3 is quadratic and $1-$P2 is quadratic. At $p=4$, $c=0$:
P1 $=0.0044$ at $\delta=.05$ and $0.034$ at $\delta=.4$.

**Corollary P1b (what is and is not a function of what, at fixed $\theta_0$).**
(a) P1, P1e and P3 are increasing functions of the one scalar $|V\varepsilon|$ (P1e $=\rho_e$P1, P3 $=\gamma$P1²):
*conditional on* $\theta_0$ they are monotone functions of each other. (b) P2 depends on $|Y\varepsilon|$, the part of
$M_1[\varepsilon]n$ inside $\operatorname{col}M_0$, a different quadratic form in $\varepsilon$; $(V\varepsilon,Y\varepsilon)$ are
complementary components of one vector, so P2 is not a function of P1 and carries no size information to first order
(it is $1-O(\delta^2)$: $1-$P2 $=2.4\times10^{-10}$ at $\delta=10^{-4}$ and $0.004$ at $\delta=.4$ for $p=4$, $c=.4$). (c) With $K=V'V$ on $\lambda^\perp$,
$\sqrt{\kappa_{\min}(K)},|\varepsilon|\le|V\varepsilon|\le\sqrt{\kappa_{\max}(K)},|\varepsilon|$: P1 is a function of $\hat S_{1w}$ alone **iff**
$K\propto I$ and $\theta_0$ is fixed. $K\not\propto I$ for $p-1\ge2$ on the grid: $\sqrt{\kappa_{\max}/\kappa_{\min}}=1.14$–$1.17$,
so P1 is within about $\pm8%$ of proportional to $\hat S_{1w}$ at fixed $\theta_0$, and not exactly proportional.

#### Result P2 (first-order sampling behaviour)

*Setting.* $\sqrt N(\hat\theta-\theta^*)\to N(0,A)$ with $A=A(\vartheta,\pi)$ of G2 (the pooled sandwich), $\delta>0$ and
$\pi$ fixed, $N=N_1/\pi_1$ the total sample size. For a statistic $T(\theta)$ with $W$ fixed at its population value,
$\mathrm{ASE}(T)=\sqrt{g'Ag/N}$, $g=\partial T/\partial\theta$ at $\theta^*$, and $z_T=T(\theta^*)/\mathrm{ASE}(T)$.

*Why $W$ may be fixed.* $\hat W^{1/2}=W^{1/2}(1+O_p(N^{-1/2}))$, and in $\sigma_{\min}$ it multiplies $M_1[\varepsilon]n$ (Result
P1), already $O(\varepsilon)$; so its effect on P1 is a relative $O_p(N^{-1/2})$, against $O_p(1/(\delta\sqrt N))$ for the terms kept.
This is *least* justified in the safe cells ($\delta=.4$, where the two are of the same order) and is not checked with data.

**(i) $\eta$ is regular on $\mathcal S$; $\zeta$ is not.** $n_\eta=0$, so the $\eta$ columns of $\Delta$ are independent of
the span of the $\zeta$ columns, $\hat\eta$ is asymptotically normal even at $\delta=0$ (any generalized-inverse sandwich
gives the same $\eta$-block), and $A_{\eta\eta}(\delta)$ stays bounded as $\delta\to0^+$. *Proof of boundedness.* Write the
SVD form of $A$ from Result P4, $A=\nu\nu'C_{mm}/\sigma_{\min}^2+(\nu r'+r\nu')/\sigma_{\min}+R$, with $r,R=O(1)$; $\nu_\eta=\delta n_{1\eta}+O(\delta^2)$ (the tilt of the near-null vector,
P1(4)) and $\sigma_{\min}=\delta\sqrt a$ (G3), so every term is $O(1)$ in the $\eta$ block. **The limit is not the $\delta=0$
value.** Its excess over the pseudo-inverse sandwich at $\delta=0$ is the tilt term $n_{1\eta}n_{1\eta}',b/a^2$ plus a cross term; at the four grid
$(c,p)$ the trace of $A_{\eta\eta}$ is 3.6–5.9% above the $\delta=0$ value and the tilt term alone accounts for 72–86% of
the gap (chunk `pst-regular`). So $\hat S_{1w}$ has a continuous first-order law, but "the law at $\delta=0$" and
"the limit of the law as $\delta\to0^+$" differ.

**(ii) The law of the intercepts-level spread, valid down to $\delta=0$.** From $\varepsilon=P_\lambda^\perp(\tau-\hat c\lambda)$ and
$\partial(P_\lambda^\perp\tau)=P_\lambda^\perp(d\tau-\hat c,d\lambda)$ on $\mathcal S$,
$$N|\lambda|^2\hat S_{1w}^2\ \Rightarrow\ |\sqrt N\varepsilon+\xi|^2,\quad \xi\sim N(0,\Sigma_\perp),\quad
\Sigma_\perp=T A_{\eta\eta}T',\ T=[P_\lambda^\perp,,-\hat cP_\lambda^\perp],$$
a weighted non-central $\chi^2$ (the Wald statistic for equal $r$, G1's and the preregistration's $S_2$, is the same quadratic form with $\Sigma_\perp^+$). So
$$E\hat S_{1w}^2=S_{1w}^2+\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\perp/(N|\lambda|^2)+o(N^{-1}),\qquad S_{1w}=\delta,S_{1w}(d\circ\lambda,\lambda),$$
a **noise floor** $\hat S_{1w}\approx(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\perp/N|\lambda|^2)^{1/2}$ at $\delta=0$, nearly free of $\delta$ ($\operatorname{tr}A_{\eta\eta}$ moves 5% over $\delta\le.4$), falling as $N^{-1/2}$,
and dependent on $\pi$, $c$, $d$, $\lambda$ and group 2 through $A$. This law does not need $z\gg1$: it needs only that
$\hat\eta$ be normal. (Chunk `pst-law`: formula and Monte Carlo draws of the first-order law agree to 0–4%.)
Numerically, the $z$ of this spread, $z_{\hat S}=\sqrt N S_{1w}/\mathrm{ASE}$ with the pooled $A$ at $N=2N_1$, equals G2's pre-fit $z$ (group 1 configural, $N_1$) to
0.8% over the 12 cells: tying $\tau,\lambda$ across groups adds almost nothing about the spread, because $\omega_j$ absorbs
group 2. *Observed, not derived.*

**(iii) When the delta method fails (the analogue of G2's $z\gg1$).** $T\in{$P1, P1e, P3, $\hat S_{1w}}$ are norms of $\varepsilon$ (not
differentiable at $\varepsilon=0$) and, for all but $\hat S_{1w}$, functions of $\hat\zeta$. The linearization needs
(a) $z_T\gg1$ and (b) $\hat\zeta$ near $\zeta^*$, i.e. $\mathrm{SE}(\hat\phi_2)/\phi_2\ll1$. By G3,
$\mathrm{SE}(\hat\phi_2)\sim|n_\phi|\sqrt b/(a,\delta\sqrt N)$, so (b) reads $\delta\sqrt N\gg k$, and numerically
$\mathrm{SE}(\hat\phi_2)/\phi_2\approx k/(\delta\sqrt N)$ with $k=2.6$–$3.9$ over the grid ($N$ total): 1.7–2.1 (N$_g$=500) and 0.8–1.1 (N$_g$=2000) at $\delta=.05$; 0.43–0.55 and 0.22–0.27 at $\delta=.2$; 0.25–0.31 and 0.13–0.15 at $\delta=.4$.
(a) and (b) are the same condition up to constants because both $|\varepsilon|/\mathrm{sd}(\hat\varepsilon)$ and
$\phi_2/\mathrm{sd}(\hat\phi_2)$ scale as $\delta\sqrt N$. They are necessary, not shown sufficient. Pushing the Gaussian first-order
law of $\hat\theta$ through each statistic (chunk `pst-push`, no data; 600 draws per cell, so each ratio carries about 3% Monte Carlo error) shows the following ratios of the pushed-forward SD to the delta-method ASE (numbers from the R scratch run):
P1: 0.95–1.04 for every $z\ge5$, 0.84–0.93 for $z\approx2$–4, 0.54–0.73 below $z\approx1.5$ (overstated). $\hat S_{1w}$: 0.94–1.04 from $z\approx5$, 0.76–0.88 for $z<4$.
P1e: 1.09–1.16 for $z\ge20$, 1.3–3.2 for $z\approx12$–17, 2.3–12.9 below $z\approx11$ (understated). P3: 1.07–1.26 at $z\approx4$–5, 1.5–5.5 for $z\approx2$–3, 7–59 below $z\approx1.5$.
So P1 and $\hat S_{1w}$ have a usable delta-method SE from $z\approx5$; P1e and P3 do not at any $z$ the grid reaches below about 20 and 5 respectively. The tabulated $z$ (range over the 4 $(c,p)$; $N_g=500$ | $2000$):

| $\delta$ | P1 | P1e | P3 | $\hat S_{1w}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .05 | 0.7–1.2 | 1.4–2.3 | 1.9–2.4 | 3.8–4.7 | 0.3–0.4 | 0.6–0.8 | 1.3–1.8 | 2.6–3.7 |
| .2 | 2.5–4.2 | 5.1–8.4 | 6.6–8.2 | 13.2–16.4 | 1.2–1.5 | 2.3–2.9 | 5.0–7.0 | 10.0–14.0 |
| .4 | 4.2–6.7 | 8.5–13.3 | 10.4–12.5 | 20.8–25.0 | 2.1–2.5 | 4.1–5.1 | 9.0–12.3 | 17.9–24.6 |

At $\delta=.05$ the Gaussian law also places 10–32% of its mass at $\hat\phi_2\le10^{-3}$ (0–4% at $\delta=.2$, none at $.4$): outside the
parameter space. That is a statement about the Gaussian approximation, not a prediction of non-convergence.

**(iv) P1 is not a function of the spread in sampling.** P1 $\approx|V(\hat\zeta)\hat\varepsilon|/s_1(\hat\zeta)$ depends on $\hat\zeta$ through $V$ and $s_1$, and
$\hat\zeta$ is the poorly determined part. Decomposing the delta-method variance of $\log$P1 into the $\hat\eta$ part, the $\hat\zeta$ part
and twice their cross term gives shares of 0.15–0.48, 1.47–1.86 and $-0.62$ to $-1.34$ over the 12 cells (chunk `pst-decomp`): the
variance of P1 is dominated by $\hat\zeta$, not by $\hat\varepsilon$, with a strongly negative covariance between them. The first-order
correlation of P1 with $\hat S_{1w}$ is **negative**, $-0.26$ to $-0.41$ (also in the pushed-forward draws of `pst-push`: $-0.25$ to $-0.40$ in the R scratch run over the ten cells with $z_{\rm P1}\ge5$; asserted $<-0.1$);
that of P1 with P3 is $0.95$–$1.00$ (P3 $\approx\gamma$P1²), and with P1e $0.38$–$0.73$. The sign is computed, not proved; the
conjectured mechanism is the ridge: $\hat\zeta-\zeta^*$ is nearly one-dimensional (along $n$, SD $\propto1/\delta\sqrt N$) and correlates with $\hat\eta$ through the tilt $n_{1\eta}$.
So P1 and $\hat S_{1w}$ are **monotone in $\delta$ across designs** (Corollary P1a) and **not monotone, indeed weakly anti-correlated,
across replications within a design**. P1e is less noisy than P1 (its $z$ is about 2.5 times larger) because equilibration removes the column-scale part of the $\hat\zeta$
dependence, but its delta-method SE is the least reliable (above).

**(v) Dependence on $\pi$** (chunk `pst-pi`, printed). $\pi$ enters through $W$ (the values of P1, P1e) and through
$\Omega=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\Gamma_g/\pi_g)$ (the sandwich). At $p=4$, $c=0$, $\delta=.05$: P1 $=0.0044,\ 0.0037,\ 0.0023$ for $\pi_1=.5,.3,.1$,
and 0.034, 0.028, 0.017 at $\delta=.4$ (about half at $\pi_1=.1$); **P3 is unchanged by $\pi$** (0.000287, 0.000286, 0.000285); $\hat S_{1w}$'s
value does not depend on $\pi$ but its $z$ does (14.5, 11.2, 6.5 at $\delta=.4$, $N=2000$ total).

#### Result P3 (relation to Module 10's rank criterion)

**(i) The same ratio.** By spec Module 10, P1 is `e(bread_ratio)`, row 4 of `dwlsmv_breaddiag`: $\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}$
of $W_D^{1/2}\Delta$ over its non-zero columns, flagged `.n` (no flag in v1). Row 3, the numerical-rank criterion,
counts the singular values of the **same matrix** above $10^{-8}\sigma_{\max}$. So Module 10's row fires iff P1 $<10^{-8}$,
and for any post-fit cutoff $\mathrm{cut}\ge10^{-8}$:
* "Module 10 fires and P1 does not" is **empty**;
* "P1 fires and Module 10 does not" is ${10^{-8}\le\mathrm{P1}\le\mathrm{cut}}$, which contains the whole near-set region.

If the statistic called P1 is instead computed on a different diagonal weighting $W'$ (for example the unweighted $\Delta$), then
for diagonal $W>0$ the ratios differ by at most $\sqrt{\kappa(W)}$ in either direction (singular values of $W^{1/2}\Delta$ lie
between $\sqrt{w_{\min}}$ and $\sqrt{w_{\max}}$ times those of $\Delta$): structural, and at the grid population the unweighted/weighted ratio is within
1.5% ($\sqrt{\kappa(W)}\le1.25$) (chunk `pst-m10`). **Which $W$ the multi-group call of `dwlsmv_breaddiag` uses was not in
the text read** (weighting (a), $\pi_gW_g$, halves P1 at $\pi_1=.1$).

**(ii) Under sampling, Module 10 does not see the near-set region.** By P1(1), it fires iff $|V\hat\varepsilon|\lesssim10^{-8}s_1$. At
$\delta=0$ $\hat\varepsilon$ has a non-degenerate normal law on $\lambda^\perp$ (P2(i), (ii)), so the probability is the Gaussian mass of an
ellipsoid of radius $10^{-8}s_1$: at most $2.1\times10^{-16}$ for $p=4$ and $1.8\times10^{-26}$ for $p=6$ at $N\le4000$ (chunk `pst-m10`,
density at 0 times ellipsoid volume). The population values of P1 on the grid are $0.0038$–$0.06$ ($\delta=.05$–$.8$): at least five orders above the
criterion. The rank criterion is a numerical-rank test and the near-set region is a statistical-weakness region; they do not overlap
under sampling.

**(iii) The one sample-reachable exact hit: balanced items.** If every sample threshold is exactly 0 in both groups (e.g. median splits),
then $\hat\tau=0$ and $\hat\kappa_2=0$ exactly. *Proof.* The threshold residuals vanish at $\tau=0,\kappa=0$ for every $(\lambda,\omega,\phi)$,
group 1's because $\tau_j=0$ is its threshold, group 2's because $\omega_j(\tau_j-\lambda_j\kappa)=0$; the correlation residual does not
involve $(\tau,\kappa)$. So this is a global minimizer, and unique in $(\tau,\kappa)$ as soon as some $\omega_j\lambda_j\ne0$. Then $r\equiv0$: $\hat\theta\in\mathcal S$ with
$c=\kappa=0$, P1 $=0$ (to numerical noise: $10^{-12}$ with a finite-difference Jacobian, chunk `pst-m10`), P1e $=0$, P3 $=0$, P2 $=1$: all four candidates and Module 10 agree,
and this is G4(ii)'s start case reached at $\hat\theta$. Equal non-zero thresholds are *not* exact hits (@sec-marker-recovery's scope: $\hat\tau\ne s_\tau$ at the intercepts level).
That Stata's Module 10 flags this case was not executed.

#### Result P4 (relation to the preregistered harm)

**(i) An exact decomposition of the reported sandwich.** With the SVD $M=USV'$ and $C=U'W^{1/2}\Omega W^{1/2}U$,
$$A=H^{-1}M'W^{1/2}\Omega W^{1/2}MH^{-1}=\sum_{i,j}\frac{v_iv_j',C_{ij}}{\sigma_i\sigma_j}\quad\text{(exact; chunk }10^{-13}).$$
The term in the weakest direction is $v_mv_m'C_{mm}/\sigma_{\min}^2$, with $\sigma_{\min}=\mathrm{P1}\cdot\sigma_{\max}$ and
$C_{mm}=u_m'W^{1/2}\Omega W^{1/2}u_m$, a Rayleigh quotient of a correlation matrix, so $O(1)$ ($0.67$–$0.82$ at the grid cells printed by `pst-se`). Reading $A$ at $\hat\theta$ with estimated $\hat W,\hat\Omega$ gives the **reported** covariance. Then
$$\mathrm{SE}_{\rm rep}(\hat\phi_2)^2=\frac{v_{m\phi}^2,C_{mm}}{N,\sigma_{\min}^2},(1+O(\sigma_{\min})),\qquad
\mathrm{SE}_{\rm rep}(\hat\kappa_2)^2=\frac1N\Big[\frac{v_{m\kappa}^2C_{mm}}{\sigma_{\min}^2}+\frac{2v_{m\kappa}\varrho_\kappa}{\sigma_{\min}}+r_\kappa\Big],$$
$\varrho_\kappa=\sum_{i<m}v_{i\kappa}C_{mi}/\sigma_i$ and $r_\kappa$ the double sum over $i,j<m$, both $O(1)$. By G3 $v_{m\kappa}/v_{m\phi}\to(c-\kappa_2)/(-2\phi_2)$
(chunk: 0.103 against 0.104 at $c=0$, 0.036 against 0.035 at $c=.4$, $\delta=.05$). The leading term's share of $A_{\phi\phi}$ is 0.91–1.00 on every grid cell; its share of
$A_{\kappa\kappa}$ is 0.93, 0.43, 0.16 ($c=0$; $\delta=.05,.2,.4$; $p=4$) and 0.59, 0.09, 0.02 ($c=.4$). This makes G3's corollary quantitative: near $c=\kappa_2$ the weak direction does not load on $\kappa_2$, and
at $c-\kappa_2=0.1$ and the reference cell $\delta=.4$ the reported $\mathrm{SE}(\hat\kappa_2)^2$ is 98% remainder.

**(ii) Consequences for the harm of the preregistration** (SE leg: $\mathrm{SE}(\hat\kappa_2)\ge m,\mathrm{SE}_{\rm ref}$; $\mathrm{SE}_{\rm ref}$ a median of *reported* SEs):
1. The SE leg is a function of the replication's $\hat\theta,\hat W,\hat\Omega$ through the same SVD that defines P1. For a $\phi$-type SE it is, to leading order, a threshold on $\sigma_{\min}=\mathrm{P1},\sigma_{\max}$;
   for $\kappa_2$ it is a threshold on $\sigma_{\min}/\lvert v_{m\kappa}\rvert$ plus a remainder that dominates when $\lvert\hat c-\hat\kappa_2\rvert/(2\hat\phi_2)$ is small. A
   post-fit statistic that tracks the SE leg therefore does so partly **by algebra, not as independent evidence**: the quantity it is compared with is a function of the same $\hat M$.
2. The loading of the weak direction on $\kappa_2$ versus $\phi_2$, $\lvert\hat n_\kappa\rvert/\lvert\hat n_\phi\rvert=\lvert\hat c-\hat\kappa_2\rvert/(2\hat\phi_2)$, is computable from $\hat\theta$ without any SE, and indicates whether a
   $\kappa_2$-only harm criterion can see the weak direction at all; $\hat\phi_2$ always loads ($\lvert v_{m\phi}\rvert\approx0.79$–$0.85$, column `vphi` of `pst-se`).
3. The non-convergence leg is not covered by any first-order statement here. The nearest quantity is $\mathrm{SE}(\hat\phi_2)/\phi_2\approx k/(\delta\sqrt N)$ (P2(iii)).
4. Across cells, the population values of P1, P1e, P3 are increasing in $\delta$ (P1a), so as cell-level classifiers they order the preregistered cells as $\hat S_{1w}$ does; within a cell their
   replication-level spread is set by P2(iii)–(iv), where P1's relative first-order SD is $\approx7.5/\sqrt N$ at $\delta=.4$ and $\approx46/\sqrt N$ at $\delta=.05$ ($p=4$, $c=0$).

#### What Results P1–P4 do not establish

1. **Finite samples near $\delta\sqrt N=O(1)$.** Everything is first order at fixed $\delta$. The law of $(\hat\varepsilon,\hat\zeta)$ when $\delta=h/\sqrt N$ (Pitman scaling; $\hat\zeta$ non-convergent; $\sqrt N$P1 $\to|V(\hat\zeta)(h+\xi)|$ with a random limit $\hat\zeta$) is not derived, and no replication was simulated. The push-forward chunk isolates non-linearity only; it does not model non-convergence.
2. **Estimated $\hat W,\hat\Gamma$.** Treated as fixed; the argument that this is a relative $O(N^{-1/2})$ effect on P1 is a first-order sketch, weakest at $\delta=.4$, and untested with data.
3. **The closed form of $\lim_{\delta\to0^+}A_{\eta\eta}$.** The tilt term accounts for 72–86% of the gap to the $\delta=0$ value; the remainder (a cross term) is described, not computed in closed form.
4. **The sign and mechanism of corr(P1, $\hat S_{1w}$) $<0$.** Computed twice (delta method; pushed-forward draws); the ridge-tilt explanation is a conjecture.
5. **Thresholds for the delta method** ($z\approx5$ for P1 and $\hat S_{1w}$, $\ge20$ for P1e, none found for P3 up to $z\approx5$): read off 24 cells with 600 draws each; no theory. Necessary conditions only.
6. **P2.** Its usefulness: $1-$P2 is $O(\delta^2)$ and saturates ($\le0.03$ at $\delta=.8$), is parameterization-dependent, and needs a sample $\hat c$ that the model does not supply. Its sampling law is not derived (the delta method is degenerate at $\mathrm{P2}=1$ where its gradient vanishes).
7. **$G>2$, several factors, polytomous or mixed items, free group-1 metric.** $V$, $\gamma$, $\rho_e$ and the $2(G-1)$-block P3 are not derived or computed there.
8. **Which $W$ Module 10 uses for the pooled model**, and therefore whether P1 depends on $\pi$ in the shipped command.
9. **The joint law of the pre-fit $\hat S_{1w,1}$ (group 1, configural) and the post-fit statistics.** Both are functions of the same data; their correlation was not computed.
10. **The reported-SE distribution.** P4 uses the population $A$; the sampling variation of the *reported* $\mathrm{SE}(\hat\kappa_2)$ about it (through $\hat\theta$, $\hat\Gamma$) is not derived.
11. **Module 10 on the balanced case, in Stata.** Only the algebra and an R finite-difference Jacobian.
12. **No role and no cutoff** for the post-fit guard. The confirmatory results were not read as evidence or cross-checked.


#### Verification

```{r grd-setup}
# Requires @sec-invariance-id's inv-setup (inv_model, inv_jac, inv_rank, INV_TOL)
# and the setup chunk's phi2(), evaluated in this R session.
stopifnot(all(vapply(c("inv_model", "inv_jac", "inv_rank", "inv_designs", "INV_TOL", "phi2"),
                     exists, logical(1))))

grd_lam  <- function(p) seq(.6, .8, length.out = p)                     # the preregistered loadings
grd_zpat <- function(p) { z <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = p); z <- z - mean(z); z / sqrt(mean(z^2)) }
grd_S1w  <- function(tau, lam) {                                          # lambda^2-weighted spread of r
  cw <- sum(lam * tau) / sum(lam^2); sqrt(sum((tau - cw * lam)^2) / sum(lam^2)) }
grd_ratio <- function(M) { s <- svd(M, nu = 0, nv = 0)$d; min(s) / max(s) }

# Gauss-Hermite rule for E f(Z), Z ~ N(0, 1) (Golub-Welsch); 60 nodes
grd_gh <- local({ n <- 60L; Jm <- matrix(0, n, n); b <- sqrt(seq_len(n - 1L))
  Jm[cbind(1:(n - 1L), 2:n)] <- b; Jm[cbind(2:n, 1:(n - 1L))] <- b
  e <- eigen(Jm, symmetric = TRUE); list(x = e$values, w = e$vectors[1, ]^2) })

# Population Gamma of one group's binary (tau-hat, rho-hat), statistics in inv_model's order:
# p thresholds, then the column-major lower triangle of R. y*_j = lam_j eta + e_j, eta ~ N(kap, phi),
# Var e_j = th_j, y_j = 0 iff y*_j <= tau_j. Exact up to quadrature: the two-step binary estimator is
# a smooth function of the marginal and pairwise proportions, so Gamma = J (diag(pi) - pi pi') J'.
grd_gamma1 <- function(lam, tau, kap, phi, th) {
  p <- length(lam); pats <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(0:1), p)))
  eta <- kap + sqrt(phi) * grd_gh$x
  P0 <- pnorm(sweep(outer(-eta, lam) + matrix(tau, length(eta), p, byrow = TRUE), 2, sqrt(th), "/"))
  pr <- apply(pats, 1, function(pt)
    sum(grd_gh$w * apply(ifelse(matrix(pt == 0, nrow(P0), p, byrow = TRUE), P0, 1 - P0), 1, prod)))
  sd <- sqrt(lam^2 * phi + th); ts <- (tau - lam * kap) / sd; u <- lam * sqrt(phi) / sd
  L <- which(lower.tri(diag(p)), arr.ind = TRUE)                       # column-major: (2,1), (3,1), ...
  J <- matrix(0, p + nrow(L), nrow(pats))
  for (j in seq_len(p)) J[j, ] <- (pats[, j] == 0) / dnorm(ts[j])
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(L))) {
    i <- L[k, 1]; j <- L[k, 2]; r <- u[i] * u[j]; a <- ts[i]; b <- ts[j]; s <- sqrt(1 - r^2)
    J[p + k, ] <- ((pats[, i] == 0 & pats[, j] == 0) - dnorm(a) * pnorm((b - r * a) / s) * J[i, ]
                   - dnorm(b) * pnorm((a - r * b) / s) * J[j, ]) / phi2(a, b, r)
  }
  list(Gamma = J %*% (diag(pr) - tcrossprod(pr)) %*% t(J), s = c(ts, (u %o% u)[L]), pi = pr)
}

# The preregistered population (cell c, delta, p) at the intercepts level, two groups:
# group 1 delta reference; group 2 nu = 0, kappa2 = .3, phi2 = 1.44, residual variances .4..8 (inv_sim's)
grd_pop <- function(c, delta, p, kap = .3, phi = 1.44, d = grd_zpat(p), lam = grd_lam(p)) {
  tau <- (c + delta * d) * lam; th2 <- seq(.4, .8, length.out = p)
  g1 <- grd_gamma1(lam, tau, 0, 1, 1 - lam^2); g2 <- grd_gamma1(lam, tau, kap, phi, th2)
  m <- inv_model(rep(2L, p), "intercepts")
  x <- c(tau, lam, 1 / sqrt(lam^2 * phi + th2), phi, kap)              # tau | lam | om | phi | kap
  stopifnot(max(abs(m$sigma(x) - c(g1$s, g2$s))) < 1e-12)              # inv_model reproduces the population
  list(m = m, x = x, G = list(g1$Gamma, g2$Gamma), p = p, c = c)
}

# Sandwich ACOV of the pooled DWLS estimator (@sec-multigroup-scaling, weighting (a)), times N total:
# W = blockdiag(pi_g W_g), Omega = blockdiag(Gamma_g / pi_g).  ACOV(theta-hat) = A / N.
grd_DW <- function(pop, pg = c(.5, .5)) {
  n1 <- nrow(pop$G[[1]]); i1 <- seq_len(n1); i2 <- n1 + i1
  Om <- matrix(0, 2 * n1, 2 * n1); Om[i1, i1] <- pop$G[[1]] / pg[1]; Om[i2, i2] <- pop$G[[2]] / pg[2]
  list(D = inv_jac(pop$m$sigma, pop$x), w = c(pg[1] / diag(pop$G[[1]]), pg[2] / diag(pop$G[[2]])), Om = Om)
}
grd_A <- function(pop, pg = c(.5, .5)) {
  z <- grd_DW(pop, pg); Hi <- solve(crossprod(z$D * sqrt(z$w)))
  c(z, list(A = Hi %*% (t(z$D * z$w) %*% z$Om %*% (z$D * z$w)) %*% Hi))
}
```

```{r grd-geometry}
# Result G1: S1w is the distance of tau from span(lambda), in units of ||lambda||;
# zero iff rank[lambda, tau] = 1; reverse coding, factor sign and location of r leave it unchanged;
# exactly proportional to delta along r = c + delta d. S3's and S1's failure modes.
set.seed(20261009); p <- 6L
lam <- runif(p, .4, .9); tau <- rnorm(p, 0, .5); r <- tau / lam
rw <- sum(lam^2 * r) / sum(lam^2)
stopifnot(abs(grd_S1w(tau, lam)^2 - sum(lam^2 * (r - rw)^2) / sum(lam^2)) < 1e-12,            # weighted sd of r
          abs(grd_S1w(tau, lam) - sqrt(sum(qr.resid(qr(lam), tau)^2)) / sqrt(sum(lam^2))) < 1e-12,  # projection
          abs(grd_S1w(tau, lam) - min(sapply(seq(-2, 2, by = 1e-4), function(c) sqrt(sum((tau - c * lam)^2)))) /
                sqrt(sum(lam^2))) < 1e-6)                                                     # min over c (grid)
sv <- svd(cbind(lam, tau), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d                                                  # sigma1 sigma2 = ||lam|| ||tau_perp||
stopifnot(abs(prod(sv) - sum(lam^2) * grd_S1w(tau, lam)) < 1e-12)
stopifnot(grd_S1w(.3 * lam, lam) < 1e-15, grd_S1w(0 * lam, lam) == 0,                         # the singular set
          qr(cbind(lam, .3 * lam))$rank == 1)
tr <- tau; lr <- lam; tr[2] <- -tr[2]; lr[2] <- -lr[2]                                         # reverse-code item 2
stopifnot(abs(grd_S1w(tr, lr) - grd_S1w(tau, lam)) < 1e-12,
          abs(grd_S1w(tau, -lam) - grd_S1w(tau, lam)) < 1e-12,                                 # factor sign
          abs(grd_S1w(tau + .7 * lam, lam) - grd_S1w(tau, lam)) < 1e-12)                       # r -> r + .7
for (pp in c(4L, 6L)) for (cc in c(0, .4)) {                                                   # proportional to delta
  l <- grd_lam(pp); z <- grd_zpat(pp); k <- grd_S1w(z * l, l)
  for (dl in c(0, .05, .4, .8)) stopifnot(abs(grd_S1w((cc + dl * z) * l, l) - dl * k) < 1e-12)
}
# S3 (equilibrated ratio of [1, r]) is blind to spread when the r are centred at 0: the c = 0 cells
grd_S3 <- function(r) { rho <- abs(sum(r)) / (sqrt(length(r)) * sqrt(sum(r^2))); sqrt((1 - rho) / (1 + rho)) }
z <- grd_zpat(4)
stopifnot(abs(grd_S3(.05 * z) - 1) < 1e-12, abs(grd_S3(.8 * z) - 1) < 1e-12, is.nan(grd_S3(0 * z)))
# S1 = sd(r) divides by each lambda-hat separately: one small loading inflates it, S1w is bounded by ||tau||/||lambda||
l <- c(.7, .7, .7, .02); t <- .3 * l + c(0, 0, 0, .01)
stopifnot(sqrt(mean((t / l - mean(t / l))^2)) > .2, grd_S1w(t, l) < .01)
```

```{r grd-gamma}
# The population Gamma helper: (a) pattern probabilities sum to 1; (b) the threshold
# block equals its closed form; (c) the whole Gamma equals J Cov(pi) J' with J taken by finite
# differences of the exact map (pattern probabilities -> tau, rho), solving rho with uniroot().
p <- 3L; lam <- grd_lam(p); tau <- (.4 + .2 * grd_zpat(p)) * lam; th <- seq(.4, .8, length.out = p)
g <- grd_gamma1(lam, tau, .3, 1.44, th)
stopifnot(abs(sum(g$pi) - 1) < 1e-12)
ts <- g$s[1:p]; R <- diag(p); R[lower.tri(R)] <- g$s[-(1:p)]; R <- R + t(R) - diag(p)
Gt <- outer(1:p, 1:p, Vectorize(function(i, j) if (i == j) pnorm(ts[i]) * pnorm(-ts[i]) else
            Phi2(ts[i], ts[j], R[i, j]) - pnorm(ts[i]) * pnorm(ts[j]))) / outer(dnorm(ts), dnorm(ts))
stopifnot(max(abs(Gt - g$Gamma[1:p, 1:p])) < 1e-9)
pats <- as.matrix(expand.grid(rep(list(0:1), p))); L <- which(lower.tri(diag(p)), arr.ind = TRUE)
stat <- function(pr) {
  tq <- sapply(1:p, function(j) qnorm(sum(pr[pats[, j] == 0])))
  c(tq, apply(L, 1, function(ij) { p00 <- sum(pr[pats[, ij[1]] == 0 & pats[, ij[2]] == 0])
    uniroot(function(r) Phi2(tq[ij[1]], tq[ij[2]], r) - p00, c(-.99, .99), tol = 1e-13)$root }))
}
stopifnot(max(abs(stat(g$pi) - g$s)) < 1e-8)                        # the population statistics
Jn <- inv_jac(stat, g$pi, h = 1e-6)
Gn <- Jn %*% (diag(g$pi) - tcrossprod(g$pi)) %*% t(Jn)
cat(sprintf("Gamma: max |numeric - analytic| = %.3g (max entry %.3g)\n", max(abs(Gn - g$Gamma)), max(abs(g$Gamma))))
stopifnot(max(abs(Gn - g$Gamma)) < 1e-5 * max(abs(g$Gamma)))       # set before measuring
```

```{r grd-harm}
# Results G2 and G3 at population values: exact Jacobian and sandwich, no sampling.
# Layout tau | lam | om | phi | kap: kappa2 is column q = 3p + 2, phi2 column q - 1.
seK <- function(cc, dl, pp, pg = c(.5, .5), N = 1) { A <- grd_A(grd_pop(cc, dl, pp), pg)$A; sqrt(A[nrow(A), nrow(A)] / N) }
Rk  <- function(cc, dl, pp, pg = c(.5, .5)) seK(cc, dl, pp, pg) / seK(cc, .4, pp, pg)

# (a) N enters ACOV only as 1/N: the ratio at the same N is free of N; it depends on the group shares
stopifnot(abs(seK(0, .05, 4, N = 500) / seK(0, .4, 4, N = 500) - seK(0, .05, 4, N = 2000) / seK(0, .4, 4, N = 2000)) < 1e-12,
          abs(Rk(0, .05, 4, c(.3, .7)) - Rk(0, .05, 4)) > 1e-4)

# (b) the preregistered grid, first order: R = SE(kappa2-hat; delta) / SE(kappa2-hat; delta_ok = .4)
grid <- expand.grid(delta = c(.05, .1, .2, .4, .8), c = c(0, .4), p = c(4L, 6L))
grid$R <- mapply(Rk, grid$c, grid$delta, grid$p)
print(grid, digits = 4)
h <- grid$delta == .05
stopifnot(all(grid$R[h & grid$c == 0] > 2), all(grid$R[h & grid$c == .4] < 2))   # agent's scratch run:
                                                                                   # 3.27, 2.92 and 1.56, 1.44

# (c) Result G3, the leading term. M = W^{1/2} Delta (W, Delta and Omega all at the population point);
# M0 n = 0 at delta = 0, n unit; v = P M1 n with P the projector off col(M0); a = ||v||^2,
# b = v' W^{1/2} Omega W^{1/2} v. Then delta^2 ACOV -> n n' b / a^2, so delta SE_k -> |n_k| sqrt(b) / a.
Mof <- function(cc, dl, pp) { z <- grd_DW(grd_pop(cc, dl, pp)); z$D * sqrt(z$w) }
for (pp in c(4L, 6L)) for (cc in c(0, .4)) {
  pop0 <- grd_pop(cc, 0, pp); x0 <- pop0$x; q <- length(x0)
  n <- c(numeric(2 * pp), x0[2 * pp + 1:pp], -2 * x0[q - 1], cc - x0[q]); n <- n / sqrt(sum(n^2))  # I5's null vector
  z0 <- grd_DW(pop0); M0 <- z0$D * sqrt(z0$w)
  stopifnot(max(abs(M0 %*% n)) < 1e-8, inv_rank(M0) == q - 1L)
  hh <- 1e-4; M1 <- (Mof(cc, hh, pp) - Mof(cc, -hh, pp)) / (2 * hh)
  U <- svd(M0)$u[, 1:(q - 1)]; v <- M1 %*% n; v <- v - U %*% crossprod(U, v)
  aa <- sum(v^2); bb <- drop(crossprod(v * sqrt(z0$w), z0$Om %*% (v * sqrt(z0$w))))
  dl <- 1e-3; A <- grd_A(grd_pop(cc, dl, pp))$A
  pk <- abs(n[q]) * sqrt(bb) / aa; pf <- abs(n[q - 1]) * sqrt(bb) / aa
  cat(sprintf("p %d c %.1f: delta*SE_k %.5g (leading term %.5g), delta*SE_phi %.5g (%.5g)\n", pp, cc,
              dl * sqrt(A[q, q]), pk, dl * sqrt(A[q - 1, q - 1]), pf))
  stopifnot(abs(dl * sqrt(A[q - 1, q - 1]) / pf - 1) < 1e-2,                 # 1e-2 set before measuring
            abs(dl * sqrt(A[q, q]) / pk - 1) < 1e-2)
  A4 <- grd_A(grd_pop(cc, 1e-4, pp))$A                                      # SE_k / SE_phi -> |c - kappa2| / (2 phi2)
  stopifnot(abs(sqrt(A4[q, q] / A4[q - 1, q - 1]) - abs(cc - .3) / (2 * 1.44)) < 1e-3)
  r3 <- grd_ratio(Mof(cc, 1e-3, pp)) / 1e-3; r4 <- grd_ratio(Mof(cc, 1e-4, pp)) / 1e-4
  stopifnot(abs(r3 / r4 - 1) < 1e-2)                                        # the W_D^{1/2} Delta ratio is linear in delta
}
# (d) c = kappa2: n_k = 0, kappa2 stays identified on the set; SE(kappa2-hat) bounded, SE(phi2-hat) ~ 1/delta
for (cc in c(0, .4)) {
  A2 <- grd_A(grd_pop(cc, 1e-2, 4, kap = cc))$A; A4 <- grd_A(grd_pop(cc, 1e-4, 4, kap = cc))$A; q <- nrow(A2)
  stopifnot(abs(sqrt(A4[q, q] / A2[q, q]) - 1) < 1e-2, sqrt(A4[q - 1, q - 1] / A2[q - 1, q - 1]) > 90)
}
```

```{r grd-regime}
# Result G2's condition: the first-order argument needs the spread to be large
# against its own sampling error. z = S1w / ASE(S1w-hat), from group 1's configural sandwich at the
# population point (delta method; valid for delta > 0 only). Descriptive, except two bounds.
grd_V1 <- function(pop) {                      # N_1 x ACOV of group 1's configural (tau-hat, lam-hat)
  p <- pop$p; L <- lower.tri(diag(p)); s1 <- function(z) c(z[1:p], tcrossprod(z[p + 1:p])[L])
  D <- inv_jac(s1, pop$x[1:(2 * p)]); w <- 1 / diag(pop$G[[1]])
  Hi <- solve(crossprod(D * sqrt(w))); Hi %*% t(D * w) %*% pop$G[[1]] %*% (D * w) %*% Hi
}
grd_z1 <- function(cc, dl, pp) {               # z at N_1 = 1
  pop <- grd_pop(cc, dl, pp); x1 <- pop$x[1:(2 * pp)]
  g <- inv_jac(function(z) grd_S1w(z[1:pp], z[pp + 1:pp]), x1)
  grd_S1w(x1[1:pp], x1[pp + 1:pp]) / sqrt(drop(crossprod(g, grd_V1(pop) %*% g)))
}
zt <- expand.grid(delta = c(.05, .1, .2, .4, .8), c = c(0, .4), p = c(4L, 6L))
zt$z1 <- mapply(grd_z1, zt$c, zt$delta, zt$p)
for (N in c(500L, 1000L, 2000L)) zt[[paste0("z_N", N)]] <- zt$z1 * sqrt(N)
print(zt, digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(zt$z_N500[zt$delta >= .4] > 8),                  # safe cells: first order holds
          all(zt$z_N2000[zt$delta == .05] < 4))                # delta = .05: it does not, at any grid N
                                                               # bounds 8 and 4 chosen after the agent's scratch run measured >= 8.88 and <= 3.68
```

```{r grd-start}
# Result G4 on design A (p = 5, inv_start's layout): the start is on I5's set iff
# the group-1 sample thresholds are all equal; spec 4.8's second point leaves it iff that common value
# is nonzero; nothing that keeps thresholds fixed can leave it at 0; and the start check is blind to
# a population on the set when the true loadings differ.
mI <- inv_model(inv_designs$A, "intercepts"); q <- 17L; Jx <- function(x) inv_jac(mI$sigma, x)
# theta positions in spec 4.8 G6 order (tau, lambda, psi, nu, omega, alpha) for layout tau|lam|om|phi|kap
pos <- c(1:5, 6:10, 12:16, 11, 17); ph <- (sqrt(5) - 1) / 2
second <- function(x0, blocks) { i <- unlist(list(lam = 6:10, phi = 16, om = 11:15, kap = 17)[blocks])
  x0[i] <- x0[i] + .1 * ((pos[i] * ph) %% 1 - .5); x0 }
lit <- c("lam", "phi"); lamonly <- "lam"; all4 <- c("lam", "phi", "om", "kap")
for (t in c(0, .3)) {
  x0 <- inv_start(mI, as.list(rep(t, 5)))
  stopifnot(inv_rank(Jx(x0)) == q - 1L)                                            # on the set at theta0
  k <- if (t == 0) q - 1L else q                                                   # second point: leaves iff t != 0
  stopifnot(inv_rank(Jx(second(x0, lit))) == k, inv_rank(Jx(second(x0, lamonly))) == k,
            inv_rank(Jx(second(x0, all4))) == k)                                   # also with om, kap perturbed
}
x0 <- inv_start(mI, as.list(c(-.1, 0, .05, .1, .2))); stopifnot(inv_rank(Jx(x0)) == q)   # unequal thresholds: off the set
x0 <- inv_start(mI, as.list(rep(.3, 5))); x0[6:10] <- c(.5, .6, .7, .8, .9)              # identified model (r unequal),
stopifnot(inv_rank(Jx(x0)) == q)                                                          # once lam moves off equal starts
xs <- inv_point(mI, as.list(.4 * inv_lam), inv_lam)                                      # population on the set (r = .4)
x0 <- inv_start(mI, as.list(.4 * inv_lam))                                               # its start: s_tau unequal
stopifnot(inv_rank(Jx(xs)) == q - 1L, inv_rank(Jx(x0)) == q)                             # the start check passes
cat(sprintf("blind spot: start ratio %.3g, population ratio %.3g\n", grd_ratio(Jx(x0)), grd_ratio(Jx(xs))))
```


#### Verification of Results P1–P4

Executed by the main session, 2026-10-09 (see the note under Results P1–P4); the drafting agent's scratch run is not evidence. They require
`@sec-invariance-id`'s `inv-setup` and `inv-start` and this section's `grd-setup` and `grd-regime`; new names start with `pst_`. Every
numeric tolerance was **chosen after measuring**, as each comment says. `pst-push` and `pst-law` draw random numbers (seeded).

```{r pst-setup}
# Requires @sec-invariance-id's inv-setup and this section's grd-setup and grd-regime
# (grd_V1, grd_z1). Every new name starts with pst_.
stopifnot(all(vapply(c("inv_model", "inv_jac", "inv_rank", "inv_point", "inv_start", "grd_pop", "grd_A",
                       "grd_DW", "grd_gamma1", "grd_S1w", "grd_V1", "grd_z1"), exists, logical(1))))

# inv_model(rep(2L, p), "intercepts") layout: tau | lam | om | phi | kap  (q = 3p + 2; phi, kap are group 2's)
pst_ix <- function(p) list(tau = 1:p, lam = p + 1:p, om = 2 * p + 1:p, phi = 3 * p + 1L, kap = 3 * p + 2L,
                           eta = 1:(2 * p), zeta = (2 * p + 1):(3 * p + 2))
pst_M     <- function(pop, x, w) sqrt(w) * inv_jac(pop$m$sigma, x)       # M = W^{1/2} Delta, W fixed at w
pst_chat  <- function(x, p) { ix <- pst_ix(p); sum(x[ix$lam] * x[ix$tau]) / sum(x[ix$lam]^2) }  # lambda^2-weighted mean of r
pst_null  <- function(x, p, cc) {                                           # I5's null vector at (omega, phi, kappa; c), unit length
  ix <- pst_ix(p); n <- c(numeric(2 * p), x[ix$om], -2 * x[ix$phi], cc - x[ix$kap]); n / sqrt(sum(n^2)) }

# The four post-fit candidates (and the intercepts-level spread) at one parameter point.
#   P1  sigma_min / sigma_max of M                       (Module 10 row 4 = e(bread_ratio), same matrix)
#   P1e the same after scaling each column of M to unit norm
#   P2  |<nhat, v_min>|, nhat = pst_null at chat = lambda^2-weighted mean of tau/lambda; returned as 1 - P2
#   P3  lambda_min / lambda_max of the Schur complement of M'M for (phi, kappa) given all other parameters
#   S1w the intercepts-level spread grd_S1w(tau, lambda)  (NOT the pre-fit statistic of group 1's configural fit)
pst_stats <- function(M, x, p) {
  q <- ncol(M); sv <- svd(M, nu = 0); s <- sv$d
  cn <- sqrt(colSums(M^2)); se <- svd(sweep(M, 2, cn, "/"), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d
  H <- crossprod(M); f <- c(q - 1L, q); r <- seq_len(q - 2L)
  ev <- eigen(H[f, f] - H[f, r] %*% solve(H[r, r], H[r, f]), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  ix <- pst_ix(p)
  c(P1 = s[q] / s[1], P1e = se[q] / se[1], P3 = min(ev) / max(ev), S1w = grd_S1w(x[ix$tau], x[ix$lam]),
    oP2 = 1 - abs(sum(pst_null(x, p, pst_chat(x, p)) * sv$v[, q])))
}

# V: the response of the weakest direction to a displacement of tau off the set (Result P1).
# pop0 = grd_pop(c, 0, p) is ON the set. Columns of V are P M_1[e_k] n for an orthonormal basis e_k of
# lambda-perp (tau-coordinates), P the projector off col(M_0); Vin holds the part inside col(M_0).
pst_V <- function(pop0, w, h = 1e-4) {
  p <- pop0$p; x0 <- pop0$x; q <- length(x0); cc <- pop0$c
  M0 <- pst_M(pop0, x0, w); n <- pst_null(x0, p, cc); stopifnot(max(abs(M0 %*% n)) < 1e-8)
  sv0 <- svd(M0); U <- sv0$u[, seq_len(q - 1L)]
  Q <- qr.Q(qr(cbind(x0[p + 1:p], diag(p)[, seq_len(p - 1L)])))[, 2:p, drop = FALSE]  # orthonormal basis of lambda-perp
  M1n <- sapply(seq_len(p - 1L), function(k) {
    e <- numeric(q); e[1:p] <- Q[, k]
    drop(((pst_M(pop0, x0 + h * e, w) - pst_M(pop0, x0 - h * e, w)) / (2 * h)) %*% n) })
  list(V = M1n - U %*% crossprod(U, M1n), Vin = crossprod(U, M1n) / sv0$d[seq_len(q - 1L)],
       Q = Q, M0 = M0, n = n, x0 = x0, s = sv0$d, w = w, pop0 = pop0, q = q, p = p)
}
```

```{r pst-first-order}
# Result P1: sigma_min(M(theta)) = ||V eps|| + O(||eps||^2) for theta = theta_0 + (eps, 0), eps in lambda-perp;
# P1e = rho_e P1 and P3 = gamma P1^2 with rho_e, gamma functions of theta_0 only; 1 - P2 = (1/2)||M_0^+ M_1 n||^2.
set.seed(20261010)
pst_tab <- NULL
for (p in c(4L, 6L)) for (cc in c(0, .4)) {
  pop0 <- grd_pop(cc, 0, p); w0 <- grd_DW(pop0)$w; B <- pst_V(pop0, w0); q <- B$q
  ev <- eigen(crossprod(B$V), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  stopifnot(all(ev > 0))                                                   # V has full column rank p - 1: v != 0 in every direction
  pst_tab <- rbind(pst_tab, data.frame(p = p, c = cc, sigma_max = B$s[1], aniso = sqrt(max(ev) / min(ev))))
  for (tt in c(1e-3, 1e-2)) for (rep in 1:3) {                             # (i): random directions in lambda-perp
    u <- rnorm(p - 1L); u <- u / sqrt(sum(u^2)); x <- B$x0; x[1:p] <- x[1:p] + tt * drop(B$Q %*% u)
    smin <- svd(pst_M(pop0, x, w0), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d[q]
    stopifnot(abs(smin / sqrt(sum((B$V %*% (tt * u))^2)) - 1) < 1e-2)       # chosen after measuring (numpy scratch: <= 1.3e-3)
    st <- pst_stats(pst_M(pop0, x, w0), x, p)
    stopifnot(abs(st[["oP2"]] / (.5 * sum((B$Vin %*% (tt * u))^2)) - 1) < 5e-2)  # chosen after measuring (R scratch: see below)
    if (tt == 1e-3 && rep == 1) cat(sprintf("  1-P2 / (||Y eps||^2 / 2) - 1 = %.2e at t = 1e-3\n", st[["oP2"]] / (.5 * sum((B$Vin %*% (tt * u))^2)) - 1))
  }
  # the smooth factors, as closed forms at the set
  cn <- sqrt(colSums(B$M0^2)); s1e <- svd(sweep(B$M0, 2, cn, "/"), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d[1]
  rho_e <- B$s[1] / (sqrt(sum((cn * B$n)^2)) * s1e)
  H <- crossprod(B$M0); f <- c(q - 1L, q); r <- seq_len(q - 2L)
  l2 <- max(eigen(H[f, f] - H[f, r] %*% solve(H[r, r], H[r, f]), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)
  gam <- B$s[1]^2 / (sum(B$n[f]^2) * l2)
  eff <- eigen(H[f, f], symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values       # the UNprofiled (phi, kappa) block of M'M
  esc <- eigen(H[f, f] - H[f, r] %*% solve(H[r, r], H[r, f]), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  stopifnot(min(eff) / max(eff) > .3, min(abs(esc)) < 1e-10 * max(esc))     # raw block regular, profile singular on the set
                                                                           # (chosen after measuring: ratio .59-.99; profile ~1e-16)
  po <- grd_pop(cc, 1e-3, p); st <- pst_stats(pst_M(po, po$x, grd_DW(po)$w), po$x, p)
  cat(sprintf("p %d c %.1f: rho_e %.4f (pop %.4f), gamma %.3f (pop %.3f)\n", p, cc, rho_e, st[["P1e"]] / st[["P1"]],
              gam, st[["P3"]] / st[["P1"]]^2))
  stopifnot(abs(rho_e / (st[["P1e"]] / st[["P1"]]) - 1) < 1e-3,            # chosen after measuring (scratch: 5e-5)
            abs(gam / (st[["P3"]] / st[["P1"]]^2) - 1) < 1e-3)
}
print(pst_tab, digits = 4)
# P1 is not a function of the spread alone: eigenvalues of V'V on lambda-perp are not all equal
stopifnot(all(pst_tab$aniso > 1.05), all(pst_tab$aniso < 1.5))              # chosen after measuring (scratch: 1.14-1.17)
```

```{r pst-regular}
# The regular block eta = (tau, lambda) has no component in I5's null vector. Its sandwich
# ACOV stays bounded as delta -> 0+, but its limit is NOT the delta = 0 value (pseudo-inverse sandwich): the
# near-null right vector tilts into eta by O(delta), and the tilt times the O(1/delta) ridge uncertainty is O(1).
pst_pinv <- function(H, tol = 1e-10) {
  s <- svd(H); k <- sum(s$d > tol * s$d[1])
  s$v[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE] %*% (t(s$u[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]) / s$d[seq_len(k)]) }
for (p in c(4L, 6L)) for (cc in c(0, .4)) {
  ie <- pst_ix(p)$eta
  tr <- sapply(c(.4, .05, 1e-2, 1e-4), function(dl) { A <- grd_A(grd_pop(cc, dl, p))$A; sum(diag(A[ie, ie])) })
  pop0 <- grd_pop(cc, 0, p); z0 <- grd_DW(pop0); w0 <- z0$w; q <- 3 * p + 2L
  Hp <- pst_pinv(crossprod(z0$D * sqrt(w0))); Bm <- t(z0$D * w0) %*% z0$Om %*% (z0$D * w0); Ap <- Hp %*% Bm %*% Hp
  tr0 <- sum(diag(Ap[ie, ie]))
  stopifnot(max(tr) / min(tr) < 1.2,                       # bounded in delta (chosen after measuring: <= 1.05)
            abs(tr[4] / tr0 - 1) > 0.02)                   # not the delta = 0 value (chosen after measuring: 3.6-5.9%)
  # the tilt term n1_eta n1_eta' b / a^2, n1 = -M0^+ M1 n with M1 = dM/ddelta along the preregistered path
  Mp <- function(dl) { o <- grd_pop(cc, dl, p); pst_M(o, o$x, grd_DW(o)$w) }
  h <- 1e-5; M1 <- (Mp(h) - Mp(-h)) / (2 * h); M0 <- pst_M(pop0, pop0$x, w0); n <- pst_null(pop0$x, p, cc)
  sv0 <- svd(M0); U <- sv0$u[, seq_len(q - 1L)]; y <- drop(M1 %*% n)
  v <- y - U %*% crossprod(U, y); a <- sum(v^2); b <- drop(crossprod(v * sqrt(w0), z0$Om %*% (v * sqrt(w0))))
  n1 <- -drop(sv0$v[, seq_len(q - 1L)] %*% (crossprod(U, y) / sv0$d[seq_len(q - 1L)]))
  A4 <- grd_A(grd_pop(cc, 1e-4, p))$A
  dif <- A4[ie, ie] - Ap[ie, ie]; pred <- tcrossprod(n1[ie]) * b / a^2
  cat(sprintf("p %d c %.1f: tr A_eta at delta .4/.05/.01/1e-4 = %s; delta=0 pinv %.3f; |diff| %.3f, tilt term %.3f, residual %.3f\n",
              p, cc, paste(round(tr, 3), collapse = "/"), tr0, norm(dif, "F"), norm(pred, "F"), norm(dif - pred, "F")))
  stopifnot(norm(dif - pred, "F") < .5 * norm(dif, "F"))   # tilt term explains most of the gap (chosen after measuring: residual 14-28%)
}
```

```{r pst-law}
# Result P2, first order. T(theta-hat) for T in (P1, P1e, P3, Shat1w), with M's W fixed at the population value
# (its sampling error enters P1 at relative order N^{-1/2}, against 1/(delta sqrt N) for the terms kept).
# Delta method: sqrt(N) ASE(T) = sqrt(g' A g), g = dT/dtheta at theta*, A the pooled sandwich of grd_A.
pst_f <- function(pop, w) function(x) pst_stats(pst_M(pop, x, w), x, pop$p)[c("P1", "P1e", "P3", "S1w")]
pst_cells <- expand.grid(delta = c(.05, .2, .4), c = c(0, .4), p = c(4L, 6L))
pst_law <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pst_cells)), function(i) {
  d <- pst_cells$delta[i]; cc <- pst_cells$c[i]; p <- pst_cells$p[i]
  pop <- grd_pop(cc, d, p); za <- grd_A(pop); f <- pst_f(pop, za$w); val <- f(pop$x)
  G <- inv_jac(f, pop$x, h = 1e-6); ase1 <- sqrt(rowSums((G %*% za$A) * G))        # sqrt(N) x ASE, 4 statistics
  ix <- pst_ix(p)
  out <- data.frame(delta = d, c = cc, p = p, stat = names(val), value = unname(val), zN1 = unname(val / ase1))
  out$seph_N1 <- sqrt(za$A[ix$phi, ix$phi]) / pop$x[ix$phi]                      # sqrt(N) SE(phi2-hat)/phi2
  out }))
# z at N per group (N total = 2 N_g, pi = (1/2, 1/2)):  z = zN1 * sqrt(2 N_g);  SE(phi2)/phi2 = seph_N1 / sqrt(2 N_g)
pst_law$z_Ng500 <- pst_law$zN1 * sqrt(1000); pst_law$z_Ng2000 <- pst_law$zN1 * sqrt(4000)
pst_law$sephi_Ng500 <- pst_law$seph_N1 / sqrt(1000); pst_law$sephi_Ng2000 <- pst_law$seph_N1 / sqrt(4000)
print(subset(pst_law, select = c(delta, c, p, stat, value, z_Ng500, z_Ng2000, sephi_Ng500, sephi_Ng2000)), digits = 3)
# The intercepts-level spread has (numerically) the same z as G2's pre-fit configural spread: tying tau and lambda
# across groups adds little information about the spread because omega absorbs group 2.
sp <- subset(pst_law, stat == "S1w")
gz <- mapply(function(cc, d, p) grd_z1(cc, d, p), sp$c, sp$delta, sp$p)           # G2's z at N_1 = 1
rel <- abs(sp$zN1 * sqrt(2) / gz - 1)                                                # N total = 2 N_1
cat(sprintf("max |z_int(N = 2 N_1) / z_G2(N_1) - 1| = %.3f\n", max(rel)))
stopifnot(max(rel) < .05)                                                            # chosen after measuring (scratch: 0.008)
# the first-order law of Shat1w^2: E[Shat^2] = S^2 + tr(Sigma_perp) / (N |lam|^2),  Sigma_perp = T A_eta T', T = [Pperp, -chat Pperp]
set.seed(20261011)
for (d in c(.05, .2)) {
  p <- 4L; pop <- grd_pop(0, d, p); za <- grd_A(pop); ix <- pst_ix(p); lam <- pop$x[ix$lam]; N <- 1000
  Pp <- diag(p) - tcrossprod(lam) / sum(lam^2); cw <- pst_chat(pop$x, p); Tm <- cbind(Pp, -cw * Pp)
  noise <- sum(diag(Tm %*% za$A[ix$eta, ix$eta] %*% t(Tm))) / (N * sum(lam^2))
  Lc <- t(chol((za$A[ix$eta, ix$eta] + t(za$A[ix$eta, ix$eta])) / (2 * N)))
  X <- pop$x[ix$eta] + Lc %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p * 1e5), 2 * p)
  s2 <- apply(X, 2, function(e) grd_S1w(e[1:p], e[p + 1:p])^2)
  S2 <- grd_S1w(pop$x[ix$tau], lam)^2
  cat(sprintf("delta %.2f: MC E[S^2] - S^2 = %.5f, formula %.5f\n", d, mean(s2) - S2, noise))
  stopifnot(abs((mean(s2) - S2) / noise - 1) < .08)                                  # chosen after measuring (R scratch: 0% at delta .05, 3.8% at .2)
}
```

```{r pst-push}
# When does the delta method fail? Push the Gaussian first-order law theta-hat ~ N(theta*, A/N)
# through each statistic (W fixed at the population value; no data, no estimation). This isolates the
# non-linearity of T(theta); it says nothing about whether theta-hat is Gaussian, which fails where the Gaussian law
# leaves the parameter space (draws with phi2-hat <= 1e-3 are dropped and counted; inv_jac needs sqrt(phi)).
set.seed(20261012)
pst_push <- function(cc, d, p, Ng, nd = 600L) {
  pop <- grd_pop(cc, d, p); za <- grd_A(pop); f <- pst_f(pop, za$w); N <- 2 * Ng; ix <- pst_ix(p)
  G <- inv_jac(f, pop$x, h = 1e-6); ase1 <- sqrt(rowSums((G %*% za$A) * G))
  Lc <- t(chol((za$A + t(za$A)) / (2 * N)))
  X <- replicate(nd, pop$x + drop(Lc %*% rnorm(length(pop$x)))); ok <- X[ix$phi, ] > 1e-3
  R <- t(apply(X[, ok, drop = FALSE], 2, f)); val <- f(pop$x)
  data.frame(delta = d, c = cc, p = p, Ng = Ng, stat = names(val), z = sqrt(N) * val / ase1,
             r_P1_S1w_push = cor(R[, "P1"], R[, "S1w"]),
             sd_ratio = apply(R, 2, sd) / (ase1 / sqrt(N)), q05 = apply(R, 2, quantile, .05) / val,
             q50 = apply(R, 2, quantile, .5) / val, q95 = apply(R, 2, quantile, .95) / val, out = mean(!ok), row.names = NULL)
}
pst_pf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pst_cells)), function(i)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(500L, 2000L), function(Ng) pst_push(pst_cells$c[i], pst_cells$delta[i], pst_cells$p[i], Ng)))))
print(pst_pf, digits = 3)
p1 <- subset(pst_pf, stat == "P1")
stopifnot(all(p1$sd_ratio[p1$z >= 5] > .85 & p1$sd_ratio[p1$z >= 5] < 1.15),   # P1: delta method holds from z ~ 5 (chosen after measuring: R scratch 0.95-1.04)
          all(p1$sd_ratio[p1$z < 1.5] < .9),                                    # and overstates the spread below z ~ 1.5 (chosen after measuring: 0.54-0.73)
          all(p1$r_P1_S1w_push[p1$z >= 5] < -.1))                               # P1 and the spread are negatively correlated in the pushed-forward draws too
                                                                                # (chosen after measuring: R scratch -0.25 to -0.40)
```

```{r pst-decomp}
# Where P1's first-order variance comes from. log T = log T(eta, zeta); shares of g'Ag of the eta-part, the
# zeta-part and twice their cross term (cross < 0 means eta-hat and zeta-hat errors partly cancel in T);
# and the first-order correlation among the four statistics.
pst_dec <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pst_cells)), function(i) {
  d <- pst_cells$delta[i]; cc <- pst_cells$c[i]; p <- pst_cells$p[i]
  pop <- grd_pop(cc, d, p); za <- grd_A(pop); f <- pst_f(pop, za$w); val <- f(pop$x); ix <- pst_ix(p)
  G <- inv_jac(f, pop$x, h = 1e-6); Gl <- G / val                              # gradient of log T
  sh <- function(g) { te <- drop(g[ix$eta] %*% za$A[ix$eta, ix$eta] %*% g[ix$eta])
    tz <- drop(g[ix$zeta] %*% za$A[ix$zeta, ix$zeta] %*% g[ix$zeta])
    tc <- 2 * drop(g[ix$eta] %*% za$A[ix$eta, ix$zeta] %*% g[ix$zeta]); c(eta = te, zeta = tz, cross = tc) / (te + tz + tc) }
  Cv <- G %*% za$A %*% t(G); Rr <- Cv / sqrt(outer(diag(Cv), diag(Cv)))
  data.frame(delta = d, c = cc, p = p, sh_eta = sh(Gl[1, ])[["eta"]], sh_zeta = sh(Gl[1, ])[["zeta"]],
             sh_cross = sh(Gl[1, ])[["cross"]], r_P1_S1w = Rr[1, 4], r_P1_P1e = Rr[1, 2], r_P1_P3 = Rr[1, 3],
             r_P1e_S1w = Rr[2, 4]) }))
print(pst_dec, digits = 2)
stopifnot(all(pst_dec$sh_zeta > pst_dec$sh_eta),                                # zeta-hat dominates P1's first-order variance
          all(pst_dec$r_P1_S1w < -.1),                                          # P1 and the spread are negatively correlated within a cell
          all(pst_dec$r_P1_P3 > .9))                                            # P3 is nearly P1 (P3 ~ gamma P1^2)
# (chosen after measuring: sh_zeta 1.47-1.86 vs sh_eta .15-.48; r_P1_S1w -.41 to -.26; r_P1_P3 .95-1.00, R scratch)
```

```{r pst-pi}
# Dependence on the group shares pi = (pi_1, 1 - pi_1) at fixed total N: through W = blockdiag(pi_g W_g)
# (the value of P1, P1e, P3) and through Omega = blockdiag(Gamma_g / pi_g) (the sandwich A). Printed, not asserted.
pst_pi <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(.5, .3, .1), function(p1) do.call(rbind, lapply(c(.05, .4), function(d) {
  p <- 4L; cc <- 0; pop <- grd_pop(cc, d, p); pg <- c(p1, 1 - p1); za <- grd_A(pop, pg); f <- pst_f(pop, za$w)
  val <- f(pop$x); G <- inv_jac(f, pop$x, h = 1e-6); ase1 <- sqrt(rowSums((G %*% za$A) * G)); N <- 2000
  data.frame(pi1 = p1, delta = d, stat = names(val), value = unname(val), z_N2000 = sqrt(N) * unname(val) / ase1) }))))
print(pst_pi, digits = 3)
```

```{r pst-m10}
# Result P3: P1 is Module 10's own ratio. (a) weights: for diagonal W > 0 the weighted and unweighted ratios
# differ by at most sqrt(kappa(W)) (structural); at the grid population they differ by < 2% (chosen after
# measuring). (b) pi: P1 depends on the group shares through W = blockdiag(pi_g W_g). (c) Under continuous sampling
# P(P1 < 1e-8) is the Gaussian mass of a ball of radius ~1e-8 around the set. (d) The exact-hit event: balanced items.
for (p in c(4L, 6L)) for (cc in c(0, .4)) for (dl in c(.05, .4)) {
  pop <- grd_pop(cc, dl, p); D <- inv_jac(pop$m$sigma, pop$x); ratio <- function(w) { s <- svd(sqrt(w) * D, nu = 0, nv = 0)$d; s[length(s)] / s[1] }
  w5 <- grd_DW(pop, c(.5, .5))$w; ru <- ratio(rep(1, length(w5))); rw <- ratio(w5); kW <- max(w5) / min(w5)
  stopifnot(rw / ru <= sqrt(kW) * (1 + 1e-9), rw / ru >= 1 / sqrt(kW) * (1 - 1e-9), abs(ru / rw - 1) < .03)
  r13 <- ratio(grd_DW(pop, c(.1, .9))$w) / rw
  cat(sprintf("p %d c %.1f d %.2f: P1(pi=.5) %.4g, unweighted/weighted %.3f, sqrt(kappa W) %.2f, P1(pi=.1)/P1(pi=.5) %.2f\n",
              p, cc, dl, rw, ru / rw, sqrt(kW), r13))
  stopifnot(r13 > .4, r13 < .7)                                                # chosen after measuring (scratch: .51-.52)
}
pst_bound <- function(cc, p, N) {                                              # P(P1 < 1e-8) at delta = 0, first order, p = grid
  pop0 <- grd_pop(cc, 0, p); z0 <- grd_DW(pop0); w0 <- z0$w; B <- pst_V(pop0, w0); q <- B$q
  Hp <- pst_pinv(crossprod(z0$D * sqrt(w0))); Ap <- Hp %*% (t(z0$D * w0) %*% z0$Om %*% (z0$D * w0)) %*% Hp
  Tm <- cbind(t(B$Q), -cc * t(B$Q), matrix(0, p - 1L, p + 2L))              # eps_perp coordinates = Q'(dtau - c dlam)
  Cu <- Tm %*% Ap %*% t(Tm) / N; k <- p - 1L; r <- 1e-8 * B$s[1]
  vol <- pi^(k / 2) / gamma(k / 2 + 1) * r^k / sqrt(det(crossprod(B$V)))        # {u : u'V'Vu <= r^2}
  vol / ((2 * pi)^(k / 2) * sqrt(det(Cu))) }
for (p in c(4L, 6L)) for (cc in c(0, .4)) for (N in c(1000, 4000)) {
  b <- pst_bound(cc, p, N); cat(sprintf("p %d c %.1f N %d: P(P1 < 1e-8 | delta = 0) ~ %.1e\n", p, cc, N, b))
  stopifnot(b < 1e-12)                                                          # chosen after measuring (scratch: <= 2.1e-16)
}
# (d) balanced items: all sample thresholds exactly 0 in both groups. tau = 0, kappa = 0 gives zero threshold
# residual for ANY (lambda, omega, phi); the correlations do not involve tau or kappa. So theta-hat has tau-hat = 0
# (r = 0 for every item: I5's set, c = 0 = kappa) exactly, whatever the sampling error in the correlations.
for (p in c(4L, 6L)) {
  m <- inv_model(rep(2L, p), "intercepts"); x <- inv_point(m, as.list(numeric(p)), grd_lam(p))
  x[pst_ix(p)$kap] <- 0; nT <- p + p * (p - 1) / 2
  sg <- m$sigma(x); stopifnot(all(sg[c(1:p, nT + 1:p)] == 0))                   # both groups' threshold statistics are 0
  s <- svd(inv_jac(m$sigma, x), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d; cat(sprintf("p %d balanced: sigma_min/sigma_max (unweighted) %.2e\n", p, s[length(s)] / s[1]))
  stopifnot(s[length(s)] / s[1] < 1e-8)                                         # Module 10's row 3 fires
}
```

```{r pst-se}
# Result P4: the reported sandwich at theta-hat is, EXACTLY, A = sum_ij v_i v_j' C_ij / (sigma_i sigma_j),
# C = U' W^{1/2} Omega W^{1/2} U (SVD M = U S V'). The weakest term is v v' C_mm / sigma_min^2.
pst_se <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(pst_cells)), function(i) {
  d <- pst_cells$delta[i]; cc <- pst_cells$c[i]; p <- pst_cells$p[i]
  pop <- grd_pop(cc, d, p); za <- grd_A(pop); sq <- sqrt(za$w); M <- sq * za$D; sv <- svd(M); q <- ncol(M)
  C <- crossprod(sv$u, (za$Om * outer(sq, sq)) %*% sv$u); A2 <- sv$v %*% (C / outer(sv$d, sv$d)) %*% t(sv$v)
  lead <- tcrossprod(sv$v[, q]) * C[q, q] / sv$d[q]^2; ix <- pst_ix(p)
  stopifnot(max(abs(za$A - A2)) / max(abs(za$A)) < 1e-8)                        # chosen after measuring (numpy scratch: 1e-12)
  data.frame(delta = d, c = cc, p = p, lead_share_phi = lead[ix$phi, ix$phi] / za$A[ix$phi, ix$phi],
             lead_share_kap = lead[ix$kap, ix$kap] / za$A[ix$kap, ix$kap],
             vphi = abs(sv$v[ix$phi, q]), vkap_over_vphi = abs(sv$v[ix$kap, q] / sv$v[ix$phi, q]), gap = abs(cc - .3) / (2 * 1.44), Cmm = C[q, q]) }))
print(pst_se, digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(pst_se$lead_share_phi > .9),                                      # SE(phi2-hat) is the weak direction at every grid cell
          all(pst_se$lead_share_kap[pst_se$c == .4 & pst_se$delta == .4] < .1)) # SE(kappa2-hat) is not, at c - kappa2 = .1, delta = .4
stopifnot(all(abs(pst_se$vkap_over_vphi / pst_se$gap - 1)[pst_se$delta == .05] < .08))  # G3's ratio |c - kappa2| / (2 phi2) at delta = .05
# (all three bounds chosen after measuring: phi share .91-1.00; kappa share .02 at c = .4, delta = .4; ratio within 4%)
```


#### Confirmatory result

The frozen rule (E-037, run 2026-10-09) gives the
feasible interval **[0.14799, 0.19471]** for "warn iff $S_{1w,1}\le$ cut", bound by the harmful cell
$c=0.4$, $\delta=0.05$, $N=500$, $p=4$ below and the safe cell $c=0.4$, $\delta=0.4$, $N=500$, $p=4$ above.
No cutoff is chosen here: the choice is deferred until the guard is built, and any value picked will be
labelled *chosen after measuring*.

#### Open, not decided here

1. The post-fit statistics' role (P1 the Δ ratio, P1e equilibrated, P2 overlap with I5's null vector, P3 (decided 2026-10-09 after Results P1–P4: reported as post-fit conditioning diagnostics, no cutoff, no warning; spec Module 12)
   profile conditioning of the $(\phi_g,\kappa_g)$ block). G3 gives P1 $=O(\delta)$ at the population point;
   its sampling behaviour is not derived.
2. Its relation to Module 10's rank criterion, $\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}(W_D^{1/2}\Delta)<10^{-8}$ at $\hat\theta$: a
   numerical-rank test, while near the set the ratio is $O(\hat S_{1w})$, far above $10^{-8}$.
3. The non-configural $\hat h$ follow-up (reserved by the preregistration).
4. Whether a harm criterion should involve $\hat\phi_g$ as well as $\hat\kappa_2$ (G3's corollary). Not
   applicable to the frozen run.
5. Whether Module 3's second point should perturb thresholds, ν, ω or α under groups (O7). G4(ii) shows
   only that nothing short of moving thresholds leaves the $t=0$ case.

### Multiple groups: the pooled objective, $T$, ACOV and DIFFTEST {#sec-multigroup-scaling}

*Added 2026-10-09.* Drafted in a Cloud session from `39de00b`; corrected and executed by the main
session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2, Mplus 8.10) in two stages: Stage 1 (`mg-setup`, `mg-synth`,
`mg-premise`, no lavaan fits), then Stage 2 (the lavaan chunks) against hypotheses and criteria
**frozen before any lavaan fit** (*Verification*, below). The draft's claims about lavaan and Mplus,
originally marked as recalled, are now replaced by what the chunks and the Mplus pair measured.
The chunks use `inv_*` helpers from `@sec-invariance-id` only in `mg-we`; every new name starts
with `mg_`. **The finite-sample choices ($T$, `e(V)`) are not made here**: they wait for a review of
their implications for DIFFTEST check 10 (user, 2026-10-09).

This section derives how $G$ independent groups combine: the pooled objective, $T$, $T_3$,
ACOV, `e(V)` and DIFFTEST, which spec Module 12 and E-003 (2026-10-08) left open
before this section landed ("the pooled multiple-group scaling ($F$, $\Gamma$, $T$; $N-1$ against $N-G$) is open and needs its
own derivation"). **It does not choose among finite-sample conventions.** Where the derivation
leaves a real choice it lists the candidates with their consequences (*Decisions this section
leaves*, at the end).

#### Setting and assumptions

Stage 1 runs on each group's own $(Y_g, K)$ and returns $s_g\in\mathbb R^{D_g}$, $\hat\Gamma_g =
N_g^{-1}\sum_i\hat\psi_i\hat\psi_i'$ (empirical, no $N_g/(N_g-1)$ factor) and $N_g$. Write
$N=\sum_gN_g$, $\pi_g=N_g/N$, $W_g=\operatorname{diag}(\Gamma_g)^{-1}$ (spec §4.9's $W_D$ for
group $g$), $r_g=s_g-\sigma_g(\theta)$, $D_\bullet=\sum_gD_g$. The parameter vector $\theta$ is shared:
$\Delta_g=\partial\sigma_g/\partial\theta$ is taken with respect to the **pooled** $\theta$, with tied
parameters sharing a column (decision (12), `fidx` may repeat), so a parameter of another group
contributes a zero column. $q$ is the number of free (post-tie) parameters, the rank of
$\Delta=(\Delta_1',\dots,\Delta_G')'$.

Two assumptions, both used and neither checkable from the data:

1. **The groups are independent samples.** Then the cross-group blocks of the covariance of
   $s$ are exactly zero. If the "groups" are dependent (the same persons at two occasions, twins,
   clustered strata), every block-diagonal statement below fails, and the cross-block of $\Gamma$ has
   to come from a joint Stage 1. *This bears on the "generic dimension (groups now, occasions
   later)" constraint of 2026-10-08: occasions are not independent samples, so the machinery below
