```{r mg-t3-g1}
  fT <- function(Dl_ = Dl, Om = Gm1, th_ = th) t3_at(sig1, th_, Dl_, Om, s = s1, nT = nT1)[["T3"]]
  mk <- matrix(FALSE, 21, 16); mk[12:21, 12:16] <- TRUE
  S1 <- matrix(runif(length(Dl), -1, 1), 21) * abs(Dl) * mk; h <- 1e-6
  So <- t3_sym(21) * abs(Gm1); hO <- 1e-7
  p4 <- t3_rel(sum(g$GD * S1), (fT(Dl_ = Dl + h * S1) - fT(Dl_ = Dl - h * S1)) / (2 * h))
  p5 <- t3_rel(sum(g$GO * So), (fT(Om = Gm1 + hO * So) - fT(Om = Gm1 - hO * So)) / (2 * hO))
  # synthetic end to end, as P15, with the G = 1 objects
  p1 <- sv_parts(sig1, s1, w1, th); b0 <- sv_gn(sig1, s1, w1, x0); K <- b0$K; stK <- b0$xs[[K + 1L]] - b0$xs[[K]]
  hj <- 1e-5 * pmax(1, abs(th)); Eb <- (2 * t3_u * outer(abs(sig1(th)), rep(1, 16)) +
    t3_u * abs(Dl) * rep(abs(th) + hj, each = 21)) / rep(hj, each = 21) * mk
  Th <- t3_Theta(p1, w1, Eb, eps = 4 * t3_u, K = K, stK = stK)
  dD <- t3_dD(sig1, th); gtha <- t3_gth_abs(g, dD, g$gh, Eb, Dl, eps_max = 4 * t3_u)
  dOe <- 4 * t3_u * abs(Gm1)
  bb <- c(b1 = sum(abs(g$GD) * Eb), b2 = sum(gtha * Th) + g$a * nT1 * drop(crossprod(Th, abs(p1$J) %*% Th)),
          b3 = sum(abs(g$GO) * dOe))
  be <- t3_beval(Dl, Gm1, g$r, nT1, t3_eta_stata)
  bel <- t3_belem(g, Dl, sig1, th)
  B <- ((1 + t3_rho) * (2 * bb[["b1"]] + bb[["b2"]] + bb[["b3"]]) + be + bel) / (1 + abs(v[["T3"]])) + t3_rT(v[["T3"]])
  syn <- replicate(200, { tha <- th + runif(16, -1, 1) * Th
    Ta <- fT(Dl_ = sv_jac(sig1, tha) + matrix(runif(length(Dl), -1, 1), 21) * Eb, Om = Gm1 + t3_sym(21) * dOe, th_ = tha)
    Tb <- fT(Dl_ = Dl + matrix(runif(length(Dl), -1, 1), 21) * Eb); abs(Ta - Tb) / (1 + abs(Tb)) })
  be4 <- t3_beval(Dl, Gm1, g$r, nT1, t3_eta_q4); B4 <- B + (be4 - be) / (1 + abs(v[["T3"]]))      # SE6
  c(pi_is_1 = pl$pg == 1, Omega_identical = identical(pl$Om, Gm1), w_identical = identical(pl$w, w1),
    T3 = v[["T3"]], lavT3 = lavT3, rel_lav = abs(v[["T3"]] / lavT3 - 1), P4 = p4, P5 = p5,
    B = B, syn_max_over_B = max(syn) / B, route1x2 = 2 * bb[["b1"]] / (1 + abs(v[["T3"]])), eval = be / (1 + abs(v[["T3"]])),
    elem = bel / (1 + abs(v[["T3"]])), eval_ratio_q4 = be4 / be, B_q4 = B4, syn_max_over_B_q4 = max(syn) / B4,
    D = nrow(Dl))
})
print(signif(t3_g1, 4))
stopifnot(t3_g1[["pi_is_1"]] == 1, t3_g1[["Omega_identical"]] == 1, t3_g1[["w_identical"]] == 1,
          t3_g1[["rel_lav"]] <= 1e-6, t3_g1[["syn_max_over_B"]] <= 1)
# P4, P5 (central differences) are reported, not asserted: rounding floors that move across machines
# (8.2e-7, 2.2e-7 on 2026-10-15; 3.4e-6, 2.5e-7 on 2026-10-19; the user's option (a), 2026-10-19).
```

**Open, for the preregistration** (a list, not a draft; none is chosen here):
- **What is measured, at each count.** Each group's full $\Gamma_g$ and $N_g$, so $d\Omega$ including its
  off-diagonals; $s$; $\hat\theta$; and $T_3$, both as `e(T3)` and at full precision (`%21x`). S5's
  model-evaluation error is measured as on the grid.
- **The computing routine.** $B_{T3}$ needs a build step first: an extension of `dwlsmv_sens`, tested
  against this subsection's R, as `test_sens.do` was for S1–S5. That includes the step for
  $\partial\Delta/\partial\theta$ taken from $\Delta_c$.
- **Units and pairs.** Check 6's measure, one scalar per fit and per count pair; which pairs, and which
  axes.
- **$\rho_T$.** The neglected terms measured here are at most $3.2\times10^{-6}$ of a gradient; the grid
  used 0.01.
- **$\Theta$ for route 2.** Either the a-priori S1–S5 envelope (as here), or the measured
  $|\hat\theta_a-\hat\theta_b|$, which is computable and sharper but conditions on `e(b)`'s outcome.
- **Displaced pairs** (different $K$ or line search). Exclude them, as the grid did, or bound them
  through S4(b).
- **TS6's assumptions.** Accept $c_{\rm ch}$ and the `quadcross()` model as assumed, or add a
  Stage-1-fixed arm on which $T_3$'s count invariance is measured. Note that the different-input
  roundings ($\beta_{\rm elem}$, and $\beta_{\rm eval}$ at different inputs) cannot be zeroed by such an
  arm.
- **$|T_3|<10^{-2}$.** The posting term is not derived there: exclude such fits, or derive the term.
- **Failure floors** (`docs/prereg-template.md` §4): per side, at zero events, before freezing.
- **The confirmatory fits.** Fresh data; E, B and D are consistency-only; the levels; $d>0$.

##### Result TG: $T_g$'s change near $\bar g\approx0$, a first-order bound with a zeroth-order floor {#sec-mg-t3-tg}

*Drafted 2026-10-29 for E-041 (a draft, not frozen). The text has no chunk of its
own; its implementation and synthetic check are in @sec-mg-t3-tg-verify, where TG-D ran (see there).*

**Why.** On the exact path the cross-count change left in $\beta_2$ is almost all
$T_g=2an_T\sum_l\bar g_l\Theta_l$ (Addendum 1 of E-031, X6:
$s_g=0.90$ at the swap, 0.49 to 1.00 on the $\hat d$ points). At the stop $\hat g_c\approx0$, so $T_g$'s
*relative* change is large. This result asks whether its *absolute* change is bounded, and by what.

Write $m=\sum_l\bar g_l\Theta_l$, so $T_g=2an_Tm$, with TS4's
$\bar g=|\hat g_c|+\bar E'W|r|+\varepsilon_{\max}|\Delta_c|'W|r|$, $\hat g_c=\Delta_c'Wr$. Hold $\Theta$, $a$
and $n_T$ (their changes are $s_\Theta$ and the residual, not $s_g$). Between two evaluations $(\theta,\Delta_c,w)$
and $(\theta'=\theta+\delta,\Delta_c',w'=w\circ(1+\epsilon))$, with $r'=r(\theta')$:

**TG1 (the kinks add nothing to the bound).** Each piece of $\bar g$ is $|x|$ of something, and
$\big||x'|-|x|\big|\le|x'-x|$ elementwise. So
$|\delta m|\le\sum_l\Theta_l\big(|\delta\hat g_c|_l+|\delta(\bar E'W|r|)|_l+\varepsilon_{\max}|\delta(|\Delta_c|'W|r|)|_l\big)$
holds across a sign change of $\hat g_{c,l}$ or of any $r_k$. The kinks make $m$ non-differentiable in
$\delta$, so a *signed* linear attribution (such as $s_g$) can change sign between nearby points; they
cannot make $|\delta m|$ exceed the bound.

**TG2 (the pieces of $\delta\hat g_c$).** With $\Delta_c=\Delta+E$, $|E|\le\bar E$ (S5), and $J$ TS4's
$\tfrac12\partial^2F$ (so $\partial(\Delta'Wr)/\partial\theta=-J$):
$$
\delta\hat g_c=\underbrace{-J\delta}_{\text{smooth}}+\underbrace{(E'-E)'Wr'}_{\Delta_c\text{ redraw}}
+E'W(r'-r)+\Delta_c'(\epsilon\circ w\circ r')+O(\|\delta\|^2),
$$
$$
|\delta\hat g_c|\le|J\delta|+(\bar E+\bar E')'W|r'|+\bar E'W|\Delta||\delta|+\|\epsilon\|_\infty|\Delta_c|'W|r'|+O(\|\delta\|^2).
$$

**Consequences.**
- **Two orders.** $|J\delta|$ is first order in $\delta$. The redraw term $(\bar E+\bar E')'W|r'|$ is
  *zeroth* order: it is present at any $\delta\ne0$ (production's $\Delta_c$ is redrawn at a new $\theta$),
  and absent at $\delta=0$ (where $\Delta_c$ is bitwise the same). That is the genuinely non-smooth part,
  and it comes from $\Delta_c$'s central-difference rounding, not from $|\cdot|$.
- **The floor is small relative to $T_g$ itself.** $\bar g\ge\bar E'W|r|$, so the redraw term moves $m$
  by at most about $2\sum_l\Theta_l(\bar E'W|r|)_l\le2m$: it cannot exceed twice $T_g$. A large relative
  change of $T_g$ beyond that must come from $|J\delta|$ or $\epsilon$.
- **Why the relative figure is large.** $|\delta m|/m\lesssim(|J||\delta|+2\bar E'W|r|)/\bar g$, with
  $\bar g$ near its envelope floor. The ratio is large because the denominator is near zero; the
  numerator is bounded by smooth, computable quantities. When $\varepsilon_{\max}$ is large (the test's
  `metric_bigeps`, $10^{-6}$), $\bar g$ is not near zero and the ratio is small.
- **$\delta=0$, $\epsilon=0$:** $\delta m=0$ up to $m$'s own assembly rounding.

**Bound used by the study** (first order, direction-free, from $\|\delta\|_\infty$):
$B_g(\delta_\infty,\epsilon_\infty)=2an_T\sum_l\Theta_l\big[(|J|\mathbf 1)_l\delta_\infty+\mathbb 1[\delta_\infty>0]\,(\bar E+\bar E^{\uparrow})'W|r|^{\uparrow}
+(\bar E'W|\Delta|\mathbf 1)_l\delta_\infty+\epsilon_\infty(|\Delta_c|'W|r|^{\uparrow})_l+\varepsilon_{\max}(|\Delta_c|'W|\Delta|\mathbf1+|\partial\Delta|'W|r|)_l\delta_\infty+(|\partial\bar E|'W|r|)_l\delta_\infty\big]$,
where $^{\uparrow}$ is the quantity's elementwise upper value over $\|\theta'-\theta\|_\infty\le\delta_\infty$
(first order), $|\partial\Delta|$ the sum over $j$ of $|\partial\Delta/\partial\theta_j|$ and $|\partial\bar E|$
likewise. The $O(\delta^2)$ remainder is not bounded; at $\delta_\infty\le10^{-10}$ it is about
$10^{-10}$ of the first-order part (not shown here, a statement only).

The bound is implemented and checked in production coordinates in @sec-mg-t3-tg-verify, after Result
MS6, because it needs that section's production-form functions (`mg2_sigma`, `mg2_delta`, `mg2h_deltac`,
`mg2h_hess`, `mg2h_RJ`).


#### Check 6's a-axis inputs from one Stage 1: the envelopes $\bar E_s$, $\bar E_\varepsilon$, $\bar E_\Omega$ {#sec-mg-sensitivity-stage1}

*Executed 2026-10-19 in a full render of this file, green, all chunks (R 4.5.2, lavaan 0.7.2, Windows
ARM, the milestone laptop).*

*Added 2026-10-19 by the main session, from the approved plan E-042
(2026-10-17). It resumes after that plan's §7 stop, under the user's decisions of 2026-10-18
(E-043). The predictions are E-042's: §3 (H1–H9) was
committed at f62f495, and Addendum 2 at 00a3b79. Both were committed before any chunk below ran. The key
check on the measured pairs is reported from its one recorded run (E-042),
not re-executed here.*

**Why.** Check 6 refits every stored model over one Stage 1 computed now. The stored fit's own Stage 1 is
gone. S1–S5 (θ side) and TS1–TS7 (T3 side) take $ds$, $\varepsilon$ and $d\Omega$ **measured** between
two Stage 1 runs, and a DIFFTEST never has two. This subsection replaces those three measured inputs by
envelopes computable from **one** Stage 1, for two runs on identical data at any two processor counts.

**Labelled assumptions and disclosed choices.** Every result below is conditional on these, and none of
them is established here.
- **A1.** Mata `sum()` over at most $K_1\times K_2$ elements uses the same order at every processor
  count.
- **A2.** Mata's small matrix products (`psi_a * I_ra`, $K\times C$ times $C\times1$) are count-invariant.
- **A3.** The elementwise builtins (`invnormal`, `normal`, `normalden`, `binormal`, `exp`, `sqrt`, IEEE
  `/`) have no count-dependent code path.
- **The `quadcross()` model is Q4.** It was **chosen after Q1 failed on the measured pairs** (the key
  check, K2). That choice is post hoc, and it was the user's (2026-10-18). Q1–Q3 are kept as derived, so
  that the choice stays visible.

A1–A3 concern undocumented behaviour of Stata builtins. They stay labelled assumptions until they have
the evidence the user requires. Under branch (b) they would become load-bearing in production.

##### Result SE1: Ψ and $s$ are count-invariant under A1–A3, so $\bar E_s=0$

The reconciliation (predictions §1, R1–R15) read every routine that feeds Ψ and $s$ on the $G>1$ path.
Every operation is one of four kinds:
- exact integer arithmetic or a copy;
- a floating-point reduction or product over at most $K_1\times K_2$ cells (R7, R9, R10);
- an elementwise builtin;
- `quadcross(Psi, Psi)` (R12), the only reduction over the $N$ observations.

Ψ is a gather of per-cell table values (R11), so no floating-point arithmetic touches an $N$-length array
before `quadcross()`. Under A1–A3, $s$ and Ψ are therefore bitwise count-invariant: **$\bar E_s=0$**, and
$\Gamma_g$ can differ between counts only through R12.

This is a proof by inspection of the code in `src/`. Its premises about builtins are A1–A3. That $s$ was
bitwise identical on all 864 measured pairs (K1) is prior information, not part of the proof.

##### Result SE2: the `quadcross()` models

For one output entry, $Q=\sum_it_i$ with $t_i=\mathrm{fl}(\psi_{ij}\psi_{ik})$. The terms are the same in
both runs, so only the accumulation differs. Write $T=\sum_i|t_i|$, $N=N_g$, $u=2^{-53}$,
$\gamma_n=nu/(1-nu)$, and $\gamma^q_n$ the same with $u_q=2^{-104}$ (S3). Each model bounds the
difference between two runs, $|Q_a-Q_b|\le c_M\,T$, and the per-run relative error $\delta_M$ on a sum
of positive terms:

| Model | Accumulation | $c_M$ | $\delta_M$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 (S3(2), TS6) | double-double, one rounding | $2(u+(1+u)\gamma^q_N)$ | $u+\gamma^q_N$ |
| Q2 | $\le p$ partials, each as Q1 and rounded, combined as Q1 | $2(2u+2\gamma^q_N)(1+u)$ | $2u+2\gamma^q_N$ |
| Q3 | as Q2, partials summed in plain double, $p\le6$ | $2(u+\gamma_5(1+u)+\gamma^q_N)(1+u)$ | $u+\gamma_5(1+u)+\gamma^q_N$ |
| **Q4** | any summation at least as accurate as recursive double summation in some order | $2\gamma_{N-1}$ | $\gamma_{N-1}$ |

Q4 follows from Higham's bound for recursive summation, $|\hat Q-Q|\le\gamma_{N-1}T$, applied to each
run. It assumes no thread layout and no processor bound.

Its one premise is about StataCorp's undocumented code: that `quadcross()` is no less accurate than some
recursive double summation. That it is documented to accumulate in quad precision would imply this
premise, but its threading is not documented.

Q1's mechanism, agreement to about $10^{-30}$ before one rounding, makes a diagonal move all but
impossible. The measured pairs show diagonal moves of up to 3 ulps (result.md), so **Q1 is refuted as a
model of these data**, and TS6's $\beta_{\rm eval}$ still rests on it (open item below).

##### Result SE3: the envelopes, from one Stage 1

$T$ is not stored. By Cauchy–Schwarz, $T_{jk}\le(1+u)\,N\sqrt{\Gamma^*_{jj}\Gamma^*_{kk}}$, where
$\Gamma^*$ is the exact $\sum t/N$. A diagonal sum has positive terms, so a computed $\Gamma_{kk}$ errs
relatively by at most $\delta_M+u(1+\delta_M)$, which includes R13's division. Hence
$\Gamma^*_{kk}\le\Gamma_{kk}/(1-\delta_M-2u)$.

With $\pi_g=N_g/N$ formed once and shared by both runs (R14), elementwise and with every off-diagonal
entry included:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bar E_{\Gamma,jk}&=(1+u)\,c_M\,\frac{(1+u)\sqrt{\Gamma_{jj}\Gamma_{kk}}}{1-\delta_M-2u}+2u(1+2u)\,|\Gamma_{jk}|,\\
\bar E_{\Omega}&=\operatorname{blockdiag}_g\Big(\big[(1+u)\,\bar E_{\Gamma_g}+2u(1+u)\,|\Gamma_g|\big]/\pi_g\Big),\\
\bar E_{\varepsilon,k}&=(1+2u)\,\bar E_{\Gamma,kk}/\Gamma_{kk},\qquad \bar E_s=0\ \text{(SE1)} .
\end{aligned}
$$

- **$\bar E_\Gamma$.** The second term is R13's rounding in both runs.
- **$\bar E_\Omega$.** The extra term is R14's division in both runs.
- **$\bar E_\varepsilon$.** $\varepsilon=-(\gamma_{\rm oth}-\gamma_{\rm own})/\gamma_{\rm own}$, and the
  subtraction is exact by Sterbenz.

Every quantity on the right-hand side is the one Stage 1's $\Gamma_g$ and $N_g$.

##### Result SE4: substitution, in absolute form

The bounds take their Stage 1 inputs through these terms:
- **θ side (S1).** $S^{(A)}=|A(ds+r\circ\varepsilon)|$.
- **T3 side (TS4, TS5).** $\Theta$'s $S^{(A)}$; $\bar g$'s $\|\varepsilon\|_\infty$; and
  $\beta_3=\langle|G_\Omega|,|d\Omega|\rangle+|g_s|'|ds|$.

**A signed input cannot be replaced by its envelope inside an absolute value.** $|A(r\circ\varepsilon)|$
at $\varepsilon=+\bar E_\varepsilon$ is not a bound over $|\varepsilon|\le\bar E_\varepsilon$ (H8). The
substituted forms are therefore

$$
S^{(A)}\le|A|\,(\bar E_s+|r|\circ\bar E_\varepsilon),\qquad
\|\varepsilon\|_\infty\le\max_k\bar E_{\varepsilon,k},\qquad
\beta_3\le\langle|G_\Omega|,\bar E_\Omega\rangle+|g_s|'\bar E_s .
$$

**Monotonicity.** Each substituted term is a nonnegative matrix times a nonnegative envelope. $\Theta$
enters $\beta_2$ through $\sum_l(\cdot)_l\Theta_l+a\,n_T\Theta'|J|\Theta$, with nonnegative
coefficients, and $\bar g$ is increasing in $\|\varepsilon\|_\infty$. So the a-priori θ envelope and
$B_{T3}$ are nondecreasing in every envelope entry. Each dominates its measured-input form whenever the
measured inputs lie within $\bar E$ (H7).

Nothing else in S1–S5 or TS1–TS7 changes: $\rho$, $\rho_T$, S5's $\bar E$ for Δ, $c_{\rm ch}$ and TS6's
model enter as before. **This is a statement about the substitution, not a certification of check 6.** On
the T3 side, no claim is made for any tested fit until a `dwlsmv_sens_t3` run with $\bar E$ inputs
exists (decision 4, 2026-10-18).

##### Result SE5: what is lost

The a-priori bound is never below the measured-input bound (SE4). By how much it exceeds that bound, on
the records:
- **θ side, tested fits (key check, K7; not re-executed here).** Per unit, the a-priori maximum over the
  measured-input maximum is in $[1+1.2\times10^{-7},\,1+3.7\times10^{-6}]$ under Q1. Under Q4 it is in
  $[1+2.0\times10^{-4},\,1+5.9\times10^{-3}]$.
- **Against $10^{-10}$ (descriptive; no rule is set here).** Three of 72 units exceed $10^{-10}$ on the
  θ side, with or without substitution:
  - T3 study D20261621 metric, $1.049\times10^{-10}$;
  - grid D20261121 metric, $1.327\times10^{-10}$;
  - grid D20261121 scalar, $1.018\times10^{-10}$.
- **On design E (H9 below; R's model of production, not Stata's).** The B_T3 and Θ ratios are as the
  chunks report.

**The key check, as recorded** (result.md; R on the stored `st1.mmat` records, which are not on every
machine):
- All 864 ordered (own, other) pairs of both studies.
- **Q4:** held on every entry. Maximum ratio 0.0015 (Γ), 0.0017 (Ω), 0.0015 (ε).
- **Q1:** exceeded on one Γ diagonal entry (3 ulps, ratio 1.0095).
- **The controls:** C0 (no movement) was violated on 864 of 864 pairs. C1 ($2u|\Gamma_{jk}|$) was
  violated on 864 of 864, so the prediction that the data could not tell C1 from Q1 failed.
- **Holding on these pairs does not validate Q4 in general.**

#### Verification of SE1–SE5 on design E (R 4.5.2, lavaan 0.7.2; full render green 2026-10-19)

The predictions and thresholds were committed before any of these chunks ran: H1–H9 in
E-042 §3, and Addendum 2's choices and V0. Failed predictions are
kept, and the chunks' assertions pin the recorded outcomes.

**What the emulations are.** Design E's own Ψ is lavaan's Stage 1 influence matrix (Addendum 2). The
terms $t_i=\mathrm{fl}(\psi_{ij}\psi_{ik})$ are summed in 20 runs per model:
- Q1: double-double accumulation in 20 row orders;
- Q2 and Q3: $p\in\{1,2,4,6\}$ contiguous chunks × 5 orders;
- Q4: plain recursive double summation in 20 orders.

These are R models of the four accumulation models, not of `quadcross()`. **Holding here does not show
that `quadcross()` meets any of them.**

**Corrections before the first complete run** (none changed a threshold or an outcome):
1. V0 failed on its first evaluation, at a relative error of 1.0. lavaan's A matrix is a sum over rows,
   not a mean, so Ψ lacked a factor $N_g$. Addendum 2 fixes Ψ's scale as the one that reproduces lavaan's
   $\Gamma_g$, and V0 then held. Nothing after V0 had run.
2. `cut()` rejects one interval, at $p=1$. It was replaced by an explicit contiguous split, and the
   chunks stopped before any H output.
3. H6's Ω column printed NaN: 0/0 on the block-diagonal's structural zeros, where both $d\Omega$ and
   $\bar E_\Omega$ are 0. The check now requires $d\Omega=0$ exactly where $\bar E_\Omega=0$. H1–H5 and
   H6's Γ and ε columns had printed. They were deterministic, and identical on the rerun.

| Item | Claim | Threshold (before running) | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| V0 | crossprod(Ψ_g)/N_g is lavaan's Γ_g | $\le10^{-10}\sqrt{\Gamma_{jj}\Gamma_{kk}}$ | held (after correction 1): $2.0\times10^{-14}$, $3.5\times10^{-14}$ |
| H1 | Cauchy–Schwarz on design E's own T | every entry $\le1$ | held: max $1-1.8\times10^{-16}$ (attained on the diagonal, as it must be) |
| H2 | Q1 emulation within Q1's bound; no diagonal move | $\le1$; 0 moves | held: 0; 0 (no entry moved at all) |
| H3 | Q2 emulation within Q2's bound; some diagonal move | $\le1$; $\ge1$ | held: 0.46; 19 diagonal entries moved (up to 1 ulp) |
| H4 | Q3 emulation within Q3's bound | $\le1$ | held: 0.26 |
| H5 | **Q4 (primary)** emulation within Q4's bound; some move above Q1's bound | $\le1$; $\ge1$ | held: 0.045; 93% of entries above Q1's bound, diagonal moves up to 46 ulps |
| H6 | every pair's dΓ, dΩ, ε within the own run's $\bar E$ | $\le1$ | held: Q1 0; Q2 0.44; Q3 0.25; **Q4 0.046** |
| H7 | a priori at $\bar E$ ≥ measured-input form at 100 signed draws; $2\bar E$ ≥ $\bar E$ | $\le1$ | held: draws at most 1.000 (Θ, attained where $S^{(A)}$ is negligible) and 0.9999 ($B_{T3}$) |
| H8 | the signed substitution falls below the absolute form somewhere | $\ge1$ element | held: 27 and 23 elements; ratio down to 0.004 |
| H9 | a priori over measured-input: $B_{T3}$; Θ per element | Q1 [1, 1.01], [1, 1.001]; Q4 [1, 1.1], [1, 1.01] | Q1 held ($B_{T3}$ 1.0001–1.0002; Θ ≤ 1.0001). Q4 $B_{T3}$ held (1.069, 1.083). **Q4 Θ FAILED on loadings: 1.055** (intercepts 1.003) |

**Reading H9's failure.** It is not a §7 trigger: no measured input exceeded an envelope, and a priori ≥
measured-input held on every element (SE4). The prediction carried over K7's per-unit **maximum** (Q4 at
most $1+5.9\times10^{-3}$) to **every element**. An element whose $S^{(C)}$ and S5 terms are small
relative to $|A|\,|r|\,\bar E_\varepsilon$ moves further. That was a prediction set too tight, recorded as a
failure because a frozen prediction is never re-read after the run.

**Two things the runs show beyond the predictions.**
- **Q2 and Q3's H9 pairs did not move.** Run 1 and run 2 are both $p=1$ under the layout, so they
  reduce to Q1 on these two runs. Their H9 rows measure the envelope against $d\Omega=0$.
- **Design E's sizes, against $10^{-10}$ (reported only).** The a-priori $B_{T3}$ under Q4 is
  $2.06\times10^{-11}$ (loadings) and $1.45\times10^{-11}$ (intercepts). The measured-input values at the
  same pair are $1.92\times10^{-11}$ and $1.33\times10^{-11}$, which agree with TS7's table. This is R's
  model of production on design E. **It is not a certification of the T3 side.**

```{r s1e-setup}
# Stage 1 envelope (Results SE1-SE5): the quadcross() models of SE2, the envelopes of SE3 from ONE Stage 1,
# and the emulations. The envelope functions are keycheck.R's (E-042), unchanged in
# substance; names start with se_.
se_u <- 2^-53; se_pmax <- 6
se_gq <- function(n) n * 2^-104 / (1 - n * 2^-104)            # double-double accumulation, u_q <= 2^-104
se_gd <- function(n) n * se_u / (1 - n * se_u)                 # Higham's gamma_n in double
se_par <- function(M, N) switch(M,                             # per-run relative error delta; cross-run c: |dQ| <= c T
  Q1 = c(delta = se_u + se_gq(N),                                c = 2 * (se_u + (1 + se_u) * se_gq(N))),
  Q2 = c(delta = 2 * se_u + 2 * se_gq(N),                        c = 2 * (2 * se_u + 2 * se_gq(N)) * (1 + se_u)),
  Q3 = c(delta = se_u + se_gd(se_pmax - 1) * (1 + se_u) + se_gq(N),
         c = 2 * (se_u + se_gd(se_pmax - 1) * (1 + se_u) + se_gq(N)) * (1 + se_u)),
  Q4 = c(delta = se_gd(N - 1),                                   c = 2 * se_gd(N - 1)))
se_M <- c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4")
se_envG <- function(Gm, N, M) {                                # SE3: Ebar_Gamma for one group, from its own Gamma
  mp <- se_par(M, N); dg <- diag(Gm)
  Tb <- (1 + se_u) * N * sqrt(outer(dg, dg)) / (1 - mp[["delta"]] - 2 * se_u)   # Cauchy-Schwarz bound on T
  (1 + se_u) * mp[["c"]] * Tb / N + 2 * se_u * (1 + 2 * se_u) * abs(Gm)
}
se_bdiag <- function(L) { d <- vapply(L, nrow, 0L); O <- matrix(0, sum(d), sum(d)); o <- 0
  for (g in seq_along(L)) { O[o + seq_len(d[g]), o + seq_len(d[g])] <- L[[g]]; o <- o + d[g] }; O }
se_Ntot <- function(Ng) { N <- 0; for (n in Ng) N <- N + n; N }   # dwlsmv_omega: a serial integer sum
se_omega <- function(Gam, Ng) se_bdiag(lapply(seq_along(Gam), function(g) Gam[[g]] / (Ng[g] / se_Ntot(Ng))))
se_envs <- function(Gam, Ng, M) {                              # SE3: Ebar_Gamma, Ebar_Omega, Ebar_eps
  N <- se_Ntot(Ng); EG <- lapply(seq_along(Gam), function(g) se_envG(Gam[[g]], Ng[g], M))
  list(G = EG,
       O = se_bdiag(lapply(seq_along(Gam), function(g)
             ((1 + se_u) * EG[[g]] + 2 * se_u * (1 + se_u) * abs(Gam[[g]])) / (Ng[g] / N))),
       e = unlist(lapply(seq_along(Gam), function(g) (1 + 2 * se_u) * diag(EG[[g]]) / diag(Gam[[g]]))))
}
se_eps <- function(Ga, Gb) {                                   # eps as grid_lib's sgl_dseps: -(g_oth - g_own) / g_own
  ga <- unlist(lapply(Ga, diag)); gb <- unlist(lapply(Gb, diag)); -(gb - ga) / ga }

# Design E's own Psi (addendum 2): lavaan's Stage 1 influence matrix, muthen1984's scores times the inverse
# of its A matrix, per group, with lavaan's own Stage 1 options. V0 checks crossprod(Psi_g) / N_g against
# lavaan's Gamma_g before anything is read from it.
se_psi <- function(fit, g) {
  ns <- asNamespace("lavaan"); ov <- fit@Data@ov; on <- fit@Data@ov.names[[g]]; op <- fit@Options
  m <- ns$muthen1984(data_1 = fit@Data@X[[g]], wt = NULL, ov_names = on,
                     ov_types = ov$type[match(on, ov$name)], ov_levels = ov$nlev[match(on, ov$name)],
                     group = g, wls_w = TRUE, zero_add = op$zero.add, zero_keep_margins = op$zero.keep.margins,
                     zero_cell_warn = FALSE, zero_cell_tables = TRUE, allow_empty_cell = op$allow.empty.cell)
  A12 <- if (is.null(m$A12)) matrix(0, nrow(m$A11), ncol(m$A22)) else m$A12
  nrow(m$SC) * unname(m$SC %*% t(solve(rbind(cbind(m$A11, A12), cbind(m$A21, m$A22)))))   # lavaan's A is a sum over rows
}
se_Psi <- lapply(seq_along(sv_E$Gam), function(g) se_psi(fE1$fit, g))
se_Ng  <- vapply(se_Psi, nrow, 0)
stopifnot(identical(se_Ng, as.numeric(sv_E$n_g)))
se_v0 <- sapply(seq_along(se_Psi), function(g) { Gm <- sv_E$Gam[[g]]
  max(abs(crossprod(se_Psi[[g]]) / se_Ng[g] - Gm) / sqrt(outer(diag(Gm), diag(Gm)))) })
cat(sprintf("V0: max |crossprod(Psi_g)/N_g - Gamma_g| / sqrt(Gamma_jj Gamma_kk), by group: %s\n",
            paste(signif(se_v0, 3), collapse = ", ")))
stopifnot(se_v0 <= 1e-10)                                      # V0 (addendum 2, set before running)

# The emulations (SE2's models), on the terms t_i = fl(psi_ij psi_ik), which every run shares.
# Double-double: Knuth's TwoSum, then FastTwoSum renormalization; elementwise over all D x D entries at once.
se_dd_add <- function(h, l, x) {                               # (h, l) + x, in double-double
  s <- h + x; bb <- s - h; e <- (h - (s - bb)) + (x - bb); e <- e + l
  hi <- s + e; list(h = hi, l = e - (hi - s))
}
se_dd_sum <- function(P, rows) {                               # sum over 'rows' of the term matrices, then one rounding
  D <- ncol(P); h <- l <- matrix(0, D, D)
  for (i in rows) { z <- se_dd_add(h, l, tcrossprod(P[i, ])); h <- z$h; l <- z$l }
  h + l
}
se_plain <- function(P, rows) {                                # recursive double summation (not sum(): long double)
  D <- ncol(P); a <- matrix(0, D, D); for (i in rows) a <- a + tcrossprod(P[i, ]); a }
se_chunks <- function(rows, p) split(rows, ceiling(seq_along(rows) * p / length(rows)))   # p contiguous chunks
se_run <- function(P, M, ord, p = 1L) switch(M,                # one emulated quadcross(Psi, Psi) under model M
  Q1 = se_dd_sum(P, ord),
  Q2 = { pr <- lapply(se_chunks(ord, p), function(r) se_dd_sum(P, r))     # partials rounded to double,
         h <- l <- 0 * pr[[1]]                                             # combined in double-double
         for (x in pr) { z <- se_dd_add(h, l, x); h <- z$h; l <- z$l }; h + l },
  Q3 = Reduce(`+`, lapply(se_chunks(ord, p), function(r) se_dd_sum(P, r))),   # partials in plain double
  Q4 = se_plain(P, ord))
se_Tabs <- function(P) {                                       # T = sum_i |t_i|, double-double (error ~1e-30 relative)
  D <- ncol(P); h <- l <- matrix(0, D, D)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(P))) { z <- se_dd_add(h, l, abs(tcrossprod(P[i, ]))); h <- z$h; l <- z$l }; h + l }
set.seed(20261019)
se_layout <- list(Q1 = data.frame(p = 1L, k = 1:20), Q2 = expand.grid(k = 1:5, p = c(1L, 2L, 4L, 6L)),
                  Q3 = expand.grid(k = 1:5, p = c(1L, 2L, 4L, 6L)), Q4 = data.frame(p = 1L, k = 1:20))
se_ord <- lapply(se_Ng, function(n) lapply(1:20, function(k) sample.int(n)))   # the 20 row orders per group
se_Q <- lapply(se_M, function(M) {                             # se_Q[[M]][[run]][[group]]: the quadcross() output
  L <- se_layout[[M]]
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(L)), function(j) lapply(seq_along(se_Psi), function(g)
    se_run(se_Psi[[g]], M, se_ord[[g]][[L$k[j]]], L$p[j])))
})
names(se_Q) <- se_M
se_T <- lapply(se_Psi, se_Tabs)
se_Gam <- lapply(se_Q, function(R) lapply(R, function(Qg) Map(`/`, Qg, se_Ng)))   # Gamma = Q / rows(Y)

```

```{r s1e-models}
# H1-H5 (predictions section 3, addendum 2). H1: Cauchy-Schwarz on design E's own T, with Gamma from the
# Q1 emulation. H2-H5: every pairwise |dQ| (the range over runs, entrywise) within the model's bound on the
# actual T; diagonal moves; power against Q1.
se_h1 <- sapply(seq_along(se_Psi), function(g) {
  Gm <- se_Gam$Q1[[1]][[g]]; dg <- diag(Gm)
  max(se_T[[g]] / ((1 + se_u) * se_Ng[g] * sqrt(outer(dg, dg)) / (1 - se_par("Q1", se_Ng[g])[["delta"]] - 2 * se_u))) })
se_rng <- function(R, g) { X <- simplify2array(lapply(R, `[[`, g)); apply(X, 1:2, max) - apply(X, 1:2, min) }
se_hm <- t(sapply(se_M, function(M) {
  r <- lapply(seq_along(se_Psi), function(g) { d <- se_rng(se_Q[[M]], g); T <- se_T[[g]]; N <- se_Ng[g]
    c(ratio = max(d / (se_par(M, N)[["c"]] * T)), over_Q1 = mean(d > se_par("Q1", N)[["c"]] * T),
      any_over_Q1 = any(d > se_par("Q1", N)[["c"]] * T), diag_moved = sum(diag(d) > 0), moved = sum(d > 0),
      max_ulps_diag = max(diag(d) / (2^(floor(log2(diag(se_Q[[M]][[1]][[g]]))) - 52)))) })
  c(ratio = max(sapply(r, `[[`, "ratio")), frac_over_Q1 = mean(sapply(r, `[[`, "over_Q1")),
    any_over_Q1 = as.numeric(any(sapply(r, `[[`, "any_over_Q1") == 1)), diag_moved = sum(sapply(r, `[[`, "diag_moved")),
    entries_moved = sum(sapply(r, `[[`, "moved")), max_ulps_diag = max(sapply(r, `[[`, "max_ulps_diag")))
}))
cat(sprintf("H1: max T_jk over its Cauchy-Schwarz bound, by group: %s
", paste(format(se_h1, digits = 17), collapse = ", ")))
print(signif(se_hm, 4))
stopifnot(se_h1 <= 1,                                                        # H1
          se_hm["Q1", "ratio"] <= 1, se_hm["Q1", "diag_moved"] == 0,         # H2
          se_hm["Q2", "ratio"] <= 1, se_hm["Q2", "diag_moved"] >= 1,         # H3
          se_hm["Q3", "ratio"] <= 1,                                         # H4
          se_hm["Q4", "ratio"] <= 1, se_hm["Q4", "any_over_Q1"] == 1)        # H5
```

```{r s1e-propagate}
# H6: for every model's emulated runs, Gamma = Q/N, Omega and eps formed as production forms them; every
# ordered pair (own a, other b) within the envelopes computed from the own run alone.
se_h6 <- t(sapply(se_M, function(M) {
  G <- se_Gam[[M]]; n <- length(G); worst <- c(Gamma = 0, Omega = 0, eps = 0)
  for (a in seq_len(n)) { E <- se_envs(G[[a]], se_Ng, M); Oa <- se_omega(G[[a]], se_Ng)
    for (b in seq_len(n)[-a]) {
      dG <- max(unlist(Map(function(x, y, e) max(abs(y - x) / e), G[[a]], G[[b]], E$G)))
      dd <- abs(se_omega(G[[b]], se_Ng) - Oa); stopifnot(all(dd[E$O == 0] == 0)); dO <- max(dd[E$O > 0] / E$O[E$O > 0])
      de <- max(abs(se_eps(G[[a]], G[[b]])) / E$e)
      worst <- pmax(worst, c(dG, dO, de)) } }
  worst }))
print(signif(se_h6, 3))
stopifnot(se_h6 <= 1)                                                        # H6
```

```{r s1e-substitute}
# SE4 on design E, at the T3 section's stored fit (t3_lev): the measured-input forms (t3_B's) and the
# a-priori forms (absolute: S^(A) -> |A|(Ebar_s + |r| o Ebar_eps), ||eps|| -> max Ebar_eps, beta_3 -> <|G_Omega|,
# Ebar_Omega>), with Ebar_s = 0 under A1-A3 (conditional). Everything that does not depend on the Stage 1
# inputs is computed once per level.
se_Bf <- function(o, eta = t3_eta_stata) {                                  # eta: SE6
  w <- t3_w0; g <- t3_grad(o$sig, o$th, o$D, t3_Om); mk <- t3_mask(o$nm); Eb <- t3_Ebar(o$sig, o$th, o$D, mk)
  pp <- sv_parts(o$sig, sv_s, w, o$th); dD <- t3_dD(o$sig, o$th)
  ghc <- drop(crossprod(o$D, w * (sv_s - o$sig(o$th))))
  be <- t3_beval(o$D, t3_Om, g$r, t3_nT, eta); bel <- t3_belem(g, o$D, o$sig, o$th); T3 <- g$v[["T3"]]
  Th0 <- t3_Theta(pp, w, Eb, eps = 0, K = o$K, stK = o$stK)                 # S^(A) = 0: the rest of Theta
  function(dOm, eps, apriori = FALSE) {
    Th <- if (apriori) Th0 + drop(abs(pp$A) %*% (abs(pp$r) * eps))           # |A|(|r| o Ebar_eps), Ebar_s = 0
          else Th0 + abs(drop(pp$A %*% (pp$r * eps)))                          # |A(ds + r o eps)|, ds = 0
    gtha <- t3_gth_abs(g, dD, ghc, Eb, o$D, eps_max = max(abs(eps)))
    bb <- t3_beta(g, Eb, gtha, Th, pp$J, dOm = abs(dOm))
    B <- ((1 + t3_rho) * (2 * bb[["b1"]] + bb[["b2"]] + bb[["b3"]]) + be + bel) / (1 + abs(T3)) + t3_rT(T3)
    list(B = B, Theta = Th, SA_signed = abs(drop(pp$A %*% (pp$r * eps))), SA_abs = drop(abs(pp$A) %*% (abs(pp$r) * eps)))
  }
}
se_fn <- lapply(t3_lev, se_Bf)
# The emulated pair of addendum 2: own = run 1, other = run 2 of each model; Ebar from run 1's Gamma.
se_pair <- lapply(setNames(nm = se_M), function(M) { G <- se_Gam[[M]]
  list(E = se_envs(G[[1]], se_Ng, M), dOm = se_omega(G[[2]], se_Ng) - se_omega(G[[1]], se_Ng), eps = se_eps(G[[1]], G[[2]])) })
stopifnot(max(abs(se_omega(se_Gam$Q4[[1]], se_Ng) - t3_Om) / sqrt(outer(diag(t3_Om), diag(t3_Om)))) <= 1e-10)  # follows from V0

# H7: monotonicity. A priori at Ebar >= the measured-input form at 100 signed draws within Ebar; 2 Ebar >= Ebar.
set.seed(20261020)
se_h7 <- sapply(names(se_fn), function(lev) { f <- se_fn[[lev]]
  sapply(se_M, function(M) { E <- se_pair[[M]]$E; n <- nrow(t3_Om)
    ap <- f(E$O, E$e, TRUE); ap2 <- f(2 * E$O, 2 * E$e, TRUE)
    dr <- replicate(100, { m <- f(t3_sym(n) * E$O, runif(length(E$e), -1, 1) * E$e)
      c(Th = max(m$Theta / ap$Theta), B = m$B / ap$B) })
    c(draw_Theta = max(dr["Th", ]), draw_B = max(dr["B", ]),
      Ebar_over_2Ebar_Theta = max(ap$Theta / ap2$Theta), Ebar_over_2Ebar_B = ap$B / ap2$B) }) }, simplify = "array")
print(signif(apply(se_h7, 1:2, max), 6))
stopifnot(se_h7 <= 1)                                                        # H7

# H8: the signed substitution is not a bound: eps = +Ebar_eps in |A(ds + r o eps)| falls below |A|(Ebar_s + |r| o Ebar_eps)
se_h8 <- sapply(names(se_fn), function(lev) { z <- se_fn[[lev]](0 * t3_Om, se_pair$Q4$E$e, TRUE)
  c(n_below = sum(z$SA_signed < z$SA_abs), min_ratio = min(z$SA_signed / z$SA_abs)) })
print(signif(se_h8, 3))
stopifnot(se_h8["n_below", ] >= 1)                                           # H8

# H9 (step 5 on design E): a priori over measured-input, for B_T3 and per element of Theta. Every model is
# reported; Q1's and Q4's ranges are the preregistered ones (Q4 primary, addendum 2).
se_h9 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(se_fn), function(lev) { f <- se_fn[[lev]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(se_M, function(M) { z <- se_pair[[M]]
    ap <- f(z$E$O, z$E$e, TRUE); ms <- f(z$dOm, z$eps); rt <- ap$Theta / ms$Theta
    data.frame(level = lev, model = M, B_meas = ms$B, B_apriori = ap$B, B_ratio = ap$B / ms$B,
               Theta_ratio_min = min(rt), Theta_ratio_max = max(rt),
               max_dOm = max(abs(z$dOm)), max_eps = max(abs(z$eps))) })) }))
print(format(se_h9, digits = 6), row.names = FALSE)
se_in <- function(x, lo, hi) all(x >= lo & x <= hi)
# H9 as run: Q1 held and Q4's B_T3 held; Q4's Theta per element FAILED on loadings (1.055 > 1.01), kept (see
# the text). The assertions pin the recorded outcome.
se_th <- function(M, lev) unlist(se_h9[se_h9$model == M & se_h9$level %in% lev, c("Theta_ratio_min", "Theta_ratio_max")])
stopifnot(se_in(se_h9$B_ratio[se_h9$model == "Q1"], 1, 1.01), se_in(se_th("Q1", c("loadings", "intercepts")), 1, 1.001),
          se_in(se_h9$B_ratio[se_h9$model == "Q4"], 1, 1.1), se_in(se_th("Q4", "intercepts"), 1, 1.01),
          min(se_th("Q4", "loadings")) >= 1, max(se_th("Q4", "loadings")) > 1.01,      # H9 as run: failed
          se_h9$B_ratio >= 1, se_h9$Theta_ratio_min >= 1)                              # a priori >= measured, every model
cat(sprintf("B_T3 a priori under Q4: %s (reported against 1e-10 only)\n",
            paste(sprintf("%s %.3g", se_h9$level[se_h9$model == "Q4"], se_h9$B_apriori[se_h9$model == "Q4"]), collapse = ", ")))
```

##### Result SE6: TS6's $\beta_{\rm eval}$ under Q4

*Added 2026-10-20 by the main session (milestone laptop, R 4.5.2, lavaan 0.7.2). Predictions Q4-1 to
Q4-10 are in E-044, committed (33b487d) before the chunk below first ran.*

TS6 bounds each `quadcross()` output's cross-run difference by $\eta_{Q1}(n,X)=2uX$, with
$X=\sum|\text{terms}|$. SE2 refutes Q1 on the measured pairs. Under Q4 (chosen after Q1 failed; post hoc,
the user's choice), the terms are the same in both runs, and each run's reduction of $n$ terms errs by at
most $\gamma_{n-1}X$. Hence

$$
\eta_{Q4}(n,X)=2\gamma_{n-1}X .
$$

- **Where it applies.** $n=D$ for $P$, $\Omega W\Delta$, `B`, `C`, $w'\operatorname{diag}\Omega$,
  $(\Omega\circ\Omega)w$ with its $w'$-product, and $r'Wr$. $n=q$ for $E^{-1}B$, $E^{-1}C$ and
  $(E^{-1}B)^2$. $n$ counts the block diagonal's structural zeros. Adding an exact 0 is exact, so this
  is conservative.
- **What does not change.** `cholinv()` ($c_{\rm ch}$, still assumed), `sum(diagonal())` ($2\gamma_q$),
  the scalar roundings, and $\beta_{\rm elem}$.
- **Consequence.** Since $u<\gamma_{n-1}\le(n-1)u(1+10^{-14})$ for $2\le n\le D$, the ratio satisfies
  $1<\beta^{Q4}_{\rm eval}/\beta^{Q1}_{\rm eval}\le D-1$. $B_{T3}$ is increasing in $\beta_{\rm eval}$, so every
  containment that held at Q1's $\beta_{\rm eval}$ holds at Q4's.
- **Scope.** This makes TS6 consistent with SE2's model. It does not show that `quadcross()` meets Q4's
  premise, and it changes no tolerance. `dwlsmv_sens_t3` in `src/` still computes the Q1 form, which is
  the user's to change.

**On design E** (R's model of production; $D=42$, $q=27$ metric and $23$ scalar; $G=1$ has $D=21$):

| | metric | scalar | $G=1$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\beta^{Q4}_{\rm eval}/\beta^{Q1}_{\rm eval}$ | 3.58 | 4.09 | 2.73 |
| $\beta^{Q4}_{\rm eval}/(1+\lvert T_3\rvert)$ | $1.11\times10^{-11}$ | $6.95\times10^{-12}$ | |
| $B_{T3}$, Q1 → Q4 (TS7's synthetic point) | $1.92\to2.72\times10^{-11}$ (1.42×) | $1.33\to1.86\times10^{-11}$ (1.39×) | $1.03\to1.26\times10^{-11}$ (1.22×) |
| a-priori $B_{T3}$ (SE4, Q4 envelopes) | $2.86\times10^{-11}$ | $1.97\times10^{-11}$ | |

Every figure is below $10^{-10}$, which is reported, not tested. **Why the growth is small:** every term
that changes has $n\ge q$, so it grows by at least $q-1$. A ratio of 3.58 (metric) or 4.09 (scalar)
therefore means that at least 90% or 85% of $\beta^{Q1}_{\rm eval}$ sits in the terms that do not change:
the assumed `cholinv()` constant, `sum(diagonal())` and the scalar roundings.

| Item | Claim | Threshold (before running) | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4-1, Q4-2 | growth of $\beta_{\rm eval}$, $G=2$; $G=1$ | $[10,41]$; $[5,20]$ | **failed:** 3.58, 4.09; 2.73 |
| Q4-3, Q4-4 | growth of $B_{T3}$, $G=2$; $G=1$ | $[2,8]$; $[1.5,5]$ | **failed:** 1.42, 1.39; 1.22 |
| Q4-5 | $1<$ growth $\le D-1$ | exact | held |
| Q4-6 | P15, P16 and the $G=1$ synthetic run inside $B^{Q4}_{T3}$; the one-shift check | $\le1$; $\le10^{-12}$ | held: $\le0.62$; 0 |

**Reading the failures.** Q4-1 to Q4-4 were guesses that assumed most of $\beta_{\rm eval}$ came from
length-$D$ reductions. It did not. They are kept, because a frozen prediction is never re-read after the
run. **Q4-9:** under Q4, a route-1 change at its bound (Δ's evaluation noise, aligned) no longer exceeds
the evaluation term. E4's sensitivity statement therefore does not carry over to Q4. This is no
counterexample to $B_{T3}$, which contains both terms.

```{r s1e-ts6q4}
  b1 <- t3_beval(o$D, t3_Om, g$r, t3_nT, t3_eta_stata); b4 <- t3_beval(o$D, t3_Om, g$r, t3_nT, t3_eta_q4)
  ghs <- drop(crossprod(o$D, t3_w0 * (sv_s - o$sig(o$th))))
  Bs <- function(eta) t3_B(o, o$D, o$th, ghs, t3_Om, 4 * t3_u * abs(t3_Om), eps = 4 * t3_u, K = o$K, stK = o$stK,
                           eta = eta)$B
  B1 <- Bs(t3_eta_stata); B4 <- Bs(t3_eta_q4); z <- t3_e2e[[lev]]
  # P16's production-like point: beta_eval does not depend on a trigger's dOm or eps, so every trigger's B moves
  # by one shift. Trigger 1 is recomputed in full as a check of that.

  gc <- t3_grad(o$sig, b0c$x, Dc, t3_Om); ghc <- drop(crossprod(Dc, t3_w0 * (sv_s - o$sig(b0c$x))))
  shift <- (t3_beval(Dc, t3_Om, gc$r, t3_nT, t3_eta_q4) - t3_beval(Dc, t3_Om, gc$r, t3_nT, t3_eta_stata)) /
           (1 + abs(gc$v[["T3"]]))
  Bp4 <- z$trig[, "B"] + shift; n <- nrow(t3_Om)
  set.seed(301); Xi <- matrix(sample(c(-1, 1), n * n, TRUE), n); Xi[lower.tri(Xi)] <- t(Xi)[lower.tri(Xi)]
  Om2 <- t3_Om * (1 + Xi * t3_u)
  Bt1 <- t3_B(o, Dc, b0c$x, ghc, t3_Om, Om2 - t3_Om, eps = (1 / diag(Om2)) / t3_w0 - 1, K = b0c$K, stK = o$stK,
              eta = t3_eta_q4)$B
  # E4 under Q4: each route's |change|, recovered from the recorded ratio over beta_eval(Q1) + r_T
  rq <- t3_rT(T3) * dn; ch <- t3_rt[c("r1_over_red2", "r2_over_red2", "r3_over_red2"), lev] * (b1 + rq)
  # H9 with beta_eval(Q4) in both forms: Q4's envelopes and Q4's emulated pair

  c(D = nrow(o$D), q = ncol(o$D), R_eval = b4 / b1, eval_q1 = b1 / dn, eval_q4 = b4 / dn,
    B_syn_q1 = B1, B_syn_q4 = B4, B_ratio = B4 / B1, P15_syn = z$syn_max / B4, P15_aligned = z$worst * z$B_syn / B4,
    P16 = max(z$trig[, "cd"] / Bp4), shift_check = abs(Bt1 / Bp4[1] - 1),
    E1 = t3_ev["max_abs_change", lev] / b4, E2 = b4 / t3_beval_abs(o$D, t3_Om, g$r, t3_nT, t3_eta_q4),
    E4_r1 = ch[[1]] / (b4 + rq), E4_r2 = ch[[2]] / (b4 + rq), E4_r3 = ch[[3]] / (b4 + rq),
    H9_B_ratio = ap / ms, B_apriori_q4 = ap, B_meas_q4 = ms)
})
q4_g1 <- t3_g1[c("D", "eval_ratio_q4", "B", "B_q4", "syn_max_over_B_q4")]
```

#### A tolerance for comparisons that cross a processor count or a Stata version: the step channel {#sec-mg-sensitivity-step}

*Added 2026-10-19 by the main session at the user's request, after `test_sens_t3.do` failed under StataMP
16.1 (E-047, 2026-10-19). The predictions are E-048's,
committed at c030c37 before any chunk below ran. Nothing in `src/`, the tests, their references or any
tolerance changes here.*

**Why.** `test_sens_t3.do`'s r1 and r2 compare `dwlsmv_sens_t3`'s outputs with references made by
another Stata run (StataMP 18, six processors), to $10^{-12}$ relative. A diagnostic at 1, 2 and 4
processors on the milestone laptop found the following:
- Ω moves by ulps between counts, and the iteration count is equal at every count.
- The misses (up to $4\times10^{-8}$) sit in $\beta_2$ and $B_{T3}$.
- They enter through $S^{(C)}$, which is linear in the last step $|\theta_K-\theta_{K-1}|$. That step is
  small, and it carries its iterates' ulp-driven shifts at full size.

No fixed tolerance follows from that. This subsection derives one from the run being checked.

**Assumptions** (labelled; none established here):
- A1–A3, conditional;
- Q4, chosen after Q1 failed (disclosed);
- **A5:** at equal $K$, the $K-1$ iterate's input-driven shift lies within the same envelope $\Theta$ as
  the $K$ iterate's;
- **A7:** an assumed evaluation floor $f_j=10^3u|o_j|$, like $c_{\rm ch}$;
- **A6**, for the cross-version use only: StataMP 16 and 18 differ in this computation only by arithmetic
  of the kinds Q4 and S3 bound. A6 is the user's to judge, and nothing here tests it.

##### Result ST1: the channels

Let two runs $a$, $b$ on identical data ($ds=0$ under A1–A3) have equal $K$ and line-search history.
The comparison vector $o$ is a function of $(\hat\theta,\ st=\theta_K-\theta_{K-1},\ \Omega)$, with the
synthetic inputs of the test held fixed. Telescoping one input at a time:
$$
o_a-o_b=\big[o(\theta_a,st_a,\Omega_a)-o(\theta_a,st_b,\Omega_a)\big]+\big[o(\theta_a,st_b,\Omega_a)-o(\theta_b,st_b,\Omega_a)\big]+\big[o(\theta_b,st_b,\Omega_a)-o(\theta_b,st_b,\Omega_b)\big].
$$

**The step channel needs no linearization.** $o$ depends on $st$ only through $|st|$, inside
$S^{(C)}=K\,|P^{-1}|\,(\cdot)\,|st|+\dots$, which has nonnegative coefficients. $\Theta$, $\beta_2$ and
$B_{T3}$ are then nondecreasing in $|st|$ (SE4's argument). With $|st_a-st_b|\le|\Delta\theta_K|+|\Delta\theta_{K-1}|\le2\Theta_b$
(TS4's $\Theta$, and A5 for the $K-1$ iterate):
$$
|{\rm first\ term}|_j\le o_j\big(|st_b|+2\Theta_b\big)-o_j\big(\max(|st_b|-2\Theta_b,0)\big)=:\Delta_{{\rm step},j}.
$$

**The θ̂ and Ω channels are first order,** as TS4 and TS5:
- $\Delta_{\theta,j}=\sum_l|\partial o_j/\partial\theta_l|\,\Theta_{b,l}$;
- $\Delta_{\Omega,j}=\langle|\partial o_j/\partial\Omega|,\bar E_\Omega\rangle$, with $\bar E_\Omega$ SE3's
  envelope under Q4, from run $b$'s $\Gamma_g$.

Here the gradients are central differences of $o$ (R's model). In Stata they would come from the same
routine evaluated at displaced inputs.

##### Result ST2: the tolerance

$$
\tau_j=\Delta_{{\rm step},j}+(1+\rho)\big(\Delta_{\theta,j}+\Delta_{\Omega,j}\big)+f_j,\qquad
|o_{a,j}-o_{b,j}|\le\tau_j,
$$

with $\rho=0.01$, as in TS7. Every term is computed from run $b$ alone.

- **Uniformity.** The uniformity condition of TS2 applies to the two first-order channels and is
  covered by $\rho$, as there.
- **Cross-version use.** Applied to a reference from another Stata version, $\tau$ is valid only under
  A6.

##### Verification on design E (R 4.5.2, lavaan 0.7.2; 2026-10-19)

**The runs.** Design E's 20 emulated Q4 Ω's (`@sec-mg-sensitivity-stage1`): run $b$ is run 1, and runs
$a$ are runs 2–20. Each run refits from the same ULS start at $b$'s production $K$, with halving on. The
inputs follow the test's "none" and "full" cases (the test's $ds$ term is absent, since t3_B takes none).
This is R's model of production, not Stata's.

**Corrections before the recorded run** (none changed a threshold or an outcome): 0/0 on $\beta_3$,
which is exactly 0 in "none", stopped the first run before any outcome printed. The ratio now requires an
exact zero difference wherever $\tau=0$, as H6 does.

| Item | Prediction | Threshold (before running) | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | equal $K$ and halvings | 0 displaced | held: 0 |
| T1 | A5: $\lvert\Delta\theta_K\rvert$, $\lvert\Delta\theta_{K-1}\rvert\le\Theta_b$ | $\le1$ | held: at most $5.7\times10^{-4}$ |
| T2 | the step moves | $\ge1$ pair per level | held: 19 of 19 |
| T3 | $o_3$, $o_7$, Θ nondecreasing in $\lvert st\rvert$ | all | held |
| T4 | **$\lvert o_a-o_b\rvert\le\tau$, every column and Θ element** | $\le1$ | **held: at most 0.0034** |
| T5 | without $\Delta_{\rm step}$, violated on $\ge1$ pair (cols 3, 7, Θ) | $\ge1$ | held as worded: 76 violations, **all on loadings; 0 on intercepts**. The first run's assertion was per level, stricter than the committed text, and failed there. The assertion now matches the text. Recorded, not re-read |
| T6 | ratio distribution, $\tau_j/\lvert o_j\rvert$ | reported | $\tau_3/\lvert o_3\rvert$: $4.3\times10^{-9}$ (loadings), $8.2\times10^{-9}$ (intercepts). The step channel is at most 0.03% of $\tau$, so here $\tau$ is set by the θ̂ and Ω channels |
| T7 | R's $\tau_3$ against Stata's measured misses | reported | **R's $\tau_3$ is below Stata's measured misses**: $8.2\times10^{-9}$ against $1.85\times10^{-8}$ (scalar, two processors); $4.3\times10^{-9}$ against $1.4$–$4.0\times10^{-8}$ (metric, Stata 18 reference) |

**What this shows, and what it does not.**
- **The form of τ holds on R's emulated pairs, with a wide margin (T4).** On these pairs the step
  channel matters on loadings (T5).
- **R's model does not reproduce Stata's step sensitivity.** R's fit stops at $K=4$ with $|st|$ up to
  $3\times10^{-6}$, so the relative move of $|st|$, and with it $\Delta o_3$ ($1$–$2.5\times10^{-11}$), is
  far smaller than at Stata's $K=5$ stop. There $|st|\sim10^{-7}$, and $\Delta o_3$ reaches
  $1.85\times10^{-8}$.
- **T7 is therefore a warning, not a verdict.** $\tau$ evaluated at R's fit says nothing about $\tau$ at
  Stata's fit, where the step channel is relatively larger. Whether $\tau$ covers the Stata misses can be
  learned only by computing it in Mata at Stata's own fit.
- **Nothing here certifies `test_sens_t3`'s cases 1, 3 and 4 against the Stata 18 reference.** That
  needs A6.

**At Stata's own fits, τ FAILED (Mata diagnostic, 2026-10-19).** E-048, with
predictions M0–M6 committed first (a102e19).
- **Case 2 (scalar) at 2 processors misses by 6.36 τ**, in β₂.
- Against the Stata 18 reference, metric_full and metric_none miss by 3.76 τ (conditional on A6).
- A5 held (≤ 0.027 of Θ), and the step channel is at most $5\times10^{-4}$ of τ. **The step is
  therefore not the mechanism**, and ST2's τ is not a valid tolerance for `test_sens_t3`.
- **Read after the result (a hypothesis):** the miss is TS4's $O(\bar E/h)$ noise in $\partial\Delta/\partial\theta$
  from differences of $\Delta_c$. It is redrawn whenever θ̂ moves at all, so it is zeroth order in the
  trigger, as S5(c), and invisible to a first-order θ̂ channel. A revised tolerance needs its own
  derivation and predictions.

**Open** (a list; none is chosen here):
- Whether to derive a tolerance that carries the $\partial\Delta/\partial\theta$ redraw term, or to give
  `test_sens_t3` another reference policy. The user's decision.
- A6, for cases 1, 3 and 4.
- A5 beyond these pairs; it held at about $6\times10^{-4}$ here.
- A7's constant.

```{r stt-setup}
# The step-sensitivity tolerance (Results ST1-ST3), on design E's emulated Q4 pairs of
# @sec-mg-sensitivity-stage1. Run b: Omega from emulated run 1; runs a: runs 2-20. Each run refits from the
# same ULS start at run b's production K, halving on. Names start with stt_. Predictions:
# E-048 (committed before any of this ran).
stt_Om  <- lapply(se_Gam$Q4, function(G) se_omega(G, se_Ng))
stt_Eb  <- se_envs(se_Gam$Q4[[1]], se_Ng, "Q4")$O                           # SE3, from run b alone
stt_fit <- function(o, Om) { w <- 1 / diag(Om); b <- sv_gn(o$sig, sv_s, w, o$x0, K = o$K)
  list(th = b$x, thK1 = b$xs[[o$K]], st = b$xs[[o$K + 1L]] - b$xs[[o$K]], halv = b$halv, Om = Om) }
stt_inp <- function(Om, case) { n <- nrow(Om)
  if (case == "none") list(dOm = 0 * Om, eps = 0)
  else list(dOm = 4 * se_u * abs(Om) * sin(outer(1:n, 1:n, "+")), eps = 3e-16 * cos(1:n)) }
# o: the test's comparison vector, R's model: T3, then (2 beta_1, beta_2, beta_3, beta_eval, beta_elem) and
# B_T3 in check 6's units (dwlsmv_sens_t3 columns 1-7), then Theta (r2). |st| enters only through S^(C).
stt_o <- function(o, th, st, Om, case) {
  z <- stt_inp(Om, case); Dl <- sv_jac(o$sig, th)
  gh <- drop(crossprod(Dl, (1 / diag(Om)) * (sv_s - o$sig(th))))
  b <- t3_B(o, Dl, th, gh, Om, z$dOm, z$eps, K = o$K, stK = abs(st))
  c(T3 = b$T3, setNames(b$terms, c("b1x2", "b2", "b3", "beval", "belem")), B = b$B,
    setNames(b$Theta, paste0("Th", seq_along(th))))
}
stt_cols <- c("T3", "b1x2", "b2", "b3", "beval", "belem", "B")
stt_rho <- t3_rho
# ST3: the tolerance from run b alone. The step channel is exact (o is nondecreasing in |st|, T3); the theta
# and Omega channels are first order, by central differences; f is the assumed evaluation floor (A7).
stt_tau <- function(o, fb, case) {
  ob <- stt_o(o, fb$th, fb$st, fb$Om, case); Th <- ob[grepl("^Th", names(ob))]
  dstep <- stt_o(o, fb$th, abs(fb$st) + 2 * Th, fb$Om, case) - stt_o(o, fb$th, pmax(abs(fb$st) - 2 * Th, 0), fb$Om, case)
  dth <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(seq_along(fb$th), function(l) { h <- 1e-5 * max(1, abs(fb$th[l]))
    abs(stt_o(o, replace(fb$th, l, fb$th[l] + h), fb$st, fb$Om, case) -
        stt_o(o, replace(fb$th, l, fb$th[l] - h), fb$st, fb$Om, case)) / (2 * h) * Th[l] }))
  ij <- which(upper.tri(stt_Eb, diag = TRUE) & stt_Eb > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  dOm <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ij)), function(k) { i <- ij[k, 1]; j <- ij[k, 2]
    h <- 1e-6 * abs(fb$Om[i, j]); E <- matrix(0, nrow(fb$Om), ncol(fb$Om)); E[i, j] <- E[j, i] <- h
    abs(stt_o(o, fb$th, fb$st, fb$Om + E, case) - stt_o(o, fb$th, fb$st, fb$Om - E, case)) / (2 * h) * stt_Eb[i, j] }))
  list(ob = ob, Th = Th, dstep = dstep, dth = dth, dOm = dOm, f = 1e3 * se_u * abs(ob),
       tau = dstep + (1 + stt_rho) * (dth + dOm) + 1e3 * se_u * abs(ob))
}
stt_run <- lapply(names(t3_lev), function(lev) { o <- t3_lev[[lev]]
  fits <- lapply(stt_Om, function(Om) stt_fit(o, Om))
  lapply(setNames(nm = c("none", "full")), function(case) {
    tb <- stt_tau(o, fits[[1]], case)
    oa <- sapply(fits[-1], function(fa) stt_o(o, fa$th, fa$st, fa$Om, case))
    list(tb = tb, oa = oa, fits = fits) }) })
names(stt_run) <- names(t3_lev)

```

```{r stt-check}
# T0-T7 (predictions section 3), thresholds set before running.
stt_rr <- function(d, t) { T <- d * 0 + t; stopifnot(all(d[T == 0] == 0)); x <- d / T; x[T == 0] <- 0; x }   # 0/0 only where both are exactly 0
stt_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(stt_run), function(lev) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("none", "full"), function(case) {
  z <- stt_run[[lev]][[case]]; tb <- z$tb; fb <- z$fits[[1]]; fa <- z$fits[-1]; o <- t3_lev[[lev]]
  d <- abs(z$oa - tb$ob)                                                     # |o_a - o_b|, one column per pair
  r4 <- stt_rr(d, tb$tau); r5 <- stt_rr(d, tb$tau - tb$dstep)
  Thk <- grepl("^Th", names(tb$ob)); ctl <- names(tb$ob) %in% c("b2", "B") | Thk
  tg <- sapply(seq(0, 2, by = 0.1), function(t) stt_o(o, fb$th, t * abs(fb$st), fb$Om, case))
  mono <- all(apply(tg[names(tb$ob) %in% c("b2", "B") | Thk, , drop = FALSE], 1, function(x) all(diff(x) >= 0)))
  data.frame(level = lev, case = case,
    T0_displaced = sum(sapply(fa, `[[`, "halv") != fb$halv),
    T1_thK = max(sapply(fa, function(f) max(abs(f$th - fb$th) / tb$Th))),
    T1_thK1 = max(sapply(fa, function(f) max(abs(f$thK1 - fb$thK1) / tb$Th))),
    T2_step_moves = sum(sapply(fa, function(f) any(f$st != fb$st))),
    T3_monotone = mono,
    T4_max = max(r4), T4_arg = rownames(r4)[which(r4 == max(r4), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, 1]],
    T5_nostep_viol = sum(r5[ctl, ] > 1),
    T7_tau3_rel = tb$tau[["b2"]] / abs(tb$ob[["b2"]]), T7_tauB_rel = tb$tau[["B"]] / abs(tb$ob[["B"]]),
    max_dstep3_rel = max(d["b2", ]) / abs(tb$ob[["b2"]]))
}))))
print(format(stt_res, digits = 4), row.names = FALSE)
stt_t6 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(stt_run), function(lev) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("none", "full"), function(case) {
  z <- stt_run[[lev]][[case]]; tb <- z$tb; d <- abs(z$oa - tb$ob)
  data.frame(level = lev, case = case, col = stt_cols, ratio_max = apply(stt_rr(d[stt_cols, ], tb$tau[stt_cols]), 1, max),
             tau_rel = stt_rr(tb$tau[stt_cols], abs(tb$ob[stt_cols])),
             step_share = stt_rr(tb$dstep[stt_cols], tb$tau[stt_cols])) }))))
print(format(stt_t6, digits = 3), row.names = FALSE)                          # T6, reported only
with(stt_res, stopifnot(T0_displaced == 0, T1_thK <= 1, T1_thK1 <= 1, T2_step_moves >= 1,   # T0-T2
# T5 as worded (>= 1 pair overall) held, on loadings only; the first run's assertion was per level, stricter
# than the committed prediction, and failed on intercepts (0). Recorded in the text.
                        T3_monotone, T4_max <= 1,                                           # T3, T4
                        sum(T5_nostep_viol) >= 1))                           # T5
```

##### The ∂Δ/∂θ evaluation-noise diagnostic (2026-10-19, after M2 failed)

*Predictions and thresholds: E-048 §6, committed at 1d682bb before
anything ran; outcomes in its Addendum 2. Stata side: E-048, read
by `ddelta_noise.R` (`ddelta_noise.log`). R side: the chunk below. Diagnostic only. Nothing in `src/`,
the tests, their references or any tolerance changes, and no wider τ is sought.*

**The question.** After M2 failed, the working hypothesis H was that β₂ depends on `dwlsmv_sens_ddelta`,
which takes central differences (h = 1e-4) of production's Δ_c, whose correlation rows are themselves
central differences (h = 1e-5). On this reading, β₂ carries rounding noise of about 1e-7 relative, and
that noise is redrawn whenever θ̂ moves at all.

**Exact arithmetic, level by level** (§6.1 of the predictions):
- Design E has one factor and no β, so MS2.1's degree-2 case does not arise.
- ω enters as ω_iω_kV_ik, and the threshold rows as ω(τ − ν − λα). So σ is multilinear, and in exact
  arithmetic block l of ∂Δ/∂θ is invariant along e_l, and only along e_l.
- v_l = ⟨G_Δ, block l⟩ inherits no invariance, because G_Δ moves along every direction.
- β₂ is smooth and O(δ), up to kinks from |v_l|.

**Stata (StataMP 16.1, scalar fit of `test_sens_t3`, one session; fits at 1, 2 and 4 processors, every
evaluation at 1).**
- **Preconditions held.**
  - The fits reproduce the 2026-10-19 CSVs bitwise (N0), and the refit base reproduces o₁ (N1).
  - β₂'s split T_g + T_v + T_J reproduces β₂ (N2). At the base, T_v = Σ|v_l|Θ_l is all but 1e-4 of β₂.
  - The evaluation is count-invariant: o, Δ_c and dD are bitwise equal at 1, 2 and 4 processors (E1).
- **Fixed θ̂, Ω from the other counts' Stage 1:**
  - Δ_c and dD are bitwise unchanged (F1).
  - o₃ moves 2.1e-15 and 2.3e-15, and v 3.5e-15 and 5.9e-14, all relative (F2). **The miss vanishes.**
  - F3 failed on one piece: T_g moved 2.3e-12 relative at 4 processors, against the threshold 1e-12. Θ and
    T_J held.
- **θ̂ swapped alone (θ₂ at run 1's Stage 1) reproduces the miss exactly:** |Δo₃| / measured miss = 1.000
  (S1).
  - 99.9% of Δβ₂ is in T_v (S2's first part held).
  - **S2's second part FAILED:** v's own change, with Θ held, is at most 0.73 of ΔT_v. Θ moved 1.0e-8
    relative at the swap, so at least a quarter of the jump enters T_v through Θ, not v.
- **Along the actual direction d̂, from one ulp to δ = 1e-10, every derivative-carrying quantity is
  flat.** Each was classed noise (D1–D4 held):
  - Δ_c at 5e-12 to 4e-11 relative;
  - dD at 4–6e-8;
  - v at 0.5–2e-8;
  - Θ at 0.5–4e-8;
  - J at 4–6e-9;
  - o₃ at 4e-9 to 3.7e-8. The measured 1.85e-8 is a typical draw.
  - Only the extension (δ ≥ 1e-9) shows o₃ growing, ∝ δ.
- **Along single e_l (λ, ψ and ω; l_d is ψ itself, element 17):**
  - dD's block l is noise along e_λ and e_ψ, at about 3–7e-8, the exact-arithmetic invariance
    notwithstanding.
  - o₃ is flat to δ = 1e-11 and then grows ∝ δ. So its class is "undetermined" by the frozen rule, and
    **L1 failed** for λ, ψ and l_d.
  - Along e_ω, dD's block l sits at 5e-13 to 1.5e-12 relative and o₃ is linear from 1 ulp: **L1 failed**
    there too. The predicted noise plateau is absent along ω. This is consistent with ω scaling V
    after differencing rather than moving the points at which V is evaluated.
- **The e_τ control:**
  - Δ_c's and dD's correlation rows are bitwise invariant along e_τ, as predicted, and dD as a whole is
    invariant.
  - **L2 FAILED on its band:** o₃ grows exactly ∝ δ, to 2.66e-8 at δ = 1e-10, against ≤ 1e-11.
  - The growth sits in T_g: the ḡ elements are 1e-10 to 1e-8 at the stopped iterate, so their relative
    sensitivity to θ is large. It is genuine, first-order variation (class "genuine"), not a jump. At the
    actual move's size (about 1e-12) it would be about 3e-10 relative.

**R's model (design E, "intercepts", at R's own point; not Stata's θ̂).**
- C0 held: σ is multilinear, with a second difference of 4.3e-16·max|σ|.
- C1 held: exact block l moves at most 4.4e-15 along e_l, while another block moves 0.16 at δ = 0.1.
- C2's classes held: along d_R the exact ∂Δ/∂θ is genuine (r = 2.68·δ), and the production-like dD_c is
  noise, flat at 4–6e-8.
- **C2's ratio FAILED:** the plateau over the exact r is 190 at δ = 1e-10, against ≥ 1e3. By then the
  exact derivative's own genuine change (2.7e-10) has grown inside three decades of the plateau.
- C3 held: at the base, dD_c − dD is 3.1e-8 relative, within 10× of the plateau's median, 6.4e-8.
- C4 held: along e_τ, dD_c's correlation rows are bitwise invariant.

**Verdict, by the rule frozen in §6.4: undetermined.**
- **Not "supported":** S2, L2 and C2 failed.
- **One refutation clause is ambiguous, and it is recorded rather than resolved.** The clause is "L2
  fails with o₃ jumping at ≥ 1e-9 along e_τ". As the R reader encodes it (magnitude only), it fires. Its
  stated meaning, a zeroth-order jump through a channel that does not touch Δ_c, is not what happened:
  the change along e_τ is linear in δ and lies in T_g. **A literal reading gives "refuted". Which
  reading stands is the user's call.**
- **What the items that held establish, without promoting H:**
  - The 2-processor miss is triggered by θ̂'s move, not by Ω's (F2, S1).
  - It is zeroth order in that move: a flat plateau from one ulp to 1e-10 (D4).
  - It sits in T_v (S2's first part), and it rides on noise in the finite-difference derivatives that T_v
    reads: dD (D2; C2's classes and C3 in R) and Θ (through dwlsmv_sens's J).
- **H as worded** ("through v") is too narrow: at least a quarter of the jump comes through Θ.

```{r stt-ddelta-noise}
# Evaluation noise against genuine variation in dDelta/dtheta (predictions section 6, C0-C4), on R's model at
# R's own point (t3_lev$intercepts; not Stata's theta-hat, whose parameterization differs). Exact dDelta/dtheta_l:
# complex-step Delta, central-differenced in theta_l at eta = 0.1 max(1, |theta_l|), exact by C0. Production's:
# sv_cdjac's Delta (central differences on the lambda and phi correlation columns, h = 1e-5), differenced at
# h = 1e-4 max(1, |theta_l|), as dwlsmv_sens_ddelta does. Names start with dn_.
dn_o <- t3_lev$intercepts; dn_th <- dn_o$th; dn_q <- length(dn_th); dn_sig <- dn_o$sig
dn_cdj <- sv_cdjac("intercepts")
dn_blk <- function(jac, x, hf) do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(dn_q), function(l) {
  h <- hf * max(1, abs(x[l])); e <- replace(numeric(dn_q), l, h)
  (jac(dn_sig, x + e) - jac(dn_sig, x - e)) / (2 * h) }))
dn_ex <- function(x) dn_blk(sv_jac, x, 0.1)                                # exact (C0)
dn_pr <- function(x) dn_blk(dn_cdj, x, 1e-4)                               # production's construction
dn_bi <- function(l) ((l - 1) * dn_q + 1):(l * dn_q)
dn_rb <- function(X, X0) max(sapply(seq_len(dn_q), function(l) {          # r: per block, max over blocks
  b0 <- X0[, dn_bi(l)]; d <- max(abs(X[, dn_bi(l)] - b0)); if (max(abs(b0)) > 0) d / max(abs(b0)) else d }))
dn_cls <- function(r) {                                                    # r at (ulp, 1e-15, ..., 1e-10)
  if (all(r == 0)) "invariant" else if (r[2] > 0 && r[2] >= 0.1 * r[7]) "noise" else
  if ((r[2] > 0 && r[7] >= 1e3 * r[2]) || (r[2] == 0 && r[7] > 0)) "genuine" else "undetermined" }
dn_del <- c(1e-15, 1e-14, 1e-13, 1e-12, 1e-11, 1e-10, 1e-9, 1e-8, 1e-7, 1e-6)
nT <- sum(dn_o$nm == "tau"); dn_crow <- c(nT + 1:10, 2 * nT + 10 + 1:10)   # correlation rows, groups 1 and 2
stopifnot(length(dn_sig(dn_th)) == 2 * nT + 20)
# C0: sigma multilinear, the second difference in each theta_l at t = -1, 0, 1
dn_c0 <- max(sapply(seq_len(dn_q), function(l) { e <- replace(numeric(dn_q), l, 1)
  max(abs(dn_sig(dn_th + e) - 2 * dn_sig(dn_th) + dn_sig(dn_th - e))) })) / max(abs(dn_sig(dn_th)))
# C1: exact block l invariant along e_l; some block m != l moves along e_l
dn_X0 <- dn_ex(dn_th); dn_P0 <- dn_pr(dn_th)
dn_c1 <- t(sapply(seq_len(dn_q), function(l) {
  own <- sapply(c(dn_del[1:6], 0.1), function(d) { X <- dn_ex(replace(dn_th, l, dn_th[l] + d * max(1, abs(dn_th[l]))))
    b0 <- dn_X0[, dn_bi(l)]; max(abs(X[, dn_bi(l)] - b0)) / max(max(abs(b0)), 1e-300) * (max(abs(b0)) > 0) +
    max(abs(X[, dn_bi(l)] - b0)) * (max(abs(b0)) == 0) })
  X <- dn_ex(replace(dn_th, l, dn_th[l] + 0.1 * max(1, abs(dn_th[l]))))
  oth <- max(sapply(setdiff(seq_len(dn_q), l), function(m) { b0 <- dn_X0[, dn_bi(m)]
    if (max(abs(b0)) > 0) max(abs(X[, dn_bi(m)] - b0)) / max(abs(b0)) else 0 }))
  c(own = max(own), other = oth) }))
# C2-C4: the grid along d_R and along e_l (first lambda, first tau, phi)
dn_dirs <- list(dR = cos(seq_len(dn_q)) / max(abs(cos(seq_len(dn_q)))))
for (n in c("lam", "tau", "phi")) dn_dirs[[n]] <- replace(numeric(dn_q), which(dn_o$nm == n)[1], 1)
dn_grid <- lapply(dn_dirs, function(d) {
  k <- which.max(abs(d)); ulp <- 2^(floor(log2(abs(dn_th[k]))) - 52)      # one ulp of the largest component
  t(sapply(c(ulp, dn_del), function(dl) { x <- dn_th + dl * d; X <- dn_ex(x); P <- dn_pr(x)
    c(delta = dl, r_ex = dn_rb(X, dn_X0), r_pr = dn_rb(P, dn_P0),
      corr_changed = sum(P[dn_crow, ] != dn_P0[dn_crow, ])) })) })
dn_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(dn_grid), function(n) { g <- dn_grid[[n]]; s <- 1:7
  data.frame(dir = n, class_exact = dn_cls(g[s, "r_ex"]), class_prod = dn_cls(g[s, "r_pr"]),
             r_pr_min = min(g[s, "r_pr"]), r_pr_med = median(g[s, "r_pr"]), r_pr_max = max(g[s, "r_pr"]),
             r_ex_max = max(g[s, "r_ex"]), ratio_min = min(g[s, "r_pr"] / g[s, "r_ex"]),
             corr_changed = sum(g[s, "corr_changed"])) }))
dn_c3 <- max(abs(dn_P0 - dn_X0)) / max(abs(dn_X0))
cat(sprintf("C0 second difference / max|sigma|: %.3g\n", dn_c0))
cat(sprintf("C1 own block along e_l (max over l): %.3g; max over l of the largest other block: %.3g\n",
            max(dn_c1[, "own"]), max(dn_c1[, "other"])))
print(format(dn_res, digits = 3), row.names = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("C3 |dD_prod - dD_exact| / |dD_exact| at the base: %.3g (d_R plateau median %.3g)\n",
            dn_c3, dn_res$r_pr_med[dn_res$dir == "dR"]))
print(signif(dn_grid$dR, 3))
# Held items asserted; C2's ratio (>= 1e3 at every delta <= 1e-10) FAILED at 190 and is recorded, not asserted.
stopifnot(dn_c0 <= 1e-13,                                                              # C0
          max(dn_c1[, "own"]) <= 1e-12, max(dn_c1[, "other"]) >= 1e-4,                  # C1
          dn_res$class_exact[dn_res$dir == "dR"] %in% c("genuine", "invariant"),
          dn_res$class_prod[dn_res$dir == "dR"] == "noise",                             # C2, classes
          dn_c3 >= 1e-9, dn_c3 <= 1e-5, dn_c3 / dn_res$r_pr_med[dn_res$dir == "dR"] <= 10,
          dn_res$r_pr_med[dn_res$dir == "dR"] / dn_c3 <= 10,                            # C3
          dn_res$corr_changed[dn_res$dir == "tau"] == 0)                                # C4
```
