```{r mgb-checks}
    stopifnot(ck$refused, identical(ck$rules, rep("b", length(ck$groups))), abs(ck$hits[[1]]$detail[[1]]$theta - (-0.0125)) < 1e-12,
              identical(ck$groups, if (l == "configural") 1:2 else 1L))
    for (bm in c("free", "tied", "g2only"))
      stopifnot(!c11_check(mgb_c11(mgb_table(d$K, d$fac, l, bm, fixlam = list(item = 4L, val = 0.9))))$refused)
    # beta fixed at 0 is legal: Theta_44 = 1 - .81 = .19
    stopifnot(!c11_check(mgb_c11(mgb_table(d$K, d$fac, l, "fixed", fixlam = list(item = 4L, val = 0.9), bval = 0)))$refused)
  }
  # H-C2
  P <- MGB_DESIGNS$P; T0 <- function(l, bm) mgb_table(P$K, P$fac, l, bm)
  for (l in c("metric", "scalar")) {
    a <- mgb_nest(T0(l, "tied"), T0(l, "free"))
    stopifnot(a$ok, a$d == 1L, a$d == mgb_df(P$K, P$fac, l, 1L) - mgb_df(P$K, P$fac, l, 2L))
    b <- mgb_nest(T0(l, "none"), T0(l, "free")); stopifnot(b$ok, b$d == 2L, b$d == mgb_df(P$K, P$fac, l, 0L) - mgb_df(P$K, P$fac, l, 2L))
    f <- mgb_nest(T0(l, "fixed"), T0(l, "free")); stopifnot(f$ok, f$d == 2L)           # fixed at .4 against free
    r <- mgb_nest(T0(l, "free"), T0(l, "fixed")); stopifnot(!r$ok)                     # the reverse: a free beta fixed in H1
  }
  base <- T0("metric", "free")
  h0 <- mgb_retie(T0("metric", "tied"), function(R) { R$tie[R$type == "lambda" & R$i == 1L] <- NA_integer_; R })   # beta tied, lambda_1 untied
  h1 <- mgb_retie(base, function(R) { R$tie[R$type == "lambda" & R$i == 2L] <- NA_integer_; R })                 # beta free, lambda_1 tied, lambda_2 untied
  stopifnot(h0$npar == base$npar, h1$npar - h0$npar == 1L)
  cnt <- mgb_nest(h0, h1, closure = FALSE); clo <- mgb_nest(h0, h1, closure = TRUE)
  stopifnot(cnt$ok, cnt$d == 1L, !clo$ok, any(grepl("equates rows", clo$why)))         # count-and-status accepts; closure refuses
  # the valid cousin: beta tied and lambda_1 TIED in H0, beta free and lambda_1 untied in H1
  g0 <- T0("metric", "tied")
  g1 <- mgb_retie(base, function(R) { R$tie[R$type == "lambda" & R$i == 1L] <- NA_integer_; R })
  stopifnot(mgb_nest(g0, g1)$ok, mgb_nest(g0, g1)$d == 2L)
  # (d): the level step
  stopifnot(!mgb_nest(T0("metric", "free"), T0("configural", "free"))$ok)
  stopifnot(!mgb_nest(T0("metric", "free"), T0("configural", "free"), closure = FALSE)$ok)
})
```

```{r mgb-infer-prereg}
# Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2), once, in a full re-run of this document after the
# freeze (c23218b): GATE PASSED. 84 of 84 fits usable, no failure, 28 cells covered; P2/P3 gaps <= 8.9e-16; H-I1 <= 2.8e-13;
# H-I2 <= 1.3e-11; H-I3 scalar vcov moved >= 2.0e-2 with T3 <= 1.7e-13, other levels <= 1.1e-13
# (E-051).
# Preregistered re-run of H-I1/H-I2/H-I3 (user, 2026-10-10, option (a), conditional on the helper
# audit and these rules being written in before the freeze). Gate for O2's beta lift under option (e): beta fitting and
# inference. It does NOT bear on DIFFTEST. Depends on: mgb-lav-funs (mgb_syntax, mgb_sim, mgb_fit), mgb-lavaan
# (mgb_from_lavaan, mgb_lav_map), mgb-infer (mgb_mut, MGB_TOL_T3, MGB_TOL_V, MGB_TOL_MUT), mgb-core (mgb_table, mgb_df,
# mgb_nb, MGB_DESIGNS, MGB_YPATHS), mg2-core, mg2-lavaan (mg2_lav_implied, MG2_TOL_IMP), mg2-lavdelta (MG2_TOL_LD),
# mg-setup and mg-lavaan (mg_pool, mg_traces_q, mg_ab, mg_acov, mg_rel, mg_parts, mg_Tcand, mg_T_convention), inv-setup.
#
# Design (frozen): designs P, M, B, S, W, Z, Y x levels configural, thresholds, metric, scalar; beta free (untied) on
# every path (Y: paths 2<-1 and 3<-2, MGB_YPATHS); three datasets per design, seed = 20261100 + 10 * design index
# (P = 1 ... Y = 7) + rep; N = (1200, 2800). 7 x 4 = 28 cells, 84 fits.
#
# Helper audit (main session, before the freeze), and what this chunk does about each finding:
#  A1 mgb_sim builds exactly two factors (cbind(f1, f2), c(phi1, ph22)[fac]); it cannot generate Y. Y uses the new
#     mgb_sim_y below: the same construction with f3 = alpha_3 + beta f2 + e3; group 1 has alpha = 0, phi_1 = 1,
#     psi = (1, 1) and unit total latent-response variance; group 2 has phi_1 = 1.44, psi = (1.3, 1.2),
#     alpha = (.3, .2, .1), theta = seq(.4, .8). The values for f3 were chosen before any run, mirroring mgb_sim.
#     mgb_sim itself is unchanged and is used for the other six designs.
#  A2 mgb_infer and mgb_fit_all do not pass `paths`; for Y they would silently use the default single path. This
#     chunk passes `paths` to mgb_table, mgb_syntax (through mgb_fit) and mgb_nb explicitly.
#  A3 The thresholds level was never fitted against lavaan (mgb-lavaan covered configural, metric, scalar). Every fit
#     therefore passes the preconditions P1-P3 before H-I1/H-I2 are read, so a syntax/table mismatch cannot pass
#     silently. mgb_lav_map already stops on an unmatched parameter.
#  A4 mgb_sim stops on an empty category. The stop is caught and the dataset recorded as unusable (rule U1).
#  A5 mg_rel(x, ref) = max|x - ref| / max|ref|: relative to the largest entry, not entrywise. H-I2 uses it as in
#     mgb-infer (unchanged); this is stated, not altered.
#
# Comparison rules (frozen):
#  P1 lavaan's df = mgb_df (Result B4), lavaan's npar = the table's npar, rank(Delta at lavaan's estimates) = npar.
#  P2 sigma at lavaan's estimates (mg2_sigma) = lavInspect(fit, "implied") within MG2_TOL_IMP = 1e-10.
#  P3 every closed-form Delta column = lavaan's matching column within MG2_TOL_LD = 1e-10.
#  H-I1 |T3 / chisq.scaled - 1| <= MGB_TOL_T3 = 1e-8 (T lavaan's unscaled statistic, mg_T_convention).
#  H-I2 mg_rel(ACOV / (N - G) mapped to lavaan's basis, vcov(fit)) <= MGB_TOL_V = 1e-7.
#  H-I3 at the scalar level the zeroed-beta-threshold mutant moves vcov by more than MGB_TOL_MUT = 1e-4 and leaves T3
#       within MGB_TOL_T3; at configural, thresholds and metric it leaves vcov within MGB_TOL_V (vacuous where kappa = 0;
#       at thresholds kappa = 0 as alpha is fixed at 0 in both groups).
#  All bounds are the existing ones, set before measuring; none is changed here.
#
# Unusable-cell rules (frozen):
#  U1 A dataset with an empty category (mgb_sim's stop), or a fit lavaan reports as not converged, is UNUSABLE:
#     recorded with its reason, excluded from P1-P3 and H-I1-H-I3, and never dropped silently.
#  U2 Any other error, or a converged fit that fails P1, P2 or P3, is a FAILURE of the gate, not an unusable fit.
#  U3 A usable fit over any H-I bound is a FAILURE of the gate. A failure is kept as a failure; nothing is loosened.
#  U4 A cell (design x level) with no usable fit is NOT ESTABLISHED. The gate PASSES only if all 28 cells have at least
#     one usable fit and there is no failure; otherwise the outcome is FAILED (any failure) or NOT ESTABLISHED.
mgb_sim_y <- function(K, fac, N = c(1200L, 2800L), bet = .4, phi1 = c(1, 1.44), psi = list(c(1, 1), c(1.3, 1.2)),
                      alpha = c(.3, .2, .1), seed = 1L) {
  set.seed(seed); p <- length(K); lam <- 0.55 + 0.04 * seq_len(p); tau <- inv_tau(K)
  one <- function(n, ph1, ps, al, th) {
    f1 <- rnorm(n, al[1], sqrt(ph1)); f2 <- al[2] + bet * f1 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(ps[1]))
    f3 <- al[3] + bet * f2 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(ps[2])); Fm <- cbind(f1, f2, f3)
    sapply(seq_len(p), function(j) findInterval(lam[j] * Fm[, fac[j]] + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(th[j])), tau[[j]]))
  }
  v2 <- bet^2 * phi1[1] + psi[[1]][1]; v3 <- bet^2 * v2 + psi[[1]][2]
  th1 <- 1 - lam^2 * c(phi1[1], v2, v3)[fac]; th2 <- seq(.4, .8, length.out = p)
  d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:2, times = N),
                  rbind(one(N[1], phi1[1], psi[[1]], c(0, 0, 0), th1), one(N[2], phi1[2], psi[[2]], alpha, th2)))
  names(d)[-1] <- paste0("y", seq_len(p))
  for (g in 1:2) for (j in seq_len(p)) stopifnot(length(unique(d[d$g == g, j + 1L])) == K[j])
  d
}
mgbp_one <- function(dn, di, rep, level) {
  d <- MGB_DESIGNS[[dn]]; paths <- if (dn == "Y") MGB_YPATHS else list(c(2L, 1L)); seed <- 20261100L + 10L * di + rep
  base <- data.frame(design = dn, level = level, rep = rep, seed = seed, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  dat <- tryCatch(if (dn == "Y") mgb_sim_y(d$K, d$fac, seed = seed) else mgb_sim(d$K, d$fac, seed = seed),
                  error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(dat, "error"))                                                  # U1: only the empty-category stop is unusable
    return(cbind(base, status = if (grepl("== K[j]", conditionMessage(dat), fixed = TRUE)) "UNUSABLE" else "FAILURE",
                 reason = paste("data:", conditionMessage(dat))))
  out <- tryCatch({
    r <- mgb_fit(dat, d$K, d$fac, level, "free", paths)
    if (!isTRUE(r$conv)) return(cbind(base, status = "UNUSABLE", reason = "lavaan did not converge"))
    tab <- mgb_table(d$K, d$fac, level, "free", paths); fit <- r$fit
    th <- mgb_from_lavaan(tab, fit); mp <- mgb_lav_map(tab, fit)
    p1 <- as.integer(r$df) == mgb_df(d$K, d$fac, level, mgb_nb("free", length(paths))) &&
          as.integer(r$npar) == tab$npar && inv_rank(r$delta) == tab$npar
    gap_imp <- max(abs(mg2_sigma(tab, th) - mg2_lav_implied(fit)))
    gap_d <- max(abs(mg2_dcols(tab, th)[, mp$m] - do.call(rbind, lavTech(fit, "delta"))))
    inf <- function(mutate = NULL) {
      pp <- mg_parts(fit); D <- mg2_delta(tab, th); if (!is.null(mutate)) D <- mutate(D, tab)
      Dg <- lapply(1:2, function(g) D[mg2_off(tab)[g] + seq_len(mg2_Dg(tab)[g]), , drop = FALSE])
      po <- mg_pool(pp$Gam, Dg, pp$wv, pp$n_g); stopifnot(po$Dtot == pp$Dtot, po$q == tab$npar)
      ab <- mg_ab(mg_traces_q(po), po$Dtot - po$q)
      Tc <- mg_Tcand(pp); hit <- names(Tc)[abs(Tc / fit@test$standard$stat - 1) < 1e-9]
      stopifnot(identical(hit, mg_T_convention[["h1"]]))
      T3 <- ab[["a"]] * Tc[[hit]] + ab[["b"]]
      S <- matrix(0, mp$nfree, tab$npar); S[cbind(seq_len(mp$nfree), tab$rows$fidx[mp$fr_rows][mp$m])] <- 1
      Vm <- S %*% (mg_acov(po) / (po$N - po$G)) %*% t(S)
      c(T3 = abs(T3 / unname(fitMeasures(fit, "chisq.scaled")) - 1), V = mg_rel(Vm, unname(vcov(fit))))
    }
    m0 <- inf(); m1 <- inf(mgb_mut)
    pre_ok <- p1 && gap_imp < MG2_TOL_IMP && gap_d < MG2_TOL_LD
    hi_ok <- m0[["T3"]] <= MGB_TOL_T3 && m0[["V"]] <= MGB_TOL_V &&
             if (level == "scalar") m1[["V"]] > MGB_TOL_MUT && m1[["T3"]] <= MGB_TOL_T3 else m1[["V"]] <= MGB_TOL_V
    cbind(base, status = if (pre_ok && hi_ok) "PASS" else "FAILURE",
          reason = if (!pre_ok) "precondition P1-P3" else if (!hi_ok) "H-I bound" else "",
          df_ok = p1, gap_imp = gap_imp, gap_delta = gap_d, T3 = m0[["T3"]], V = m0[["V"]], T3_mut = m1[["T3"]],
          V_mut = m1[["V"]])
  }, error = function(e) cbind(base, status = "FAILURE", reason = paste("error:", conditionMessage(e))))
  out
}
mgbp_dn <- c("P", "M", "B", "S", "W", "Z", "Y")
mgbp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(mgbp_dn), function(di) do.call(rbind, lapply(MGB_LEVELS, function(l)
          do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(rep) {
            x <- mgbp_one(mgbp_dn[di], di, rep, l)
            for (v in c("df_ok", "gap_imp", "gap_delta", "T3", "V", "T3_mut", "V_mut")) if (is.null(x[[v]])) x[[v]] <- NA
            x }))))))
rownames(mgbp) <- NULL; print(mgbp, digits = 3)
mgbp_cells <- aggregate(status ~ design + level, mgbp, function(s) sum(s == "PASS"))
mgbp_outcome <- if (any(mgbp$status == "FAILURE")) "FAILED" else if (any(mgbp_cells$status == 0L)) "NOT ESTABLISHED" else "PASSED"
cat("usable fits:", sum(mgbp$status != "UNUSABLE"), "of", nrow(mgbp), "; unusable:", sum(mgbp$status == "UNUSABLE"),
    "; failures:", sum(mgbp$status == "FAILURE"), "\nGATE:", mgbp_outcome, "\n")
stopifnot(mgbp_outcome == "PASSED")                                            # the preregistered gate (U4)
```

```{r mgb-fixed-prereg}
# Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2), once, in a full re-run of this document after the
# freeze (20189f5): GATE PASSED. 168 of 168 fits usable, no failure, 56 cells covered; P1 exact; P2 <= 5.6e-16,
# P3 <= 2.7e-15; H-I1 <= 8.7e-14; H-I2 <= 9.1e-12; N1 min gap 0.198 (> 1e-2); N2 max gap 5.6e-16
# (E-052, summarised by `summary.R`).
# Frozen 2026-10-10 before any run; design size decided by the user (option (a), the full 168-fit
# grid mirroring mgb-infer-prereg; declined: a reduced M/Y grid, which would leave admitted shapes unfitted).
# Preregistered gate for widening O2's admitted beta pattern to a beta FIXED at a nonzero value in every group
# (user's sequence, 2026-10-10: "preregister the fixed-nonzero extension, including the helper change and
# negative-control margin, before execution"). It bears on fitting and inference with a fixed beta, not on DIFFTEST,
# and not on a beta absent from some groups (validated separately, later). Depends on everything mgb-infer-prereg
# depends on, plus mgb_sim_y and MGB_DESIGNS from mgb-infer-prereg / mgb-core.
#
# Design (to freeze): designs P, M, B, S, W, Z, Y x the four levels x fixed values bval in {0.4, 0}; every path fixed
# at bval in both groups (Y: both MGB_YPATHS); three datasets per design, seed = 20261200 + 10 * design index + rep,
# N = (1200, 2800), data from mgb_sim / mgb_sim_y unchanged (raw beta 0.4). The two values are fitted to the SAME
# datasets. 7 x 4 x 2 = 56 cells, 168 fits.
#   bval = 0.4 is the generating raw beta. It is the population value in group 1 at every level, and in group 2
#   where group 2's factor scale is tied to group 1's (metric with psi free, scalar). At configural and thresholds
#   (and metric for a factor whose psi the generator fixes) group 2's psi is fixed at 1 while the truth has
#   phi_1 = 1.44, psi_2 = 1.3, so group 2's population beta on that scale is not 0.4 (0.4 * 1.2 / sqrt(1.3) = 0.421
#   for designs P-Z). "Correct" therefore means correct in group 1 only, there. The H bounds are agreement with
#   lavaan, not fit, so a misspecified fixed value does not bear on them; it is stated, not used.
#   DECIDED (user, 2026-10-10, option (a)): one value, 0.4, in both groups at every level, recorded as exact in
#   group 1 only where group 2's scale is untied. Declined: (b) group-specific values (0.4, 0.421), which would need a
#   second helper change and would widen the admitted pattern to unequal fixed values across groups.
#   bval = 0 is a wrong value (the path omitted). It is the existing "none" table with a fixed zero row added.
#
# Helper change (the only one): mgb_syntax gains `bval` and the beta mode "fixed", written c(bval,bval)*f<b>, the
# lavaan form of a fixed value in both groups (an added argument with a default and an added switch arm: every
# earlier call is unchanged). Nothing else in mgb-lav-funs changes; mgb_fit is given the syntax explicitly. mgb_table already has mode "fixed" (bval, default 0.4) and mgb_nb counts it as 0.
#
# Rules: P1-P3 and H-I1, H-I2 of mgb-infer-prereg, unchanged, with nb = mgb_nb("fixed", .) = 0. H-I3 is not run: it
# zeroes the threshold entries of beta COLUMNS, and a fixed beta has no column (vacuous, stated).
# Negative control (margin set here, before any run):
#  N1 at bval = 0.4, sigma computed from a copy of the table whose fixed beta values are set to 0 (lavaan's
#     estimates unchanged) must differ from lavaan's implied sigma by MORE than MGBF_MARGIN = 1e-2 in every usable
#     fit. A priori basis, not measured: dropping beta = 0.4 moves a group-1 cross-factor polychoric by
#     lambda_i lambda_j beta phi_1, at least 0.59 * 0.71 * 0.4 ~ 0.17 at the generating values with lambda = 0.55 +
#     0.04 j; the margin sits an order below that and eight orders above MG2_TOL_IMP.
#  N2 at bval = 0 the same copy changes nothing: its gap must be within MG2_TOL_IMP (a control on the control).
#  A fit failing N1 or N2 is a FAILURE (rule U2's class); the margin is not moved after the run.
# Unusable/failure rules: U1-U4 of mgb-infer-prereg, with 56 cells in U4.
MGBF_MARGIN <- 1e-2
mgbf_one <- function(dn, di, rep, level, bval) {
  d <- MGB_DESIGNS[[dn]]; paths <- if (dn == "Y") MGB_YPATHS else list(c(2L, 1L)); seed <- 20261200L + 10L * di + rep
  base <- data.frame(design = dn, level = level, bval = bval, rep = rep, seed = seed, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  dat <- tryCatch(if (dn == "Y") mgb_sim_y(d$K, d$fac, seed = seed) else mgb_sim(d$K, d$fac, seed = seed),
                  error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(dat, "error"))
    return(cbind(base, status = if (grepl("== K[j]", conditionMessage(dat), fixed = TRUE)) "UNUSABLE" else "FAILURE",
                 reason = paste("data:", conditionMessage(dat))))
  tryCatch({
    r <- mgb_fit(dat, d$K, d$fac, level, syntax = mgb_syntax(d$K, d$fac, level, "fixed", paths, bval = bval))
    if (!isTRUE(r$conv)) return(cbind(base, status = "UNUSABLE", reason = "lavaan did not converge"))
    tab <- mgb_table(d$K, d$fac, level, "fixed", paths, bval = bval); fit <- r$fit
    th <- mgb_from_lavaan(tab, fit); mp <- mgb_lav_map(tab, fit); imp <- mg2_lav_implied(fit)
    p1 <- as.integer(r$df) == mgb_df(d$K, d$fac, level, mgb_nb("fixed", length(paths))) &&
          as.integer(r$npar) == tab$npar && inv_rank(r$delta) == tab$npar
    gap_imp <- max(abs(mg2_sigma(tab, th) - imp))
    gap_d <- max(abs(mg2_dcols(tab, th)[, mp$m] - do.call(rbind, lavTech(fit, "delta"))))
    t0 <- tab; t0$rows$val[t0$rows$type == "beta"] <- 0
    gap_neg <- max(abs(mg2_sigma(t0, th) - imp))
    pp <- mg_parts(fit); D <- mg2_delta(tab, th)
    Dg <- lapply(1:2, function(g) D[mg2_off(tab)[g] + seq_len(mg2_Dg(tab)[g]), , drop = FALSE])
    po <- mg_pool(pp$Gam, Dg, pp$wv, pp$n_g); stopifnot(po$Dtot == pp$Dtot, po$q == tab$npar)
    ab <- mg_ab(mg_traces_q(po), po$Dtot - po$q)
    Tc <- mg_Tcand(pp); hit <- names(Tc)[abs(Tc / fit@test$standard$stat - 1) < 1e-9]
    stopifnot(identical(hit, mg_T_convention[["h1"]]))
    T3 <- abs((ab[["a"]] * Tc[[hit]] + ab[["b"]]) / unname(fitMeasures(fit, "chisq.scaled")) - 1)
    S <- matrix(0, mp$nfree, tab$npar); S[cbind(seq_len(mp$nfree), tab$rows$fidx[mp$fr_rows][mp$m])] <- 1
    V <- mg_rel(S %*% (mg_acov(po) / (po$N - po$G)) %*% t(S), unname(vcov(fit)))
    pre_ok <- p1 && gap_imp < MG2_TOL_IMP && gap_d < MG2_TOL_LD
    hi_ok <- T3 <= MGB_TOL_T3 && V <= MGB_TOL_V
    neg_ok <- if (bval != 0) gap_neg > MGBF_MARGIN else gap_neg < MG2_TOL_IMP
    cbind(base, status = if (pre_ok && hi_ok && neg_ok) "PASS" else "FAILURE",
          reason = if (!pre_ok) "precondition P1-P3" else if (!hi_ok) "H-I bound" else if (!neg_ok) "negative control" else "",
          df_ok = p1, gap_imp = gap_imp, gap_delta = gap_d, gap_neg = gap_neg, T3 = T3, V = V)
  }, error = function(e) cbind(base, status = "FAILURE", reason = paste("error:", conditionMessage(e))))
}
mgbf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(mgbp_dn), function(di) do.call(rbind, lapply(MGB_LEVELS, function(l)
          do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.4, 0), function(bv) do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(rep) {
            x <- mgbf_one(mgbp_dn[di], di, rep, l, bv)
            for (v in c("df_ok", "gap_imp", "gap_delta", "gap_neg", "T3", "V")) if (is.null(x[[v]])) x[[v]] <- NA
            x }))))))))
rownames(mgbf) <- NULL; print(mgbf, digits = 3)
mgbf_cells <- aggregate(status ~ design + level + bval, mgbf, function(s) sum(s == "PASS"))
mgbf_outcome <- if (any(mgbf$status == "FAILURE")) "FAILED" else if (any(mgbf_cells$status == 0L)) "NOT ESTABLISHED" else "PASSED"
cat("usable fits:", sum(mgbf$status != "UNUSABLE"), "of", nrow(mgbf), "; unusable:", sum(mgbf$status == "UNUSABLE"),
    "; failures:", sum(mgbf$status == "FAILURE"), "\nGATE:", mgbf_outcome, "\n")
stopifnot(mgbf_outcome == "PASSED")                                            # the preregistered gate (U4, 56 cells)
```

```{r mgb-absent-prereg}
# Executed 2026-10-11 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2), once, in a full re-run after the freeze (41e7a2f):
# S2 PASSED, S1 PASSED, SM PASSED. 240 of 240 fits (21 of 21 datasets) usable and passing; P1, P3s hold everywhere;
# P2 <= 6.7e-16, P3 <= 1.8e-15; H-I1 <= 2.0e-13; H-I2 <= 1.0e-11; H-I3 as predicted (moves: 39 fits, min 1.4e-3;
# vacuous: 201 fits, max 3.8e-12); N1 min 0.0825; N2 0; N3 <= 1.8e-16 (144 fits, 18 datasets). Boundary (reported
# only): 32 fits from ONE dataset (Y, seed 20261371, every level and pattern), min Theta* -0.039; all 32 passed.
# (E-053, `summary.R`, `summary.log`.)
# Frozen 2026-10-11 before any run (user: "agree on all counts"): the separate SM scope; N2 vacuous
# where both groups receive an injection (Y patterns 7, 8: no untouched group), stated, not replaced; N3 for the
# one-path designs only, Y resting on N1 and N2. Pre-freeze checks without data: E-053.
# Preregistered gate for admitting a beta ABSENT from one of two groups (present, free, in the other): orientations
# g2only (absent in group 1) and g1only (absent in group 2). The user's design, 2026-10-11, with the refinements
# agreed then. It bears on fitting and inference only, not on DIFFTEST (check 8's guard already refuses any groups
# table with a beta row), and on G = 2 only: admission, if any, is restricted to two groups. Depends on
# mgb-infer-prereg (mgb_sim_y and its dependencies), mgb-rank-y (MGB_YPAT), mgb-fixed-prereg (mgbp_dn).
#
# PRIOR INFORMATION (before this freeze): mgb-rank / mgb-rank-y (rank = npar and df = Result B2 in every cell of
# this grid); the feasibility pilot (E-053: 48 fits from 6 datasets, all usable; boundary in
# 3 fits from 1 dataset). The pilot computed no agreement quantity and set no threshold here.
#
# Design (to freeze):
#   one-path designs P, M, B, S, W, Z x 4 levels x {g2only, g1only}                         48 cells
#   design Y x 4 levels x 8 per-path patterns (path 1 = 2<-1, path 2 = 3<-2):                32 cells
#     1 (g2only, free) 2 (free, g2only) 3 (g1only, free) 4 (free, g1only) 5 (g2only, g2only) 6 (g1only, g1only)
#     7 (g2only, g1only) 8 (g1only, g2only); 5 and 6 are Y's primary cells (not counted twice)
#   3 replicates; seed = 20261300 + 10 * design index (P = 1, M = 2, B = 3, S = 4, W = 5, Z = 6, Y = 7) + rep.
#   80 cells, 240 fits, 21 DISTINCT DATASETS. Data mgb_sim / mgb_sim_y unchanged: beta = 0.4 in BOTH groups, so the
#   absent group is deliberately misspecified (user; kept after the pilot).
# UNIT OF REPLICATION (user, 2026-10-11, option (a)): the dataset. Each is reused across levels and
# orientations/patterns (one-path: 8 fits per dataset; Y: 32). Every count below is reported as affected fits AND
# distinct affected datasets; results at different levels of one dataset are not independent. The gate can establish
# whether the implementation agrees with lavaan on these datasets and specifications; it cannot establish a precise
# population failure rate or broad robustness to sampling variation.
#
# Scopes and admission (orientation-specific):
#   S2 = one-path g2only cells + Y patterns 1, 2, 5      S1 = one-path g1only cells + Y patterns 3, 4, 6
#   SM = Y patterns 7, 8 (both orientations at once)
#   Admit g2only iff S2 PASSES; g1only iff S1 PASSES; a table carrying both orientations (on different paths) iff
#   S1, S2 and SM all PASS. Never admitted by this gate: G > 2; a beta fixed (nonzero) in one group and absent or
#   free in another; a beta free in one group and fixed nonzero in another.
#
# Rules per fit (bounds unchanged from mgb-infer-prereg / mgb-fixed-prereg):
#  P1  lavaan's df = Result B2 (mgb_df with mgb_nb summed per path), lavaan's npar = the table's, rank(Delta) = npar.
#  P2  sigma at lavaan's estimates within MG2_TOL_IMP = 1e-10 of lavaan's implied.
#  P3  every Delta column within MG2_TOL_LD = 1e-10 of lavaan's.
#  P3s in LAVAAN's Delta, each beta column is exactly 0 in every row of the group where that beta is absent.
#  H-I1 |T3 / chisq.scaled - 1| <= 1e-8.     H-I2 mg_rel(e(V), vcov) <= 1e-7.
#  H-I3 the zeroed-beta-threshold mutant (mgb_mut). Prediction, derived before the freeze: a beta column's threshold
#       entries are lambda times the mean of its predictor factor in the beta's own group. Those means are 0 except in
#       group 2 at the scalar level (alpha_2 free; for Y's path 3<-2 the predictor mean is alpha_2 + beta alpha_1).
#       So: MOVES (vcov changes by > MGB_TOL_MUT = 1e-4 and T3 stays within 1e-8) iff level = scalar and a beta is
#       present in group 2; otherwise VACUOUS (vcov within 1e-7). In particular scalar g1only (one-path, and Y
#       pattern 6) is vacuous: the only beta column has nonzero entries in group 1's rows only, where every factor
#       mean is fixed at 0. A predicted no-change is not a failed control; a deviation either way is a FAILURE.
#  N1  inject each absent beta, at the present group's estimate, into the absent group's B (a fixed row; theta and
#      every other row unchanged); the absent group's sigma must move by more than MGBA_MARGIN = 1e-2 (max abs).
#      Motivation, not proof: at the generating values a cross-factor polychoric moves by at least
#      0.59 * 0.71 * 0.4 ~ 0.17 in group 1; N3 makes the change exact per fit.
#  N2  the injection leaves the present group's sigma and Delta rows unchanged, within 1e-10.
#  N3  (one-path designs) the observed sigma change in the absent group equals the closed form within 1e-10: with b
#      the injected value and psi_11, alpha_1 the absent group's: correlations of an F1 item j and an F2 item k move by
#      om_j om_k lam_j lam_k b psi_11, of two F2 items by om_j om_k lam_j lam_k b^2 psi_11, of two F1 items by 0;
#      an F2 item's threshold moves by -om_j lam_j b alpha_1 (zero unless alpha_1 is free). Y is covered by N1 and N2.
#  Boundary (reported, not a criterion): min Theta* over both groups at lavaan's estimates.
# Unusable / failure / outcome: U1-U4 of mgb-infer-prereg, per scope. A scope PASSES iff it has no FAILURE and every
# cell in it has at least one usable fit; FAILED if any failure; otherwise NOT ESTABLISHED.
MGBA_MARGIN <- 1e-2
MGBA_DI <- setNames(seq_along(mgbp_dn), mgbp_dn)
mgba_cells <- function() {
  out <- list()
  for (dn in setdiff(mgbp_dn, "Y")) for (l in MGB_LEVELS) for (o in c("g2only", "g1only"))
    out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- list(dn = dn, level = l, pat = o, beta = o, paths = list(c(2L, 1L)),
                                    scope = if (o == "g2only") "S2" else "S1")
  ypat <- list("1" = c("g2only", "free"), "2" = c("free", "g2only"), "3" = c("g1only", "free"),
               "4" = c("free", "g1only"), "5" = c("g2only", "g2only"), "6" = c("g1only", "g1only"),
               "7" = c("g2only", "g1only"), "8" = c("g1only", "g2only"))
  for (l in MGB_LEVELS) for (pn in names(ypat))
    out[[length(out) + 1L]] <- list(dn = "Y", level = l, pat = paste0("Y", pn), beta = ypat[[pn]],
                                    paths = MGB_YPATHS, scope = c(S2 = "125", S1 = "346", SM = "78") |>
                                      (\(s) names(s)[grepl(pn, s, fixed = TRUE)])())
  stopifnot(length(out) == 80L)
  out
}
# The absent group's beta rows, injected at the present group's estimate (a fixed row added; fidx unchanged).
mgba_inject <- function(tab, th) {
  R <- tab$rows; base <- R[, c("g", "type", "i", "j", "free", "val", "tie")]; add <- base[0, ]
  for (r in which(R$type == "beta")) {
    ga <- 3L - R$g[r]
    if (!any(R$type == "beta" & R$g == ga & R$i == R$i[r] & R$j == R$j[r]))
      add <- rbind(add, mg2_row(ga, "beta", R$i[r], R$j[r], free = FALSE, val = th[R$fidx[r]]))
  }
  t2 <- mg2_table(tab$K, tab$m, rbind(base, add))
  stopifnot(t2$npar == tab$npar, identical(t2$rows$fidx[seq_len(nrow(R))], R$fidx))
  list(tab = t2, groups = unique(add$g))
}
mgba_one <- function(ce, rep) {
  d <- MGB_DESIGNS[[ce$dn]]; seed <- 20261300L + 10L * MGBA_DI[[ce$dn]] + rep
  base <- data.frame(design = ce$dn, level = ce$level, pattern = ce$pat, scope = ce$scope, rep = rep, seed = seed,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  dat <- tryCatch(if (ce$dn == "Y") mgb_sim_y(d$K, d$fac, seed = seed) else mgb_sim(d$K, d$fac, seed = seed),
                  error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(dat, "error"))
    return(cbind(base, status = if (grepl("== K[j]", conditionMessage(dat), fixed = TRUE)) "UNUSABLE" else "FAILURE",
                 reason = paste("data:", conditionMessage(dat))))
  tryCatch({
    r <- mgb_fit(dat, d$K, d$fac, ce$level, ce$beta, ce$paths)
    if (!isTRUE(r$conv)) return(cbind(base, status = "UNUSABLE", reason = "lavaan did not converge"))
    tab <- mgb_table(d$K, d$fac, ce$level, ce$beta, ce$paths); fit <- r$fit
    th <- mgb_from_lavaan(tab, fit); mp <- mgb_lav_map(tab, fit); imp <- mg2_lav_implied(fit)
    off <- mg2_off(tab); Dg <- mg2_Dg(tab); grow <- function(g) off[g] + seq_len(Dg[g])
    p1 <- as.integer(r$df) == mgb_df(d$K, d$fac, ce$level, mgb_nb(ce$beta, length(ce$paths))) &&
          as.integer(r$npar) == tab$npar && inv_rank(r$delta) == tab$npar
    gap_imp <- max(abs(mg2_sigma(tab, th) - imp))
    Dl <- do.call(rbind, lavTech(fit, "delta")); gap_d <- max(abs(mg2_dcols(tab, th)[, mp$m] - Dl))
    rl <- mp$fr_rows[mp$m]                                                       # our row of lavaan's column k
    p3s <- all(vapply(which(tab$rows$type[rl] == "beta"), function(k) all(Dl[grow(3L - tab$rows$g[rl[k]]), k] == 0), NA))
    # H-I1, H-I2, H-I3 exactly as mgb-infer-prereg
    inf <- function(mutate = NULL) {
      pp <- mg_parts(fit); D <- mg2_delta(tab, th); if (!is.null(mutate)) D <- mutate(D, tab)
      Dgl <- lapply(1:2, function(g) D[grow(g), , drop = FALSE])
      po <- mg_pool(pp$Gam, Dgl, pp$wv, pp$n_g); stopifnot(po$Dtot == pp$Dtot, po$q == tab$npar)
      ab <- mg_ab(mg_traces_q(po), po$Dtot - po$q)
      Tc <- mg_Tcand(pp); hit <- names(Tc)[abs(Tc / fit@test$standard$stat - 1) < 1e-9]
      stopifnot(identical(hit, mg_T_convention[["h1"]]))
      S <- matrix(0, mp$nfree, tab$npar); S[cbind(seq_len(mp$nfree), tab$rows$fidx[mp$fr_rows][mp$m])] <- 1
      c(T3 = abs((ab[["a"]] * Tc[[hit]] + ab[["b"]]) / unname(fitMeasures(fit, "chisq.scaled")) - 1),
        V = mg_rel(S %*% (mg_acov(po) / (po$N - po$G)) %*% t(S), unname(vcov(fit))))
    }
    m0 <- inf(); m1 <- inf(mgb_mut)
    moves <- ce$level == "scalar" && any(tab$rows$type == "beta" & tab$rows$g == 2L)
    hi3 <- if (moves) m1[["V"]] > MGB_TOL_MUT && m1[["T3"]] <= MGB_TOL_T3 else m1[["V"]] <= MGB_TOL_V
    # N1-N3
    ij <- mgba_inject(tab, th); s0 <- mg2_sigma(tab, th); s1 <- mg2_sigma(ij$tab, th)
    ga <- ij$groups; gp <- setdiff(1:2, ga)
    n1 <- max(abs(s1 - s0)[unlist(lapply(ga, grow))])
    n2 <- if (length(gp)) max(abs((s1 - s0)[unlist(lapply(gp, grow))]),
                              abs(mg2_delta(ij$tab, th) - mg2_delta(tab, th))[unlist(lapply(gp, grow)), ]) else 0
    n3 <- NA_real_
    if (ce$dn != "Y") {
      P <- mg2_pars(tab, th)[[ga]]; b <- th[tab$rows$fidx[tab$rows$type == "beta"]]; fac <- d$fac; p <- length(fac)
      lam <- rowSums(P$Lam); om <- P$om; ps1 <- P$Psi[1, 1]; a1 <- P$al[1]
      dR <- outer(seq_len(p), seq_len(p), function(j, k) om[j] * om[k] * lam[j] * lam[k] *
              ifelse(fac[j] != fac[k], b * ps1, ifelse(fac[j] == 2L, b^2 * ps1, 0)))
      itm <- rep(seq_len(p), d$K - 1L)
      dT <- ifelse(fac[itm] == 2L, -om[itm] * lam[itm] * b * a1, 0)
      n3 <- max(abs((s1 - s0)[grow(ga)] - c(dT, dR[lower.tri(dR)])))
    }
    tmin <- min(unlist(mg2_thetastar(tab, th)))
    pre_ok <- p1 && gap_imp < MG2_TOL_IMP && gap_d < MG2_TOL_LD && p3s
    hi_ok <- m0[["T3"]] <= MGB_TOL_T3 && m0[["V"]] <= MGB_TOL_V && hi3
    neg_ok <- n1 > MGBA_MARGIN && n2 <= MG2_TOL_IMP && (is.na(n3) || n3 <= MG2_TOL_IMP)
    cbind(base, status = if (pre_ok && hi_ok && neg_ok) "PASS" else "FAILURE",
          reason = if (!pre_ok) "precondition P1-P3s" else if (!hi_ok) "H-I bound" else if (!neg_ok) "negative control" else "",
          df_ok = p1, gap_imp = gap_imp, gap_delta = gap_d, p3s = p3s, T3 = m0[["T3"]], V = m0[["V"]],
          h3_moves = moves, V_mut = m1[["V"]], n1 = n1, n2 = n2, n3 = n3, min_thetastar = tmin)
  }, error = function(e) cbind(base, status = "FAILURE", reason = paste("error:", conditionMessage(e))))
}
mgba_cols <- c("df_ok", "gap_imp", "gap_delta", "p3s", "T3", "V", "h3_moves", "V_mut", "n1", "n2", "n3", "min_thetastar")
mgba <- do.call(rbind, lapply(mgba_cells(), function(ce) do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(rep) {
  x <- mgba_one(ce, rep); for (v in mgba_cols) if (is.null(x[[v]])) x[[v]] <- NA; x }))))
rownames(mgba) <- NULL; mgba$dataset <- paste(mgba$design, mgba$seed); print(mgba, digits = 3)
stopifnot(nrow(mgba) == 240L, length(unique(mgba$dataset)) == 21L)
mgba_count <- function(rows) sprintf("%d fit(s), %d dataset(s)", sum(rows), length(unique(mgba$dataset[rows])))
mgba_scope <- function(sc) {
  x <- mgba[mgba$scope == sc, ]; cells <- aggregate(status ~ design + level + pattern, x, function(s) sum(s == "PASS"))
  out <- if (any(x$status == "FAILURE")) "FAILED" else if (any(cells$status == 0L)) "NOT ESTABLISHED" else "PASSED"
  cat(sprintf("scope %s: %s ; cells %d ; usable %s ; unusable %s ; failures %s\n", sc, out, nrow(cells),
      mgba_count(mgba$scope == sc & mgba$status != "UNUSABLE"), mgba_count(mgba$scope == sc & mgba$status == "UNUSABLE"),
      mgba_count(mgba$scope == sc & mgba$status == "FAILURE")))
  out
}
mgba_out <- vapply(c("S2", "S1", "SM"), mgba_scope, "")
cat("boundary (reported only): ", mgba_count((mgba$min_thetastar <= 0) %in% TRUE), "\n")
cat("ADMIT g2only:", mgba_out[["S2"]] == "PASSED", "; g1only:", mgba_out[["S1"]] == "PASSED",
    "; both orientations in one table:", all(mgba_out == "PASSED"), "\n")
```

## Gate 1: the sample-statistic index map {#sec-gate1}

Every other gate produced mathematics. This one produces an *object* — the
table that says what each element of $s$ is, and where it sits in $s$, in
$\Gamma$ and in $\Delta$. It is the least interesting gate and the one whose
errors are hardest to see, because an index error does not crash: it silently
compares the wrong pair of statistics and reports a tolerance failure that
looks like a numerical problem.

The ordering itself was settled in §4.2 and verified against lavaan. What is
open is the arithmetic: given the ordering, where does a given statistic live?

### The forward map

Let there be $p$ observed variables, variable $j$ having $K_j$ categories and
therefore $C_j = K_j - 1$ thresholds. Write $T = \sum_{j=1}^p C_j$ for the
total number of thresholds and $P = \binom{p}{2}$ for the number of pairs, so
that $s$ has length $D_s = T + P$.

Thresholds come first, grouped by variable, ascending within variable:

$$
\text{pos}(\tau_{jc}) \;=\; \sum_{m<j} C_m \;+\; c ,
\qquad c = 1,\dots,C_j .
$$

Correlations follow, in column-major lower-triangle order. For a pair $(i,j)$
with $i<j$,

$$
\text{pos}(\rho_{ij}) \;=\; T \;+\; \underbrace{(i-1)p - \tfrac{i(i-1)}{2}}_{\text{pairs with first index } <\, i} \;+\; (j-i).
$$

Both are $O(1)$ given a prefix-sum of $C$, so no Mata routine ever searches the
table to find a position. That matters more than it looks: Module 4 asks for a
position once per $\Gamma$ entry, and $\Gamma$ is $D_s \times D_s$.

### The inverse map

Going the other way — position $\to$ identity — is needed only for
diagnostics, but it is what turns a tolerance failure into a sentence a human
can read ("worst cell is `y2|t1` against `y3~~y4`"), so it is worth having
exactly rather than approximately.

For $s \le T$ the answer is a lookup in the prefix-sum of $C$. For the
correlation block, with $r = s - T$, the first index $i$ is the smallest
integer satisfying $ip - \tfrac{i(i+1)}{2} \ge r$, which solves in closed form:

$$
i \;=\; \left\lceil \frac{(2p-1) - \sqrt{(2p-1)^2 - 8r}}{2} \right\rceil ,
\qquad
j \;=\; r - \left[(i-1)p - \tfrac{i(i-1)}{2}\right] + i .
$$

A ceiling applied to a floating-point square root is normally a thing to
distrust — if the argument lands a hair below an integer the result is wrong by
one, and the failure is off-by-one in a diagnostic, which is worse than no
diagnostic. Here it is safe, and for a structural reason rather than by luck.
At a block boundary, $r = ip - \tfrac{i(i+1)}{2}$, and substituting gives

$$
(2p-1)^2 - 8r \;=\; (2p - 2i - 1)^2 ,
$$

a perfect square of an odd integer. So at exactly the points where the ceiling
could tip, the square root is of an exactly representable integer square and is
computed exactly. Verified below for all $p \le 500$.

### Verification

Three properties, over the four fixture designs plus four shapes the fixtures
do not cover (a single variable; twelve binary variables; two 9-threshold
variables; and a ragged six-variable design):

1. the closed forms reproduce, entry for entry, the ordering built by
   construction — which is the ordering already verified against
   `lavInspect(fit, "gamma")`;
2. the map is a bijection onto $1,\dots,D_s$ — no gaps, no collisions;
3. the inverse round-trips from every position, and the identity it recovers
   matches the label at that position.

```{r gate1-index-map}
#| cache: true

# Reference ordering, built by construction: slow, and obviously correct.
ref_labels <- function(C) {
  p   <- length(C)
  tau <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(p), function(j) sprintf("y%d|t%d", j, seq_len(C[j]))))
  ij  <- which(lower.tri(matrix(0, p, p)), arr.ind = TRUE)
  ij  <- ij[order(ij[, "col"], ij[, "row"]), , drop = FALSE]
  c(tau, sprintf("y%d~~y%d", ij[, "col"], ij[, "row"]))
}

pos_tau <- function(C, j, c) sum(C[seq_len(j - 1L)]) + c

pos_rho <- function(C, i, j) {                    # requires i < j
  p <- length(C)
  sum(C) + (i - 1L) * p - i * (i - 1L) / 2L + (j - i)
}

inv_pos <- function(C, s) {
  p <- length(C); T <- sum(C)
  if (s <= T) {
    cum <- cumsum(C)
    j   <- which(s <= cum)[1]
    return(list(type = "threshold", i = j, k = s - if (j > 1) cum[j - 1] else 0))
  }
  r <- s - T
  i <- ceiling(((2 * p - 1) - sqrt((2 * p - 1)^2 - 8 * r)) / 2)
  list(type = "polychoric", i = i,
       j = r - ((i - 1) * p - i * (i - 1) / 2) + i)
}

DESIGNS <- list(
  A = c(1, 1), B = c(1, 1, 1), C = c(2, 2), D = c(3, 3, 2, 2),   # the fixtures
  E = c(1), F = c(5, 1, 3, 2, 4, 1), G = rep(1, 12), H = c(9, 9) # stress shapes
)

report <- data.frame()
for (nm in names(DESIGNS)) {
  C <- DESIGNS[[nm]]; p <- length(C); Tt <- sum(C); D <- Tt + p * (p - 1) / 2
  lab <- ref_labels(C)

  built <- character(D)
  for (j in seq_len(p)) for (k in seq_len(C[j]))
    built[pos_tau(C, j, k)] <- sprintf("y%d|t%d", j, k)
  if (p > 1) for (i in 1:(p - 1)) for (j in (i + 1):p)
    built[pos_rho(C, i, j)] <- sprintf("y%d~~y%d", i, j)

  ok_order  <- identical(built, lab)
  ok_biject <- !any(built == "") && length(unique(built)) == D

  ok_inv <- TRUE
  for (s in seq_len(D)) {
    z    <- inv_pos(C, s)
    back <- if (z$type == "threshold") pos_tau(C, z$i, z$k) else pos_rho(C, z$i, z$j)
    want <- if (z$type == "threshold") sprintf("y%d|t%d", z$i, z$k)
            else                       sprintf("y%d~~y%d", z$i, z$j)
    if (back != s || want != lab[s]) ok_inv <- FALSE
  }

  report <- rbind(report, data.frame(design = nm, p = p, T = Tt, D = D,
                                     order = ok_order, bijection = ok_biject,
                                     inverse = ok_inv))
}
report
```

```{r gate1-discriminant}
#| cache: true

# The ceiling is safe because the discriminant at every block boundary is the
# perfect square (2p - 2i - 1)^2.
ok <- TRUE
for (p in 2:500) for (i in 1:(p - 1)) {
  r <- i * p - i * (i + 1) / 2
  if ((2 * p - 1)^2 - 8 * r != (2 * p - 2 * i - 1)^2) ok <- FALSE
}
cat("perfect-square identity holds at every boundary, p <= 500:", ok, "\n")

# And the ceiling itself agrees with a brute-force scan everywhere.
inv_i_closed <- function(p, r) ceiling(((2*p - 1) - sqrt((2*p - 1)^2 - 8*r)) / 2)
inv_i_scan   <- function(p, r) { i <- 1L; while (i*p - (i+1L)*i/2L < r) i <- i + 1L; i }
bad <- 0L; n <- 0L
for (p in 2:200) for (r in seq_len(p * (p - 1) / 2)) {
  n <- n + 1L
  if (inv_i_closed(p, r) != inv_i_scan(p, r)) bad <- bad + 1L
}
cat(sprintf("%d (p, r) combinations, %d disagreements with the scan\n", n, bad))
```

### The one design decision this forces

The map is keyed on $C$, the vector of per-variable threshold counts, and on
nothing else. It does not need the data, the estimates, or the model. That is
worth stating because it is what lets Module 0 build the map *before* Stage 1
runs, and lets every later module take the map as an input rather than
reconstructing it — reconstruction in two places being the classic way the two
copies drift apart.

It also means an empty interior category is not this object's problem. If a
category is unobserved, $C_j$ as *declared by the model* still governs the map;
what changes is that the corresponding row of $\Gamma$ is degenerate, which is
§4.5.6's concern and is caught by Module 10's rank check. Keeping those two
issues apart is deliberate: an index map that silently shrinks when a category
happens to be empty in one sample would make $\Gamma$ non-conformable with
$\Delta$ for reasons no error message would explain.

### What Gate 1 hands downstream

A `statmap` object with one row per element of $s$, carrying `stat_type`,
`var_i`, `var_j`, `thr_k`, the lavaan-style `label`, and the closed-form
accessors above. Modules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8 all take it as an input. The
labels are the harness's alignment key — §4.2 requires the comparison to be by
name and not by position, and this is the object that makes that possible.


## Module 8: the robust sandwich and its sample-size divisor {#sec-acov}

Not a gate — spec §4.10's formula was never in doubt — but three things Module 8
relies on were not written down anywhere: the conditions under which the sandwich
is the right covariance, an exact identity for its threshold block, and which
divisor turns it into `e(V)`. The first is standard; the second is a test oracle
that needs no reference software; the third is a convention, and is pinned here
against lavaan's source rather than assumed.

### The linearization

$\hat\theta$ minimises $F(\theta) = (s - \sigma(\theta))'\hat W(s - \sigma(\theta))$
with $\hat W = \operatorname{diag}(\hat\Gamma)^{-1}$ (spec convention: $W_D$, not
its inverse — see the notational trap in @sec-gate5). At the minimum,

$$\Delta(\hat\theta)'\hat W\,\big(s - \sigma(\hat\theta)\big) = 0.$$

Expand $\sigma(\hat\theta) = \sigma_0 + \Delta_0(\hat\theta - \theta_0) +
O_p(\lVert\hat\theta-\theta_0\rVert^2)$ about the true $\theta_0$, with
$\sigma_0 = \sigma(\theta_0)$ and $\Delta_0 = \Delta(\theta_0)$. Under a correctly
specified model $s - \sigma_0 = O_p(N^{-1/2})$, hence so is $\hat\theta - \theta_0$,
and three substitutions each cost only $O_p(N^{-1})$ because each multiplies
something already $O_p(N^{-1/2})$:

- $\Delta(\hat\theta) \to \Delta_0$;
- $\hat W \to W = \operatorname{diag}(\Gamma)^{-1}$, since $\hat W - W = O_p(N^{-1/2})$;
- the quadratic remainder of the expansion.

What is left is

$$\sqrt N(\hat\theta - \theta_0) = (\Delta_0'W\Delta_0)^{-1}\Delta_0'W\,
  \sqrt N(s - \sigma_0) + o_p(1)
  \;\xrightarrow{d}\; N(0,\ \operatorname{ACOV}),$$

$$\boxed{\;\operatorname{ACOV} = (\Delta'W\Delta)^{-1}\,\Delta'W\,\Gamma\,W\Delta\,
  (\Delta'W\Delta)^{-1}\;}$$

using §4.4's $\sqrt N(s-\sigma_0) \to N(0,\Gamma)$. Estimated by plugging in the
sign-canonicalized $\hat\theta$'s $\Delta$ and the stored $\hat\Gamma$.

**Two scope statements the derivation makes, not merely permits.**

*The bread is the expected information $\Delta'W\Delta$*, not the Hessian of $F$.
The Hessian adds $-2\sum_k r_k W_{kk}\,\partial^2\sigma_k/\partial\theta\partial\theta'$
with $r = s - \sigma(\hat\theta)$; that term is $O_p(N^{-1/2})$ and drops out of the
limit, but not out of a finite sample. lavaan's default is `information =
"expected"`, and its fixture SEs depend on that — the `m8-lavaan` chunk below
measures how far `"observed"` moves them.

*Correct specification is assumed.* Under misspecification $s - \sigma_0$ does not
vanish ($\sigma_0$ is then a pseudo-true value), so neither the estimation error in
$\hat W$ nor the second-derivative term drops out. Neither v1 nor lavaan's
`robust.sem` includes them. That is a property of the estimator both implement,
and an honest limit of the reported SEs, not a discrepancy between the two.

### The threshold block is $\Gamma_{\tau\tau}$ exactly

Partition $\theta = (\tau, \omega)$, thresholds first per spec §4.8, and
$s = (s_\tau, s_\rho)$. In v1 every threshold is a free parameter of its own and
$\sigma_\tau(\theta) = \tau$, while thresholds do not enter the population
polychoric (@sec-gate2, Finding 2). So $\Delta$ is block diagonal with an
**identity** threshold block (Finding 3):

$$\Delta = \begin{pmatrix} I_T & 0 \\ 0 & \Delta_\omega \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad W = \begin{pmatrix} W_\tau & 0 \\ 0 & W_\rho \end{pmatrix}
  \ \text{(diagonal)},$$

$$\Delta'W\Delta = \begin{pmatrix} W_\tau & 0 \\ 0 & \Delta_\omega'W_\rho\Delta_\omega
  \end{pmatrix},\qquad
  (\Delta'W\Delta)^{-1}\Delta'W = \begin{pmatrix} I_T & 0 \\ 0 & L \end{pmatrix}
  =: A,\quad L = (\Delta_\omega'W_\rho\Delta_\omega)^{-1}\Delta_\omega'W_\rho .$$

Then $\operatorname{ACOV} = A\,\Gamma A'$, block by block:

$$\boxed{\;\operatorname{ACOV}_{\tau\tau} = \Gamma_{\tau\tau},\qquad
  \operatorname{ACOV}_{\omega\tau} = L\,\Gamma_{\rho\tau},\qquad
  \operatorname{ACOV}_{\omega\omega} = L\,\Gamma_{\rho\rho}L'\;}$$

Three consequences, each checkable without reference software:

1. **Threshold SEs are $\sqrt{\operatorname{diag}(\Gamma_{\tau\tau})/(N-1)}$** under
   the divisor below — no $\Delta$, no weight, no model. $W_\tau$ cancels
   entirely. A structural parameter has no influence on a threshold's SE, which
   is exactly what a saturated threshold block should give.
2. **$\operatorname{ACOV}_{\omega\omega}$ does not depend on $\Gamma_{\tau\tau}$ or
   $\Gamma_{\tau\rho}$.** The structural parameters' SEs see only the correlation
   block of Γ. Perturbing the threshold rows of Γ must leave them unchanged.
3. **The identity is exact in production, not approximate.** `dwlsmv_delta_cols()`
   writes the threshold block as a literal identity and leaves the off-diagonal
   blocks at literal zero (`test_delta.do` check 1 asserts both at exactly 0.0);
   only $\Delta_\omega$ carries central-difference noise. So a failure of
   $\operatorname{ACOV}_{\tau\tau} = \Gamma_{\tau\tau}$ beyond the sandwich's own
   floating-point budget is a coding error.

`dwlsmv_acov()` should nevertheless compute the general formula, not this
factorization: the identity is the oracle, and an implementation built on it
could not be tested by it.

### The divisor: $e(V) = \operatorname{ACOV}/(N-1)$

The limit fixes ACOV, not the divisor: $\operatorname{ACOV}/N$ and
$\operatorname{ACOV}/(N-1)$ are equally valid estimates of $\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta)$.
**$N - 1$ is a compatibility convention and not a result** — the same status, and
the same choice, as $T = (N-1)F$ in @sec-gate5.

It is read from lavaan 0.7.2's source, not inferred from its output:
`lav_model_vcov()` divides the $N$-scaled sandwich by `ntotal - ngroups` for every
estimator other than normal-likelihood ML; and `lav_samp_from_data()` builds Γ as
$N$ times the Muthén (1984) weight matrix, applying the $N/(N-1)$ factor only when
`gamma.n.minus.one = TRUE`, which it is not by default. The weight is
`WLS.VD = 1/diag(Γ)`, and `lav_model_nvcov_robust_sem()` assembles
$E^{-1}\Delta'W\Gamma W\Delta E^{-1}$ with $E = \Delta'W\Delta$.

**What the fixtures can and cannot pin.** "Γ, then $/(N-1)$" and
"$\Gamma\cdot N/(N-1)$, then $/N$" are the same number, so lavaan's SEs pin only
the product; which of the two lavaan does is known from the code above. For this
project the split is not a choice: Γ is already fixed by Module 4, which matches
`lavInspect(fit, "gamma")` at 1.4e-13, so the divisor is what remains. The
alternative, $/N$, misses lavaan by exactly $\sqrt{N/(N-1)} - 1$ in every SE —
$1.0\times10^{-4}$ at $N = 5000$, *inside* spec §7.2's SE tier as it stood until
2026-09-24. No tolerance then would surface it; the current $10^{-5}$ tier does. Module 8's test must therefore require $/(N-1)$ and reject $/N$, the
pattern `test_fit.do` check 5 uses for $T$.

### Verification

**Level 1 — the block identity, on synthetic inputs.** Pure linear algebra, so any
conformable Γ and $\Delta_\omega$ exercise it. Γ is built as an outer product, as
production builds it, so that its threshold rows can be perturbed while its
correlation block is held fixed.

```{r m8-L1}
sandwich <- function(Dl, Gm) {                  # spec 4.10, general form
  w  <- 1 / diag(Gm)                            # W_D kept a vector
  WD <- w * Dl
  Bi <- solve(crossprod(Dl, WD))
  Bi %*% crossprod(WD, Gm %*% WD) %*% Bi
}

set.seed(808)
Tn <- 6; Dr <- 6; q <- 4; n <- 400            # T thresholds, rho stats, omega params
Psi <- matrix(rnorm(n * (Tn + Dr)), n)
Psi[, Tn + 1:Dr] <- Psi[, Tn + 1:Dr] + Psi[, 1:Dr] %*% diag(0.4, Dr)  # tau-rho coupling
Gm  <- crossprod(Psi) / n
Dom <- matrix(rnorm(Dr * q), Dr, q)
Dl  <- rbind(cbind(diag(Tn), matrix(0, Tn, q)),
             cbind(matrix(0, Dr, Tn), Dom))
tt  <- 1:Tn; oo <- Tn + 1:q; rr <- Tn + 1:Dr

V   <- sandwich(Dl, Gm)
Wr  <- 1 / diag(Gm)[rr]
L   <- solve(crossprod(Dom, Wr * Dom)) %*% t(Wr * Dom)

Psi2 <- Psi; Psi2[, tt] <- matrix(rnorm(n * Tn), n) * 3   # new threshold rows only
Gm2  <- crossprod(Psi2) / n
V2   <- sandwich(Dl, Gm2)

rel <- function(a, b) max(abs(a - b)) / max(abs(b))
data.frame(
  check = c("ACOV_tautau vs Gamma_tautau",
            "ACOV_omegatau vs L Gamma_rhotau",
            "ACOV_omegaomega vs L Gamma_rhorho L'",
            "ACOV_omegaomega moved by perturbing Gamma's tau rows",
            "Gamma_rhorho moved by that perturbation (must be 0)",
            "Gamma_taurho moved by that perturbation (must be large)",
            "ACOV_tautau moved by that perturbation (must be large)",
            "asymmetry of ACOV",
            "min eigenvalue of ACOV"),
  value = signif(c(rel(V[tt, tt], Gm[tt, tt]),
                   rel(V[oo, tt], L %*% Gm[rr, tt]),
                   rel(V[oo, oo], L %*% Gm[rr, rr] %*% t(L)),
                   max(abs(V2[oo, oo] - V[oo, oo])),
                   max(abs(Gm2[rr, rr] - Gm[rr, rr])),
                   max(abs(Gm2[tt, rr] - Gm[tt, rr])),
                   max(abs(V2[tt, tt] - V[tt, tt])),
                   max(abs(V - t(V))),
                   min(eigen(V, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values)), 3))
```

Read the perturbation rows together. The three control rows say what the
perturbation did: it left $\Gamma_{\rho\rho}$ exactly alone and changed both
$\Gamma_{\tau\rho}$ and $\Gamma_{\tau\tau}$ substantially (the latter visible through
$\operatorname{ACOV}_{\tau\tau}$). The row above them is the claim:
$\operatorname{ACOV}_{\omega\omega}$ did not notice. Without the controls a zero
there could mean the perturbation missed.

**Level 2 — the sandwich is the sampling covariance, by Monte Carlo.** Level 1
proves algebra; this proves the linearization, which is the only claim above that
is asymptotic. The reference is the Monte Carlo standard deviation of $\hat\theta$
across replications — the §7.3 approach, one level up — judged per parameter by a
$z$ statistic against the SD's own Monte Carlo error, never by percentage. As a
contrast that must fail, the "optimal-weight" standard error
$\sqrt{\operatorname{diag}((\Delta'W\Delta)^{-1})/(N-1)}$ — correct only if $W$
were $\Gamma^{-1}$ — is carried alongside.

The estimates come from lavaan, so this checks the formula against the estimator's
actual sampling behaviour, not against lavaan's SE code: the SEs are rebuilt from
lavaan's $\Delta$ and Γ with the `sandwich()` above. What it cannot do is resolve
the divisor — $N$ against $N-1$ is 0.05% at $N = 1000$, far below a Monte Carlo SD's
2% resolution at this replication count. That is Level 3's job.

```{r m8-L2}
#| cache: true
library(lavaan)
set.seed(8008)
R <- 1000; nMC <- 1000; lam <- 0.7
thB <- list(qnorm(cumsum(c(.15, .35, .30, .20))[-4]),     # the running designs,
            qnorm(cumsum(c(.40, .35, .25))[-3]))          # restated to stand alone
thr <- list(thB[[1]], thB[[1]], thB[[2]], thB[[2]])

one <- function() {
  f  <- rnorm(nMC)
  d  <- as.data.frame(lapply(1:4, function(j)
          ordered(findInterval(lam * f + sqrt(1 - lam^2) * rnorm(nMC), thr[[j]]),
                  levels = 0:length(thr[[j]]))))
  names(d) <- paste0("y", 1:4)
  fit <- sem("f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", data = d, ordered = names(d),
             estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta")
  Dl <- lavTech(fit, "delta")[[1]]; Gm <- lavTech(fit, "gamma")[[1]]
  c(coef(fit),
    sqrt(diag(sandwich(Dl, Gm)) / (nMC - 1)),
    sqrt(diag(solve(crossprod(Dl, (1 / diag(Gm)) * Dl))) / (nMC - 1)))
}
sims <- t(replicate(R, one()))
np   <- ncol(sims) / 3
est  <- sims[, 1:np]; seS <- sims[, np + 1:np]; seO <- sims[, 2 * np + 1:np]

sdE  <- apply(est, 2, sd)
zof  <- function(se) (colMeans(se) - sdE) /
          sqrt(sdE^2 / (2 * (R - 1)) + apply(se, 2, var) / R)
crit <- qnorm(1 - 0.01 / (2 * np))            # Bonferroni, 1% family-wise
data.frame(param = colnames(est), mc_sd = signif(sdE, 4),
           sandwich = signif(colMeans(seS), 4), z_sandwich = round(zof(seS), 2),
           optimal_W = signif(colMeans(seO), 4), z_optimal = round(zof(seO), 2))
c(max_abs_z_sandwich = max(abs(zof(seS))), max_abs_z_optimal = max(abs(zof(seO))),
  criterion = crit)
```

The criterion is fixed before looking: $\max|z|$ over the free parameters against a
1% family-wise Bonferroni bound. The optimal-weight contrast can only fail on the
structural rows: on the threshold rows it *equals* the sandwich, because
$(\Delta'W\Delta)^{-1}_{\tau\tau} = W_\tau^{-1} = \operatorname{diag}(\Gamma_{\tau\tau})$,
which is $\operatorname{ACOV}_{\tau\tau}$'s diagonal — the block identity again, from
a direction nobody arranged. The contrast is informative exactly where
$W_\rho \ne \Gamma_{\rho\rho}^{-1}$ matters.

**Level 3 — lavaan's implementation, from its own objects.** On the committed
`case_D` data and the exact tier-2 call of `fixtures/generate/20_lavaan_reference.R`,
rebuild the sandwich from lavaan's own $\Delta$, `WLS.VD` and Γ and compare with
`lavTech(fit, "vcov")` and with the committed fixture SEs under each candidate
divisor. It also confirms the Level 1 identity on real inputs — lavaan's threshold
SEs against $\sqrt{\operatorname{diag}(\Gamma_{\tau\tau})/(N-1)}$ with no $\Delta$ at
all — and measures what `information = "observed"` would have changed.

```{r m8-lavaan}
#| cache: true
library(lavaan)
root <- file.path("..", "..")
dat  <- read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "data", "case_D.csv"))
dat[] <- lapply(dat, ordered)
fitD <- function(...) sem("f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", data = dat, ordered = names(dat),
                          estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta",
                          test = "scaled.shifted", zero.add = c(0.5, 0.0), ...)
fit <- fitD()
N   <- lavInspect(fit, "nobs")
Dl  <- lavTech(fit, "delta")[[1]]
Gm  <- unclass(lavInspect(fit, "gamma"))           # labelled; values = lavTech's
stopifnot(max(abs(Gm - lavTech(fit, "gamma")[[1]])) == 0)
V_l <- lavTech(fit, "vcov")

pt   <- parTable(fit); fr <- pt[pt$free > 0, ]; fr <- fr[order(fr$free), ]
labs <- paste0(fr$lhs, fr$op, fr$rhs)
fx   <- read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "expected", "lavaan_case_D_parameters.csv"),
                 colClasses = "character")
se_fx <- as.numeric(fx$se[match(labs, fx$label)])     # full precision, never float-typed
stopifnot(!anyNA(se_fx))

nV   <- sandwich(Dl, Gm)
relS <- function(se) max(abs(se - se_fx) / se_fx)
isT  <- fr$op == "|"
thl  <- paste0(fr$lhs, "|", fr$rhs)[isT]             # Gamma's labels for those rows

fo <- fitD(information = "observed")
se_e <- parameterEstimates(fit)$se; se_o <- parameterEstimates(fo)$se; ok <- se_e > 0

data.frame(
  check = c("WLS.VD vs 1/diag(Gamma), max abs",
            "sandwich/(N-1) vs lavTech vcov, rel to max entry",
            "SE: sandwich/(N-1) vs fixture, max rel",
            "SE: sandwich/N     vs fixture, max rel",
            "sqrt(N/(N-1)) - 1",
            "threshold SE vs sqrt(diag Gamma_tautau/(N-1)), max rel",
            "threshold ACOV block vs Gamma_tautau, rel to max entry",
            "information = observed vs expected, max rel SE"),
  value = signif(c(max(abs(fit@SampleStats@WLS.VD[[1]] - 1 / diag(Gm))),
                   max(abs(nV / (N - 1) - V_l)) / max(abs(V_l)),
                   relS(sqrt(diag(nV) / (N - 1))),
                   relS(sqrt(diag(nV) / N)),
                   sqrt(N / (N - 1)) - 1,
                   max(abs(se_fx[isT] - sqrt(diag(Gm)[thl] / (N - 1))) / se_fx[isT]),
                   max(abs(nV[isT, isT] - Gm[thl, thl])) / max(abs(Gm[thl, thl])),
                   max(abs(se_o - se_e)[ok] / se_e[ok])), 3))
```

lavaan orders its free parameters loadings-first, not thresholds-first, so the
threshold rows are selected by operator and Γ's rows by label — never by position.

### What the verification shows

Executed 2026-09-23 under R 4.6.0 and lavaan 0.7.2 by extracting these three chunks
with `knitr::purl` and running them from this directory; the document as a whole
was not re-rendered, since Quarto is not installed on the development machine.

- **Level 1.** All three block identities hold to 1.1e-16 – 4.6e-16 relative.
  $\operatorname{ACOV}_{\omega\omega}$ moved by exactly 0 when Γ's threshold rows
  were replaced, while the controls show that perturbation left $\Gamma_{\rho\rho}$
  at exactly 0 change and moved $\Gamma_{\tau\rho}$ by 0.66 and
  $\operatorname{ACOV}_{\tau\tau}$ by 8.4.
- **Level 2.** Over 1000 replications at $N = 1000$, the sandwich's $\max|z|$ is
  2.27 against a criterion of 3.38; the optimal-weight contrast fails at 6.22, on a
  loading. Its threshold rows coincide with the sandwich's to every printed digit,
  as predicted above.
- **Level 3.** The sandwich rebuilt from lavaan's objects matches `lavTech(fit,
  "vcov")` to 4.9e-15 and the committed fixture SEs to 3.1e-15 under $/(N-1)$; under
  $/N$ it misses by 1.00e-4, which is $\sqrt{N/(N-1)} - 1$ to the printed digits.
  lavaan's threshold SEs equal $\sqrt{\operatorname{diag}(\Gamma_{\tau\tau})/(N-1)}$
  to 2.7e-15 with no $\Delta$ involved, and the threshold block of the sandwich
  equals $\Gamma_{\tau\tau}$ to 9.2e-17. `information = "observed"` would have moved
  the SEs by up to 3.0e-3 relative, so the expected-information bread is not a
  detail. *Corrected 2026-09-24:* this first said "three times spec §7.2's SE
  tier". The tier is $10^{-4}$ absolute plus $10^{-3}$ relative, and for SEs near
  0.02 the absolute term dominates, making it ~0.5% relative; `test_acov.do`'s
  end-to-end check passes case D under observed information. The information
  type is pinned by the check fed lavaan's own inputs, at $10^{-12}$.

The floor in Level 3 is the fixture, not the arithmetic: `write.csv` keeps 15
significant digits.

### What Module 8 needs

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| $\Delta$ at the canonical $\hat\theta$ | `fit.Delta` (Module 7) |
| $\hat\Gamma$, $N$-scaled, no $N/(N-1)$ | `fit.stage1.Gamma` (Module 4) |
| $W_D = \operatorname{diag}(\Gamma)^{-1}$ | re-formed as a vector; never stored |
| $N$ | `fit.stage1.N` |

`dwlsmv_acov(Delta, Gamma)` returns the boxed ACOV and nothing else;
`dwlsmv_ev(ACOV, N)` returns $\operatorname{ACOV}/(N-1)$ and nothing else. The tests
this section implies: the block identity at a floating-point budget (Level 1, on
our own inputs); the formula fed lavaan's own $\Delta$ and Γ against the fixture
SEs, tight (Level 3); end to end from our own $\hat\theta$ and $\hat\rho$, at the
tier those inherit; and the divisor in isolation, requiring $/(N-1)$ and rejecting
$/N$.


## Module 10: the rank of $\hat\Gamma$ {#sec-gamma-rank}

*Added 2026-09-24, before Module 10.* Module 10 must tell **exact** rank
deficiency, which has a cause that can be named, from **numerical**
ill-conditioning, which is the only thing a singular-value cutoff should
decide (E-054, *Rank-deficient Γ*). This section proves the
exact causes and measures the spectra. It does not choose a cutoff.

**Scope.** v1 only: ordinal and binary indicators. The argument uses the fact
that every $\psi$ column is a lookup on at most two *discrete* coordinates of
an observation. A continuous indicator breaks that at the first step, so the
bound must be re-derived for v2 rather than carried over.

**Notation.** $Y$ is the $N\times p$ matrix exactly as `dwls_sample_stats()`
receives it: after listwise deletion, restricted to the $p$ indicators whose
thresholds and polychorics make up $s$, in $K$'s column order, coded
$0,\dots,K_j-1$. A **pattern** is a row of that matrix, and $n_{\text{pat}}$ is
the number of distinct rows. Variables outside the $p$ indicators and rows
removed by listwise deletion do not count. A declared category that is never
observed would not count either, but it cannot reach this point:
`dwlsmv_thresholds()` aborts on an empty category. Patterns are written
$y^{(1)},\dots,y^{(n_{\text{pat}})}$, with counts $n_m \ge 1$ that sum to
$N$. Spec §4.2 already uses $P$ for the number of *pairs* (`map.P`), and that
is why this count is not called $P$.

### The pattern lemma

**Lemma 1.** There is a map $g:\{0..K_1-1\}\times\dots\times\{0..K_p-1\}\to\mathbb R^D$
with $\hat\psi_i = g(Y_i)$ for every $i$. It depends on the rest of the sample only
through sample-level constants: $\hat q$, $\hat\tau$, $\hat\rho$, and each pair's
$u$, $\hat I_{\rho\rho}$, $\hat I_{\rho a}$, $\hat I_{\rho b}$.

*Proof, read from the production code.* `dwlsmv_psi_matrix()` fills threshold
column $(j,c)$ with `psi_tau[koff[j] + Y[.,j] + 1, pos]`, a lookup in
`dwlsmv_psi_tau_table(q)` on $Y_{ij}$ alone. It fills correlation column
$(j,k)$ with `flat[Y[.,vi]*K2 + Y[.,vj] + 1]`, a lookup on $(Y_{ij},Y_{ik})$ in
`dwlsmv_psi_rho_table()`, whose entries are built from the pair fit and the
two staircases and from nothing indexed by $i$. No weight, row index, covariate
or other variable enters. $\square$

Stack the distinct rows of $\Psi$ as $G = [g(y^{(1)}),\dots,g(y^{(n_{\text{pat}})})]'$,
which is $n_{\text{pat}}\times D$, and let $E\in\{0,1\}^{N\times n_{\text{pat}}}$ be the
pattern incidence matrix. Then $\Psi = EG$, and production's uncentred
$\hat\Gamma = \Psi'\Psi/N$ (`dwls_gamma()`) is

$$\hat\Gamma = G'\,\operatorname{diag}(n_m/N)\,G,
\qquad \operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma = \operatorname{rank}G \le \min(D, n_{\text{pat}}).$$

### Centring, and what it buys

**Lemma 2.** In exact arithmetic,
$\bar\psi_\tau = 0$ and $\bar\psi_{\rho_{jk}} = S_{jk}(\hat\rho_{jk}) / (N\hat I_{\rho\rho})$,
where $S_{jk}(\rho) = \sum_{rs} n_{rs}u_{rs}(\rho)$ is the pair's score.

*Proof.* $\sum_i \mathbb 1\{Y_{ij}<c\} = N\hat q_{jc}$ by the definition of
$\hat q$, so every threshold column sums to zero. Averaging the boxed
$\psi_\rho$ of @sec-general over $i$ gives
$\hat I_{\rho\rho}^{-1}[N^{-1}\sum_i u_{r_is_i} - \sum_c \hat I_{\rho a_c}\bar\psi_{a_c}
- \sum_d \hat I_{\rho b_d}\bar\psi_{b_d}]$. The two propagation sums vanish
because $\bar\psi_\tau = 0$, whatever the weight $W$ used for $\hat I$.
$\square$

The same step shows why the naive $\psi$ is also centred (@sec-general,
Level 3): centring only sees the direct term.

**Theorem 1.** Let $\hat\Gamma_c = N^{-1}\sum_i(\hat\psi_i-\bar\psi)(\hat\psi_i-\bar\psi)'$
and $r^* = \min(D,\, n_{\text{pat}}-1)$. Then

1. $\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma_c \le r^*$;
2. $\hat\Gamma = \hat\Gamma_c + \bar\psi\bar\psi'$, so $\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma \le \min(D, n_{\text{pat}})$, and if $\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma_c = r < D$ then
   $$0 \le \lambda_{r+1}(\hat\Gamma) \le \lVert Q\bar\psi\rVert^2 \le \lVert\bar\psi_\rho\rVert^2,$$
   with $Q$ the orthogonal projector onto $\operatorname{null}(\hat\Gamma_c)$;
3. if every pair's score vanishes at $\hat\rho$, then $\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma \le r^*$.

*Proof.* (1) The rows of the centred matrix take the $n_{\text{pat}}$ values
$g_m - \bar\psi$, and $\sum_m n_m(g_m-\bar\psi) = 0$ with every $n_m>0$. That
is a nontrivial linear dependence, so the span has dimension at most
$n_{\text{pat}}-1$. (2) The decomposition is the usual one for second moments.
By Courant–Fischer, $\lambda_{r+1}(A+vv') = \min_{\dim T = D-r}\max_{x\in T}x'(A+vv')x$.
Taking $T = \operatorname{null}(A)$ gives the bound $\max_{x}(x'v)^2 = \lVert Qv\rVert^2$.
The last inequality holds because $\bar\psi_\tau = 0$. (3) This is (2) with
$\bar\psi = 0$. $\square$

**What "exact" means in floating point** *(re-derived 2026-10-02 for option
B; it replaces an argument from the retired polish's
$|\text{step}| < 10^{-15}$)*. $\bar\psi_\tau$ is zero to rounding.
$\bar\psi_\rho$ is the score residual, $\bar S/\hat I$ per pair (Lemma 2).

Apply Theorem 1(2) to the scale-free matrix $R\hat\Gamma R$, with
$R = \operatorname{diag}(\hat\Gamma)^{-1/2}$ (`corrsc()`):
- its centred part is $R\hat\Gamma_cR$, with the same rank and null-space
  dimension;
- its mean vector $R\bar\psi$ has entries of modulus $z_k$
  (@sec-gamma-budgets).

So, for pairs stopped by the rule, by $(\ast)$ of @sec-gamma-budgets:
$$\lambda_{r+1}(R\hat\Gamma R) \le \textstyle\sum_k z_k^2
  \le \sum_{\text{pairs}} 4\tau_{S,k}^2/J_k.$$
The eigensolver's floor is near $\varepsilon\,\lambda_1(R\hat\Gamma R) \ge
\varepsilon$, since $\lambda_1$ is at least the unit diagonal. The extra
eigenvalue is therefore invisible when $\sum_k z_k^2 < \varepsilon$. That
condition is sufficient, not necessary.

On a1 and a2, refitted by `rf_root()`, the bound is $4.3\times10^{-25}$ and
$1.8\times10^{-25}$, against floors of $2.1\times10^{-15}$ and
$3.1\times10^{-15}$. The $(r^*+1)$-th singular-value ratio stays below
$10^{-15}$ (`budgets-tauS`). So for pairs stopped by the rule on these designs
the $n_{\text{pat}}-1$ bound is still observed as exact. That is a
measurement, conditional on the same $\tilde\pi_{\min}$ as $(\ast)$, not an
a-priori statement.

The centring flag does **not** guarantee it. A pair just under $z = 10^{-6}$
contributes $10^{-12} \gg \varepsilon$, so Theorem 1's $n_{\text{pat}}-1$
bound can be visibly lost by a pair the flag passes.

**When it fails.** A pair whose $\hat\rho$ does not satisfy
$|\bar S| \le \tau_S$ on recomputation breaks the premise: statuses 2, 3, 4
and 8, and status 7 unless its cap hit while probing a root already found.
`dwls_sample_stats()` warns about such pairs and still builds $\hat\Gamma$
from them. The rigorous statement is then $\min(D, n_{\text{pat}})$, with one
extra eigenvalue no larger than $\lVert Q\bar\psi\rVert^2$, which in
scale-free form is at most $\sum_k z_k^2$, with $z_k = |\bar S_k|/\sqrt{J_k}$
computable per pair. Level 2 measures that this bound is attained.

`converged = 0` is not the same set as the pairs that break the premise.
Statuses 5 and 6, and status 7 when the endpoint check's cap ended it, stopped
on the rule, so $(\ast)$ covers them. It does not cover two things:
- whether their root is the right one: uniqueness (@sec-rootfind) is
  unproved;
- for status 6 reached through the zero-probe branch ($\hat\rho = 0$,
  $\bar S(0) = 0$, neither probe certified), whether $\hat\rho$ is a maximum
  at all. Status 6 is also reached through the endpoint check after a clean
  root; that is the kind observed.

### Two sharper exact statements

**Theorem 2 (pairwise span).** Let $M$ be the $N \times (1 + T + \sum_{j<k}C_jC_k)$
matrix $[\mathbf 1 \mid \mathbb 1\{Y_j = c\} \mid \mathbb 1\{Y_j=c, Y_k=d\}]$,
$c,d\ge1$. Every column of $\Psi$ is a function of at most two coordinates of
the row, so $\operatorname{col}(\Psi)\subseteq\operatorname{col}(M)$. The same
holds for the centred matrix, since $\mathbf 1\in\operatorname{col}(M)$. The
centred matrix is also orthogonal to $\mathbf 1$. Hence
$\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma_c \le \min(D, \operatorname{rank}M - 1)$. Because
$\operatorname{rank}M \le n_{\text{pat}}$, this is never weaker than
Theorem 1.

*For binary data, under exact centring, it is an equality:*
$\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma = \operatorname{rank}M - 1$. Write
$\Psi = MC$ in the basis $[\mathbf 1, z_j, z_jz_k]$. $C$'s non-constant block
is block triangular with diagonal entries $1/\phi(\hat\tau_j)$ and
$\phi_2\sum_{rs}\pi_{rs}^{-1}/\hat I_{\rho\rho} > 0$, so it is invertible. Then
$\mathbb R^{1+D} = \operatorname{col}(C)\oplus\operatorname{span}(e_1)$ gives
$\operatorname{col}(M) = \operatorname{col}(\Psi)\oplus\operatorname{span}(\mathbf 1)$.
On every design below $\operatorname{rank}M - 1 \ge \min(D, n_{\text{pat}}-1)$,
so Theorem 2 is recorded for completeness. Production does not need it.

**Theorem 3 (the threshold block, exactly).** Let $Z$ be the $N\times T$ matrix
of cumulative indicators $\mathbb 1\{Y_{ij} < c\}$. Then
$\Psi_\tau = (Z - \mathbf 1\hat q')\operatorname{diag}(1/\phi(\hat\tau))$, so

$$\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma_{\tau\tau} = \operatorname{rank}[\mathbf 1 \mid Z] - 1,$$

and $\hat\Gamma$ is singular whenever $\hat\Gamma_{\tau\tau}$ is. Two cases:

- **The interior-empty mode of spec §4.5.6.** Two nested columns of one
  variable coincide. v1's Module 1 aborts on it.
- **Threshold aliasing across variables.** $\mathbb 1\{Y_j<c\} = \mathbb 1\{Y_k<d\}$
  on every row, or any other linear relation among the columns of
  $[\mathbf 1\mid Z]$. Every category can be non-empty, $\hat\rho_{jk}$ can be
  interior and $n_{\text{pat}}-1$ can far exceed $D$, and $\hat\Gamma$ is still
  exactly singular. Theorem 1 does not see it. Level 3 constructs one.

**What is not an exact degeneracy.** A category of count 1 and a
near-duplicate pair are both ill-conditioning, not rank loss. The designs below
measure each.

The bread $\Delta'W_D\Delta$ depends on $\hat\Gamma$ only through
$\operatorname{diag}(\hat\Gamma)$. A singular $\hat\Gamma$ therefore cannot make
it singular, and Level 4 confirms it is full rank on every design.

### Verification

**Designs.** All use fixed seeds or are derived deterministically from the
committed `case_D.csv`. Each $n_{\text{pat}}$ is counted on $Y$ as
`dwls_sample_stats()` would receive it. The data have no missing values, so
listwise deletion removes nothing.

| | Design | $N$ | $D$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| a1 | ordinal, $p = 10$, $K = 3$, one factor $\lambda = 0.7$ | 50 | 65 |
| a2 | binary, $p = 12$, $q = 0.3$, $\lambda = 0.7$, redrawn until no $2\times2$ cell is empty | 40 | 78 |
| b1 | `case_D`, $y_1$'s boundary category 0 cut to one observation | 5000 | 16 |
| b2 | `case_D`, $y_1$'s interior category 1 cut to one observation | 5000 | 16 |
| c | `case_D` thresholds, $\lambda_1 = \lambda_2 = \sqrt\rho$, $\rho \in \{.9,.99,.999,.9999\}$ | 5000 | 16 |
| d | `case_D`, the healthy control | 5000 | 16 |

Design c is correctly specified: $\rho_{12} = \lambda_1\lambda_2 = \rho$. a2's
redraw keeps lavaan's `zero.add` for $2\times2$ tables from acting, since
production adds nothing.

```{r rank-core}
#| cache: true
library(lavaan)

# psi_tab() of @sec-normaliser, guarded for one thing only: a model cell whose
# probability underflows to <= 0 in floating point gives u = NaN, and 0 * NaN
# poisons the W-weighted sums even though an EMPTY cell has W = 0. Zeroing u
# there changes no weighted sum and no gathered entry, since an empty cell is
# never looked up. A non-empty cell that underflows is left to fail loudly.
psi_tab0 <- function(a, b, rho, W) {
  P <- cellP(a, b, rho); Pr <- dP_drho(a, b, rho)
  bad <- W == 0 & !(P > 0)
  P[bad] <- 1; Pr[bad] <- 0
  u   <- Pr / P
  Irr <- sum(W * u * u)
  Ira <- sapply(seq_along(a), function(c) sum(W * u * dP_da(a, b, rho, c) / P))
  Irb <- sapply(seq_along(b), function(d) sum(W * u * dP_db(a, b, rho, d) / P))
  qa <- pnorm(a); qb <- pnorm(b)
  pa <- outer(seq_len(length(a) + 1), seq_along(a), function(r, c) ((r <= c) - qa[c]) / dnorm(a[c]))
  pb <- outer(seq_len(length(b) + 1), seq_along(b), function(s, d) ((s <= d) - qb[d]) / dnorm(b[d]))
  (u - outer(as.vector(pa %*% Ira), as.vector(pb %*% Irb), "+")) / Irr
}

# rho-hat as Module 2 is MEANT to find it: a bracketed root of the score, then
# the same Fisher-scoring polish, stopped at |step| < 1e-15. Empty cells are
# dropped from the score (0 log pi = 0), which is what makes rho near 1
# reachable at all. Production does NOT reach this root on designs c.99 and
# above -- see "What production does" below. This is the correct rho-hat, not
# a reproduction of production's.
rk_rho <- function(yj, yk, a, b) {
  n <- table(factor(yj, 0:length(a)), factor(yk, 0:length(b)))
  S <- function(r) { v <- n * dP_drho(a, b, r) / cellP(a, b, r); sum(v[n > 0]) }
  lo <- -0.5; hi <- 0.5
  while (isTRUE(S(hi) > 0)) { nx <- 1 - (1 - hi) / 2; if (!is.finite(S(nx)) || nx > 1 - 1e-7) break; hi <- nx }
  while (isTRUE(S(lo) < 0)) { nx <- -1 + (1 + lo) / 2; if (!is.finite(S(nx)) || nx < 1e-7 - 1) break; lo <- nx }
  r <- uniroot(S, c(lo, hi), tol = 1e-14)$root
  for (it in 1:25) {
    P <- cellP(a, b, r); Dr <- dP_drho(a, b, r)
    step <- (S(r) / length(yj)) / sum((Dr^2 / P)[P > 0])
    if (abs(step) < 1e-15) break
    r <- r + step
  }
  r
}

# The N x D influence matrix, gathered by lookup exactly as dwlsmv_psi_matrix()
# gathers it: threshold columns from the staircase, correlation columns from the
# per-pair table, pairs in the index map's column-major lower-triangle order.
rk_psi <- function(Y, K, rho = NULL) {
  p <- ncol(Y); pr <- combn(p, 2)
  th <- lapply(1:p, function(j) nrm_thr(Y[, j], K[j]))
  Pt <- do.call(cbind, lapply(1:p, function(j) {
    q <- pnorm(th[[j]])
    sapply(seq_along(q), function(c) ((Y[, j] < c) - q[c]) / dnorm(th[[j]][c]))
  }))
  if (is.null(rho)) rho <- apply(pr, 2, function(v)
    rk_rho(Y[, v[1]], Y[, v[2]], th[[v[1]]], th[[v[2]]]))
  Pc <- sapply(seq_len(ncol(pr)), function(k) {
    j <- pr[1, k]; l <- pr[2, k]
    W <- prop.table(table(factor(Y[, j], 0:(K[j] - 1)), factor(Y[, l], 0:(K[l] - 1))))
    psi_tab0(th[[j]], th[[l]], rho[k], W)[cbind(Y[, j] + 1, Y[, l] + 1)]
  })
  list(Psi = cbind(Pt, Pc), rho = rho, Tn = ncol(Pt))
}

# [1 | main-effect dummies | pairwise interaction dummies]   (Theorem 2)
rk_M <- function(Y, K) {
  p <- ncol(Y); pr <- combn(p, 2)
  me <- do.call(cbind, lapply(1:p, function(j) outer(Y[, j], seq_len(K[j] - 1), "==") * 1))
  ia <- do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(pr)), function(k) {
    j <- pr[1, k]; l <- pr[2, k]
    g <- expand.grid(c = seq_len(K[j] - 1), d = seq_len(K[l] - 1))
    sapply(seq_len(nrow(g)), function(m) (Y[, j] == g$c[m]) * (Y[, l] == g$d[m]))
  }))
  cbind(1, me, ia)
}
# the cumulative indicators Z   (Theorem 3)
rk_Z <- function(Y, K) do.call(cbind, lapply(seq_len(ncol(Y)), function(j)
  outer(Y[, j], seq_len(K[j] - 1), "<") * 1))

n_pat  <- function(Y) nrow(unique(Y))               # distinct rows of Y as Stage 1 sees it
sv     <- function(G) svd(G, nu = 0, nv = 0)$d
ratios <- function(G) { d <- sv(G); d / d[1] }       # quote ratios, never sigma_min alone
nrank  <- function(G, cut) sum(ratios(G) > cut)
corrsc <- function(G) G / sqrt(outer(diag(G), diag(G)))   # W_D^{1/2} Gamma W_D^{1/2}

rk_gen <- function(N, lam, thr) {
  f <- rnorm(N)
  sapply(seq_along(lam), function(j)
    findInterval(lam[j] * f + sqrt(1 - lam[j]^2) * rnorm(N), thr[[j]]))
}
rk_lav <- function(Y) {                              # the tier-2 call's options
  d <- as.data.frame(lapply(seq_len(ncol(Y)), function(j) ordered(Y[, j])))
  names(d) <- paste0("y", seq_len(ncol(Y)))
  sem(paste("f =~", paste(names(d), collapse = " + ")), data = d, ordered = names(d),
      estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta", zero.add = c(0.5, 0.0))
}

root <- file.path("..", "..")
YD   <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "data", "case_D.csv")))
KD   <- c(4, 4, 3, 3)
thD  <- list(qnorm(cumsum(c(.15, .35, .30, .20))[-4]), qnorm(cumsum(c(.15, .35, .30, .20))[-4]),
             qnorm(cumsum(c(.40, .35, .25))[-3]),      qnorm(cumsum(c(.40, .35, .25))[-3]))

set.seed(24091)
Ya1 <- rk_gen(50, rep(0.7, 10), rep(list(qnorm(c(.40, .75))), 10))
set.seed(24092)
repeat {
  Ya2 <- rk_gen(40, rep(0.7, 12), rep(list(qnorm(0.3)), 12))
  if (all(apply(combn(12, 2), 2, function(v)
        all(table(factor(Ya2[, v[1]], 0:1), factor(Ya2[, v[2]], 0:1)) > 0)))) break
}
Yb1 <- YD; Yb1[which(Yb1[, 1] == 0)[-1], 1] <- 1
Yb2 <- YD; Yb2[which(Yb2[, 1] == 1)[-1], 1] <- 2
Yc  <- lapply(c(0.9, 0.99, 0.999, 0.9999), function(r) {
  set.seed(2409); rk_gen(5000, c(sqrt(r), sqrt(r), 0.7, 0.7), thD) })

designs <- c(list(a1 = list(Y = Ya1, K = rep(3, 10)), a2 = list(Y = Ya2, K = rep(2, 12)),
                  b1 = list(Y = Yb1, K = KD),         b2 = list(Y = Yb2, K = KD)),
             setNames(lapply(Yc, function(y) list(Y = y, K = KD)),
                      c("c.9", "c.99", "c.999", "c.9999")),
             list(d = list(Y = YD, K = KD)))
own <- lapply(designs, function(x) rk_psi(x$Y, x$K))
```

**Level 1: Lemma 1, Lemma 2 and Theorem 1 on every design.** $\hat\Gamma$
here is our own $\Psi'\Psi/N$ at our own $\hat\rho$.

```{r rank-L1}
#| cache: true
L1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(designs), function(nm) {
  Y <- designs[[nm]]$Y; Ps <- own[[nm]]$Psi; N <- nrow(Y); D <- ncol(Ps)
  pb <- colMeans(Ps); tn <- own[[nm]]$Tn
  G  <- crossprod(Ps) / N
  kx <- min(D, n_pat(Y) - 1)
  r  <- ratios(G)
  data.frame(design = nm, N = N, D = D, n_pat = n_pat(Y),
             psi_rows = nrow(unique(Ps)),
             same_rows = nrow(unique(cbind(Y, Ps))) == n_pat(Y),
             rank_M = qr(rk_M(Y, designs[[nm]]$K), tol = 1e-9)$rank,
             bound = kx,
             rank_1e_12 = nrank(G, 1e-12),
             rank_1e_14 = nrank(G, 1e-14), rank_1e_8 = nrank(G, 1e-8),
             ratio_at_bound = r[kx],
             ratio_next = if (kx < D) r[kx + 1] else NA,
             psibar_tau = max(abs(pb[1:tn])), psibar_rho = max(abs(pb[-(1:tn)])))
}))
L1
stopifnot(L1$psi_rows == L1$n_pat, L1$same_rows,           # psi_i is a function of Y_i alone
          L1$psibar_tau < 1e-14, L1$psibar_rho < 1e-13,    # centred: exact / to the polish
          L1$rank_1e_12 <= L1$bound,                       # Theorem 1
          L1$rank_1e_12 == L1$bound,                       # ... attained on every design here
          L1$rank_1e_14 == L1$bound, L1$rank_1e_8 == L1$bound,  # ... at any cutoff in [1e-14, 1e-8]
          L1$rank_M - 1 >= L1$bound)                       # Theorem 2 never sharper here
stopifnot(with(L1[L1$bound < L1$D, ], all(ratio_at_bound > 1e-5 & ratio_next < 1e-15)))
```

**Level 2: what centring buys.** Move every $\hat\rho$ of design a1 off its
root by $\delta$. $\bar\psi$ becomes the score residual, and the
$n_{\text{pat}}$-th eigenvalue must appear, no larger than
$\lVert Q\bar\psi\rVert^2$ and growing as $\delta^2$.

```{r rank-L2}
#| cache: true
x  <- designs$a1; k0 <- n_pat(x$Y) - 1
L2 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1e-3, 1e-5, 1e-7), function(dl) {
  Ps <- rk_psi(x$Y, x$K, rho = own$a1$rho + dl)$Psi; N <- nrow(Ps)
  pb <- colMeans(Ps)
  Gc <- crossprod(sweep(Ps, 2, pb)) / N
  Q  <- eigen(Gc, symmetric = TRUE)$vectors[, -(1:k0)]
  lam <- eigen(crossprod(Ps) / N, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  data.frame(delta = dl, psibar_norm2 = sum(pb^2), Qpsibar_norm2 = sum(crossprod(Q, pb)^2),
             lambda_npat = lam[k0 + 1], fp_floor = 64 * .Machine$double.eps * lam[1],
             lambda_npat_over_bound = lam[k0 + 1] / sum(crossprod(Q, pb)^2),
             ratio_npat = lam[k0 + 1] / lam[1])
}))
L2
stopifnot(L2$lambda_npat <= L2$Qpsibar_norm2 + L2$fp_floor,
          L2$lambda_npat_over_bound > 0.5,
          abs(-diff(log10(L2$lambda_npat)) - 4) < 0.1)      # delta^2: four decades per two
```

**Level 3: the two sharper exact statements.** The binary equality of
Theorem 2 is checked on a2. For Theorem 3, $y_1$ and $y_2$ each keep a
single observation in category 0, and it is the same observation. Then
$\mathbb 1\{y_1<1\}$ and $\mathbb 1\{y_2<1\}$ are the same vector. Every
category is still non-empty and the pair is interior, yet $\hat\Gamma$ is
exactly singular.

```{r rank-L3}
#| cache: true
Yal <- YD
i0  <- which(YD[, 1] == 0 & YD[, 2] == 0)[1]
Yal[setdiff(which(Yal[, 1] == 0), i0), 1] <- 1
Yal[setdiff(which(Yal[, 2] == 0), i0), 2] <- 1
al  <- rk_psi(Yal, KD)
Gal <- crossprod(al$Psi) / nrow(Yal)
L3 <- data.frame(
  check = c("binary a2: rank(Gamma) - (rank(M) - 1)",
            "aliased: n_pat", "aliased: D", "aliased: rank at 1e-12",
```
