```{r rank-L3}
            "aliased: identical columns y1|t1, y2|t1 (max abs diff)",
            "aliased: rho_12 inside the 0.999 bound",
            "aliased: smallest ratio"),
  value = c(nrank(crossprod(own$a2$Psi) / 40, 1e-12) - (L1$rank_M[L1$design == "a2"] - 1),
            n_pat(Yal), ncol(al$Psi), nrank(Gal, 1e-12),
            max(abs(al$Psi[, 1] - al$Psi[, 4])), abs(al$rho[1]) < 0.999,
            min(ratios(Gal))))
L3
stopifnot(L3$value[1] == 0, L3$value[4] == L3$value[3] - 1, L3$value[5] == 0, L3$value[6] == 1)

L3b <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(names(designs), "aliased"), function(nm) {
  x  <- if (nm == "aliased") list(Y = Yal, K = KD) else designs[[nm]]
  Ps <- if (nm == "aliased") al$Psi else own[[nm]]$Psi
  Tn <- sum(x$K - 1)
  data.frame(design = nm, T = Tn,
             rank_1Z_minus_1 = qr(cbind(1, rk_Z(x$Y, x$K)))$rank - 1,
             rank_Gtautau = nrank(crossprod(Ps[, 1:Tn]) / nrow(Ps), 1e-12))
}))
L3b
stopifnot(L3b$rank_Gtautau == L3b$rank_1Z_minus_1)
```

**Level 4: lavaan's Γ, and the spectra.** lavaan is the Γ computation here. It
is also a cross-check on the normalization: our lookup-gathered $\Psi$, at
*lavaan's* $\hat\rho$, must reproduce `lavTech(fit, "gamma")` under $/N$ and
uncentred, and must miss under $/(N-1)$. `ratio_min` is
$\sigma_{r^*}/\sigma_1$ of $\hat\Gamma$, the smallest singular value that is
nonzero by construction. `ratio_corr` is the same ratio for the scale-free
$W_D^{1/2}\hat\Gamma W_D^{1/2}$, which is what the downstream weighting sees.
`bread_ratio` is $\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}$ of $\Delta'W_D\Delta$ from
lavaan's $\Delta$ and $W_D = \operatorname{diag}(\hat\Gamma)^{-1}$.

```{r rank-lavaan}
#| cache: true
fits <- lapply(designs, function(x) suppressWarnings(rk_lav(x$Y)))
LV <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(designs), function(nm) {
  Y <- designs[[nm]]$Y; N <- nrow(Y); f <- fits[[nm]]
  G  <- lavTech(f, "gamma")[[1]]
  rl <- f@SampleStats@cov[[1]][t(combn(ncol(Y), 2))]
  Pl <- rk_psi(Y, designs[[nm]]$K, rho = rl)$Psi
  Dl <- lavTech(f, "delta")[[1]]
  B  <- crossprod(Dl, (1 / diag(G)) * Dl)
  kx <- min(ncol(G), n_pat(Y) - 1)
  data.frame(design = nm,
             gap_N   = max(abs(G - crossprod(Pl) / N)) / max(abs(G)),
             gap_Nm1 = max(abs(G - crossprod(Pl) / (N - 1))) / max(abs(G)),
             gap_ctr = max(abs(G - crossprod(sweep(Pl, 2, colMeans(Pl))) / N)) / max(abs(G)),
             rho_lav_minus_own = max(abs(rl - own[[nm]]$rho)),
             rank_1e_12 = nrank(G, 1e-12), bound = kx,
             ratio_min  = min(ratios(G)[1:kx]),
             ratio_corr = min(ratios(corrsc(G))[1:kx]),
             bread_q = ncol(Dl), bread_ratio = min(ratios(B)))
}))
LV
stopifnot(LV$gap_N < 1e-9, LV$gap_Nm1 > 1e-4,
          LV$rank_1e_12 == LV$bound,
          LV$bread_ratio > 1e-6)

tails <- lapply(names(designs), function(nm) {        # the spectrum around r*, for the record
  G <- lavTech(fits[[nm]], "gamma")[[1]]; kx <- min(ncol(G), n_pat(designs[[nm]]$Y) - 1)
  r <- ratios(G); signif(r[max(1, kx - 5):min(length(r), kx + 2)], 3) })
names(tails) <- names(designs); tails
```

### What the verification shows

Executed 2026-09-24 under R 4.6.0 and lavaan 0.7.2. The whole file, with this
section in place, was extracted with `knitr::purl` and every chunk run in order
from this directory; every assertion in the file passed. The document was not
re-rendered. **Every figure is a single run on the fixed seeds above.**

- **Lemma 1.** On all nine designs, the number of distinct rows of $\Psi$
  equals $n_{\text{pat}}$, and pairing each row of $Y$ with its row of $\Psi$
  adds no distinct rows. $\bar\psi_\tau \le 5.7\times10^{-16}$ and
  $\bar\psi_\rho \le 9.1\times10^{-16}$.
- **Theorem 1 is attained.** a1: $n_{\text{pat}} = 50$, $D = 65$, rank 49.
  a2: $n_{\text{pat}} = 30$, $D = 78$, rank 29. The gap at the bound is about
  twelve decades: $\sigma_{49}/\sigma_1 = 4.8\times10^{-4}$ against
  $\sigma_{50}/\sigma_1 = 8.2\times10^{-17}$ (a1), and $4.6\times10^{-3}$
  against $1.3\times10^{-16}$ (a2). Every relative cutoff from $10^{-14}$ to
  $10^{-8}$ gives the same rank (asserted at both ends). The other designs have
  $n_{\text{pat}} - 1 \ge 65 > D$ and are full rank.
- **Level 2.** At $\delta = 10^{-3}, 10^{-5}, 10^{-7}$ the $n_{\text{pat}}$-th
  eigenvalue is 0.9999, 1.0000 and 0.97 of $\lVert Q\bar\psi\rVert^2$. So the
  bound is essentially attained, and it falls four decades per two decades of
  $\delta$.
- **Level 3.** Binary a2 meets Theorem 2's equality exactly. The aliased
  design has $n_{\text{pat}} = 82$, $D = 16$, $\hat\rho_{12} = 0.470$ and
  rank 15, with smallest ratio $1.2\times10^{-16}$. $\operatorname{rank}[\mathbf 1\mid Z]-1$
  predicts $\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma_{\tau\tau}$ on all ten designs.
- **lavaan.** It reproduces $\Psi'\Psi/N$ at its own $\hat\rho$ to
  $\le 1.7\times10^{-13}$ relative, and to $1.5\times10^{-10}$ on b2. Under
  $/(N-1)$ it misses by $1/(N-1)$. It builds Γ **uncentred**: on c.9999,
  lavaan caps $\hat\rho_{12}$ at 0.999 against a root of 0.99987, so
  $\bar\psi\ne0$. There the uncentred form matches to $6.5\times10^{-14}$ and
  the centred form misses by $4.7\times10^{-6}$. This is Lemma 2's premise
  failing at a bound, as described above.

| design | $n_{\text{pat}}$ | $r^*$ | `ratio_min` | `ratio_corr` | `bread_ratio` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a1 | 50 | 49 | 4.8e-4 | 5.0e-4 | 7.5e-3 |
| a2 | 30 | 29 | 4.6e-3 | 6.1e-3 | 1.4e-2 |
| b1 boundary count 1 | 109 | 16 | 1.5e-3 | 1.3e-1 | 4.3e-4 |
| b2 interior count 1 | 104 | 16 | 2.8e-4 | 2.3e-4 | 1.4e-2 |
| c, ρ = .9 | 101 | 16 | 8.9e-3 | 5.7e-2 | 1.5e-2 |
| c, ρ = .99 | 85 | 16 | 4.5e-4 | 1.9e-2 | 8.9e-4 |
| c, ρ = .999 | 74 | 16 | 1.7e-5 | 5.5e-3 | 3.3e-5 |
| c, ρ = .9999 (lavaan capped at .999) | 66 | 16 | 3.2e-5 | 1.6e-3 | 6.6e-5 |
| d control | 139 | 16 | 6.7e-2 | 1.2e-1 | 1.4e-2 |

**What the spectra suggest, without choosing anything.** The raw ratio mixes
scale with collinearity, and the three sparse designs separate them cleanly.
**b1** is scale: the one observation in the boundary category gives
$\hat\Gamma_{y_1|t_1,y_1|t_1} = 348$. The scale-free ratio is 0.13, as healthy
as the control. **b2** is genuine near-collinearity: its near-null vector is
$(y_1|t_1 - y_1|t_2)/\sqrt2$, the approach to §4.5.6's interior-empty mode. The
scale-free ratio stays at $2.3\times10^{-4}$. **c** is both: the raw smallest
direction is $\hat\rho_{12}$'s own variance, whose diagonal is
$1.6\times10^{-4}$ at ρ = .999. The scale-free ratio shrinks about as
$\sqrt{1-\rho}$ (a factor of ~3.2 per decade), but its near-null direction
is **not** a single stable one. *Corrected 2026-09-25.* This paragraph first
said it "contrasts $y_1$'s correlations with $y_2$'s", which is true at
ρ = .9, .999 and .9999 but not at .99. There the direction is
$y_1|t_2 - y_2|t_2$ ($\pm0.63$), the near-version of Theorem 3's threshold
aliasing: case D gives $y_1$ and $y_2$ identical thresholds, so
$\mathbb 1\{y_1<t_2\}\approx\mathbb 1\{y_2<t_2\}$ as ρ → 1. Our Γ and lavaan's
agree on this at every point. The *population* Γ (exact pattern enumeration,
a read-only agent's screen) puts the threshold contrast smallest from ρ = .99
onward. So the two smallest scale-free eigenvalues are nearly equal along c,
and sampling decides their order. These are one-off measurements, not
assertions. No design comes near
the rounding floor except the exact cases, and the bread is full rank on
every design.

### What production does on these designs

Everything above is the *correct* $\hat\Gamma$, built from the root of each
pair's score. A one-off Stata measurement on 2026-09-24 ran production's
`dwls_sample_stats()` (StataMP 18, six processors, a scratch do-file outside
the repository) on the a1, b2, aliased and c designs, exported from these
chunks. It is recorded here because it bounds what the table can be taken to
say about production, and it is **not** asserted anywhere yet.

- **The exact cases reproduce.** On a1 production's $\hat\Gamma$ has rank 49
  (eigenvalue ratio cutoff $10^{-10}$; the smallest ratio is
  $-6.0\times10^{-17}$). On the aliased design it has rank 15 of 16, with ratio
  $3.7\times10^{-16}$, and nothing warns. b2's smallest ratio is
  $2.80\times10^{-4}$, as above.
- **Design c does not reproduce.** At ρ = .99, `dwls_sample_stats()` aborts
  inside `dwlsmv_cellprob()` with rc 3300 and no message: the `_error()` text
  was over Stata's 100-character limit. The message was fixed on 2026-09-25,
  and the path is now rc 3498 with its text. The abort itself remains. At ρ = .999 and .9999 it returns
  $\hat\rho_{12} = 0.972$ and $0.982$, against roots of 0.99875 and 0.99987.
  Production bounds $\rho$ at 0.999 exactly as lavaan does
  (`0.999*tanh(z)`), so at .9999 even a Module 2 that did not stall would
  stop at the bound. Both stalls, however, fall short of the bound as well
  as of the root. It flags the pair as not converged, and builds $\hat\Gamma$ from it anyway,
  with $\max|\bar\psi| = 0.12$ and $0.14$. That $\hat\Gamma$ *looks* healthy:
  its smallest ratios are $1.5\times10^{-3}$ and $4.4\times10^{-4}$.

What the code showed is this. Module 2's d0 evaluator,
`dwlsmv_polychoric_ll()`, returned missing when `min(P) <= 0` over *every*
model cell, including cells that are empty in the data and contribute
$0\cdot\log\pi = 0$. The Fisher-scoring polish and `dwlsmv_pairinfo()` called
`dwlsmv_cellprob()`, which aborts on the same condition.

This section first recorded, as "not yet demonstrated", the hypothesis that a
corner cell underflowing before the root is what stops the optimizer.
@sec-emptycells demonstrates it on two failing Monte Carlo tables at
$\rho = .98$, and it was **half right**. There is cancellation: a corner's true
probability falls below the $2^{-55}$ grid that its rectangle difference lives on,
from $\rho \approx .975$. But a cancellation-free route does not help in Stata,
because `binormal()` has an **absolute** floor and returns exactly 0 for the
same cells from $\rho = .97$ on. What resolves it is not computing them: an empty
cell contributes nothing to the likelihood, the score, the empirical
information or $\hat\Gamma$. @sec-emptycells states this as mathematics, and
lists what production changes.

Design c at .999 and .9999 was not re-measured for this purpose. Its stalls at
0.972 and 0.982 are consistent with the same mechanism, but that is not
demonstrated.

For Module 10 the consequence stands: **a spectrum cannot detect a stalled
pair**, because the resulting $\hat\Gamma$ is well conditioned. The centring
residual $\bar\psi_\rho$ can, and by Theorem 1(2) it is the quantity that controls
the eigenvalue the stall adds. A $\bar\psi$ check detects a failed score
equation. It does not detect a missing propagation term (@sec-general, Level
3), and must not be read as doing so.

## Module 2: empty cells in the pairwise fit {#sec-emptycells}

*Added 2026-09-26, before Module 2's fix.* On near-duplicate indicators Module 2
aborts or stalls from $\rho \approx .98$ (E-055, *Open decisions →
Module 2 near ±1*). This section proves that the empty cells of a pair's table
carry no information about $\hat\rho$ or its influence function, shows why they
cannot be computed near the root anyway, and settles which scaler the
Fisher-scoring polish may use. It changes no estimator: every quantity below is
the one @sec-general and @sec-normaliser already define, evaluated where it was
always defined.

### The statement

Fix a pair with counts $n_{rs}$, $N = \sum_{rs} n_{rs}$. Let
$\mathcal O = \{(r,s) : n_{rs} > 0\}$ be its observed cells and $\mathcal E$ the
empty ones. For $(r,s)\in\mathcal E$ the term $n_{rs}\log\pi_{rs}$ is
identically $0$ for every $\pi_{rs} > 0$, so

$$\ell(\rho) = \sum_{rs} n_{rs}\log\pi_{rs}(\rho)
            = \sum_{\mathcal O} n_{rs}\log\pi_{rs}(\rho) =: \ell_{\mathcal O}(\rho)$$

on all of $(-1,1)$, where every true $\pi_{rs}$ is positive. Differentiating,

$$S(\rho) = \sum_{\mathcal O} n_{rs}u_{rs},
\qquad
\hat I_{\rho\rho}(\hat\pi) = \sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi_{rs}u_{rs}^2,
\qquad
\hat I_{\rho a_c}(\hat\pi) = \sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi_{rs}u_{rs}
   \frac{\partial_{a_c}\pi_{rs}}{\pi_{rs}},$$

with $\hat\pi_{rs} = n_{rs}/N$, and $\psi_{\rho,i}$ looks up $u$ at a cell
$(r_i,s_i)\in\mathcal O$. **So $\hat\rho$, the score, the empirical information of
@sec-normaliser and every gathered $\psi_\rho$ entry are functions of
$\{\pi_{rs}, \nabla\pi_{rs} : (r,s)\in\mathcal O\}$ alone.** $\ell_{\mathcal O}$ is not
a different likelihood: it *is* $\ell$, written without its zero terms. What it
adds is that it remains defined where a computed empty-cell probability is
$\le 0$, which $\ell$ in floating point does not.

The empty cells' probabilities enter exactly three things, none of which
production estimates:

| Quantity | Depends on $\pi_{\mathcal E}$? |
|---|---|
| $\ell$, $S$, $\hat\rho$ | no |
| $\hat I_{\rho\rho}(\hat\pi)$, $\hat I_{\rho a}(\hat\pi)$, $\hat I_{\rho b}(\hat\pi)$ — what v1 ships | no |
| $\psi_\rho$ at observed cells, hence $\hat\Gamma$ | no |
| $\psi_\rho$ table entries at empty cells | yes, but never gathered (Lemma 1 of @sec-gamma-rank) |
| the expected information $I(\pi) = \sum_{rs}(\partial_\rho\pi_{rs})^2/\pi_{rs}$, i.e. `dwlsmv_pairinfo()` at $W = \pi$ | **yes** |
| the identity $\sum_{rs}\pi_{rs} = 1$, used for $E[g_i] = 0$ | yes (population only) |

The fifth row has a consequence for tests. $W = \pi$ is the unit-test oracle of
@sec-normaliser, and at $W = \pi$ an empty cell has weight $\pi_{rs}$, not $0$. Where
a computed $\pi_{rs}$ is $\le 0$ the oracle is not a distribution, and no
zero-weight rule can rescue it. **The $W = \pi$ oracle is therefore usable only
where every computed cell is positive** — on the tables below, $\rho$ below about
.97.

### Why this matters numerically

Near-duplicate indicators leave the table's corner cells empty, and their true
probabilities fall off a cliff. On the two tables of Level E1 the corner
$\pi_{14} = P(Y_1^* < a_1,\ Y_2^* > b_3)$ is $3.5\times10^{-11}$ at $\rho = .95$,
$1.4\times10^{-16}$ at $.97$ and $3.7\times10^{-23}$ at $.98$.

**The rectangle difference cannot represent them, however accurate $\Phi_2$ is.**

*Lemma (the grid of a rectangle difference).* Let every nonzero corner value
$C$ of a cell's rectangle satisfy $|C| \ge 2^{e+52}$. Then each corner is an
integer multiple of $2^e$; so is every sum or difference of them, and rounding
such a value to the nearest double keeps it one — exactly, if its magnitude is
below $2^{e+53}$, and onto a coarser grid of multiples of $2^e$ otherwise. So
the computed cell lies in $2^e\mathbb Z$: it is either $\le 0$ or $\ge 2^e$.
$\square$

For a corner cell, $\pi_{14} = \Phi(a_1) - \Phi_2(a_1,b_3;\rho)$ with both terms in
$[\tfrac18,\tfrac14)$, so $2^e = 2^{-55} = 2.78\times10^{-17}$. Once the true
value is below $2^{-56}$ the computed one is noise on that grid, and its sign is
the sign of the rounding. Level E1 asserts the lemma on every cell of both tables
at nine values of $\rho$, and asserts that both corners are below $2^{-56}$ from
$\rho = .975$ on.

That is cancellation, but a cancellation-free route does not rescue these cells
in Stata. A one-off Stata measurement on 2026-09-26 (StataMP 18, pair $(y_1,y_2)$
of both replicates, **not asserted anywhere**):

- by the rectangle difference, the corners read $0$ or $\pm2.776\times10^{-17}$ /
  $\pm5.551\times10^{-17}$ — multiples of $2^{-55}$, as the lemma requires — for
  every $\rho$ from .97 to .9989; on `mc_c_98_0007`, $+2.776\times10^{-17}$ at
  .98 and $-2.776\times10^{-17}$ at .994;
- from the cell's own orthant, `binormal(a1, -b3, -rho)`, which involves no
  cancellation, Stata returns **exactly 0 from $\rho = .97$ up**. At .95 both routes
  give $3.454\times10^{-11}$; at .96, $3.168\times10^{-13}$ (orthant) against
  $3.169\times10^{-13}$ (rectangle).

The true values at .97 are $1.4\times10^{-16}$ and $8.2\times10^{-17}$ (Level
E1), so `binormal()` has an **absolute** accuracy floor near $10^{-16}$. No
formula built on it can compute these cells, and none needs to: the statement
above says the fit never reads them.

**What the whole-table rule does with this.** Before the fix, Module 2's d0
evaluator returned missing whenever $\min_{rs}\pi_{rs} \le 0$ over *all* cells, and
the polish called `dwlsmv_cellprob()`, which aborts on the same condition. With
the corners' signs set by rounding, the whole-table feasible set is a union of
fragments that ends before the root. In Stata on `mc_c_98_0002` the
log-likelihood was missing at .975 and .98 but finite at .985, and the optimizer
stopped short (one-off, as above). Level E4 shows the same in R's arithmetic.

### The polish: its fixed point, and when it converges

Production's d0 optimizer locates the root to about $10^{-8}$, and a scoring
iteration finishes it:

$$\rho_{k+1} = g(\rho_k), \qquad g(\rho) = \rho + \frac{S(\rho)}{N\,c(\rho)},$$

for some scaler $c(\rho) > 0$.

*Fixed point.* For any finite $c > 0$, $g(\rho) = \rho \iff S(\rho) = 0$. So every
positive scaler has the same fixed points, the roots of the score. **The scaler
chooses the path, never the root.** $\square$

*Convergence.* Write $H(\rho) = -S'(\rho)/N$, the observed information per
observation. At a root $\rho^*$,

$$g'(\rho^*) = 1 - \frac{H(\rho^*)}{c(\rho^*)} + \frac{S(\rho^*)}{N}\,
   \frac{d}{d\rho}\frac{1}{c}\Big|_{\rho^*} = 1 - \frac{H}{c},$$

so the iteration contracts locally if and only if $|1 - H/c| < 1$, i.e.
$0 < H/c < 2$ (Ostrowski), with the error multiplied by $1 - H/c$ at each step.
Positivity of $c$ gives the fixed point and **not** convergence.

The two natural scalers differ from $H$ by different remainders. Differentiating
$S/N = \sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi_{rs}\,\partial_\rho\pi_{rs}/\pi_{rs}$,

$$H = \hat I_{\rho\rho}(\hat\pi) - \sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi_{rs}
      \frac{\partial^2_\rho\pi_{rs}}{\pi_{rs}},
\qquad
1 - \frac{H}{\hat I_{\rho\rho}(\hat\pi)} =
  \frac{\sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi_{rs}\,\partial^2_\rho\pi_{rs}/\pi_{rs}}
       {\hat I_{\rho\rho}(\hat\pi)}.$$

The numerator's expectation is $\sum_{rs}\partial^2_\rho\pi_{rs} = 0$ only when the
sum runs over **all** cells. A sparse table drops the empty cells from it, and
nothing then keeps it small. The expected scaler $I(\pi)$ carries the empty
cells' $(\partial_\rho\pi)^2/\pi$ instead. Both rates are $O_p(N^{-1/2})$ at a
correct model, and neither is guaranteed below 1 in a finite sample. **So the
choice is made on measurement, not proof.** Level E5 measures it on the
twelve-pattern design of `test_gammadiag.do` check 3. There the empirical scaler
gives $1 - H/c = -1.35$ on pair $(2,3)$, and the polish diverges. The expected
scaler gives $-0.16$ and converges.

**The scaler production uses** is the expected information over cells whose
*computed* probability is positive,

$$c(\rho) = \sum_{\{rs:\ \tilde\pi_{rs} > 0\}}
   \frac{(\partial_\rho\pi_{rs})^2}{\tilde\pi_{rs}},$$

with $\tilde\pi$ the computed values. This is `rk_rho()`'s rule in chunk
`rank-core`. It has four properties:

1. It never divides by a non-positive number.
2. Where every computed cell is positive, it is the pre-fix scaler term for
   term, so the pre-fix polish is reproduced bitwise (asserted in Level E5).
3. It is positive whenever some cell with $\tilde\pi > 0$ has
   $\partial_\rho\pi \ne 0$.
4. It departs from the true $I(\pi)$ only on the unrepresentable cells
   $\mathcal U = \{rs\in\mathcal E: \pi_{rs} < 2^{e_{rs}}\}$. There, by the lemma,
   a cell kept in the sum has $\tilde\pi \ge 2^{e_{rs}}$ and so adds at most
   $(\partial_\rho\pi)^2/2^{e_{rs}}$. A cell masked out removes its true
   $(\partial_\rho\pi)^2/\pi$. A relative change $s \le \tfrac12$ in $c$ moves
   $1 - H/c$ by at most $|H/c|\,|s|/(1-|s|) \le 4s$ when $|1-H/c| < 1$. Level E6
   bounds $s$ on the two tables and asserts $|1-H/c| + 4s < 1$.

### Verification

Chunks `setup`, `gate3-core` (`cellP`, `dP_drho`, `dP_da`, `dP_db`), `norm-core`
(`infoW`) and `rank-core` (`psi_tab0`, `rk_rho`) must have run. Every name defined
here starts with `ec_`, so nothing later in the file is disturbed. The two tables
are pair $(y_1,y_2)$ of Monte Carlo replicates `mc_c_98_0007` (production aborts)
and `mc_c_98_0002` (production stalls), with their counts embedded. The replicate
`.dta` files are gitignored. Thresholds are recomputed from the counts in
`dwlsmv_cumprop()`'s arithmetic, cumulative count over $N$.

```{r ec-core}
#| cache: true
# Depends on: setup (Phi2, phi2), gate3-core (cellP, dP_drho, dP_da, dP_db),
# norm-core (infoW), rank-core (psi_tab0, rk_rho). Every name defined here
# starts with ec_ so nothing downstream of this section is clobbered.

# The two failing Monte Carlo tables, pair (y1, y2), rows y1 = 0..3, cols y2 = 0..3.
ec_tabs <- list(
  mc_c_98_0007 = matrix(c(679,   92,    0,   0,
                           81, 1523,  152,   0,
                            0,  169, 1226, 102,
                            0,    0,   91, 885), 4, byrow = TRUE),
  mc_c_98_0002 = matrix(c(665,   88,    0,   0,
                          100, 1456,  167,   0,
                            0,  152, 1275, 101,
                            0,    0,  116, 880), 4, byrow = TRUE))

# Module 1's thresholds, in dwlsmv_cumprop()'s arithmetic: cumulative COUNT / N.
# (nrm_thr() of @sec-normaliser sums proportions instead; the two can differ in
# the last bit, which is why this is not nrm_thr.)
ec_thr <- function(m) qnorm(cumsum(m)[-length(m)] / sum(m))
ec_ab  <- function(n) list(a = ec_thr(rowSums(n)), b = ec_thr(colSums(n)))
ec_expand <- function(n) {                        # rk_rho() takes the variables, not the table
  ij <- which(n > 0, arr.ind = TRUE)
  list(yj = rep(ij[, 1] - 1, n[ij]), yk = rep(ij[, 2] - 1, n[ij]))
}
ec_rho <- function(n) { ab <- ec_ab(n); y <- ec_expand(n); rk_rho(y$yj, y$yk, ab$a, ab$b) }

# The statement's observed-cells quantities, O = {n > 0}, at an explicit P.
ec_obs <- function(a, b, rho, n, P = cellP(a, b, rho)) {
  O <- n > 0; W <- n / sum(n); Dr <- dP_drho(a, b, rho); u <- Dr[O] / P[O]
  list(ll  = sum(n[O] * log(P[O])),
       S   = sum(n[O] * u),
       Irr = sum(W[O] * u * u),
       Ira = sapply(seq_along(a), function(c) sum(W[O] * u * dP_da(a, b, rho, c)[O] / P[O])),
       Irb = sapply(seq_along(b), function(d) sum(W[O] * u * dP_db(a, b, rho, d)[O] / P[O])))
}
ec_S <- function(n, a, b, x) ec_obs(a, b, x, n)$S

# The two candidate polish scalers. "exp" is rk_rho's: the expected information
# over cells whose COMPUTED probability is positive. "emp" is the empirical one.
ec_scaler <- function(n, a, b, x, type) {
  P <- cellP(a, b, x); Dr <- dP_drho(a, b, x)
  if (type == "exp") sum((Dr^2 / P)[P > 0]) else sum(((n / sum(n)) * (Dr / P)^2)[n > 0])
}
ec_polish <- function(n, a, b, x0, type, maxit = 25) {   # production's loop and stopping rule
  x <- x0; N <- sum(n)
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    step <- (ec_S(n, a, b, x) / N) / ec_scaler(n, a, b, x, type)
    if (abs(step) < 1e-15) return(list(x = x, it = it, rule = TRUE))
    x <- x + step
  }
  list(x = x, it = maxit, rule = FALSE)
}
# H = -S'(rho)/N, the observed information per observation, by central difference
ec_H <- function(n, a, b, x, h) -(ec_S(n, a, b, x + h) - ec_S(n, a, b, x - h)) / (2 * h * sum(n))

# Cancellation-free cell probabilities: each cell integrated over its own strip,
# on the upper normal tail wherever the strip lies above 0, so a cell of 1e-40 is
# computed to relative accuracy rather than as a difference of two 0.15s.
ec_strip <- function(lo, hi) ifelse(lo > 0, pnorm(lo, lower.tail = FALSE) - pnorm(hi, lower.tail = FALSE),
                                    pnorm(hi) - pnorm(lo))
ec_cellx <- function(a, b, rho) {
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf); sg <- sqrt(1 - rho^2)
  outer(seq_len(length(a) + 1), seq_len(length(b) + 1), Vectorize(function(r, s)
    integrate(function(x) dnorm(x) * ec_strip((B[s] - rho * x) / sg, (B[s + 1] - rho * x) / sg),
              A[r], A[r + 1], rel.tol = 1e-13, abs.tol = 0)$value))
}
ec_celly <- function(a, b, rho) t(ec_cellx(b, a, rho))  # the same, integrating over the other variable

# The lemma's grid: 2^e for each cell, the smallest ulp among its nonzero corners.
ec_gran <- function(a, b, rho) {
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf)
  C <- outer(seq_along(A), seq_along(B), Vectorize(function(r, s) Phi2(A[r], B[s], rho)))
  ul <- ifelse(C == 0, Inf, 2^(floor(log2(abs(C))) - 52))
  outer(seq_len(length(a) + 1), seq_len(length(b) + 1), Vectorize(function(r, s)
    min(ul[r, s], ul[r + 1, s], ul[r, s + 1], ul[r + 1, s + 1])))
}

# Run fun with cellP() replaced, so psi_tab0 and infoW are reused by name.
ec_with_P <- function(fun, Pfun) {
  environment(fun) <- list2env(list(cellP = Pfun), parent = globalenv()); fun
}

ec_fit <- lapply(ec_tabs, function(n) c(ec_ab(n), list(n = n, rho = ec_rho(n))))
```

**Level E1: the corner cells' true values, and the lemma.** `ec_cellx()` and
`ec_celly()` integrate over different variables and share no arithmetic beyond
`pnorm`. Each asks `integrate()` for $10^{-13}$ relative, so their agreement is
asserted at $2\times10^{-13}$. That requested tolerance is a target on
`integrate()`'s error estimate, not a guarantee, which is why a second route is
used at all.

```{r ec-L1}
#| cache: true
ec_grid <- c(0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.975, 0.98, 0.985, 0.99)   # chosen: around the cliff
ec_L1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ec_fit), function(nm) {
  f <- ec_fit[[nm]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(ec_grid, function(r) {
    Px <- ec_cellx(f$a, f$b, r); Py <- ec_celly(f$a, f$b, r); Pr <- cellP(f$a, f$b, r)
    g  <- ec_gran(f$a, f$b, r)
    data.frame(table = nm, rho = r,
               pi14 = Px[1, 4], pi41 = Px[4, 1],        # true, cancellation-free
               rect14 = Pr[1, 4], rect41 = Pr[4, 1],    # cellP, rectangle difference
               grid14 = g[1, 4], grid41 = g[4, 1],
               xy_relgap = max(abs(Px / Py - 1)),
               rect_absgap = max(abs(Pr - Px)),
               on_grid = all(Pr / g == round(Pr / g)))
  }))
}))
format(ec_L1, digits = 4)
stopifnot(ec_L1$xy_relgap < 2e-13,                 # two routes, each asked for 1e-13
          ec_L1$on_grid,                           # the lemma: every cell, every rho
          with(ec_L1, all(grid14 == 2^-55 & grid41 == 2^-55)),
          with(ec_L1[ec_L1$rho >= 0.975, ], all(pi14 < 2^-56 & pi41 < 2^-56)))
```

**Level E2: the root.** `rk_rho()` sums the score over observed cells. The root
must be interior, bracketed by a sign change of $S$ over $\pm10^{-6}$ (a width
chosen for the purpose), and must meet `rk_rho()`'s own stopping rule
$|S/N|/c < 10^{-15}$. The same root is then found with the cancellation-free
cells. The two differ only through $\tilde\pi - \pi$ on observed cells, whose
first-order effect on the root is
$\sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi|u|\,|\tilde\pi-\pi|/\pi\,/H$. The assertion allows twice
that (the factor 2, chosen, covers the second-order remainder). It adds
`uniroot`'s $10^{-15}$ and the stopping rule's $10^{-15}c/H$.

```{r ec-L2}
#| cache: true
ec_L2 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ec_fit), function(nm) {
  f <- ec_fit[[nm]]; n <- f$n; N <- sum(n); r <- f$rho; O <- n > 0
  P  <- cellP(f$a, f$b, r); Dr <- dP_drho(f$a, f$b, r); Px <- ec_cellx(f$a, f$b, r)
  cx <- sum((Dr^2 / P)[P > 0]); H <- ec_H(n, f$a, f$b, r, 1e-5)
  Sx <- function(x) ec_obs(f$a, f$b, x, n, P = ec_cellx(f$a, f$b, x))$S
  rx <- uniroot(Sx, r + c(-1e-6, 1e-6), tol = 1e-15)$root
  pert <- sum((n / N * abs(Dr / P) * abs(P - Px) / Px)[O]) / H
  data.frame(table = nm, rho_hat = sprintf("%.17g", r),
             interior = abs(r) < 0.999,
             bracket  = ec_S(n, f$a, f$b, r - 1e-6) > 0 && ec_S(n, f$a, f$b, r + 1e-6) < 0,
             step_at_root = abs(ec_S(n, f$a, f$b, r) / N) / cx,
             S_over_N = ec_S(n, f$a, f$b, r) / N,
             S_rounding_floor = (sum(O) + 2) * .Machine$double.eps * sum((n / N * abs(Dr / P))[O]),
             cancellation_free_minus = rx - r,
             budget = 2 * pert + 1e-15 + 1e-15 * cx / H)
}))
ec_L2
stopifnot(ec_L2$interior, ec_L2$bracket,
          ec_L2$step_at_root < 1e-15,              # rk_rho's own stopping rule
          abs(ec_L2$S_over_N) <= ec_L2$S_rounding_floor,  # ... and below the sum's rounding floor
          abs(ec_L2$cancellation_free_minus) <= ec_L2$budget)
```

**Level E3: invariance.** Every empty cell's probability is overwritten in six
ways: as computed, $0$, $\pm2^{-55}$, its true value, and $10^{-3}$. The last is
absurd on purpose, to show the invariance has nothing to do with smallness. The
observed-cells log-likelihood, score, $\hat I_{\rho\rho}$, $\hat I_{\rho a}$,
$\hat I_{\rho b}$ and the observed entries of `psi_tab0()` at $W = \hat\pi$ must
be **identical**, bitwise. They are not a tolerance question. An empty cell
enters them only as $0\cdot u$, with $u$ finite, or not at all. Adding an exact
zero to a sum leaves it bit for bit unchanged. The whole-table log-likelihood
and the whole-table expected information are printed alongside, and they move.

```{r ec-L3}
#| cache: true
ec_L3 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ec_fit), function(nm) {
  f <- ec_fit[[nm]]; n <- f$n; r <- f$rho; E <- n == 0; O <- !E; W <- n / sum(n)
  P0 <- cellP(f$a, f$b, r); Px <- ec_cellx(f$a, f$b, r)
  perturb <- list(as_computed = P0,
                  empty_0     = replace(P0, E, 0),
                  empty_neg   = replace(P0, E, -2^-55),
                  empty_pos   = replace(P0, E,  2^-55),
                  empty_true  = replace(P0, E, Px[E]),
                  empty_1e_3  = replace(P0, E, 1e-3))
  res <- lapply(perturb, function(P) {
    q  <- ec_obs(f$a, f$b, r, n, P = P)
    ps <- ec_with_P(psi_tab0, function(a, b, rho) P)(f$a, f$b, r, W)
    Dr <- dP_drho(f$a, f$b, r)
    list(obs = c(q$ll, q$S, q$Irr, q$Ira, q$Irb, ps[O]),
         ll_whole = suppressWarnings(sum(n * log(P))),     # NaN warnings are the point
         I_exp_whole = sum(Dr^2 / P))
  })
  data.frame(table = nm, perturbation = names(perturb),
             observed_quantities_identical = sapply(res, function(z) identical(z$obs, res$as_computed$obs)),
             ll_whole_table = sapply(res, `[[`, "ll_whole"),
             I_expected_whole_table = sapply(res, `[[`, "I_exp_whole"), row.names = NULL)
}))
ec_L3
stopifnot(ec_L3$observed_quantities_identical)

# ... and they ARE @sec-normaliser's empirical information, bitwise, compared
# where infoW() is defined: every cell positive, the empty ones at their true values.
ec_true_P <- function(n) function(a, b, rho) {
  P <- cellP(a, b, rho); E <- n == 0; P[E] <- ec_cellx(a, b, rho)[E]; P }
stopifnot(all(sapply(ec_fit, function(f) {
  q <- ec_obs(f$a, f$b, f$rho, f$n)
  I <- ec_with_P(infoW, ec_true_P(f$n))(f$a, f$b, f$rho, f$n / sum(f$n))
  identical(c(q$Irr, q$Ira, q$Irb), c(I$Irr, I$Ira, I$Irb)) })))
```

**Level E4: the two feasibility rules in R's arithmetic.** The whole-table rule
($\min_{rs}\tilde\pi_{rs} > 0$) and the observed-cells rule
($\min_{\mathcal O}\tilde\pi_{rs} > 0$) are evaluated on a $10^{-4}$ grid from .95 to
.999, a grid chosen before looking. Only the second is asserted. The first
depends on the sign of rounding noise (the lemma), so its pattern is a fact
about this platform's `integrate()` and is printed, not asserted.

```{r ec-L4}
#| cache: true
ec_g4 <- seq(0.95, 0.999, by = 1e-4)
ec_L4 <- lapply(ec_fit, function(f) {
  O <- f$n > 0
  m <- t(sapply(ec_g4, function(x) { P <- cellP(f$a, f$b, x)
         c(whole = min(P) > 0, observed = min(P[O]) > 0) }))
  rl <- rle(m[, "whole"])
  list(whole_table_runs = data.frame(feasible = rl$values, points = rl$lengths,
                                     from = ec_g4[cumsum(c(1, head(rl$lengths, -1)))]),
       observed_rule_feasible_everywhere = all(m[, "observed"]),
       whole_rule_feasible_at_root = min(cellP(f$a, f$b, f$rho)) > 0)
})
ec_L4
stopifnot(sapply(ec_L4, `[[`, "observed_rule_feasible_everywhere"))
```

**Level E5: the polish scaler on a sparse design.** The design is
`test_gammadiag.do`'s `dwlsmv_t_gd_fewpat()`: twelve patterns, pattern $r$
repeated $9+r$ times, so $N = 186$ and $K = (4,4,3,3)$. Every pair is polished
from $\hat\rho + 10^{-8}$ with each scaler, 25 steps, and the stopping rule
$|\text{step}| < 10^{-15}$. The offset is chosen to match the d0 optimizer's
$\sim10^{-8}$ floor (`dwls_polychoric.mata`'s header).

$H$ comes from a central difference at $h = 10^{-5}$. Its step-size dependence
is asserted below $10^{-4}$ relative against $h = 10^{-4}$. That is far inside
the smallest margin the conclusions use: 0.35, the distance of pair $(2,3)$'s
empirical rate from $-1$.

The agreement budget for the converged polishes comes from the stopping rule. At
exit, $|S/N| < 10^{-15}c$, so $|\rho - \rho^*| \lesssim 10^{-15}c/H$ for each of
the two runs. Add the score's evaluation jitter $e_S/H$ for each run, where
$e_S = \sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi|u|\,(\delta/\tilde\pi + (|\mathcal O|+2)\varepsilon)$
and $\delta$ is `cellP()`'s measured error on observed cells at the root.

```{r ec-L5}
#| cache: true
# test_gammadiag.do's dwlsmv_t_gd_fewpat(): twelve patterns, pattern r repeated 9 + r times
ec_pat <- matrix(c(0,1,0,2, 1,3,0,0, 2,0,1,1, 3,2,2,0, 0,2,2,1, 1,0,1,2,
                   2,1,0,0, 3,3,1,2, 1,2,2,1, 2,3,0,1, 0,0,1,0, 3,1,2,2), 12, byrow = TRUE)
ec_Yf <- ec_pat[rep(1:12, 9 + 1:12), ]
ec_Kf <- c(4, 4, 3, 3)
ec_L5 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(combn(4, 2, simplify = FALSE), function(v) {
  n <- unclass(table(factor(ec_Yf[, v[1]], 0:(ec_Kf[v[1]] - 1)),
                     factor(ec_Yf[, v[2]], 0:(ec_Kf[v[2]] - 1))))
  a <- ec_thr(rowSums(n)); b <- ec_thr(colSums(n)); N <- sum(n)
  r  <- rk_rho(ec_Yf[, v[1]], ec_Yf[, v[2]], a, b)
  H5 <- ec_H(n, a, b, r, 1e-5); H4 <- ec_H(n, a, b, r, 1e-4)
  ce <- ec_scaler(n, a, b, r, "emp"); cx <- ec_scaler(n, a, b, r, "exp")
  P  <- cellP(a, b, r); Dr <- dP_drho(a, b, r)
  x0 <- r + 1e-8
  pe <- ec_polish(n, a, b, x0, "emp"); px <- ec_polish(n, a, b, x0, "exp")
  dl <- max(abs(P - ec_cellx(a, b, r))[n > 0])
  eS <- sum((n / N * abs(Dr / P) * (dl / P + (sum(n > 0) + 2) * .Machine$double.eps))[n > 0])
  data.frame(pair = paste0(v, collapse = ","), N = N, empty = sum(n == 0), rho = r,
             I_emp = ce, I_exp = cx, H = H5, H_h_relgap = abs(H4 / H5 - 1),
             rate_emp = 1 - H5 / ce, rate_exp = 1 - H5 / cx,
             emp_rule = pe$rule, emp_it = pe$it, emp_err_ratio = abs(pe$x - r) / abs(x0 - r),
             emp_S_over_N = abs(ec_S(n, a, b, pe$x)) / N,
             exp_rule = px$rule, exp_it = px$it, exp_minus_rk = px$x - r,
             budget = (1e-15 * 2 * cx + 2 * eS) / H5,
             all_positive = min(P) > 0,
             masked_is_prefix = if (min(P) > 0) identical(cx, sum(Dr^2 / P)) else NA)
}))
format(ec_L5, digits = 4)
stopifnot(ec_L5$N == 186,
          ec_L5$H_h_relgap < 1e-4,
          abs(ec_L5$rate_exp) < 1, ec_L5$exp_rule,          # masked expected: contracts, meets the rule
          abs(ec_L5$exp_minus_rk) <= ec_L5$budget,
          with(ec_L5[ec_L5$pair == "2,3", ],                 # empirical: does not contract ...
               rate_emp < -1 & !emp_rule & emp_err_ratio > 1),
          with(ec_L5[ec_L5$pair == "1,2", ],                 # ... or contracts too slowly for 25 steps
               abs(rate_emp) < 1 & !emp_rule & emp_err_ratio < 1),
          ec_L5$masked_is_prefix[ec_L5$all_positive])       # bitwise the pre-fix scaler
```

**Level E6: the masked expected scaler on the two high-$\rho$ tables.** The
polish starts at $\hat\rho - 0.01$, an offset chosen to lie well outside the
d0 optimizer's floor. It must meet the stopping rule and land on `rk_rho()`'s
root within the Level E5 budget.

The scaler's departure from the true expected information is then bounded on
$\rho\in[.97,.99]$, a grid chosen to straddle the cliff. For
$\mathcal U = \{n = 0,\ \pi < 2^{e}\}$, `share_add` is the most a kept cell can add
(Property 4), and `share_remove` is the true share that masking can drop. Both are
relative to the scaler. The assertion is Property 4's $|1-H/c| + 4s < 1$.

```{r ec-L6}
#| cache: true
ec_L6 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ec_fit), function(nm) {
  f <- ec_fit[[nm]]; n <- f$n; N <- sum(n); r <- f$rho
  x0 <- r - 0.01
  px <- ec_polish(n, f$a, f$b, x0, "exp")
  P  <- cellP(f$a, f$b, r); Dr <- dP_drho(f$a, f$b, r); H <- ec_H(n, f$a, f$b, r, 1e-5)
  cx <- ec_scaler(n, f$a, f$b, r, "exp"); ce <- ec_scaler(n, f$a, f$b, r, "emp")
  dl <- max(abs(P - ec_cellx(f$a, f$b, r))[n > 0])
  eS <- sum((n / N * abs(Dr / P) * (dl / P + (sum(n > 0) + 2) * .Machine$double.eps))[n > 0])
  sh <- sapply(seq(0.97, 0.99, by = 1e-3), function(x) {
    Pc <- cellP(f$a, f$b, x); Px <- ec_cellx(f$a, f$b, x); g <- ec_gran(f$a, f$b, x)
    Dc <- dP_drho(f$a, f$b, x); U <- n == 0 & Px < g; cm <- sum((Dc^2 / Pc)[Pc > 0])
    c(add = sum(Dc[U]^2 / g[U]) / cm, remove = sum(Dc[U]^2 / Px[U]) / cm, U = sum(U)) })
  data.frame(table = nm, rate_exp = 1 - H / cx, rate_emp = 1 - H / ce,
             start = x0, rule = px$rule, it = px$it, minus_rk = px$x - r,
             budget = (1e-15 * 2 * cx + 2 * eS) / H,
             max_U = max(sh["U", ]), share_add = max(sh["add", ]), share_remove = max(sh["remove", ]))
}))
format(ec_L6, digits = 4)
stopifnot(ec_L6$rule, abs(ec_L6$minus_rk) <= ec_L6$budget,
          abs(ec_L6$rate_exp) + 4 * pmax(ec_L6$share_add, ec_L6$share_remove) < 1)
```

**Level E7: the reference values for production's unit test.** These are the
numbers `fixtures/generate/10_fixtures.R` writes to
`fixtures/expected/highrho_polychoric.csv`, with its own restatement of
`cellP`, `dP_drho` and `rk_rho`. They are printed at 17 significant digits,
because `write.csv()` would give 15. `tests/unit/test_polychoric.do` Level L9
reads them and asserts production's $\hat\rho$ within spec §7.2's $10^{-8}$.
The generator's 17 digits equalled these exactly when compared on 2026-09-26;
nothing asserts that agreement.

```{r ec-L7}
ec_ref <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ec_fit), function(nm) { f <- ec_fit[[nm]]
  data.frame(table = nm, N = sum(f$n),
             a1 = sprintf("%.17g", f$a[1]), a2 = sprintf("%.17g", f$a[2]), a3 = sprintf("%.17g", f$a[3]),
             b1 = sprintf("%.17g", f$b[1]), b2 = sprintf("%.17g", f$b[2]), b3 = sprintf("%.17g", f$b[3]),
             rho_hat = sprintf("%.17g", f$rho)) }))
ec_ref
```

### What the verification shows

Executed 2026-09-26 under R 4.6.0 by the main session, through a runner that
extracts this file's prerequisite chunks by label (`setup`, `designs`,
`gate3-core`, `norm-core`, and `psi_tab0`/`rk_rho` from `rank-core`) and runs
this section's chunks in order. Every assertion passed. **The document as a
whole was not re-rendered.** The section was drafted by an agent and executed
here, not trusted from the agent's own run. Figures are single runs. None
involves a seed.

- **E1.** The corners' true values are $3.7\times10^{-23}$ and $1.6\times10^{-23}$
  at $\rho = .98$ on `mc_c_98_0007`, and $1.5\times10^{-23}$ and $4.0\times10^{-23}$
  on `mc_c_98_0002`. At .99 they are below $10^{-41}$. The two cancellation-free
  routes agree to $1.7\times10^{-14}$ relative, at worst. `cellP()`'s rectangle
  difference is within $2.8\times10^{-16}$ absolute of the truth on every cell.
  At .95 and .96 it reproduces the true corners to four digits, $3.454\times10^{-11}$
  and $3.169\times10^{-13}$. From .975 on it reads $0$ or $\pm2^{-55}$ and
  $\pm2^{-54}$, which are exactly the values the Stata measurement reports, and
  every computed cell lies on the lemma's grid.
- **E2.** $\hat\rho = 0.98221567982694824$ (`mc_c_98_0007`) and
  $0.98027363887635555$ (`mc_c_98_0002`). $|S/N|/c = 1.2\times10^{-16}$ and
  $1.4\times10^{-16}$, inside the $10^{-15}$ rule. $|S/N| = 1.5\times10^{-14}$,
  below the sum's own rounding floor
  $(|\mathcal O|+2)\,\varepsilon\sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi|u| \approx 2.0\times10^{-14}$,
  so no more can be asked of the root. Computed with the cancellation-free
  cells, it is the same double on both tables (budget $2.2\times10^{-15}$).
- **E3.** All twelve perturbations leave every observed-cell quantity bitwise
  unchanged, and $\hat I_{\rho\rho}$, $\hat I_{\rho a}$, $\hat I_{\rho b}$ equal
  `infoW()`'s bitwise. The whole-table log-likelihood is `NaN` as computed on
  both tables, since a corner is $\le 0$ at the root. The whole-table expected
  information ranges from $-2.2\times10^8$ to `Inf` across the perturbations,
  against 127.0 and 109.6 at the true values.
- **E4. R reproduces the failure.** Under the whole-table rule, R's own `cellP()`
  is infeasible at the root on both tables. On `mc_c_98_0007` the feasible set
  is fragmented: feasible to .9704, then isolated feasible points at .9707 and
  .9778, then infeasible to .999. On `mc_c_98_0002` it ends at .9703, with no
  islands on this grid. The fragments' locations are R's rounding, and Stata's
  differ: on `mc_c_98_0002` Stata was finite at .985. The observed-cells rule is
  feasible at every grid point on both.
- **E5.** Pair $(2,3)$: $\hat I_{\rho\rho}(\hat\pi) = 0.35394$, $I = 0.71766$,
  $H = 0.83065$. The rates are $-1.347$ (empirical) and $-0.157$ (expected). The
  empirical polish's error grows 1710-fold in 25 steps, ending at
  $|S|/N = 1.4\times10^{-5}$. Pair $(1,2)$: $-0.886$ against $-0.072$. The
  empirical polish contracts (error ratio 0.049, which is $0.886^{25}$) but ends at
  $|S|/N = 5.2\times10^{-10}$, far from the rule. The other four pairs have
  $|1-H/\hat I_{\rho\rho}| \le 0.25$. The masked expected scaler converges on all
  six pairs in 4 to 10 steps, to within $8.3\times10^{-16}$ of `rk_rho()`, against
  budgets of 4.6 to $10.1\times10^{-15}$. Every computed cell of this design is
  positive, and there the masked scaler is bitwise the pre-fix one.

  **Against the one-off Stata measurement** (2026-09-26, the main session): pair
  $(2,3)$ at 0.35394, 0.71766, 0.83066, with $-1.347$ and $-0.157$, and pair
  $(1,2)$ at $-0.886$ and $-0.072$. The empirical polish ended at
  $|S|/N = 3.1\times10^{-6}$ and $9.4\times10^{-10}$. R reproduces every rate and
  information to the digits quoted. The end-points differ because production
  starts from its optimizer's point, not from $\hat\rho + 10^{-8}$.
- **E6.** From $\hat\rho - 0.01$ the masked expected polish meets the rule in 7
  and 6 steps, landing $0$ and $1.1\times10^{-16}$ from `rk_rho()`'s root, against
  budgets of $2.7\times10^{-15}$ and $2.8\times10^{-15}$. The rates there are
  $8\times10^{-4}$ and $1\times10^{-4}$, and the empirical ones $-2\times10^{-4}$ and
  $-5\times10^{-4}$, so at $N = 5000$ either scaler converges. $\mathcal U$ holds at
  most the two corners. The worst `share_add` is $4.7\times10^{-13}$ and the
  worst `share_remove` $5.1\times10^{-13}$, so the masked scaler is the expected
  information to 13 digits wherever the fit goes.

### What production must do

Each item cites the statement or level that supports it.

1. **The pairwise log-likelihood, score and feasibility check run over observed
   cells only** (the statement; E3, E4). The d0 evaluator must not return missing
   because an *empty* cell's computed probability is $\le 0$: that cell's term is
   $0$ for every positive $\pi$, and its computed value is rounding noise (the
   lemma, E1). A non-positive **observed** cell is still infeasible.
2. **The polish scaler is the expected information over cells whose computed
   probability is positive**, which is `rk_rho()`'s rule. Any positive scaler has the
   same fixed point, but convergence needs $|1-H/c| < 1$. The empirical scaler
   breaks that on a sparse table (E5), and the masked expected one does not on
   any design measured here (E5, E6). Where every computed cell is positive it is
   bitwise the pre-fix polish (E5). **In Mata the mask must be applied before the
   division**, because $x/0$ is missing and $0 \times .$ is still missing. Multiplying
   `(Dr:*Dr):/P` by `(P:>0)` therefore does not mask anything.
3. **The polish stops, and flags `converged = 0`, if a step makes an observed cell
   non-positive.** A root at which an observed cell has $\pi \le 0$ is not a root of
   this likelihood. An empty cell going non-positive is not a reason to stop
   (item 1).
4. **`dwlsmv_pairinfo()` zeroes $u$ exactly where $W = 0$ and $\tilde\pi \le 0$**, as
   `psi_tab0()` does. This changes no weighted sum and no gathered entry (E3). A
   cell with $W \ne 0$ and $\tilde\pi \le 0$ still aborts. At $W = \pi$ that
   includes a corner computed at $-2^{-55}$, so **the expected-information oracle
   aborts wherever a corner rounds negative**. It silently drops a corner computed
   at exactly $0$. Tests of the $W = \pi$ path must stay at $\rho$ where every
   computed cell is positive (the statement's last paragraph).
5. **`dwlsmv_cellprob()` keeps its aborting contract.** Callers that can meet an
   underflowed empty cell take the raw probabilities and apply items 1–4.

**Not settled here, and deliberately left open:** whether $\hat\Gamma$ is built
from a pair with `converged = 0`, rank-deficient $\hat\Gamma$, the sparse-cell and
small-count policies, and the 0.999 bound. Two further points were found here
and are not decided:

- No proof says the masked expected scaler contracts on every table. E5 and E6
  are measurements.
- A polish that exhausts its 25 steps without meeting the rule is not a
  converged fit, and item 3 does not catch that case. Module 10's centring row
  does (@sec-gamma-rank, Theorem 1(2)).

## Module 2: a bracketed root-finder on the analytic score {#sec-rootfind}

*Drafted 2026-09-29 by a read-only agent, before any change to
`dwls_polychoric()`; revised by the main session with the user's decisions of
the same day and executed by it.* E-008 (2026-09-28, *Module 2's high-ρ slow path*)
found that the 21 interior pairs flagged `converged = 0` on replicates 1–5 of
`mc_c_998`, `mc_B_995` and `mc_B_9975` sit 8.6e-10 to 5.2e-8 from the score's
root, and that the failure is `optimize()`'s d0 step collapsing, not the
likelihood. It named option B: find the root of the analytic score directly,
inside a bracket, searched only where every observed cell is positive. This
section derives that algorithm and verifies it. It changes no estimator:
$\hat\rho$ is still the root of @sec-emptycells' observed-cells score
$S(\rho) = \sum_{\mathcal O} n_{rs}u_{rs}$, with the thresholds held fixed at
Module 1's values (the two-step polychoric of @sec-general).

Throughout, $\bar S(\rho) = S(\rho)/N$, and $c(\rho)$ is the masked expected
information of @sec-emptycells, the polish's scaler. Tildes mark computed
values.

### The feasible region, and the resolvable one

*Definition.* $\rho$ is **feasible** if every observed cell's computed
probability is positive, $\min_{\mathcal O}\tilde\pi_{rs}(\rho) > 0$. This is
@sec-emptycells' observed-cells rule, which the d0 evaluator already applies.
$\tilde F$ is the set of feasible $\rho$. The true $\pi_{rs}$ are positive on all
of $(-1,1)$, so $\tilde F \ne (-1,1)$ is purely a floating-point effect: a
point is infeasible only where some observed cell's true probability is within
its absolute rounding error $\delta_P$ (below) of zero.

**$\tilde F$ is not an interval.** On 18 of the 70 pairs of Level R3, the grid
points of $\tilde F$ on the side away from the root form two runs. Near
$\rho = -1$, a strongly positive table has observed diagonal cells whose true
probabilities are far below the rounding floor. The rectangle difference returns them
as $0$ or $\pm$ a few $10^{-16}$, with signs set by rounding (the lemma of
@sec-emptycells), so feasibility there is noise. This is the "second score
sign change near $\rho = -0.999$" that E-008 (2026-09-28)
recorded on 7 pairs, seen from the other side.

A proof that such fragments cannot occur would need each cell's probability to
be unimodal in $\rho$, so that $\{\rho : \min_{\mathcal O}\pi_{rs} > t\}$ is an
interval for every $t$. That holds for two of the three kinds of cell:

- A **corner** cell is an orthant probability and monotone in $\rho$ (Plackett,
  §4.7: $\partial_\rho\Phi_2 = \phi_2 > 0$).
- An **edge** cell with $a$ finite and $b_1 < b_2$ has
  $\partial_\rho\pi = \pm[\phi_2(a,b_2;\rho) - \phi_2(a,b_1;\rho)]$. Its sign is
  that of $\rho a - (b_1+b_2)/2$, because
  $\log[\phi_2(a,b_2)/\phi_2(a,b_1)] = [\rho a(b_2-b_1) - (b_2^2-b_1^2)/2]/(1-\rho^2)$.
  That is linear in $\rho$, so it changes sign at most once.
- An **interior** cell (all four corners finite) is **not** unimodal in general.
  Level R3 exhibits a rectangle whose $\partial_\rho\pi$ changes sign five times on
  $(-1,1)$.

Even with unimodal cells the proof would fail in floating point, which is where
the fragments come from.

*Definition (adopted by the user, 2026-09-29).* $\rho$ is **resolvable**, or
**usable**, if every observed cell satisfies $\tilde\pi_{rs}(\rho) > \delta_P$:
$$\mathcal R_P = \{\rho : \min_{\mathcal O}\tilde\pi_{rs}(\rho) > \delta_P\}.$$ At a feasible point
that is not resolvable, some observed $\tilde u_{rs}$ has relative error above
1, so the sign of $\tilde{\bar S}$ is not determined by the data. The root-finder
below searches only resolvable points, and treats an unresolvable one as it
would an infeasible one. Resolvability implies feasibility. It differs from
@sec-emptycells' rule only where an observed cell is within $\delta_P$ of
underflow. On Level R3's grid, the resolvable points form **one run on every
one of the 70 pairs**, including the 18 whose feasible points do not. That is
an observation on a grid, not a proof that $\mathcal R_P$ is an interval, so
the search is confined to the connected piece of $\mathcal R_P \cap [-B, B]$
containing $0$, and a usable point found beyond an unusable one is reported
(below), never skipped.

*$\rho = 0$ is resolvable.* At $\rho = 0$, $\pi_{rs} = p_r q_s$, a product of
the two marginal category probabilities implied by Module 1's thresholds. Each
is at least $1/N$ because every category is observed. So
$\pi_{rs}(0) \ge N^{-2}$, which exceeds $\delta_P \approx 4.4\times10^{-15}$
for $N < 1.5\times10^{7}$. If it fails nonetheless, the pair has no starting
point and no status describes it: **the fit aborts** (production: rc 3498;
`rf_root()` stops). Decided by the user, 2026-09-30.

### The bracket

Write $B$ for the bound on $|\rho|$. **$B = 0.999$, a declared hard search
limit (decided by the user, 2026-09-29)**, replacing the implicit cap of
production's $\rho = 0.999\tanh z$. It enters the code as a parameter. The search
starts at $x_0 = 0$. Let $d = \operatorname{sign}\bar S(x_0)$: the root, if there
is one, lies on that side.

1. **Walk.** From the current inner point $x$, try $x' = d\,\min(B,\ 1 - (1 - d x)/2)$,
   halving the distance to $\pm1$ and capping at $\pm B$. If $x'$ is resolvable and
   $d\,\bar S(x') < 0$, the bracket is $[x, x']$ (ordered). If it is resolvable
   with $d\,\bar S(x') \ge 0$, it becomes the inner point. If it equals the inner
   point (the bound was reached with no sign change), stop: **no sign change up to
   the bound**.
2. **Frontier.** If $x'$ is unresolvable and is not $\pm B$, evaluate $d B$
   first: if it is resolvable, stop: **gap in the usable region**. This detects
   a gap only between $x'$ and the bound, not every gap. Otherwise bisect between
   the inner point and $x'$ on resolvability, evaluating $\bar S$ at every
   resolvable midpoint. A resolvable midpoint with $d\,\bar S < 0$ closes the
   bracket. If the interval shrinks to four ulps with no sign change, stop:
   **no sign change up to the usable end**.

The inequality is strict: $\bar S(x') = 0$ exactly does not close a bracket. Level
R5's $2\times2$ table shows why. Its score is positive everywhere and underflows
to exactly $0$ from $\rho = 1 - 2^{-16}$, and an exact zero there is not a root.

From $x_0 = 0$ the walk reaches $B = 0.999$ in ten trial points. The frontier
bisection runs only when a trial point is unresolvable, and costs up to about 52
more evaluations. None of the 70 pairs triggers it, because on the side each one
walks, every grid point up to $\pm0.999$ is resolvable (Level R3).

The bracket's ends are evaluated, resolvable, and of opposite computed sign:
$\bar S(\ell) > 0 > \bar S(h)$ with $\ell < h$. That orientation, positive on
the left, is a maximum's. A score whose sign is reversed walks away from the
root and is never bracketed (Level R5).

### The step: safeguarded Fisher scoring

Inside $[\ell, h]$, from the current point $x$ (the end with smaller
$|\bar S|$), the trial is the Fisher step
$$x^+ = x + \bar S(x)/c(x),$$
with $c$ the masked expected information of @sec-emptycells (its *scaler
production uses* paragraph). The step is replaced by the bisection point
$(\ell + h)/2$ when $x^+ \notin (\ell, h)$ or when $|x^+ - x|$ exceeds half the
previous step (the step is not shrinking fast enough). The trial is evaluated
and replaces the end whose computed sign it shares. Every iteration therefore
shrinks a sign-certified bracket, and bisection alone would reduce any bracket
in $(-1,1)$ to four ulps in at most about 55 iterations, so the loop terminates
whatever the Fisher step does.

**Why the expected information and not the analytic $S'$.** Three reasons, each
from this file:

1. $c > 0$ wherever some positive cell has $\partial_\rho\pi \ne 0$
   (@sec-emptycells, Property 3), so the Fisher step always points uphill in
   $\ell$. $S'$ has no sign guarantee: $\ell$ is **not concave** in $\rho$ in
   general (Level R4 shows $\bar S$ increasing on an interval), and a Newton
   step on a convex stretch points downhill.
2. $c$ is the scaler @sec-emptycells already derived and measured, with
   $1 - H/c$ between $-0.16$ and $8\times10^{-4}$ on the designs measured
   there, and $H/c$ between 0.98 and 1.06 on the 116 interior pairs of Level R1.
   Local convergence is linear at rate $|1 - H/c|$, fast enough here.
3. $S'$ needs $\partial^2_\rho\pi$, which nothing in this file derives or
   verifies yet. It would be new mathematics.

Inside a bracket, the Fisher step's convergence needs no proof. The safeguard
supplies termination, and the scaler only sets the speed.

### The stopping rule

Stop, with $\hat\rho = x$, when **both**
$$|\bar S(x)| \le \tau_S(x) \qquad\text{and}\qquad h - \ell \le \tau_\rho(x).$$

**$\tau_S$: the score's own evaluation error.** Each computed term is
$\tilde u_{rs} = \tilde D_{rs}/\tilde\pi_{rs}$, with $D = \partial_\rho\pi$ a
signed sum of four $\phi_2$ values (Plackett) and $\pi$ a rectangle difference of
four $\Phi_2$ values. To first order,
$$|\tilde{\bar S} - \bar S| \le \tau_S =
  \sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi_{rs}\,\frac{\delta_{D,rs} + |\tilde u_{rs}|\,\delta_P}{\tilde\pi_{rs}}
  + (|\mathcal O| + 2)\,\varepsilon\sum_{\mathcal O}\hat\pi_{rs}|\tilde u_{rs}|,$$
where:

- $\delta_P = 4\delta_\Phi + 3\varepsilon$: four corners, each within $\delta_\Phi$,
  and three roundings of numbers at most 1. **$\delta_\Phi = 9.39\times10^{-16}
  = 4.23\cdot2^{-52}$, chosen after measuring** (decided by the user,
  2026-09-29): the largest per-corner error of StataMP 18's `binormal()`
  against a 160-bit reference over $|\rho| \le B$ and thresholds in
  $[-2.5, 2.5]$ (`tools/measure_binormal.do`, E-056). StataMP
  16.1 on the milestone machine reproduces every figure (2026-09-30). So
  $\delta_P = 4.42\times10^{-15}$. The whole grid, to $|\rho| = 0.9999$, gives
  an envelope of $7.31\cdot2^{-52}$; thresholds outside $[-2.5, 2.5]$ are
  unmeasured. R's `mvtnorm` (TVPACK) is within $1.23\cdot2^{-52}$ per corner on the
  same grid (the tool's drafting run), so the budget is conservative for
  these chunks. An earlier
  draft took $\delta_\Phi = 2^{-52}$ from R, which `binormal()` exceeds.
- $\delta_{D,rs} = \varepsilon\sum_{\text{corners}}|\phi_2|\,(|z| + 7)$, with $z$ the
  density's exponent. `exp` amplifies its argument's relative error by $|z|$,
  and the constant covers the density's own arithmetic and the three additions.
  **Corrected 2026-10-25 (user): this is not a per-corner bound.** It misses the
  cancellation in $a^2-2\rho ab+b^2$ and in $1-\rho\cdot\rho$ for $a\approx\pm b$
  as $|\rho|\to1$. The corrected per-corner model is in @sec-deltad. Production
  still computes the expression above, and no code changed. The resulting
  $\tau_S$ bounds the score's density error with a measured margin: at most
  $0.0042\,\tau_S$ on Level R1's pairs. It is not a derived bound.
- The last term is the summation's rounding, as in @sec-emptycells Level E2.

A point with $|\bar S| \le \tau_S$ cannot be told from a root in this arithmetic.
Asking for less is asking for noise, and asking for more stops early.

**$\tau_\rho$: the width of that indistinguishable zone.** Near the root,
$\bar S(\rho^* + \Delta) \approx -H\Delta$ with $H = -\bar S'$. So the zone where
$|\bar S| \le \tau_S$ has half-width $\tau_S/H$, and its condition number is
$1/H$. The rule uses the scaler for $H$:
$$\tau_\rho(x) = 16\,\tau_S(x)/c(x) + 8\,\mathrm{ulp}(x).$$
The factor 16 is derived, not tuned. Once $|\bar S(x)| \le \tau_S$, the loop
**probes** the far side at $x \pm \tau_\rho/2$. If $H \ge c/2$, the probe moves
$\bar S$ by at least $H\tau_\rho/2 \ge 4\tau_S$, which exceeds $|\bar S(x)|$
plus the probe's own error $\tau_S$. The probe's computed sign is then certain,
and the bracket closes to width $\tau_\rho/2$. The premise $H/c \ge 1/2$ is
**measured, not proved** (Level R1 asserts it on every pair). If it fails, the
probe may land on the wrong side. Then the loop continues by bisection, so it
only slows. The $8\,\mathrm{ulp}$ term keeps $\tau_\rho$ above the spacing of
doubles.

**Why both conditions.** The width condition certifies that the computed score
changes sign inside $[\ell, h]$. A small $|\bar S|$ alone does not: a score
decaying towards zero along a boundary without crossing it satisfies it. The
$|\bar S|$ condition catches a sign change that is not a root. On a continuous
$\bar S$ with correct derivatives, a width below $\tau_\rho$ forces
$|\bar S| \lesssim H\tau_\rho + \tau_S$ at the better end. A bracket that has
shrunk while $|\bar S|$ stays large is a jump: an unresolvable gap, or a wrong
derivative. The loop does not test for it separately. It keeps shrinking the
bracket, to adjacent doubles if need be, until the evaluation cap ends it, and
the pair is returned with status **evaluation cap**, not converged; if the
loop lands on an unresolvable point first, with **unresolvable point inside the
bracket**. No separate "stalled bracket" status (decided by the user,
2026-09-30): statuses name outcomes a user can act on, not every internal exit.

A bracket is only ever built by the walk, which orients it by construction and
evaluates its ends. The code's `bracket =` entry, used only by the negative
controls, skips the walk, so it checks both properties: an end that is not
resolvable, or ends not of sign $(+, -)$, is a broken invariant and **aborts**
(production: rc 3498), rather than returning a status (decided by the user,
2026-09-30).

These tolerances are far below spec §7.2's $10^{-8}$ tier: on the 116 interior pairs of
Level R1, $\tau_\rho \le 5.4\times10^{-12}$. Level R1c checks $\tau_S$ itself
against the score recomputed from cancellation-free cells.

### Uniqueness

*Is the root unique?* **Not proved, and the easy proofs fail.**

- **$\ell$ is not concave in $\rho$.** Level R4 shows a $3\times4$ table on which
  $\bar S$ *increases* over part of $(-1,1)$, and 13 of Level R4's 156 random
  tables are non-concave as well. So concavity cannot carry the proof.
- **Per-cell unimodality fails** for interior cells (Level R3), so a
  quasi-concavity argument built cell by cell does not go through either.

What is established is empirical. On every table in Levels R3 and R4 — the 70
Monte Carlo pairs and 156 random integer tables with $K_1, K_2 \le 5$, sparse and
non-concave ones included — $\bar S$ changes sign **at most once** on the
resolvable grid. That supports a conjecture that $\ell$ is
quasi-concave (so $\bar S$ has one sign change) even where it is not concave.
It is not a proof, and no counterexample was found.

**The development test, run 2026-09-30** (`tools/mc_signcount.R`, drafted by
a read-only agent and executed by the main session). Every pair of every
replicate of the 42 paired Monte Carlo conditions, 1,086,996 pairs, was
classified on a grid fixed before running: uniform in Fisher-z with step
0.005, plus $0$ and $\pm B$, 1523 points. A point's sign counted only when
$|\bar S| > \tau_S$, at usable points only. The fast evaluator agreed with
`rf_eval()` on a check set fixed in advance: 462 points, no disagreement in
usability or sign, largest gap $0.044\,\tau_S$. **No pair has more than one
sign change, none has a gap in its usable region, and none has a single change
of minimum orientation.** Changes closer together than one grid step would go
unseen; that is the test's stated blind spot. 1,033 pairs have no sign change:

- 698 in `mc_c_999` and `mc_B_9975`, the boundary designs;
- 335 in `mc_a2n_40` (326) and `mc_a2n_60` (9). **Post hoc inspection only:**
  every one of these tables was read, nothing was refitted, and neither the
  root-finder nor its thresholds were altered. Each is a binary pair whose
  $2\times2$ table has an empty cell, so the likelihood's supremum is at
  $\pm1$ and no interior root exists (case 3 of *When there is no sign
  change*). None of a fixed-seed sample of 300 one-change pairs per condition
  has an empty cell. This validates the behaviour committed in advance; it
  does not adjust anything to fit the result.

These figures are a one-off measurement recorded here, not asserted by a chunk:
the scan takes about 70 minutes on six cores.

**Consequence for the algorithm.** Where $\bar S$ has more than one root, the
walk from $x_0 = 0$ brackets the first sign change in the direction of
$\bar S(0)$. That need not be the global maximum. Every root the loop accepts is
a local maximum by construction, because the bracket's orientation is a
maximum's. A minimum is never returned. Guaranteeing the global maximum would
need a scan whose spacing cannot be derived without a bound on the number of
roots. **Decided by the user (2026-09-29): no global scan in production;
multiple roots are tested for during development** (Levels R3 and R4 here, and
a sign-change count on a fine grid over every pair of the paired Monte Carlo
re-run). Two cheap checks stand in for the scan:

- **Consistency.** Every point evaluated in the walk left of the root must have
  $\bar S > 0$, and right of it $\bar S < 0$. Level R1 asserts it.
- **The endpoint check.** After the stopping rule holds, $\bar S$ is evaluated
  at the **last usable evaluation on each side**: $\pm B$ if usable, otherwise
  the usable end of the frontier bisection towards $\pm B$ (to four ulps). It is
  not evaluated at $\pm1$ or at a point where some observed $\tilde\pi$ is at or
  below $\delta_P$. The root is accepted only if $\bar S > \tau_S$ at the lower
  end and $\bar S < -\tau_S$ at the upper end. If $|\bar S| \le \tau_S$ at either
  end the sign is not determined: **ambiguous endpoint sign**. Otherwise an
  end has the wrong sign, so $\bar S$ changes sign at least once more, between
  that end and the bracket: **more than one sign change**. Neither is `converged = 1`. The check detects an odd
  number of extra sign changes on one side; an even number between the root and
  an end goes unseen, which is what the development test is for.

**The endpoint check's own cap: 54 evaluations per side.** The user decided on
2026-09-30 that the check has its own cap, derived from the frontier width, and
that a pair's reported evaluation count includes the check's. One side costs
one evaluation at $\pm B$, then bisections of $[\text{end}, \pm B]$ whose
initial width is below $2B < 2$. Let $u = 2^{-53}$, the spacing of doubles in
$[\tfrac12, 1)$. A computed midpoint of two numbers in $(-1, 1)$ is within
$u/2$ of the true one, so after $k$ bisections the width is below
$2^{1-k} + u$. When $|\text{out}| \ge \tfrac12$ the loop stops at width
$\le 4\,\mathrm{ulp}(\text{out}) = 4u$, which $2^{1-k} \le 3u$ guarantees:
$k \ge 54 - \log_2 3 \approx 52.4$. So **at most 53 bisections plus the
evaluation at $\pm B$: 54**, and the cap equals that bound. The premise
$|\text{out}| \ge \tfrac12$ holds when every unusable point lies outside
$[-\tfrac12, \tfrac12]$. It is **measured, not proved**: Level R3 asserts it on
its grid. Where it fails, the frontier sits nearer $0$, its ulps are finer, and
the check may reach the cap. The pair is then returned with status **evaluation
cap**, not converged. Level R2 asserts that no Monte Carlo pair reaches it.

**The two cap exits, told apart by the evaluation count.** Status 7 has two
exits, both returning $(\hat\rho, 7, k)$: the endpoint check's cap and the root
search's cap. The walk's evaluations, its frontier bisection's included, are
counted before the loop's cap test, so a root-cap exit can have $k > 40$. This
paragraph bounds $k$ at each exit under the premise the 54 already rests on:
**every unusable point lies outside $[-\tfrac12, \tfrac12]$** (measured, not
proved; Level R3). The side $d = -1$ is the mirror of $d = 1$ under exact
negation, so take $d = 1$. Let $u = 2^{-53}$.

*Before the loop.* $k_0 = 1$ evaluation at $0$, or $k_0 = 3$ when
$\bar S(0) = 0$ and both probes have one sign, so the walk starts from
$x_0 = t = \tau_\rho(0)/2 \ge 0$. The trials are
$c_{j} = \mathrm{fl}(\min(B, 1 - (1 - e_{j-1})/2))$, with $e_j$ the last usable
point. From $x_0 = 0$, $c_1 = \tfrac12$ is usable under the premise. From
$x_0 = t > 0$, $c_1 = \mathrm{fl}(\tfrac12 + t/2)$ may be unusable; that case,
$J = 0$, is treated separately below. Otherwise let $J \ge 1$ trials be usable
and trial $J+1$ unusable (a sign change at any trial ends the walk sooner).

1. *$1 - e_J \le 2^{-J}$.* By induction: if $1 - e_{j-1} \le 2^{-(j-1)}$, then
   $y = (1 - e_{j-1})/2 \le 2^{-j}$ and $1 - y \ge 1 - 2^{-j}$, a double, so
   rounding (monotone) keeps $c_j \ge 1 - 2^{-j}$. For $j \ge 2$ the
   subtraction $1 - e_{j-1}$ is exact (Sterbenz).
2. *The initial bracket width.* For $c_{J+1} \ne B$: $c_{J+1} \le 1 - y + u/2$
   with $y \le 2^{-(J+1)}$, and $c_{J+1} - e_J$ is a multiple of $u$ (both in
   $[\tfrac12, 1)$), as is $2^{-(J+1)}$; so $w_0 \le 2^{-(J+1)}$, i.e.
   $n_0 = w_0/u \le 2^{52-J}$. For $c_{J+1} = B$ ($J = 9$):
   $w_0 \le 0.999 - (1 - 2^{-9}) < 2^{-10}$, so $n_0 < 2^{43}$.
3. *Each bisection.* Both ends lie in $[\tfrac12, 1)$, where the spacing is $u$.
   $\mathrm{fl}(e + \text{out})$ lies in $[1, 2)$ and is within $u$ of the sum,
   and halving is exact, so the midpoint is a multiple of $u$ within $u/2$ of
   the true one. The new width, a multiple of $u$ at most $w/2 + u/2$, is at
   most $u\lceil n/2\rceil$. Hence $n_k \le \lceil n_0/2^k\rceil$.
4. *The stop.* $|\text{out}| \ge \tfrac12$ under the premise, so
   $4\,\mathrm{ulp}(\text{out}) = 4u$, and the loop stops at the first $k$ with
   $n_k \le 4$. That holds once $n_0/2^k \le 4$: at most $50 - J$ bisections
   when $c_{J+1} \ne B$, at most $41$ when $c_{J+1} = B$.

Counting the $J$ usable trials, the unusable one, the evaluation at $B$ (only
when $c_{J+1} \ne B$) and the bisections:

$$
k_{\text{pre}} \le k_0 + J + 1 + 1 + (50 - J) = k_0 + 52, \qquad
k_{\text{pre}} \le k_0 + 9 + 1 + 41 = k_0 + 51 \text{ at } B .
$$

*The case $J = 0$* (zero-probe start only, $k_0 = 3$). The inner end starts at
$t < \tfrac12$, so steps 1–3 do not apply: the ends are not on one grid of
spacing $u$. The coarser argument of the 54 does apply. Each computed midpoint
is within $u/2$ of the true one, so $w_k < w_0 2^{-k} + u$, with
$w_0 < \tfrac12 + u$. The loop stops once $w_0 2^{-k} \le 3u$, which takes at
most 51 bisections. So $k_{\text{pre}} \le 3 + 0 + 1 + 1 + 51 = 56$. This bound
is not shown to be attained: a targeted search (`walkbound_j0.R`, 694,014 runs
with the frontier on the premise's edge at $\tfrac12$) reaches 55 at most.

So **$k_{\text{pre}} \le 53$ from a nonzero $\bar S(0)$, and $\le 56$ from the
zero-probe start** (55 when $J \ge 1$). A bracket found mid-bisection only
lowers the count. The gap (status 4) and status 3 never reach the loop.

*The root-search cap.* The loop tests $k \ge 40$ only after the stopping rule
fails, and adds one evaluation per pass. It therefore exits with $k = 40$ if
$k_{\text{pre}} < 40$, and with $k = k_{\text{pre}}$ otherwise. **At a root-cap
exit $40 \le k \le 56$** (at most 53 unless $\bar S(0) = 0$ exactly; 55
observed).

*The endpoint cap.* The capped side has used exactly $54$ ($k$ reaches 54 and
the next pass returns). The other side uses at least 1. Before the check, the
walk path has used at least 2 (the evaluation at $0$ and the bracketing trial).
The zero-probe-closed path (the crossing at $[-t, t]$) has used 3, and a
supplied bracket 2. **At an endpoint-cap exit $k \ge 57$** (58 on the
zero-probe-closed path). The figure 56 used earlier counted one evaluation
before the check. That is a valid lower bound but not the sharp one.

*Consequences.* Under the premise, `iterations` $\le 56$ at status 7 means the
root search's cap, and $\ge 57$ means the endpoint check's. The derived margin
is 1 evaluation, and 4 unless $\bar S(0) = 0$ exactly.
The zero-probe-closed path can return status 7, but only through the endpoint
cap. Its loop is never entered, so it never meets the root-search cap. **Without
the premise the walk has no bound short of the double range.** When trial 0.5
is unusable, the bisection runs towards a frontier near 0 at that frontier's
ulps: $k_{\text{pre}} = 62, 86, 385, 1049$ for frontiers at $10^{-3}$,
$10^{-10}$, $10^{-100}$, $10^{-300}$. The two exits then overlap in `iterations`.
The 54 shares this premise.

**What a premise failure now costs, and the policy that follows** (decided by
the user, 2026-10-02). For the 54, a failure of the premise costs at most a cap
hit: the pair is returned as *evaluation cap* and treated as non-root. For the
split above it costs more. A root-search-cap pair whose walk bisected towards a
frontier near $0$ can reach $k \ge 57$ and would be read as an endpoint cap,
putting a pair with no root under the group A contract and into Γ̂. So the
split is **not used yet**: every status 7 stays with the non-root statuses
(interim (iii) of 2026-10-02). The bound needs the premise only to make the
first walk trial usable; once it is, every later unusable trial lies beyond
$\tfrac12$ and steps 1–4 hold without it. Except for the zero-probe start with
$J = 0$, a per-pair check of that trial's usability may therefore replace the
premise. That check was derived (2026-10-03): with the first trial usable, both
bisection ends stay in $[\tfrac12, 1)$, so the bounds hold with no further
premise; status 7 with $k \le 56$ is the root-search cap by counting alone; the
zero-probe start with $J = 0$ is unbounded (94, 84, 74 pre-loop evaluations
at $t = 10^{-12}, 10^{-9}, 10^{-6}$ on synthetic evaluators). **It was not
adopted** (decided by the user): it needs the pair's table and a replay of the
root finder's opening, a second copy of logic that already knows at exit which
cap fired. Instead the root finder is to report the exit itself, decided with
what the cap status means; until then every status 7 stays non-root. The step-6 row's "$k \ge 56$" for the endpoint cap is a
valid bound; the sharp one is 57, as derived here.

**$\bar S(0) = 0$ exactly: probe both sides** (decided by the user,
2026-09-30). The walk needs $d = \operatorname{sign}\bar S(0)$, which an exact
zero does not give, and running the endpoint check at $0$ would not certify a
root. The stopping rule's width condition holds vacuously at a single point.
The endpoint check sees only an odd number of extra sign changes, so a zero at
which $\bar S$ touches $0$ without crossing would pass, with the true root
elsewhere. The loop's probe certifies a crossing. With $t = \tau_\rho(0)/2$,
evaluate $\bar S(\pm t)$. Under the premise $H/c \ge \tfrac12$ (measured, as for
the loop's probe), a root at $0$ moves $\bar S$ by at least $4\tau_S$ at each
probe, so its sign there is certain. Then:

- **$\bar S(-t) > \tau_S$ and $\bar S(t) < -\tau_S$:** a certified
  maximum-oriented crossing. The bracket is $[-t, t]$, of width
  $\tau_\rho(0)$, so the stopping rule holds at $x = 0$, and the endpoint check
  runs as for any root.
- **Both beyond $\tau_S$ with the same sign $d$:** $\bar S$ touches $0$ at $0$
  without crossing. The walk starts from the probe on side $d$, as it would
  from $0$.
- **Otherwise** (a probe within $\tau_S$ of $0$, of minimum orientation, or
  unusable): the sign cannot be established, and the status is **ambiguous
  endpoint sign**, not converged.

The two probes count as evaluations. Level R5 forces each branch on the first
FAIL pair.

### When there is no sign change

These cases are described here. $B = 0.999$ is decided; what the fit reports
in each case, and whether such a pair enters $\hat\Gamma$, are open (see the
open list).

1. **No sign change up to the bound.** $\bar S$ keeps the sign of $\bar S(0)$ at
   every resolvable point up to $\pm B$. This happens both when $\ell$ keeps
   rising to $\pm1$ and when the root lies between $B$ and $\pm1$. The two cannot
   be told apart without evaluating beyond $B$. The four `mc_c_999` pairs that
   production reports at the bound are this case (Level R1): $\bar S(0.999)$ is
   0.03 to 1.08, and `rk_rho()`, which searches to $1 - 10^{-7}$, finds roots
   between 0.99900 and 0.99913. The algorithm reports $x = \pm B$ with
   `converged = 0`, as production does now.
2. **No sign change up to the usable end.** The resolvable set ends before
   $\pm B$ with the sign unchanged. None of the pairs here reach it, since each
   is resolvable up to $B$ on the side it walks. The path is exercised only by a
   negative control (Level R5).
3. **The empty-cell boundary estimate.** When the table's empty cells make the
   likelihood increase all the way to $\pm1$ (a $2\times2$ table with one empty
   cell is the simplest case), the supremum sits at $\rho = \pm1$ and no root
   exists. On Level R5's $2\times2$ table, $\bar S \ge 0$ at $1 - 2^{-k}$ for
   every $k \le 30$, and it is exactly $0$ from $k = 16$ on. The algorithm cannot
   tell this from case 1 at $B$. It returns unconverged at $B = 0.999$ and at
   $B = 1 - 2^{-30}$ alike.

### Verification

Chunks `setup`, `gate3-core` (`cellP`, `dP_drho`, `phi2s`), `rank-core`
(`rk_rho`) and `ec-core` (`ec_thr`, `ec_H`) must have run. Every name defined here
starts with `rf_`. The Monte Carlo replicates are gitignored generated data
(`fixtures/replication/`), read with `haven`. The chunks stop with a message if
they are absent.

Level R1 fits all 120 pairs of replicates 1–5 of `mc_c_998`, `mc_c_999`,
`mc_B_995` and `mc_B_9975`. Seventy of them are the diagnostics' three groups
(`tools/diag_polychoric_conv.do` and `conv2.do`, run 2026-09-28): **FAIL**, the
21 interior `converged = 0` pairs; **CTRL**, the 45 other pairs with
$\hat\rho > .98$; and **BOUND**, the four `mc_c_999` pairs at the bound. The
remaining 50 are "other". Production's
$\hat\rho$ and the diagnostic's Stata root for the 21 FAIL pairs are embedded
from that run's `CONV|` lines. The log is not committed, so they are printed for
comparison and not asserted.

```{r rf-core}
#| cache: true
# Depends on: setup (phi2), gate3-core (cellP, dP_drho), rank-core (rk_rho),
# ec-core (ec_thr, ec_H). Every name defined here starts with rf_.
rf_eps  <- .Machine$double.eps
# The spacing of doubles at x. log2() can round across a power of 2 just below
# it, so the exponent is corrected by exact powers of 2 (found by the 2026-10-01
# review: the uncorrected form was off by a factor 2 on 222 of 240 such points).
rf_ulp  <- function(x) { ax <- max(abs(x), 2^-1022); e <- floor(log2(ax))
  if (2^e > ax) e <- e - 1; if (2^(e + 1) <= ax) e <- e + 1; 2^(e - 52) }
rf_dPhi <- 9.3908313968469e-16  # per-corner error of Stata's binormal(), |rho| <= 0.999: chosen after measuring (tools/measure_binormal.do)
rf_dP   <- 4 * rf_dPhi + 3 * rf_eps

# Per cell: sum over its four corners of |phi2| (|z| + 7), z the density's exponent.
rf_absD <- function(a, b, x) {
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf)
  w <- outer(A, B, Vectorize(function(p, q) if (!is.finite(p) || !is.finite(q)) 0 else
         phi2(p, q, x) * ((p^2 - 2 * x * p * q + q^2) / (2 * (1 - x^2)) + 7)))
  w[-1, -1] + w[-nrow(w), -1] + w[-1, -ncol(w)] + w[-nrow(w), -ncol(w)]
}

# One evaluation: feasibility (pos), resolvability (res), S/N, the masked expected
# scaler c, and tau_S. dS is the derivative routine, replaced only by the negative controls.
rf_eval <- function(n, a, b, x, dS = dP_drho) {
  P <- cellP(a, b, x); O <- n > 0; ps <- all(P[O] > 0)
  if (!all(P[O] > rf_dP)) return(list(x = x, res = FALSE, pos = ps))
  D <- dS(a, b, x); w <- n[O] / sum(n); u <- D[O] / P[O]; pos <- P > 0
  list(x = x, res = TRUE, pos = TRUE, S = sum(w * u), c = sum((D^2 / P)[pos]),
       tauS = sum(w * (rf_eps * rf_absD(a, b, x)[O] + abs(u) * rf_dP) / P[O]) +
              (sum(O) + 2) * rf_eps * sum(w * abs(u)))
}
rf_taur <- function(e) 16 * e$tauS / e$c + 8 * rf_ulp(e$x)

# The walk (and, if a trial is infeasible, the frontier bisection) on side d.
rf_side <- function(f, e0, d, B) {
  ein <- e0; k <- 0; seen <- list()
  repeat {
    cand <- d * min(B, 1 - (1 - d * ein$x) / 2)
    if (cand == ein$x) return(list(inner = ein, case = "no sign change up to the bound", k = k, seen = seen))
    e <- f(cand); k <- k + 1; seen[[k]] <- e
    if (e$res && d * e$S < 0) return(list(inner = ein, outer = e, case = "bracket", k = k, seen = seen))
    if (e$res) { ein <- e; next }
    if (cand != d * B) {                                   # usable again at the bound: a gap, not an end
      eB <- f(d * B); k <- k + 1; seen[[k]] <- eB
      if (eB$res) return(list(inner = ein, case = "gap in the usable region", k = k, seen = seen))
    }
    out <- cand
    while (abs(out - ein$x) > 4 * rf_ulp(out)) {
      m <- (ein$x + out) / 2; e <- f(m); k <- k + 1; seen[[k]] <- e
      if (!e$res) { out <- m; next }
      if (d * e$S < 0) return(list(inner = ein, outer = e, case = "bracket", k = k, seen = seen))
      ein <- e
    }
    return(list(inner = ein, case = "no sign change up to the usable end", frontier = out, k = k, seen = seen))
  }
}

# The last usable evaluation on side d: d * B if usable, else the frontier bisection from ein.
# capc: the endpoint check's own cap per side, 54 evaluations (derived in the text).
rf_end <- function(f, d, B, ein, capc = 54) {
  e <- f(d * B); k <- 1
  if (e$res) return(list(e = e, k = k, capped = FALSE))
  out <- d * B
  while (abs(out - ein$x) > 4 * rf_ulp(out)) {
    if (k >= capc) return(list(e = ein, k = k, capped = TRUE))
    m <- (ein$x + out) / 2; e <- f(m); k <- k + 1
    if (e$res) ein <- e else out <- m
  }
  list(e = ein, k = k, capped = FALSE, frontier = out)
}

# The root-finder. bracket = c(l, h) skips the walk (negative controls only).
# Every stop() here is an abort (production: rc 3498), not a status.
rf_root <- function(n, a, b, B = 0.999, dS = dP_drho, f = NULL, bracket = NULL, cap = 40, capc = 54) {
  if (is.null(f)) f <- function(x) rf_eval(n, a, b, x, dS)
  out <- function(e, conv, case, k, L = NULL, R = NULL, seen = list(), ends = NULL, kc = NA)
    list(rho = e$x, converged = conv, case = case, evals = k, evals_check = kc, e = e,
         L = L, R = R, seen = seen, ends = ends)
  if (is.null(bracket)) {
    e0 <- f(0)
    if (!e0$res) stop("abort: rho = 0 is not resolvable")
    k0 <- 1; seen0 <- list(e0)
    if (e0$S == 0) {                                       # an exact zero at 0: probe both sides (the text)
      tr <- rf_taur(e0); pm <- f(-tr / 2); pp <- f(tr / 2); k0 <- 3; seen0 <- list(pm, e0, pp)
      cert <- function(e, s) e$res && s * e$S > e$tauS
      if (cert(pm, 1) && cert(pp, -1)) {                   # a certified crossing: close and verify
```
