```{r rf-core}
        L <- pm; R <- pp; x <- e0; k <- k0; seen <- seen0
        lo <- rf_end(f, -1, B, L, capc); hi <- rf_end(f, 1, B, R, capc)
        amb <- abs(lo$e$S) <= lo$e$tauS || abs(hi$e$S) <= hi$e$tauS
        ok  <- lo$e$S > lo$e$tauS && hi$e$S < -hi$e$tauS
        case <- if (lo$capped || hi$capped) "evaluation cap" else
                if (amb) "ambiguous endpoint sign" else if (ok) "root" else "more than one sign change"
        return(out(x, case == "root", case, k, L, R, seen, list(lo$e, hi$e), lo$k + hi$k))
      }
      if (cert(pm, 1) && cert(pp, 1)) e0 <- pp else        # touching, not crossing: walk on from the probe
      if (cert(pm, -1) && cert(pp, -1)) e0 <- pm else
      return(out(e0, FALSE, "ambiguous endpoint sign", k0, seen = seen0))
    }
    d <- sign(e0$S); sd <- rf_side(f, e0, d, B); k <- k0 + sd$k
    if (sd$case != "bracket") return(out(sd$inner, FALSE, sd$case, k, seen = c(seen0, sd$seen)))
    L <- if (d > 0) sd$inner else sd$outer; R <- if (d > 0) sd$outer else sd$inner
    seen <- c(seen0, sd$seen)
  } else {
    L <- f(bracket[1]); R <- f(bracket[2]); k <- 2; seen <- list(L, R)
    if (!L$res || !R$res) stop("abort: unresolvable bracket end")
    if (!(L$S > 0 && R$S < 0)) stop("abort: bracket not maximum-oriented")
  }
  x <- if (abs(L$S) < abs(R$S)) L else R; dxold <- R$x - L$x
  repeat {
    tr <- rf_taur(x)
    if (abs(x$S) <= x$tauS && R$x - L$x <= tr) {
      # Endpoint check at the last usable evaluation on each side of R_P and [-B, B].
      lo <- rf_end(f, -1, B, L, capc); hi <- rf_end(f, 1, B, R, capc)
      amb <- abs(lo$e$S) <= lo$e$tauS || abs(hi$e$S) <= hi$e$tauS
      ok  <- lo$e$S > lo$e$tauS && hi$e$S < -hi$e$tauS
      case <- if (lo$capped || hi$capped) "evaluation cap" else
              if (amb) "ambiguous endpoint sign" else if (ok) "root" else "more than one sign change"
      return(out(x, case == "root", case, k, L, R, seen, list(lo$e, hi$e), lo$k + hi$k))
    }
    if (k >= cap) return(out(x, FALSE, "evaluation cap", k, L, R, seen))
    if (abs(x$S) <= x$tauS) {                               # probe the far side
      xn <- if (identical(x, L)) x$x + tr / 2 else x$x - tr / 2
      if (!(xn > L$x && xn < R$x)) xn <- (L$x + R$x) / 2
    } else {
      st <- x$S / x$c; xn <- x$x + st
      if (!(xn > L$x && xn < R$x) || abs(st) > abs(dxold) / 2) { xn <- (L$x + R$x) / 2; st <- (R$x - L$x) / 2 }
      dxold <- st
    }
    e <- f(xn); k <- k + 1; seen[[length(seen) + 1]] <- e
    if (!e$res) return(out(x, FALSE, "unresolvable point inside the bracket", k, L, R, seen))
    if (e$S > 0) L <- e else R <- e
    x <- if (abs(L$S) < abs(R$S)) L else R
  }
}

# The replicates and the three groups of the 2026-09-28 diagnostics.
root <- file.path("..", "..")
rf_dir <- file.path(root, "fixtures", "replication")
rf_Y <- function(cond, rep) {

  if (!file.exists(f)) stop("replicate not found (gitignored generated data): ", f)
  as.matrix(as.data.frame(haven::read_dta(f)))
}

rf_pair <- function(cond, rep, i, j) {
  Y <- rf_Y(cond, rep); yi <- Y[, i]; yj <- Y[, j]
  n <- unclass(table(factor(yi, 0:max(yi)), factor(yj, 0:max(yj))))
  list(n = n, a = ec_thr(rowSums(n)), b = ec_thr(colSums(n)), yi = yi, yj = yj)
}
rf_bound <- data.frame(cond = "mc_c_999", rep = c(1, 3, 4, 5), i = 1, j = 2)   # production: rc 5 at the bound
# Every pair of replicates 1-5 of the four conditions; the groups are assigned in Level R1.
rf_pairs <- local({
  g <- expand.grid(i = 1:4, j = 1:4); g <- g[g$i < g$j, ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("mc_c_998", "mc_c_999", "mc_B_995", "mc_B_9975"), function(cd)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(r) data.frame(cond = cd, rep = r, i = g$i, j = g$j)))))
})
```

**Level R1: the 120 pairs.** Each pair is fitted by `rk_rho()`, the file's
reference root, and by `rf_root()`. The FAIL pairs are also compared with
production's `optimize()` result, as embedded. CTRL is every pair whose
`rk_rho()` exceeds .98 and that is neither FAIL nor BOUND, which reproduces the
diagnostic's selection. The group sizes are asserted as 21, 45 and 4. Every
non-BOUND pair must converge: FAIL, CTRL and the 50 others.

The agreement budget with `rk_rho()` follows from the two stopping rules.
`rf_root()`'s bracket has width at most $\tau_\rho$. `rk_rho()` stops at
$|\bar S|/c < 10^{-15}$, which puts it within $(10^{-15}c + \tau_S)/H$ of a
computed sign change. The budget is the sum, with $H$ from `ec_H()` at
$h = 10^{-5}$.

```{r rf-L1}
#| cache: true
rf_L1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(rf_pairs)), function(k) {
  p <- rf_pairs[k, ]; q <- rf_pair(p$cond, p$rep, p$i, p$j)
  rk <- rk_rho(q$yi, q$yj, q$a, q$b); r <- rf_root(q$n, q$a, q$b)
  key <- function(D) D$cond == p$cond & D$rep == p$rep & D$i == p$i & D$j == p$j
  fl <- key(rf_fail)
  H  <- ec_H(q$n, q$a, q$b, r$rho, 1e-5)
  # consistency: every evaluated feasible point left of the root has S > 0, right of it S < 0
  sx <- do.call(rbind, lapply(r$seen, function(e) if (e$res) c(e$x, e$S)))
  cons <- all(sign(sx[, 2]) == ifelse(sx[, 1] < r$rho, 1, ifelse(sx[, 1] > r$rho, -1, sign(sx[, 2]))) |
              abs(sx[, 2]) <= r$e$tauS)
  data.frame(cond = p$cond, rep = p$rep, pair = paste0(p$i, ",", p$j),
             group = if (any(fl)) "FAIL" else if (any(key(rf_bound))) "BOUND" else if (rk > 0.98) "CTRL" else "other",
             rk = rk, rf = r$rho, converged = r$converged, case = r$case, evals = r$evals,
             evals_check = r$evals_check,
             end_lo = if (is.null(r$ends)) NA else r$ends[[1]]$x,
             end_hi = if (is.null(r$ends)) NA else r$ends[[2]]$x,
             S_over_N = r$e$S, tauS = r$e$tauS, taur = rf_taur(r$e),
             width = if (r$converged) r$R$x - r$L$x else NA,
             H_over_c = H / r$e$c, minus_rk = r$rho - rk,
             budget = rf_taur(r$e) + (1e-15 * r$e$c + r$e$tauS) / H,
             consistent = cons,
             rho_dp = if (any(fl)) rf_fail$rho_dp[fl] else NA,
             root_stata = if (any(fl)) rf_fail$root_stata[fl] else NA)
}))
table(rf_L1$group)
G <- rf_L1[rf_L1$group %in% c("FAIL", "CTRL"), ]; Bd <- rf_L1[rf_L1$group == "BOUND", ]
I <- rf_L1[rf_L1$group != "BOUND", ]                      # every interior pair of the 20 replicates
format(G[, c("cond", "rep", "pair", "group", "rf", "evals", "S_over_N", "tauS", "taur",
             "width", "H_over_c", "minus_rk", "budget")], digits = 3)
Bd[, c("cond", "rep", "pair", "rf", "converged", "case", "evals", "S_over_N", "rk")]
with(G[G$group == "FAIL", ], data.frame(cond, rep, pair,
     old_minus_new = rho_dp - rf, stata_root_minus_new = root_stata - rf))
c(max_abs_minus_rk_over_budget = max(abs(I$minus_rk) / I$budget),
  max_S_over_tauS = max(abs(I$S_over_N) / I$tauS), max_taur = max(I$taur),
  H_over_c_min = min(I$H_over_c), H_over_c_max = max(I$H_over_c))
stopifnot(sum(rf_L1$group == "FAIL") == 21, sum(rf_L1$group == "CTRL") == 45, nrow(Bd) == 4,
          I$converged, I$case == "root",                  # every interior pair, the old failures included
          abs(I$S_over_N) <= I$tauS, I$width <= I$taur,
          I$H_over_c >= 0.5,                               # the probe's premise, measured
          abs(I$minus_rk) <= I$budget,
          I$consistent,
          !Bd$converged, Bd$case == "no sign change up to the bound",
          Bd$rf == 0.999, Bd$S_over_N > 0, Bd$rk > 0.999)
```

**Level R1c: $\tau_S$ bounds the score's measured error.** At each FAIL and CTRL
root, $\bar S$ is recomputed with @sec-emptycells' cancellation-free cell
probabilities (`ec_cellx()`, asked for $10^{-13}$ relative), which changes only
the $\pi$ half of the error model. Asserted: the gap is within $\tau_S$.

```{r rf-L1c}
#| cache: true
rf_L1c <- do.call(rbind, lapply(which(rf_L1$group %in% c("FAIL", "CTRL")), function(k) {
  p <- rf_L1[k, ]; ij <- as.integer(strsplit(p$pair, ",")[[1]]); q <- rf_pair(p$cond, p$rep, ij[1], ij[2])
  O <- q$n > 0; Px <- ec_cellx(q$a, q$b, p$rf); D <- dP_drho(q$a, q$b, p$rf)
  e <- rf_eval(q$n, q$a, q$b, p$rf)
  data.frame(group = p$group, gap = abs(e$S - sum(q$n[O] / sum(q$n) * D[O] / Px[O])), tauS = e$tauS)
}))
c(max_gap_over_tauS = max(rf_L1c$gap / rf_L1c$tauS), max_gap = max(rf_L1c$gap))
stopifnot(rf_L1c$gap <= rf_L1c$tauS)
```

**Level R2: cost.** The evaluation count of each fit, by group. Production's
`optimize()` spent 6,457 to 12,351 evaluations on the FAIL pairs and 27 to 75
on the controls (E-057). Each `rf_root()` evaluation costs one
`cellP()` and one `dP_drho()`, as a d0 evaluation plus its score would.

```{r rf-L2}
aggregate(evals ~ group, data = rf_L1, FUN = function(v) c(min = min(v), median = median(v), max = max(v)))
aggregate(evals_check ~ group, data = rf_L1, FUN = function(v) c(min = min(v), median = median(v), max = max(v)))
table(end_lo_at_bound = rf_L1$end_lo == -0.999, end_hi_at_bound = rf_L1$end_hi == 0.999, useNA = "ifany")
stopifnot(max(rf_L1$evals) < 40,                           # the cap, 40: chosen after measuring; never reached
          max(rf_L1$evals_check, na.rm = TRUE) <= 2 * 54,  # the endpoint cap, 54 per side: derived
          rf_L1$case != "evaluation cap")
```

**Level R3: the feasible and resolvable sets, and the single sign change, on a
grid.** For every FAIL, CTRL and BOUND pair, feasibility, resolvability and the
sign of $\bar S$ are evaluated on a symmetric grid of spacing .005 that contains
$0$ and $\pm0.999$. The spacing was chosen before looking. The first draft's grid
omitted $+0.999$ and so could not see roots above .996, and was corrected.
Asserted:

- on the side the walk takes, every grid point is resolvable;
- $\bar S$ changes sign exactly once there, between the grid points around
  `rf_root()`'s root (never, for BOUND);
- on the far side, every resolvable $\bar S$ points back towards the root;
- the positivity rule is fragmented on at least one pair (the finding above).

The counts of fragmented feasible and resolvable sets are printed. Also asserted:
the interior rectangle below has a $\partial_\rho\pi$ with at least two sign
changes, so cell-wise unimodality is false.

```{r rf-L3}
#| cache: true
rf_s3 <- seq(0.004, 0.999, by = 0.005); rf_g3 <- c(-rev(rf_s3), 0, rf_s3)   # includes 0 and +-0.999
rf_L3 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(which(rf_L1$group != "other"), function(k) {
  p <- rf_L1[k, ]; ij <- as.integer(strsplit(p$pair, ",")[[1]])
  q <- rf_pair(p$cond, p$rep, ij[1], ij[2])
  ev <- lapply(rf_g3, function(x) rf_eval(q$n, q$a, q$b, x))
  fe <- sapply(ev, `[[`, "res"); fp <- sapply(ev, `[[`, "pos"); S <- sapply(ev, function(e) if (e$res) e$S else NA)
  d  <- sign(S[rf_g3 == 0])                                  # the side the walk takes
  wk <- d * rf_g3 >= 0; far <- !wk                           # walk side (0 included) and far side
  sw <- sign(S[wk & fe]); xw <- rf_g3[wk & fe]; ch <- which(diff(sw) != 0)
  rl <- rle(fe[far]); rp <- rle(fp[far])
  data.frame(cond = p$cond, rep = p$rep, pair = p$pair, group = p$group,
             walk_side_all_feasible = all(fe[wk]),
             walk_side_changes = length(ch),
             change_brackets_root = length(ch) == 1 && min(xw[ch], xw[ch + 1]) <= p$rf && max(xw[ch], xw[ch + 1]) >= p$rf,
             far_unresolvable = sum(!fe[far]), far_resolvable_runs = sum(rl$values),
             far_infeasible = sum(!fp[far]), far_feasible_runs = sum(rp$values),
             far_S_points_to_root = all(d * S[far & fe] > 0),
             min_abs_unresolvable = if (all(fe)) NA else min(abs(rf_g3[!fe])))
}))
rf_L3[rf_L3$far_feasible_runs > 1 | rf_L3$far_resolvable_runs > 1,
      c("cond", "rep", "pair", "far_infeasible", "far_feasible_runs", "far_unresolvable", "far_resolvable_runs")]
c(pairs = nrow(rf_L3), far_feasible_fragmented = sum(rf_L3$far_feasible_runs > 1),
  far_resolvable_fragmented = sum(rf_L3$far_resolvable_runs > 1),
  far_with_infeasible = sum(rf_L3$far_infeasible > 0), max_far_infeasible = max(rf_L3$far_infeasible),
  max_far_unresolvable = max(rf_L3$far_unresolvable))
rf_int <- list(a = c(-0.7777489, 0.7817380), b = c(0.4872438, 0.9672265))   # found by random search
rf_dint <- sapply(seq(-0.9999, 0.9999, length.out = 4001), function(r) with(rf_int,
  phi2(a[2], b[2], r) - phi2(a[1], b[2], r) - phi2(a[2], b[1], r) + phi2(a[1], b[1], r)))
rf_int_changes <- sum(diff(sign(rf_dint)) != 0)
rf_int_changes
In <- rf_L3$group != "BOUND"
stopifnot(rf_L3$walk_side_all_feasible,                   # the walk never meets an infeasible point
          rf_L3$walk_side_changes[In] == 1, rf_L3$change_brackets_root[In],
          rf_L3$walk_side_changes[!In] == 0,               # BOUND: no sign change up to 0.999
          rf_L3$far_S_points_to_root,                      # far side: every resolvable S points back
          any(rf_L3$far_feasible_runs > 1),                # the positivity rule IS fragmented (the finding)
          rf_L3$min_abs_unresolvable >= 0.5 | is.na(rf_L3$min_abs_unresolvable),  # the endpoint cap's premise
          rf_int_changes >= 2)
```

**Level R4: uniqueness without concavity.** First a fixed $3\times4$ table on
which $\bar S$ increases over part of the grid (so $\ell$ is not concave) and still
changes sign once. Then a random search: tables with $K_1, K_2 \in \{2,\dots,5\}$,
cell weights drawn as $\text{Exp}(1)^{m}$ with $m \in \{1,3,6\}$, a random
share of cells emptied, and the result rounded to integer counts totalling
about 1000. Draws with an empty row or column are discarded. $\bar S$ is scanned
at spacing .02 on the resolvable part of $[-0.98, 0.98]$. The design and the 300
draws were chosen before looking. **Integer rounding was added after a first
run**: with fractional counts (cells of weight $10^{-8}$ counted as observed),
the positivity rule's scan found up to three sign changes on 7 of 228 tables. In
the two tables inspected, the extra changes sat at points where an observed
cell's computed probability was below $10^{-15}$. Under the resolvability rule,
which was adopted after that run, the same fractional tables showed none (a
drafting measurement that this file does not repeat). Asserted: no table has more than one sign change. The
numbers of tables and of non-concave tables are printed.

```{r rf-L4}
#| cache: true
rf_nc <- matrix(c(  0.00, 0.37, 0.00, 111.39,
                  197.50, 0.08, 0.01,  10.90,
                  672.11, 2.31, 3.07,   2.24), 3, byrow = TRUE)
rf_scan <- function(n, g) { a <- ec_thr(rowSums(n)); b <- ec_thr(colSums(n))
  sapply(g, function(x) { e <- rf_eval(n, a, b, x); if (e$res) e$S else NA }) }
rf_g4 <- seq(-0.98, 0.98, by = 0.02)
S_nc <- rf_scan(rf_nc, rf_g4)
rf_L4a <- c(max_increase = max(diff(S_nc), na.rm = TRUE),
            sign_changes = sum(diff(sign(S_nc[is.finite(S_nc)])) != 0))
rf_L4a
set.seed(20260929)
rf_L4 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:300, function(k) {
  K1 <- sample(2:5, 1); K2 <- sample(2:5, 1)
  n <- matrix(rexp(K1 * K2)^sample(c(1, 3, 6), 1), K1); n[runif(K1 * K2) < runif(1, 0, 0.6)] <- 0
  if (any(rowSums(n) == 0) || any(colSums(n) == 0)) return(NULL)
  n <- round(n / sum(n) * 1000)
  if (any(rowSums(n) == 0) || any(colSums(n) == 0) || length(n) < 4) return(NULL)
  S <- rf_scan(n, rf_g4); s <- sign(S[is.finite(S) & S != 0])
  data.frame(k = k, K1 = K1, K2 = K2, sign_changes = sum(diff(s) != 0),
             nonconcave = any(diff(S) > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
}))
c(tables = nrow(rf_L4), nonconcave = sum(rf_L4$nonconcave), max_sign_changes = max(rf_L4$sign_changes))
stopifnot(rf_L4a["max_increase"] > 0, rf_L4a["sign_changes"] == 1, rf_L4$sign_changes <= 1)
```

**Level R5: no sign change, and the negative controls.** Each control must be
caught, meaning it produces a flagged result or an assertion failure, never a
silently accepted wrong root.

- **Empty-cell boundary (no sign change, not a control).** A $2\times2$ table
  with one empty cell, $n = (50, 0; 10, 40)$. $\bar S \ge 0$ at $1 - 2^{-k}$,
  $k = 1, \dots, 30$, with exact zeros. The fit must be unconverged at
  $B = 0.999$ and at $B = 1 - 2^{-30}$. With a non-strict walk test
  ($d\bar S \le 0$), the exact zeros would close a bracket and the loop would
  accept a "root" where $\bar S$ merely underflows.
- **Reversed score.** `dP_drho` negated. On every FAIL pair it must not return a
  converged root.
- **Dropped term.** `dP_drho` without its $+\phi_2(a_{r-1}, b_{s-1})$ corner. The
  root-finder may converge on the wrong score, so this is caught by the
  comparison, not the algorithm: its root must miss `rk_rho()` by more than Level
  R1's budget on every FAIL pair.
- **Unresolvable bracket end.** A bracket whose upper end is a point where an
  observed cell's computed probability is $\le 0$, found by scanning towards
  $-1$ on the first FAIL pair. It must abort. So must a bracket $[0, 0.5]$,
  positive at both ends (**not maximum-oriented**), and an evaluator that
  declares $\rho = 0$ unresolvable.
- **The endpoint check's cap.** The first FAIL pair with that cap at 10 per
  side: **evaluation cap**.
- **An exact zero at $\rho = 0$**, forced on the first FAIL pair: touching
  ($\bar S(0)$ set to 0) must walk on and find the true root, within Level R1's
  budget; crossing ($\bar S = -\operatorname{sign}(x)\max(|x|c, 2\tau_S)$, a
  control's contrivance so that every nonzero point is decisive) must return
  **root** at exactly $0$; flat ($\bar S = 0$ on $|x| < 10^{-6}$) must return
  **ambiguous endpoint sign**.
- **Added 2026-10-01 at the end-of-module protocol; (ii) given its hole
  2026-10-02.** Each was shown on 2026-10-02 to fail under its mutant applied
  to `rf_root()` itself, with the mutant defined only just before these
  controls, so every earlier assertion ran unmutated (main session's run,
  R 4.6.0). The mutation numbers are those of the 2026-10-01 option B campaign
  (E-057, that date's end-of-module row; an earlier campaign
  reuses the numbers), and each mutation is stated here in full because that
  campaign's catalogue is not committed.
  - **(i) Probe side**, from surviving Mata mutant M35: in the touching branch
    with both probes positive, `e0 = pp` replaced by `e0 = pm`, so the walk
    starts from $-t$. Touching, with $(0.4999, 0.5)$ unusable: only a walk started from
    the wrong probe meets it, so the right one must find the root. Under the
    mutant: **gap in the usable region** after 5 evaluations.
  - **(ii) Both probes negative**, from the review's reading of the code: no
    Mata mutation exercised this branch. The reversed score with
    $\bar S(0) = 0$, and $(-0.5, -0.4999)$ unusable, the mirror of (i). It
    must give **no sign change up to the usable end** at the walk's last
    usable point, the unusable frontier within four ulps beyond it. The
    branch deleted gives **ambiguous endpoint sign**. The walk started from
    $+t$ gave the same answer as the right one until the hole was added,
    because both first steps, $\mp 0.5 \pm t/2$, were usable. With the hole
    it ends at $-0.4999$, still **no sign change up to the usable end**, after
    56 evaluations against the right walk's 55: only the end's position
    tells them apart, which is why the end is asserted, exactly, against the
    walk from $-t$ rather than by status and count.
  - **(iii) The width condition**, from Mata mutant M53, which the main session
    added (it was not a survivor): the loop's stop test
    `abs(x[3]) <= x[5] & R[1] - L[1] <= tr` cut to `abs(x[3]) <= x[5]`. $\bar S = \tfrac12\tau_S$ on
    $[0.996, 0.9975]$, inside the walk's bracket $[1 - 2^{-8}, 1 - 2^{-9}]$
    (asserted) but away from the root, which is asserted to lie in the
    bracket and outside the stretch. The score condition holds there and the
    width condition does not, so the probes creep by $\tau_\rho/2$ until the
    **evaluation cap**. Under the mutant the loop accepts $0.99609375$ as
    **root** after 10 evaluations. That a flat stretch of this width ends in
    the cap status is the current behaviour, accepted by the user 2026-10-02;
    it is to be re-examined when the open question of what the cap status
    means is decided.
- **Fragmented resolvable set.** An evaluator that declares $[.97, .985]$
  unresolvable, an island the real pairs do not have. On `mc_c_998` replicate 1
  the walk steps into it, finds $B$ usable beyond it, and must report **gap in
  the usable region**. (The first draft, without the check at $B$, took the
  island for the usable end.)
- **A second sign change.** An evaluator whose $\bar S$ is made negative below
  $\rho = -0.5$ on the first FAIL pair. The root near 0.998 is still bracketed
  and refined; the endpoint check must report **more than one sign change**.
- **A zero at an end.** The same with $\bar S$ set to $0$ below $-0.5$: **ambiguous
  endpoint sign**.
- **The evaluation cap.** The first FAIL pair with the cap at 5: **evaluation
  cap**.

```{r rf-L5}
#| cache: true
rf_bd <- matrix(c(50, 0, 10, 40), 2, byrow = TRUE); a2 <- ec_thr(rowSums(rf_bd)); b2 <- ec_thr(colSums(rf_bd))
rf_S_bd <- sapply(1 - 2^-(1:30), function(x) rf_eval(rf_bd, a2, b2, x)$S)   # every point resolvable
rf_L5_bd <- c(min_S_to_edge = min(rf_S_bd), exact_zeros = sum(rf_S_bd == 0),
              first_zero = which(rf_S_bd == 0)[1],
              converged_B0999 = rf_root(rf_bd, a2, b2)$converged,
              converged_Bnear1 = rf_root(rf_bd, a2, b2, B = 1 - 2^-30)$converged)
rf_L5_bd
rf_dP_drop <- function(a, b, rho) {                 # dP_drho without its +phi2(A[r], B[s]) corner
  A <- c(-Inf, a, Inf); B <- c(-Inf, b, Inf)
  outer(seq_len(length(a) + 1), seq_len(length(b) + 1), Vectorize(function(r, s)
    phi2s(A[r + 1], B[s + 1], rho) - phi2s(A[r], B[s + 1], rho) - phi2s(A[r + 1], B[s], rho)))
}
F1 <- rf_L1[rf_L1$group == "FAIL", ]
rf_L5 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(F1)), function(k) {
  p <- F1[k, ]; ij <- as.integer(strsplit(p$pair, ",")[[1]]); q <- rf_pair(p$cond, p$rep, ij[1], ij[2])
  rev  <- rf_root(q$n, q$a, q$b, dS = function(a, b, x) -dP_drho(a, b, x))
  drop <- rf_root(q$n, q$a, q$b, dS = rf_dP_drop)
  data.frame(cond = p$cond, rep = p$rep, pair = p$pair,
             reversed_case = rev$case, reversed_converged = rev$converged,
             dropped_converged = drop$converged, dropped_miss = abs(drop$rho - p$rk), budget = p$budget)
}))
rf_L5[, c("cond", "rep", "pair", "reversed_case", "dropped_converged", "dropped_miss")]
q1 <- rf_pair(F1$cond[1], F1$rep[1], 1, 2)
x_inf <- NA; for (x in -1 + 2^-(1:52)) if (!rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x)$pos) { x_inf <- x; break }
rf_abort <- function(expr) tryCatch({ expr; "no abort" }, error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
rf_L5_inf <- rf_abort(rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, bracket = c(-0.5, x_inf)))
rf_L5_ori <- rf_abort(rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, bracket = c(0, 0.5)))         # S > 0 at both ends
rf_L5_z0  <- rf_abort(rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = function(x)
  if (x == 0) list(x = x, res = FALSE) else rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x)))
rf_L5_cc  <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, capc = 10)                          # the endpoint cap
rf_L5_isl <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = function(x)
  if (x >= 0.97 && x <= 0.985) list(x = x, res = FALSE) else rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x))
# The statuses the endpoint check and the cap produce, each forced on the first FAIL pair.
rf_fake <- function(g) function(x) { e <- rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x); if (e$res) e$S <- g(x, e$S); e }
rf_L5_two <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = rf_fake(function(x, S) if (x < -0.5) -abs(S) else S))
rf_L5_amb <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = rf_fake(function(x, S) if (x < -0.5) 0 else S))
rf_L5_cap <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, cap = 5)
# An exact zero at rho = 0: touching (the true root is at .998), crossing, and flat.
rf_L5_s0t <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = rf_fake(function(x, S) if (x == 0) 0 else S))
# crossing: S = -sign(x) max(|x| c, 2 tau_S), so every nonzero point's sign is decisive against its own tau_S
rf_L5_s0c <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = function(x) { e <- rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x)
  if (e$res) e$S <- -sign(x) * max(abs(x) * e$c, 2 * e$tauS); e })
rf_L5_s0f <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = rf_fake(function(x, S) if (abs(x) < 1e-6) 0 else S))
# Added 2026-10-01 from the review. (i) Touching, and the walk must start from the
# probe on side d: (0.4999, 0.5) declared unusable, which only a walk from -t meets.
rf_L5_s0s <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = function(x) {
  if (x > 0.4999 && x < 0.5) return(list(x = x, res = FALSE))
  e <- rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x); if (e$res && x == 0) e$S <- 0; e })
# (ii) Touching with both probes negative: the reversed score with S(0) set to 0,
# and (-0.5, -0.4999) declared unusable, the mirror of (i): only a walk from +t meets it.
rf_L5_fn <- function(x) {
  if (x > -0.5 && x < -0.4999) return(list(x = x, res = FALSE))
  e <- rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x, function(a, b, r) -dP_drho(a, b, r)); if (e$res && x == 0) e$S <- 0; e }
rf_L5_s0n <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = rf_L5_fn)
# Its end is the walk's last usable point: the unusable frontier within four ulps beyond it.
rf_L5_s0n_sd <- rf_side(rf_L5_fn, rf_L5_fn(-rf_taur(rf_L5_fn(0)) / 2), -1, 0.999)
# (iii) The width condition: |S| <= tau_S on [0.996, 0.9975], inside the walk's
# bracket [1 - 2^-8, 1 - 2^-9] but away from the root. Without the width
# condition the loop would accept 0.99609375.
rf_L5_ff <- function(x) {
  e <- rf_eval(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, x); if (e$res && x >= 0.996 && x <= 0.9975) e$S <- 0.5 * e$tauS; e }
rf_L5_flat <- rf_root(q1$n, q1$a, q1$b, f = rf_L5_ff)
rf_L5_ff0  <- rf_L5_ff(0)
rf_L5_ffsd <- rf_side(rf_L5_ff, rf_L5_ff0, sign(rf_L5_ff0$S), 0.999)
c(x_inf = x_inf, infeasible_bracket = rf_L5_inf, orientation = rf_L5_ori, rho0 = rf_L5_z0,
  endpoint_cap10 = rf_L5_cc$case, s0_touch = rf_L5_s0t$case, s0_touch_rho = rf_L5_s0t$rho,
  s0_cross = rf_L5_s0c$case, s0_cross_rho = rf_L5_s0c$rho, s0_flat = rf_L5_s0f$case,
  s0_side = rf_L5_s0s$case, s0_neg = rf_L5_s0n$case, flat_stretch = rf_L5_flat$case, island = rf_L5_isl$case,
  second_root = rf_L5_two$case, zero_at_end = rf_L5_amb$case, cap5 = rf_L5_cap$case)
stopifnot(rf_L5_bd["min_S_to_edge"] >= 0, rf_L5_bd["exact_zeros"] > 0,
          !rf_L5_bd["converged_B0999"], !rf_L5_bd["converged_Bnear1"],
          !rf_L5$reversed_converged,
          !rf_L5$dropped_converged | rf_L5$dropped_miss > rf_L5$budget,
          !is.na(x_inf), rf_L5_inf == "abort: unresolvable bracket end",
          rf_L5_ori == "abort: bracket not maximum-oriented",
          rf_L5_z0 == "abort: rho = 0 is not resolvable",
          !rf_L5_cc$converged, rf_L5_cc$case == "evaluation cap",
          rf_L5_s0t$case == "root", abs(rf_L5_s0t$rho - F1$rk[1]) <= F1$budget[1],   # walks on to the true root
          rf_L5_s0c$case == "root", rf_L5_s0c$rho == 0,
          !rf_L5_s0f$converged, rf_L5_s0f$case == "ambiguous endpoint sign",
          rf_L5_s0s$case == "root", abs(rf_L5_s0s$rho - F1$rk[1]) <= F1$budget[1],
          rf_L5_s0n$case == "no sign change up to the usable end", rf_L5_s0n$rho < 0,
          rf_L5_s0n_sd$case == "no sign change up to the usable end",
          rf_L5_s0n$rho == rf_L5_s0n_sd$inner$x, rf_L5_s0n$rho > -0.999,
          !rf_L5_fn(rf_L5_s0n_sd$frontier)$res,
          abs(rf_L5_s0n_sd$frontier - rf_L5_s0n$rho) <= 4 * rf_ulp(rf_L5_s0n_sd$frontier),
          !rf_L5_flat$converged, rf_L5_flat$case == "evaluation cap",
          rf_L5_ffsd$case == "bracket", rf_L5_ffsd$inner$x == 1 - 2^-8, rf_L5_ffsd$outer$x == 1 - 2^-9,
          F1$rk[1] > 0.9975, F1$rk[1] < 1 - 2^-9,                 # the root: in the bracket, outside the stretch
          !rf_L5_isl$converged, rf_L5_isl$case == "gap in the usable region",
          !rf_L5_two$converged, rf_L5_two$case == "more than one sign change",
          !rf_L5_amb$converged, rf_L5_amb$case == "ambiguous endpoint sign",
          !rf_L5_cap$converged, rf_L5_cap$case == "evaluation cap")
```

**Level R6: the walk's evaluation bound** (drafted 2026-10-02 by a read-only
agent; executed by the main session in a whole-document run, R 4.6.0). Synthetic
evaluators exercise `rf_side()` under the premise, both sides, from $0$ and from
zero-probe starts, and assert the bounds derived under *The two cap exits*:
pre-loop count $\le 53$ from $0$, $\le 56$ in all, the root cap below the
endpoint cap's minimum, and no bound without the premise.

```{r rf-walkbound}
# Depends on: rf-core (rf_side, rf_ulp). Synthetic evaluators: rf_side's count
# depends only on usability and sign(S) along its path. Usable iff d x <= Fr;
# S has sign d below s and -d on [s, Fr].
rf_wb_mk  <- function(d, Fr, s) function(x) { y <- d * x
  if (y > Fr) list(x = x, res = FALSE) else list(x = x, res = TRUE, S = if (y < s) d else -d) }
rf_wb_run <- function(d, x0, Fr, s) { f <- rf_wb_mk(d, Fr, s); rf_side(f, f(d * x0), d, 0.999) }
set.seed(20261002)
rf_wb_t <- c(0, 10^runif(400, -16, -2), 2^-60, 1e-15, 3e-14, 0.01, 0.2, 0.4999)
rf_wb <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, -1), function(d) do.call(rbind, lapply(rf_wb_t, function(x0) {
  tr <- 1 - 2^-(1:10)
  Fs <- c(runif(60, 0.5, 0.999), tr, tr + 2^-53, tr - 2^-53, tr + 2^-40, tr - 2^-40,
          0.999 - 2^-53, 0.999 - 1e-6, 0.5, 0.5 + 2^-53)
  Fs <- Fs[Fs >= 0.5 & Fs < 0.999]                     # the premise
  k0 <- if (x0 == 0) 1 else 3
  do.call(rbind, lapply(Fs, function(Fr) {
    a <- rf_wb_run(d, x0, Fr, Inf); b <- rf_wb_run(d, x0, Fr, Fr - 2^-53)
    c2 <- rf_wb_run(d, x0, Fr, Fr - 2^-52)
    data.frame(k0 = k0, k3 = k0 + a$k, c3 = a$case,
               kb = c(k0 + b$k, k0 + c2$k), cb = c(b$case, c2$case))
  }))
}))))
rf_wb_br <- rf_wb[rf_wb$cb == "bracket", ]
rf_wb_np <- sapply(c(1e-3, 1e-10, 1e-100, 1e-300), function(Fr) 1 + rf_wb_run(1, 0, Fr, Inf)$k)
print(list(max_pre_by_k0 = tapply(rf_wb_br$kb, rf_wb_br$k0, max),
           max_status3_by_k0 = tapply(rf_wb$k3, rf_wb$k0, max), no_premise = rf_wb_np))
stopifnot(all(rf_wb$c3 == "no sign change up to the usable end"),
          max(rf_wb_br$kb[rf_wb_br$k0 == 1]) <= 53,      # derived: k0 + 52
          max(rf_wb_br$kb) <= 56, max(rf_wb$k3) <= 56,    # derived: 56 (J = 0), else k0 + 52
          max(40, rf_wb_br$kb) < 2 + 54 + 1,              # root cap below the endpoint cap's minimum
          max(rf_wb_np) > 57)                             # no bound without the premise
```

Measured by the stand-alone mirror `walkbound.R`, rerun by the main session (87,098 premise frontiers, both
sides, 407 starts): the largest pre-loop count is 53 from $0$ and 55 from a
zero-probe start, so the derived bound is attained. Of the bracketing runs,
54,697 of 116,021 reach 55.

### What the verification shows

From the main session's run, 2026-09-29, R 4.6.0, with $\delta_\Phi$ at the
Stata budget:

- **Every interior pair converges** with status `root`: the 21 FAIL pairs, the
  45 CTRL pairs and the 50 others. The largest ratio of $|\hat\rho - $
  `rk_rho()`$|$ to its budget is 0.052. $|\bar S|/\tau_S \le 0.89$ at the
  accepted point, $\tau_\rho \le 5.4\times10^{-12}$, and $H/c$ is 0.983 to 1.055,
  so the probe's premise holds with room.
- **The old failures were right to within $10^{-7}$ and wrong to flag.**
  Production's $\hat\rho$ minus the new root is $8.6\times10^{-10}$ to
  $5.2\times10^{-8}$ on the 21 FAIL pairs. The diagnostic's Stata root agrees
  with the new root to $7.0\times10^{-14}$.
- **$\tau_S$ bounds the measured score error** (Level R1c): the gap to the
  cancellation-free score is at most $0.051\,\tau_S$ ($9.0\times10^{-13}$).
- **Cost** (Level R2). The root takes 14–17 evaluations on FAIL pairs (against
  `optimize()`'s 6,457–12,351), 12–17 on CTRL, 7–10 on the others, 11 on BOUND;
  the cap of 40 is never reached. **The endpoint check costs more than the
  root**: 54 evaluations on every FAIL and CTRL pair and 103–105 on the others,
  because $\pm0.999$ is usable on the upper side of 66 pairs and on the lower
  side of none, so almost every check runs a frontier bisection to four ulps.
- **The four BOUND pairs** report *no sign change up to the bound* at
  $\hat\rho = 0.999$, with `rk_rho()` beyond 0.999.
- **Level R3:** the positivity rule's feasible set is fragmented on 18 of 70
  pairs, the usable set on none. Every walk side is usable, with exactly one
  sign change around the root (none for BOUND). One interior rectangle's
  $\partial_\rho\pi$ changes sign 5 times.
- **Level R4:** 156 random tables, 13 non-concave, none with more than one sign
  change. The fixed $3\times4$ table's $\bar S$ increases by 0.0023 and changes
  sign once.
- **Level R5:** every negative control is caught with its own status: reversed
  score (*no sign change up to the usable end* on all 21), gap, more than one
  sign change, ambiguous endpoint sign, evaluation cap (the root search's and,
  from 2026-09-30, the endpoint check's). The unresolvable and the
  wrongly oriented bracket and an unusable $\rho = 0$ abort. The three exact
  zeros at $\rho = 0$ give root (touching, walked on to the true root), root at
  $0$ (crossing) and ambiguous endpoint sign (flat). The endpoint check never
  reaches its cap, and no unusable grid point of Level R3 lies in
  $[-\tfrac12, \tfrac12]$ (main session's rerun, 2026-09-30).
  The dropped term converges to a wrong root on all 21 FAIL pairs, off by 1.31
  to 1.37, and only the comparison with `rk_rho()` catches it. The $2\times2$
  empty-cell table is unconverged at both $B$, its score exactly $0$ from
  $1 - 2^{-16}$.

### What production would do

If option B is adopted (not decided here):

1. **`dwls_polychoric()` replaces `optimize()` and the polish by the walk, the
   bracket and the safeguarded Fisher loop above.** The evaluator is the one
   the polish already uses: `dwlsmv_cellprob_raw()`, `dwlsmv_dcellprob_rho()`, and
   the observed-cells mask applied **before** the division (@sec-emptycells,
   item 2).
2. **`converged = 1` only when the stopping rule's two conditions and the
   endpoint check hold.** Every other exit is `converged = 0` with $\hat\rho$ the
   last usable point, and carries a **distinct status** (decided by the user,
   2026-09-29), so that the open decisions on boundary pairs and on
   $\hat\Gamma$ can tell them apart without refitting: *no sign change up to
   the bound*; *no sign change up to the usable end*; *gap in the usable
   region*; *more than one sign change*; *ambiguous endpoint sign*;
   *evaluation cap* (the root search's cap or the endpoint check's); and
   *unresolvable point inside the bracket*. $\rho = 0$ unresolvable, and the
   two broken bracket invariants, abort (rc 3498) instead. The status is the
   stored quantity and `converged` is set from it, never kept separately; the
   evaluation count covers every evaluation, the endpoint check's included
   (decided by the user, 2026-09-30).
   `dwlsmv_pairinfo()` can be evaluated at $\hat\rho$, because every observed
   cell there is usable.
3. **$\tau_S$ and $\tau_\rho$ are computed per evaluation, from the same
   quantities**, and are not constants.
4. **The consistency check of Level R1 is free**, since the walk has already
   evaluated the points, and can be kept as an assertion in the unit test.

### Left open by the specification

Decided by the user on 2026-09-29, and recorded in E-058: the
usability rule $\mathcal R_P$; $B = 0.999$ as a hard search limit;
$\delta_\Phi$ as the measured Stata budget over $|\rho| \le B$ and thresholds in
$[-2.5, 2.5]$; both stopping conditions; no production scan, with a development
test for multiple roots; the endpoint check; distinct statuses. On
2026-09-30 the user kept the endpoint check's frontier width at four ulps,
accepting its cost (54–105 evaluations per pair, more than the root) so that
"the last usable evaluation" is the edge of $\mathcal R_P$ to rounding. None of
the following is resolved here.

- **Boundary pairs.** What the fit reports for the no-sign-change cases,
  including the empty-cell boundary estimate at $\pm1$.
- **Thresholds beyond $[-2.5, 2.5]$.** $\delta_\Phi$ is unmeasured there; whether
  to extend the grid is to be determined.
- **$\hat\Gamma$ from `converged = 0` pairs.** Whether such a pair's $\psi_\rho$
  column enters $\hat\Gamma$.
- **The polish limit and the evaluation cap.** Production's 25-step limit
  disappears under this algorithm. The cap of 40 evaluations for the walk and
  refinement (chosen after measuring; never reached) and what its status
  implies are to be settled together with the polish item. Settled on
  2026-09-30: the endpoint check has its own derived cap (54 per side), and
  both caps end in the one status *evaluation cap*. The walk's frontier
  bisection counts toward the cap of 40, and can by itself cost up to about 64
  evaluations, so a pair whose walk meets the frontier may reach the cap
  before any Fisher step. No pair here does; the cap's value stays open.
- **The small-count threshold** (`dwlsmv_countdiag`), which this section does not
  touch.
- **Uniqueness itself** is unproved; no counterexample was found.
- **@sec-emptycells' feasibility wording.** The usability rule replaces its item
  1 (observed cells $> 0$) for the search; that section and spec Module 2
  change with the implementation.

## Module 2: the binary table with an empty cell (one-empty-cell and perfect-association pairs) {#sec-kindE}

> Renamed 2026-10-06: what this section and E-010 called *Kind E*
> is the **one-empty-cell pair**; the empty diagonal pair is the
> **perfect-association pair**; together, **empty-cell 2×2 pairs**. The anchor
> `sec-kindE` is kept so cross-references hold.

*Drafted 2026-10-02 by a read-only agent; executed by the main session in a
whole-document run, R 4.6.0.*
E-011 (2026-10-02, *The two kinds of status 2*) scheduled this
derivation before step 7: the one-empty-cell pair's lack of an interior maximum, its direction,
the two-empty-cell cases, and whether an empty-cell $2\times2$ can end at status
3. It sets no policy. Everything here holds the thresholds at Module 1's
estimates, as production does (@sec-rootfind: the two-step polychoric).

### Setting

A binary pair has table $n = (n_{rs})_{r,s=1,2}$, $N = \sum n_{rs}$, and
Module 1's thresholds
$$\Phi(a) = n_{1\cdot}/N, \qquad \Phi(b) = n_{\cdot1}/N.$$
Write $\phi = \phi_2(a,b;\rho)$ and $\sigma_{rs} = +1$ on the diagonal, $-1$ off
it. The four cells are
$\pi_{11} = \Phi_2$, $\pi_{12} = \Phi(a) - \Phi_2$, $\pi_{21} = \Phi(b) - \Phi_2$,
$\pi_{22} = 1 - \Phi(a) - \Phi(b) + \Phi_2$, with $\Phi_2 = \Phi_2(a,b;\rho)$.

**Lemma K1 (signs).** $\partial_\rho\pi_{rs} = \sigma_{rs}\,\phi$. *Proof.* Each
cell is a corner cell (@sec-rootfind, *The feasible region*), and only
$\Phi_2$ depends on $\rho$, with $\partial_\rho\Phi_2 = \phi$ (Plackett). In
`dP_drho()` three of each cell's four corners are infinite and weigh $0$, so
the computed derivative is $\sigma_{rs}\,\phi_2(a,b;\rho)$ exactly, one $\exp$
with a sign that cannot round. $\square$

So the observed-cells score of @sec-emptycells is
$$S(\rho) = \phi \sum_{\mathcal O} \sigma_{rs}\,\frac{n_{rs}}{\pi_{rs}}.$$

**Lemma K2 (the margins pin the table).** For any cell $e$ and every $\rho$,
$$\pi_{rs}(\rho) = \frac{n_{rs}}{N} + \sigma_e\sigma_{rs}\Bigl(\pi_e(\rho) - \frac{n_e}{N}\Bigr).$$
*Proof.* $\pi - n/N$ has zero row and column sums, because both $\pi$ and $n/N$
have margins $\Phi(a)$, $\Phi(b)$. A $2\times2$ matrix with zero margins is
$t\,\sigma$ for a scalar $t$; reading it at cell $e$ gives $t = \sigma_e(\pi_e - n_e/N)$. $\square$

This is where *Module 1's* thresholds matter. With any other thresholds the
margins differ and K2 fails.

### One empty cell

**Proposition K3.** Let $n_e = 0$ and the other three counts be positive. For
every $\rho \in (-1,1)$,
$$-\sigma_e\,\bar S(\rho) > \phi_2(a,b;\rho) > 0 .$$
*Proof.* Write $\varepsilon = \pi_e(\rho)$, the probability of a rectangle
with nonempty interior, so $\varepsilon > 0$ on $(-1,1)$. The two cells sharing
a row or column with $e$ have $\sigma_{rs} = -\sigma_e$, and by K2
$\pi_{rs} = n_{rs}/N - \varepsilon$, so $n_{rs}/\pi_{rs} > N$. The opposite cell
$o$ has $\sigma_o = \sigma_e$ and $\pi_o = n_o/N + \varepsilon$, so
$n_o/\pi_o < N$. Hence
$-\sigma_e\sum_{\mathcal O}\sigma_{rs}n_{rs}/\pi_{rs} > N + N - N = N$; multiply
by $\phi/N > 0$. $\square$

**Consequences.**

1. $d\ell/d\rho = S$, so the log-likelihood $\ell(\rho) = \sum_{\mathcal O} n_{rs}\log\pi_{rs}$
   is **strictly monotone** on $(-1,1)$: increasing when the empty cell is off
   the diagonal ($\sigma_e = -1$), decreasing when it is on it. There is no
   stationary point, so **no interior maximum**.
2. **The direction is $d = -\sigma_e$:** an empty off-diagonal cell sends the
   supremum to $\rho \to +1$, an empty diagonal cell to $\rho \to -1$.
3. **The supremum is the saturated likelihood.** As $\rho \to d$, the Fréchet
   bound sends the smaller of the two cells with $\sigma_{rs} = \sigma_e$ to
   $0$. By K2 those are $e$ ($\varepsilon$) and $o$ ($n_o/N + \varepsilon$), so
   $\varepsilon \to 0$ and $\pi_{rs} \to n_{rs}/N$ on every cell:
   $\ell \to \sum n_{rs}\log(n_{rs}/N)$, not attained on $(-1,1)$.
4. **$\bar S(0) \ne 0$**: $|\bar S(0)| > \phi(a)\phi(b) > 0$, so the zero-probe
   branch of @sec-rootfind never runs.

### What the root-finder does with it

**Usability along the walk.** The walk runs on $[0, dB]$. By K1 each cell is
monotone in $\rho$. The two observed cells adjacent to $e$ have
$\sigma_{rs} = d$ and increase from $\pi_{rs}(0) = p_rq_s \ge N^{-2}$. The
opposite cell decreases towards $n_o/N + \varepsilon > N^{-1}$. So every
observed cell satisfies $\pi_{rs} \ge N^{-2}$ on the whole walk. With
$|\tilde\pi - \pi| \le \delta_P$, every walk point is usable when
$N^{-2} > 2\delta_P$, $N < 1.06\times10^7$.

**The computed sign.** Let $\eta = \delta_P N^2$ bound each observed cell's
relative error. The two adjacent terms are at least $N/(1+\eta)$ each and the
opposite one at most $N/(1-\eta)$, so the computed bracket keeps the sign
$-\sigma_e$ when $2/(1+\eta) > 1/(1-\eta)$, i.e. $\eta < 1/3$:
$N < 8.68\times10^6$. The factor $\tilde\phi$ is non-negative and may
underflow to exactly $0$ near $\pm1$ (Level R5's table does from
$\rho = 1 - 2^{-16}$); the walk's inequality is strict (production
`dwlsmv_rf_side()`, `d * e[3] < 0`), so an exact $0$ does not close a bracket. The weights and the three-term sum add relative rounding
of order $5\varepsilon$, far inside the factor-2 margin.

**Corollary K4 (the assertable check).** Under those premises a one-empty-cell pair
never brackets: from $x_0 = 0$ the walk goes towards $d$, every trial point is
usable with $d\,\tilde{\bar S} \ge 0$, and the walk reaches $dB$. The result is
**status 2, $\hat\rho = dB = -\sigma_e B$ exactly**, after $1 + 10$ evaluations
(@sec-rootfind; production `dwlsmv_rf_side()` steps to $1 - (1 - d\,x)/2$,
so the trial points are $1 - 2^{-k}$, $k = 1, \dots, 9$, then $B = 0.999$ since
$1 - 2^{-10} > B$, after which the candidate equals the point and it returns 2). On a one-empty-cell table,
$$\text{status} = 2,\qquad \hat\rho = -\sigma_e\,B,\qquad \operatorname{sign}\tilde{\bar S}(0) = -\sigma_e$$
is a consistency check; any other outcome means a premise failed or the code
departs from this section. What a failure should do is not decided here.

**Premises, stated.** (i) $\delta_\Phi$ is measured for thresholds in
$[-2.5, 2.5]$ (@sec-rootfind). A binary threshold leaves that range when a
marginal proportion is below $\Phi(-2.5) = 0.0062$, which Level K2's extreme
tables do; there $\delta_P$ is an assumption, not a measurement. Whether to
extend $\delta_\Phi$'s threshold range is an open decision (E-059);
this premise depends on it. (ii) $N < 8.68\times10^6$. (iii) The chunks run R's
`cellP()`, not Stata's `binormal()`; production's result on these tables is
untested until a Stata test runs them. That test is owed with the group-B
implementation: $(\pm0.999,\ 2,\ 11)$ on L9d, one mirror, and one diagonal-pair
table.

### Two empty cells

- **Same row or column.** One variable is constant: a binary variable with an
  empty boundary category. Its threshold is infinite (`ec_thr()` returns
  $\pm\infty$), and Module 1's `dwlsmv_thresholds()` aborts naming the category
  (spec §4.5.6; `dwlsmv_crosstab.mata`'s header: such a variable has no finite
  threshold to pass to Module 2). `dwls_polychoric()` never sees the pair.
  Three empty cells are this case too.
- **A diagonal pair** ($n_{12} = n_{21} = 0$, or $n_{11} = n_{22} = 0$):
  perfect association. Take $e$ one empty cell; the other is $o$, so both
  observed cells are adjacent to $e$, with $\sigma_{rs} = -\sigma_e$ and
  $\pi_{rs} = n_{rs}/N - \varepsilon$. Then
  $$-\sigma_e\,\bar S(\rho) > 2\,\phi_2(a,b;\rho) > 0,$$
  with all terms of one sign, so the computed sign needs only $\eta < 1$.
  Both observed cells increase along the walk. **Production path, read from
  the code:** `dwlsmv_thresholds()` accepts both margins (each category is
  observed); `dwlsmv_rootfind()` evaluates $\rho = 0$ (usable,
  $\tilde{\bar S}(0) \ne 0$), `dwlsmv_rf_side()` walks to $dB$ without a
  bracket and returns 2, and `dwls_polychoric()` returns $(dB, 2, 11)$ with
  $d = +1$ for empty off-diagonal cells, $-1$ for an empty diagonal. No abort.
  The likelihood tends to the saturated one as $\rho \to d$.

### Can an empty-cell table end at status 3?

Status 3 needs an unusable trial point before $\pm B$: some observed cell's
computed probability at or below $\delta_P$. As $\rho \to d$, the only cells
whose probability tends to $0$ are the empty ones (consequence 3); every
observed cell tends to $n_{rs}/N \ge 1/N$, and on the walk it never falls below
$N^{-2}$. So under premises (i)–(ii) **neither the one-empty-cell pair nor the perfect-association pair can
end at status 3**, nor at 4 or 8, and since no bracket forms, not at 1, 5, 6 or
7 either. Level K4 measures the margin. The argument uses K2, so it is specific
to Module 1's thresholds; it says nothing about larger tables, whose interior
cells are not monotone (@sec-rootfind).

### Verification

Chunks `setup`, `gate3-core` (`cellP`, `dP_drho`), `ec-core` (`ec_thr`) and
`rf-core` (`rf_eval`, `rf_root`, `rf_dP`) must have run. Every name defined here
starts with `kE_`.

The tables: L9d, $(30, 2;\ 0, 8)$, and its four row/column mirrors (every
position of the empty cell); 48 seeded random tables, eight at each of
$N = 10, 40, 200, 1000, 5000, 10^5$, three positive counts and the empty cell
placed at random; and extreme tables $(1, N-2, 1)$ and $(N-2, 1, 1)$ at
$N = 40, 1000, 10^5$ in every position, whose thresholds leave $[-2.5, 2.5]$.

```{r kE-core}
#| cache: true
# Depends on: setup (phi2), gate3-core (cellP, dP_drho), ec-core (ec_thr),
# rf-core (rf_eval, rf_root, rf_dP). Every name defined here starts with kE_.
kE_sig <- matrix(c(1, -1, -1, 1), 2)                     # sigma_rs: +1 diagonal, -1 off
kE_put <- function(v, e) { m <- numeric(4); m[e] <- 0; m[-e] <- v; matrix(m, 2) }  # e: column-major index
kE_tabs <- local({
  L9d <- matrix(c(30, 2, 0, 8), 2, byrow = TRUE)
  t1 <- list(L9d = L9d, L9d_t = t(L9d), L9d_r = L9d[2:1, ], L9d_c = L9d[, 2:1], L9d_rc = L9d[2:1, 2:1])
  set.seed(20261002)
  for (N in c(10, 40, 200, 1000, 5000, 1e5)) for (k in 1:8) {
    p <- rexp(3); v <- 1 + as.vector(rmultinom(1, N - 3, p / sum(p)))
    t1[[sprintf("rand_N%g_%d", N, k)]] <- kE_put(v, sample(4, 1))
  }
  for (N in c(40, 1000, 1e5)) for (e in 1:4) {
    t1[[sprintf("ext1_N%g_e%d", N, e)]] <- kE_put(c(1, N - 2, 1), e)
    t1[[sprintf("ext2_N%g_e%d", N, e)]] <- kE_put(c(N - 2, 1, 1), e)
  }
  t1
})
kE_e <- function(n) which(n == 0)                           # the empty cell(s)
kE_d <- function(n) -kE_sig[kE_e(n)[1]]                     # the direction, -sigma_e
kE_ab <- function(n) list(a = ec_thr(rowSums(n)), b = ec_thr(colSums(n)))
kE_grid <- c(-0.999, -0.99, -0.9, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999)
stopifnot(all(sapply(kE_tabs, function(n) length(kE_e(n)) == 1 && all(n[n > 0] >= 1))))
length(kE_tabs)
```

**Level K1 — the lemmas, pointwise.** On the nine-point grid, for every table:
`dP_drho()` equals $\sigma\,\phi_2$ exactly (K1); `cellP()` matches K2's
$n/N + \sigma_e\sigma\,\pi_e$; and $-\sigma_e\bar S/\phi_2 \ge 1$ (K3), computed with
`rf_eval()`, wherever the point is usable and $\phi_2$ has not underflowed.
Points on the side away from $d$ may be unusable; they are not on the walk, and
the chunk asserts that every unusable point lies there. Both tolerances are `cellP()`'s quadrature error, not slack
in the lemmas: as $\rho \to d$ the bound in K3 is approached, so its margin is
below what `Phi2()`'s `rel.tol = 1e-12` resolves.

```{r kE-L1}
#| cache: true
kE_L1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(kE_tabs), function(nm) {
  n <- kE_tabs[[nm]]; ab <- kE_ab(n); e <- kE_e(n); N <- sum(n)
  r <- t(sapply(kE_grid, function(x) {
    P <- cellP(ab$a, ab$b, x); f <- phi2(ab$a, ab$b, x)
    ev <- rf_eval(n, ab$a, ab$b, x)
    c(k1 = max(abs(dP_drho(ab$a, ab$b, x) - kE_sig * f)),
      k2 = max(abs(P - (n / N + kE_sig[e] * kE_sig * P[e]))),
      res = ev$res, away = sign(x) == -kE_d(n),
      k3 = if (ev$res && f > 0) -kE_sig[e] * ev$S / f else NA)
  }))
  data.frame(table = nm, N = N, k1 = max(r[, "k1"]), k2 = max(r[, "k2"]),
             all_res = all(r[, "res"] == 1), n_unusable = sum(r[, "res"] != 1),
             unusable_away_only = all(r[, "res"] == 1 | r[, "away"] == 1),
             k3_min = min(r[, "k3"], na.rm = TRUE))
}))
# Both tolerances CHOSEN AFTER MEASURING (2026-10-02, R 4.6.0): K2's largest gap was
# 2.2e-16, K3's lowest ratio 1 - 4.6e-13. Toward d, pi_e -> 0 and the bound is
# approached, so the ratio's margin vanishes into Phi2()'s rel.tol = 1e-12 quadrature.
kE_tol_k2 <- 1e-14; kE_tol_k3 <- 1e-10
# Unusable grid points occur (extreme margins, large N), but only on the side away
# from d, which the walk never visits: only the empty cell vanishes towards d.
stopifnot(all(kE_L1$k1 == 0), all(kE_L1$k2 <= kE_tol_k2), all(kE_L1$k3_min >= 1 - kE_tol_k3),
          all(kE_L1$unusable_away_only))
c(max_k2 = max(kE_L1$k2), min_k3 = min(kE_L1$k3_min),
  tables_with_unusable = sum(kE_L1$n_unusable > 0), all_away = all(kE_L1$unusable_away_only))
```

**Level K2 — Corollary K4 on `rf_root()`.** Every table must end at
*no sign change up to the bound*, with $\hat\rho = -\sigma_e B$ exactly, after
11 evaluations, every evaluation usable with $d\,\tilde{\bar S} \ge 0$, the
sign of $\tilde{\bar S}(0)$ equal to $d$, and every observed cell's computed
probability at least $N^{-2}$ on the walk. Premise (ii) is asserted.

```{r kE-L2}
#| cache: true
kE_walk <- function(n) {
  ab <- kE_ab(n); d <- kE_d(n); N <- sum(n); O <- n > 0
  r <- rf_root(n, ab$a, ab$b)
  S <- sapply(r$seen, `[[`, "S"); x <- sapply(r$seen, `[[`, "x")
  pmin <- min(sapply(x, function(z) min(cellP(ab$a, ab$b, z)[O])))
  data.frame(N = N, d = d, case = r$case, rho = r$rho, evals = r$evals,
             all_res = all(sapply(r$seen, `[[`, "res")), signs_ok = all(d * S >= 0),
             S0_sign = sign(S[x == 0]), exact_zeros = sum(S == 0),
             SB = S[x == d * 0.999], pmin_N2 = pmin * N^2,
             ratio_min = min((d * S / sapply(r$seen, `[[`, "tauS"))[S != 0]))
}
kE_L2 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(kE_tabs, kE_walk))
stopifnot(all(kE_L2$N^2 * rf_dP < 1/3),
          all(kE_L2$case == "no sign change up to the bound"),
          all(kE_L2$rho == kE_L2$d * 0.999), all(kE_L2$evals == 11),
          all(kE_L2$all_res), all(kE_L2$signs_ok), all(kE_L2$S0_sign == kE_L2$d),
          all(kE_L2$pmin_N2 >= 1))
kE_L2[1:5, c("d", "case", "rho", "evals", "SB", "ratio_min")]     # L9d and its mirrors
c(tables = nrow(kE_L2), with_exact_zero_S = sum(kE_L2$exact_zeros > 0),
  min_S_over_tauS = min(kE_L2$ratio_min), min_pmin_N2 = min(kE_L2$pmin_N2))
```

**Level K3 — two empty cells.** A diagonal pair empty: $-\sigma_e\bar S/\phi_2 \ge 2$
on the grid and the same `rf_root()` outcome. An empty row or column: the
threshold is infinite, so the pair never reaches Module 2.

```{r kE-L3}
#| cache: true
kE_two <- list(offd_10_30 = matrix(c(10, 0, 0, 30), 2), offd_1_999 = matrix(c(1, 0, 0, 999), 2),
               offd_500_500 = matrix(c(500, 0, 0, 500), 2), diag_10_30 = matrix(c(0, 30, 10, 0), 2),
               diag_1_999 = matrix(c(0, 999, 1, 0), 2), diag_4000_6000 = matrix(c(0, 6000, 4000, 0), 2))
kE_L3 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(kE_two), function(nm) {
  n <- kE_two[[nm]]; ab <- kE_ab(n); e <- kE_e(n)[1]
  k3 <- sapply(kE_grid, function(x) { ev <- rf_eval(n, ab$a, ab$b, x); f <- phi2(ab$a, ab$b, x)
                                      if (ev$res && f > 0) -kE_sig[e] * ev$S / f else NA })
  cbind(table = nm, k3_min = min(k3, na.rm = TRUE), kE_walk(n))
}))
stopifnot(all(kE_L3$k3_min >= 2 - kE_tol_k3), all(kE_L3$case == "no sign change up to the bound"),
          all(kE_L3$rho == kE_L3$d * 0.999), all(kE_L3$evals == 11), all(kE_L3$all_res),
          all(kE_L3$signs_ok), all(kE_L3$S0_sign == kE_L3$d), all(kE_L3$pmin_N2 >= 1))
kE_row <- c(any(is.infinite(ec_thr(rowSums(matrix(c(0, 5, 0, 7), 2))))),   # empty first row
            any(is.infinite(ec_thr(colSums(matrix(c(4, 6, 0, 0), 2))))))    # empty second column
stopifnot(all(kE_row))
kE_L3[, c("table", "d", "rho", "evals", "k3_min")]
```

**Level K4 — the margin against status 3.** At the walk's last point $dB$,
the smallest observed cell's computed probability, in units of $\delta_P$, and
against its limit $n_{rs}/N$.

```{r kE-L4}
#| cache: true
kE_L4 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(kE_tabs, kE_two), function(n) {
  ab <- kE_ab(n); O <- n > 0; P <- cellP(ab$a, ab$b, kE_d(n) * 0.999)
  data.frame(N = sum(n), minP_over_dP = min(P[O]) / rf_dP,
             max_rel_to_limit = max(abs(P[O] - n[O] / sum(n)) / (n[O] / sum(n))))
}))
stopifnot(all(kE_L4$minP_over_dP > 2))
c(min_P_over_dP = min(kE_L4$minP_over_dP), worst_N = kE_L4$N[which.min(kE_L4$minP_over_dP)],
  max_rel_to_limit = max(kE_L4$max_rel_to_limit))
```

## Module 2: boundary repair of a $2\times2$ pair (O6) {#sec-o6}

> Drafted 2026-10-05 by a read-only agent. **Executed by the main session the
> same day** in place: `setup`, `gate3-core`, `norm-core` and `o6-core` …
> `o6-v` extracted from this file and run in order (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2); every
> assertion passed and the numbers quoted below reproduced. The document was not
> re-rendered. The (a)/(b) gate below was left **open** by the mathematics and
> by a pre-registered Monte Carlo (inconclusive, 2026-10-06). **The user decided
> v1 on 2026-10-06**: repair by default, Γ̂ by uncentred (a). The basis is the
> convention both reference programs use (O5, O6 and the Mplus probe in
> E-010), not a statistical result. See
> *The v1 decision, and what the centring row sees* at the end of this section.

This section derives what lavaan's default `zero.add` does to a binary pair with
one empty cell, and what each of two readings of it implies for $\psi$ and
$\hat\Gamma$. It is mathematics only. Whether dwlsmv repairs every eligible pair
or only pairs the current policy would abort (spec Module 2, *Which pairs enter
`s` and Γ̂*) is deferred and not addressed here. Notation is @sec-kindE's:
table $n$, $\sigma_{rs} = +1$ on the diagonal and $-1$ off it, Module 1's
thresholds $\Phi(a) = n_{1\cdot}/N$, $\Phi(b) = n_{\cdot1}/N$.

### The rule, from lavaan's source

Read from lavaan 0.7.2 (`lav_bvord.R`, `lav_bvord_cor_twostep_fit()`;
`lav_options.R`, `lav_options_mimic()` and `lav_options_set()`) on 2026-10-05.
The repair acts on the pair's frequency table `freq` (rows $Y_1$, columns $Y_2$)
before the one-parameter fit:

- **$2\times2$, exactly one empty cell, `zero.add[1]` $= c > 0$,
  `zero.keep.margins = TRUE`:** $+c$ on the empty cell and on its diagonal
  partner, $-c$ on the other two.
- $2\times2$, one empty cell, `zero.keep.margins = FALSE`: $+c$ on the empty
  cell only.
- $2\times2$, **two** empty cells: no repair; $\hat\rho = \pm1$ is returned with
  a warning.
- Any larger table: empty cells are **set to** `zero.add[2]` (default $0$, so a
  no-op), margins not kept.

`zero.keep.margins` defaults to the string `"default"`; `lav_options_mimic()`
turns that into `TRUE` under `mimic = "lavaan"` (the default) and `"Mplus"`,
before `lav_options_set()`'s own fallback to `FALSE` is reached. So `TRUE` is
the effective default, and the fixture generators pin it.

With a single empty cell $e$, the keep-margins rule is, in one line,
$$n^+ = n + c\,\sigma_e\,\sigma, \qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad
  n^+_{rs} = n_{rs} + c\,\sigma_e\sigma_{rs}.$$
Since $\sigma$'s rows and columns sum to zero, $N^+ = N$ and **both margins are
unchanged**. Every cell of $n^+$ is positive when the observed counts exceed
$c$; at lavaan's default $c = 0.5$ any positive integer count does. (lavaan
accepts $c \in [0, 1]$; at $c = 1$ a decremented count of 1 becomes a new empty
cell, which lavaan does not check.)

### The repaired statistics

**Thresholds.** lavaan's thresholds come from the univariate fits on the raw
data (`fit_y1`, `fit_y2` in the same function), never from `freq`. Under
keep-margins the repaired margins equal the raw ones, so the distinction is
invisible: $\hat a^+ = \hat a$, $\hat b^+ = \hat b$. Under `zero.keep.margins =
FALSE` it is not, and the raw thresholds no longer match $n^+$'s margins, so
Lemma K2 of @sec-kindE fails for $n^+$. Only keep-margins is derived below.

**The root.** The repaired score is @sec-kindE's with $n^+$ in place of $n$:
$S^+(\rho) = \phi\sum_{rs}\sigma_{rs}\,n^+_{rs}/\pi_{rs}(\rho)$. Because $n^+$
has Module 1's margins, Lemma K2 applies to it: with
$t(\rho) = \pi_{11}(\rho) - n^+_{11}/N$,
$$\pi_{rs}(\rho) = \frac{n^+_{rs}}{N} + \sigma_{rs}\,t(\rho), \qquad
  \frac{S^+}{\phi} = \sum_{rs}\frac{\sigma_{rs}\,n^+_{rs}}{n^+_{rs}/N + \sigma_{rs}t}.$$
Each term is strictly decreasing in $t$ (its derivative is
$-n^+_{rs}/(\cdot)^2$), $t$ is strictly increasing in $\rho$
($\partial_\rho\pi_{11} = \phi > 0$), and $S^+ = \phi\sum\sigma_{rs}N = 0$ at
$t = 0$. All four $n^+_{rs} > 0$ put $n^+_{11}/N$ strictly inside the Fréchet
bounds, so $t = 0$ is reached on $(-1,1)$. Hence **the root exists, is unique,
and is the saturated inversion**
$$\Phi_2(\hat a, \hat b; \hat\rho^+) = \hat p^+_{11} = \hat p_{11} + \frac{c\,\sigma_e}{N},
  \qquad \pi_{rs}(\hat\rho^+) = n^+_{rs}/N .$$
lavaan's two short cuts on the repaired table agree with this:
$\hat\rho^+ = 0$ when $n^+_{11}n^+_{22} = n^+_{12}n^+_{21}$, and
$\hat\rho^+ = -\cos(2\pi\hat p^+_{11})$ when $\hat a = \hat b = 0$, which is the
inversion of $\Phi_2(0,0;\rho) = \tfrac14 + \arcsin(\rho)/2\pi$. Its numerical
fit is bounded at $\pm0.999$.

So repair turns a one-empty-cell pair (status 2, no interior maximum) into a saturated
pair with an interior root, and @sec-rootfind brackets it.

**What it touches.** Only the pair's own entry $\hat\rho_{jk}$ of $s$. Both
thresholds are unchanged, and no other pair reads $n_{jk}$.

### The influence function, and the open gate

By the previous subsection,
$\hat\rho^+ = h(\hat q_1, \hat q_2, \hat p_{11} + c\sigma_e/N)$, with $h$ the
inversion of @sec-oracle. The shift is a constant. Its Gateaux derivative at
the empirical distribution is therefore @sec-oracle's gradient, evaluated at
the repaired point and applied to the raw centring:
$$\dot\rho^+_i = \nabla h(\hat q_1,\hat q_2,\hat p^+_{11})'
  \big(z_i - \bar z\big), \qquad
  z_i = \big(1\{Y_{1i}{=}0\},\,1\{Y_{2i}{=}0\},\,1\{Y_{1i}{=}0,Y_{2i}{=}0\}\big).$$
Asymptotically repair is irrelevant: with every true cell probability positive,
$P(\text{some cell empty}) \to 0$ exponentially, and on the complement $n^+ = n$.
Both readings below have the same first-order limit. **Which one is right is a
finite-sample question, and it is open.**

**(a) Asymptotic view (what lavaan does).** $\psi$ is @sec-general's, with
@sec-normaliser's empirical weights $W = \hat\pi = n/N$, evaluated at
$(\hat a, \hat b, \hat\rho^+)$. $\hat\Gamma = N^{-1}\sum_i\psi_i\psi_i'$ runs
over the real observations. Pseudo-counts carry no $\psi_i$, and the empty
cell has weight $0$.

**(b) Repaired-data view.** The pseudo-counts are data. $W = \hat\pi^+ =
n^+/N$, which equals $\pi(\hat\rho^+)$, so the empirical and expected
informations coincide (@sec-normaliser, Level N5) and $\psi^{(b)}$ is
@sec-oracle's boxed form at $(\hat a,\hat b,\hat\rho^+)$:
$\psi^{(b)} = \nabla h'(z - \bar z^+)$. The pair's block of $\hat\Gamma$ is
$N^{-1}\sum_{rs} n^+_{rs}\psi^{(b)}_{rs}\psi^{(b)\prime}_{rs} = \nabla h'\,V(\hat\pi^+)\,\nabla h$.

Where they differ:

1. **The normaliser.** $u_e = \phi/\pi_e(\hat\rho^+) = \phi N/c$. Under (b) the
   empty cell has weight $c/N$ and contributes $W_eu_e^2 = \phi^2N/c$ to
   $\hat I_{\rho\rho}$, as much as a cell with count $c$: the largest term in
   the sum. Under (a) it contributes nothing. So $\psi_\rho$ at the *observed*
   cells differs at $O(1)$, not $O(c/N)$.
2. **Centring.** Under (a), Lemma 2 of @sec-gamma-rank gives
   $\bar\psi_\rho = S(\hat\rho^+)/(N\hat I_{\rho\rho})$ with $S$ the *raw*
   score. By Proposition K3, $S$ has no zero on $(-1,1)$. So
   **$\bar\psi_\rho \ne 0$ for every repaired pair under (a)**, and Module 10's
   centring row will flag it. Under (b), $\sum n^+u = S^+(\hat\rho^+) = 0$ and
   the margins are unchanged, so $\psi^{(b)}$ is centred exactly.
3. **Relation to the estimator.** $\psi^{(b)}$ differs from the exact
   derivative $\dot\rho^+$ by the constant $-c\sigma_e/(N\phi)$ ($O(1/N)$).
   $\psi^{(a)}$ is the influence function of the *unrepaired* root,
   evaluated at a point that is not its root. It is not a derivative of
   the estimator that produced $\hat\rho^+$.
4. **Scope of $\hat\Gamma$.** A pseudo-count is not an observation of the
   $p$-vector. Its weight is negative on two cells, and it has no values on
   other variables. So (b) defines only the pair's
   $(\tau_j, \tau_k, \rho_{jk})$ block. It also changes that block's
   cross-variable threshold entry $\hat\Gamma_{\tau_j\tau_k}$, which (a) leaves
   untouched. Entries against other pairs or thresholds have no
   pseudo-observation to form them from. The production construction
   $N^{-1}\sum_i\psi_i\psi_i'$ cannot express (b). Patching the block in
   by hand loses the guarantee that $\hat\Gamma$ is PSD.
5. **The hybrid** ($\psi^{(b)}$ summed over the real observations only) keeps
   the production construction. It is not close to (b), because $\psi^{(b)}$
   at $e$ is large and (b) weights it.

Internal consistency, stated as it stands. (a) is consistent with the
production $\hat\Gamma$ construction and with lavaan. It is inconsistent with
the repaired estimator: it gives a non-centred $\psi$, scored on a table the
estimator did not fit. (b) is consistent with the repaired estimator. It
is inconsistent with a per-observation $\hat\Gamma$. Spec Module 2 already says
that patching the table means "Γ has to be computed consistently from the
corrected table". That sentence favours (b) over (a), but it does not choose
among (b), the hybrid, or another weighting. The gate stays open.

### Verification

Two tables, $N = 40$. T1 $= (22, 6 \mid 0, 12)$ has its empty cell off the
diagonal ($\sigma_e = -1$). T2 $= (0, 9 \mid 7, 24)$ has it on the diagonal
($\sigma_e = +1$). Neither has a zero threshold, so lavaan's $-\cos$ short cut
does not run. Tolerances: $\Phi_2$ here is `integrate()` at `rel.tol = 1e-12`.
A root or inversion therefore carries about $10^{-12}/\phi$, and a central
difference at step $h$ divides that by $h$.

```{r o6-core}
# Depends on: setup (Phi2, phi2), gate3-core (cellP, dP_drho), norm-core
# (psi_tab). Every name defined here starts with o6_.
o6_c   <- 0.5                                   # zero.add[1]
o6_sig <- matrix(c(1, -1, -1, 1), 2)            # sigma_rs: +1 diagonal, -1 off it

# lavaan 0.7.2's 2x2 repair under zero.keep.margins = TRUE, one empty cell e:
# +c on e and on its diagonal partner, -c on the other two.
o6_repair <- function(n, c = o6_c) {
  e <- which(n == 0)
  stopifnot(all(dim(n) == 2), length(e) == 1L)
  n + c * o6_sig[e] * o6_sig
}
o6_thr   <- function(n) c(qnorm(sum(n[1, ]) / sum(n)), qnorm(sum(n[, 1]) / sum(n)))
o6_Sbar  <- function(n, a, b, r) {               # observed-cells score / N
  u <- dP_drho(a, b, r) / cellP(a, b, r); sum((n * u)[n > 0]) / sum(n)
}
o6_root  <- function(n, a, b)                    # root of the score on table n
  uniroot(function(r) o6_Sbar(n, a, b, r), c(-.999, .999), tol = 1e-14)$root
o6_inv   <- function(p11, a, b)                  # saturated inversion Phi2 = p11
  uniroot(function(r) Phi2(a, b, r) - p11, c(-.999, .999), tol = 1e-14)$root

# The pair's influence table: rows are cells in column-major order (11,21,12,22),
# columns (psi_a, psi_b, psi_rho). W is the weight matrix of @sec-normaliser.
o6_psi <- function(a, b, r, W) {
  pr <- psi_tab(a, b, r, W)
  cbind(a   = (c(1, 0, 1, 0) - pnorm(a)) / dnorm(a),
        b   = (c(1, 1, 0, 0) - pnorm(b)) / dnorm(b),
        rho = as.vector(pr))
}
o6_gamma <- function(psi, w) crossprod(psi * sqrt(as.vector(w) / sum(w)))

o6_tabs <- list(T1 = matrix(c(22, 0, 6, 12), 2),   # empty off-diagonal cell (2,1)
                T2 = matrix(c(0, 7, 9, 24), 2))    # empty diagonal cell (1,1)

```

**Level O1 — the statistics.** Repair moves no margin and no threshold. The raw
score keeps the sign $-\sigma_e$ on a grid over $(-.99, .99)$ (Proposition K3).
The repaired root is interior. All three are asserted.

```{r o6-i}
o6_i <- t(sapply(o6_tabs, function(n) {
  N <- sum(n); np <- o6_repair(n); th <- o6_thr(n); e <- which(n == 0)
  grid <- seq(-.99, .99, by = .01)
  Sg <- sapply(grid, function(r) o6_Sbar(n, th[1], th[2], r))
  rp <- o6_root(np, th[1], th[2])
  c(sigma_e = o6_sig[e], N = N,
    margins_moved = max(abs(c(rowSums(np) - rowSums(n), colSums(np) - colSums(n)))),
    thr_gap = max(abs(o6_thr(np) - th)),
    raw_sign_constant = all(sign(Sg) == -o6_sig[e]),
    raw_min_abs_Sbar = min(abs(Sg)),
    rho_plus = rp,
    p11_plus = np[1, 1] / N)
}))
o6_i
stopifnot(o6_i[, "margins_moved"] == 0, o6_i[, "thr_gap"] == 0,
          o6_i[, "raw_sign_constant"] == 1)

```

T1: $\hat\rho^+ = 0.9214273$; T2: $\hat\rho^+ = -0.4113736$. Margins and
thresholds moved by exactly 0, and the raw sign was constant on both.

**Level O2 — the repaired score equation.** The root of $S^+$ equals the
saturated inversion, and $\pi(\hat\rho^+) = n^+/N$. Tolerances: $\bar S^+$
below 1e-10, root against inversion below 1e-9, cells below 1e-10; all three
come from $\Phi_2$'s accuracy above.

```{r o6-ii}
o6_ii <- t(sapply(o6_tabs, function(n) {
  N <- sum(n); np <- o6_repair(n); th <- o6_thr(n)
  rp <- o6_root(np, th[1], th[2]); ri <- o6_inv(np[1, 1] / N, th[1], th[2])
  c(Sbar_plus_at_root = o6_Sbar(np, th[1], th[2], rp),
    root_vs_inversion  = abs(rp - ri),
    pi_vs_nplus_over_N = max(abs(cellP(th[1], th[2], rp) - np / N)),
    raw_Sbar_at_root   = o6_Sbar(n, th[1], th[2], rp))
}))
o6_ii
stopifnot(abs(o6_ii[, "Sbar_plus_at_root"]) < 1e-10,
          o6_ii[, "root_vs_inversion"] < 1e-9,
          o6_ii[, "pi_vs_nplus_over_N"] < 1e-10)

```

$|\bar S^+|$ is 1.3e-14 and 4.3e-16. Root against inversion is 2.8e-15 and
3.4e-15, and the cells are 6.9e-16 and 9.4e-17. The raw score at
$\hat\rho^+$ is $+0.267$ and $-0.060$ per observation, with sign
$-\sigma_e$ in each case.

**Level O3 — numerical derivatives against the analytic influence function.**
The repaired estimator, as a functional of the raw cell proportions with the
shift held fixed, is differentiated along $\delta_{rs} - \hat P$. It must equal
$\psi^{(b)} + c\sigma_e/(N\phi)$ (item 3). Richardson extrapolation of central
differences at $h = 10^{-4}$ leaves $O(h^4)$ truncation. The tolerance 1e-6 is
the rounding budget $10^{-12}/(\phi\,h/2)$ at T2's $\phi$.

```{r o6-iii}
# T(P): the repaired estimator as a functional of the raw cell proportions P,
# with the repair held at its realised value c sigma_e / N on cell 11.
o6_T <- function(P, shift)
  c(qnorm(P[1] + P[3]), qnorm(P[1] + P[2]),
    o6_inv(P[1] + shift, qnorm(P[1] + P[3]), qnorm(P[1] + P[2])))
o6_iii <- lapply(o6_tabs, function(n) {
  N <- sum(n); np <- o6_repair(n); th <- o6_thr(n); e <- which(n == 0)
  rp <- o6_root(np, th[1], th[2]); P <- as.vector(n) / N
  shift <- o6_c * o6_sig[e] / N
  eps <- 1e-4
  cd <- function(k, h) { d <- -P; d[k] <- d[k] + 1           # central difference
    (o6_T(P + h * d, shift) - o6_T(P - h * d, shift)) / (2 * h) }
  fd <- t(sapply(1:4, function(k)                  # Gateaux derivative at P-hat,
    (4 * cd(k, eps / 2) - cd(k, eps)) / 3))         # Richardson: O(eps^4) truncation
  pb <- o6_psi(th[1], th[2], rp, np / N)          # (b): W = n+/N
  pa <- o6_psi(th[1], th[2], rp, n / N)           # (a): W = n/N
  ph <- phi2(th[1], th[2], rp); k <- -shift / ph
  list(fd = fd, pa = pa, pb = pb,
       gaps = c(b_minus_fd_minus_k = max(abs(pb - fd - cbind(0, 0, rep(k, 4)))),
                thr_cols_fd        = max(abs(pb[, 1:2] - fd[, 1:2])),
                k = k,
                a_vs_b_rho_observed = max(abs(pa[n > 0, 3] - pb[n > 0, 3]))))
})
t(sapply(o6_iii, `[[`, "gaps"))
stopifnot(sapply(o6_iii, function(x) x$gaps["b_minus_fd_minus_k"]) < 1e-6)

```

The gap is 1.2e-10 (T1) and 1.1e-9 (T2), and 4e-12 on the threshold columns.
$\psi^{(a)}_\rho$ and $\psi^{(b)}_\rho$ differ by up to 0.42 (T1) and 1.65 (T2)
at observed cells: that is item 1, at $O(1)$.

**Level O4 — the $\hat\Gamma$ block under each view, by an independent route.**
(a) is rebuilt as lavaan builds it, as $N B^{-1}(\sum_i sc_i sc_i')B^{-\top}$
from finite-difference per-observation scores, with no analytic $\partial\pi$.
(b) is rebuilt by the delta method, $J\,V(\hat\pi^+)\,J'$, with $J$ from
Richardson differences of the inversion. Tolerance 1e-6, as Level O3.

```{r o6-iv}
o6_iv <- lapply(names(o6_tabs), function(nm) {
  n <- o6_tabs[[nm]]; N <- sum(n); np <- o6_repair(n); th <- o6_thr(n)
  rp <- o6_root(np, th[1], th[2]); x <- o6_iii[[nm]]
  Ga  <- o6_gamma(x$pa, n)                        # (a)
  Gb  <- o6_gamma(x$pb, np)                       # (b), pseudo-counts as data
  Gbr <- o6_gamma(x$pb, n)                        # hybrid: (b)'s psi, raw counts

  # (a), independent route: lavaan's B^{-1} sc assembly from finite-difference
  # per-observation scores (no analytic derivative of pi is used).
  h <- 1e-6; cells <- rep(1:4, as.vector(n)); r1 <- c(1, 2, 1, 2); s1 <- c(1, 1, 2, 2)
  lP <- function(a, b, r) log(cellP(a, b, r))
  lu <- function(t, y) log(if (y == 1) pnorm(t) else 1 - pnorm(t))
  dr <- (lP(th[1], th[2], rp + h) - lP(th[1], th[2], rp - h)) / (2 * h)
  da <- (lP(th[1] + h, th[2], rp) - lP(th[1] - h, th[2], rp)) / (2 * h)
  db <- (lP(th[1], th[2] + h, rp) - lP(th[1], th[2] - h, rp)) / (2 * h)
  sc <- t(sapply(cells, function(k) c(
    (lu(th[1] + h, r1[k]) - lu(th[1] - h, r1[k])) / (2 * h),
    (lu(th[2] + h, s1[k]) - lu(th[2] - h, s1[k])) / (2 * h),
    dr[k])))
  dth <- cbind(da[cells], db[cells])
  B <- matrix(0, 3, 3)
  B[1, 1] <- sum(sc[, 1]^2); B[2, 2] <- sum(sc[, 2]^2)   # A11: separate univariate fits
  B[3, 1:2] <- crossprod(sc[, 3], dth); B[3, 3] <- sum(sc[, 3]^2)
  Bi <- solve(B); Ga_fd <- N * Bi %*% crossprod(sc) %*% t(Bi)

  # (b), independent route: delta method J V+ J' at the repaired proportions.
  P0 <- as.vector(np) / N; eps <- 1e-4
  Tq <- function(q1, q2, p11) c(qnorm(q1), qnorm(q2), o6_inv(p11, qnorm(q1), qnorm(q2)))
  z0 <- c(P0[1] + P0[3], P0[1] + P0[2], P0[1])
  cdj <- function(j, h) { d <- replace(numeric(3), j, h)
    (do.call(Tq, as.list(z0 + d)) - do.call(Tq, as.list(z0 - d))) / (2 * h) }
  J  <- sapply(1:3, function(j) (4 * cdj(j, eps / 2) - cdj(j, eps)) / 3)
  Z  <- rbind(c(1, 1, 1), c(0, 1, 0), c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 0, 0))   # z for cells 11,21,12,22
  V  <- crossprod(Z * sqrt(P0)) - tcrossprod(z0)
  Gb_dm <- J %*% V %*% t(J)

  rel <- function(A, B) max(abs(A - B)) / max(abs(B))
  list(Ga = Ga, Gb = Gb, Gbr = Gbr,
       chk = c(a_table_vs_fd_scores = rel(Ga, Ga_fd),
               b_table_vs_delta     = rel(Gb, Gb_dm),
               Grr_a = Ga[3, 3], Grr_b = Gb[3, 3], Grr_hybrid = Gbr[3, 3],
               ratio_a_over_b = Ga[3, 3] / Gb[3, 3],
               hybrid_vs_b = rel(Gbr, Gb),
               tt_cross_a_vs_b = Ga[1, 2] - Gb[1, 2],
               Grr_a_centred = Ga[3, 3] - (sum(n * matrix(x$pa[, 3], 2)) / N)^2,
               psibar_rho_a = sum(n * matrix(x$pa[, 3], 2)) / N,
               psibar_rho_b = sum(np * matrix(x$pb[, 3], 2)) / N))
})
names(o6_iv) <- names(o6_tabs)
t(sapply(o6_iv, `[[`, "chk"))
stopifnot(sapply(o6_iv, function(x) x$chk["a_table_vs_fd_scores"]) < 1e-6,
          sapply(o6_iv, function(x) x$chk["b_table_vs_delta"]) < 1e-6)
```

| | T1 | T2 |
|---|---|---|
| (a) table vs finite-difference scores | 2.2e-10 | 2.3e-10 |
| (b) table vs delta method | 6.9e-12 | 9.5e-11 |
| $\hat\Gamma_{\rho\rho}$ (a) / (a) centred / (b) / hybrid | 0.279 / 0.089 / 0.212 / 0.065 | 3.31 / 0.437 / 4.09 / 0.877 |
| $\bar\psi_\rho$ (a) / (b) | 0.436 / −2.6e-15 | −1.70 / 1.7e-15 |
| $\hat\Gamma_{\tau_1\tau_2}$, (a) − (b) | 0.091 | −0.162 |
| hybrid vs (b), max relative | 0.085 | 0.79 |

**Level O5 — ORACLE, not part of the specification.** lavaan 0.7.2 on the same
tables, with `zero.add = c(0.5, 0)` and `zero.keep.margins = TRUE`.
`lavInspect(fit, "gamma")` is indexed by name. It is compared with (a) and (b)
at lavaan's own $\hat\rho$ (matched-$\hat\rho$, abs + rel, 1e-12, the §7.2
matched-$\hat\rho$ tier) and, printed only, end to end.

```{r o6-v}

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lavaan))
o6_lab <- c("y1|t1", "y2|t1", "y1~~y2")            # indexed by name, not position
o6_v <- t(sapply(names(o6_tabs), function(nm) {
  n <- o6_tabs[[nm]]; N <- sum(n); np <- o6_repair(n); th <- o6_thr(n)
  cell <- rep(1:4, as.vector(n))
  dat <- data.frame(y1 = ordered(c(0, 1, 0, 1)[cell], levels = 0:1),
                    y2 = ordered(c(0, 0, 1, 1)[cell], levels = 0:1))

             parameterization = "delta", zero.add = c(0.5, 0),

  stopifnot(isTRUE(lavInspect(fit, "options")$zero.keep.margins))
  ss <- lavInspect(fit, "sampstat")
  rl <- ss$cov["y2", "y1"]; tl <- ss$th[o6_lab[1:2]]

  rp <- o6_root(np, th[1], th[2])
  Ga <- o6_gamma(o6_psi(th[1], th[2], rl, n / N), n)     # (a) at lavaan's rho
  Gb <- o6_gamma(o6_psi(th[1], th[2], rl, np / N), np)   # (b) at lavaan's rho
  rel <- function(A, B) max(abs(A - B) / (1 + abs(B)))   # abs + rel
  c(rho_lavaan = rl, rho_gap = abs(rl - rp), thr_gap = max(abs(tl - th)),

}))
```

**Level O6 — ORACLE, not part of the specification: the full $\hat\Gamma$ at

("does lavaan centre?"). $p = 2$ leaves out the entries between the repaired

```{r o6-vi}
# ORACLE, not specification: lavaan 0.7.2, p = 3, full Gamma vs (a).
o6_n3 <- o6_tabs$T1; o6_N3 <- sum(o6_n3); o6_cl <- rep(1:4, as.vector(o6_n3))
```

including the entries between $\rho_{12}$ and the other pairs and
thresholds. The centred variant misses by 0.17. $\bar\psi$ is 0.436 for

### The v1 decision, and what the centring row sees

Decided by the user on 2026-10-06 (E-010). Where this section's
earlier text says the (a)/(b) gate is open, it records the state before this
decision.

- **A one-empty-cell pair** is repaired by default: keep-margins,
  $c = 0.5$. $\hat\Gamma$ uses (a), uncentred.
- **A perfect-association pair** (two empty cells on a diagonal) is not repaired; lavaan does not repair
  them either. The pair aborts.
- **A repaired root with $|\hat\rho^+| \ge B$** aborts under O3. The existence
  proof above places $\hat\rho^+$ in $(-1, 1)$, not in $(-B, B)$. Truncating it
  at $B$, as lavaan's numerical fit does, would be a second silent change.

The hybrid was rejected, and (b) is not defined beyond its own block (point 4).

**Centring under (a).** In $\psi_\rho$ (@sec-normaliser), the threshold columns
have sample mean exactly zero, because Module 1's thresholds are untouched by
repair. So Lemma 2 of @sec-gamma-rank holds for the repaired pair exactly as
for any other:
$$\bar\psi_\rho = \frac{\bar S(\hat\rho^+)}{\hat I_{\rho\rho}}, \qquad
  \bar S(\hat\rho^+) = \frac1N\sum_{rs} n_{rs}\,u_{rs}(\hat\rho^+),$$
with the **raw** table. By Proposition K3 this is never zero. Its size is
$O(1)$, not $O(\tau_S)$. So Module 10's centring row, $z > 10^{-6}$, fires on
every repaired pair. There the firing reports the decided construction, not a
failed score equation. This gives the row's v1 rule for a repaired pair:

- its $\rho$ entry is excluded from the bug-report $z$;
- its $\bar\psi_\rho$ is reported separately, as the repaired pair's value.

Whether a pair was repaired is derivable from $(Y, K)$: a binary pair whose
$2\times2$ table has exactly one empty cell. The pair's threshold entries stay
under the machine-precision assertion of spec §4.5.5.

```{r o6-vii}
# Depends on: setup (Phi2), gate3-core (cellP, dP_drho), norm-core (infoW), o6-core.
# What Module 10's centring row sees on a repaired pair under (a), and the |rho+| >= B edge.
o6_tabs7 <- c(o6_tabs, list(L9d = matrix(c(30, 0, 2, 8), 2)))
o6_vii <- t(sapply(o6_tabs7, function(n) {
  N <- sum(n); np <- o6_repair(n); th <- o6_thr(n); r <- o6_root(np, th[1], th[2])
  ps <- o6_psi(th[1], th[2], r, n / N)                    # (a)
  pbar <- unname(colSums(ps * as.vector(n)) / N)          # (psibar_a, psibar_b, psibar_rho)
  I <- infoW(th[1], th[2], r, n / N)
  Sbar <- sum(n * I$u) / N                                # raw score / N at rho+
  G <- unname(o6_gamma(ps, n))
  c(psibar_thr_max = max(abs(pbar[1:2])), psibar_rho = pbar[3],
    lemma2_gap = abs(pbar[3] - Sbar / I$Irr) / abs(pbar[3]),
    z_rho = abs(pbar[3]) / sqrt(G[3, 3]))
}))
o6_vii
stopifnot(o6_vii[, "psibar_thr_max"] < 1e-15, o6_vii[, "lemma2_gap"] < 1e-12,
          o6_vii[, "z_rho"] > 1e-6 * 1e4)
# The edge: a large, nearly perfectly associated table whose repaired root lies beyond B = 0.999.

o6_rbig <- uniroot(function(r) Phi2(o6_thb[1], o6_thb[2], r) - o6_repair(o6_big)[1, 1] / sum(o6_big),
                   c(0.5, 1 - 1e-12), tol = 1e-15)$root
c(rho_plus_big = o6_rbig)
stopifnot(o6_rbig > 0.999)
```

- Lemma 2's identity holds to 6.4e-16 relative.

The $10^4$ margin in the assertion is a floor chosen after measuring. It asserts

**The edge exists.** At $N = 2001$, the table $(1000, 1 \mid 0, 1000)$ repairs to
