## Module 10: the bread's numerical-rank criterion on $W_D^{1/2}\Delta$ {#sec-bread-rank}

*Added 2026-09-26, before `dwlsmv_breaddiag()`'s code.* Spec §5 applies
Module 3's criterion, singular-value ratio $< 10^{-8}$, to
$M = W_D^{1/2}\Delta$ at $\hat\theta$. Module 3 sized $10^{-8}$ on the
**unweighted** Δ at the starting values: noise near $10^{-10}$, with columns
$O(1)$, and the smallest genuine ratio 0.226 across the tier-2 oracle
(`dwls_identify.mata`). The row weights $w_k^{1/2} = \hat\Gamma_{kk}^{-1/2}$
spread by orders of magnitude exactly where Module 10 looks: an extreme
boundary threshold has a tiny weight, and a correlation near 1 a huge one. So
the margin does not carry over by assumption (E-071,
2026-09-26). The user's instruction: 1e-8 stays a **candidate** until this
section establishes its headroom on $M$. This section does that. It does not
choose a different number.

### Where the noise is, and a bound that the weights cancel out of

Production's Δ is $\Delta_0 + E$. The threshold block is a literal identity
and the structural columns are exactly zero in threshold rows (@sec-gate2,
Finding 3), so **E lives only in the correlation rows × structural columns**.
There each entry is a central difference with
$h_c = 10^{-5}\max(1, |\theta_c|)$ (`dwlsmv_delta_cols`). Every correlation
is at most quadratic in any single loading or variance, so there is no
truncation error, only rounding: $|E_{kc}| \lesssim \varepsilon|\sigma_k|/h_c$.

By Weyl's inequality every singular value of $M = W_D^{1/2}(\Delta_0 + E)$ is
within $\lVert W_D^{1/2}E\rVert_2$ of the exact one. So the ratio read off $M$
is within about

$$\nu = \lVert W_D^{1/2}E\rVert_2 \,/\, \sigma_{\max}(M)$$

of the exact ratio. An exact deficiency reads at most $\nu$; a genuine ratio
$r$ reads at least $r - \nu$. The criterion separates them iff
$\nu \ll 10^{-8} \ll r$.

**The weights cancel from the bound on $\nu$.** Write $E_k$ and $\Delta_k$ for
row $k$. Then $\lVert W_D^{1/2}E\rVert_2 \le \lVert W_D^{1/2}E\rVert_F \le
\sqrt{P}\,\max_k w_k^{1/2}\lVert E_k\rVert$, and $\sigma_{\max}(M) \ge
\max_k w_k^{1/2}\lVert\Delta_k\rVert$, because no row is longer than
$\sigma_{\max}$. If $\lVert E_k\rVert \le \eta\lVert\Delta_k\rVert$ for every
row, the numerator's maximum is at most $\eta$ times the denominator's, so

$$\nu \le \sqrt{P}\;\eta, \qquad \eta = \max_k \lVert E_k\rVert/\lVert\Delta_k\rVert ,$$

with no weight in it. **Each weight multiplies a row's noise and its signal
alike.** A weighted matrix is therefore no noisier, relative to its largest
singular value, than its worst row is on its own.

**One factor, marker identification.** $\rho_{jk} = l_jl_k\psi$, so
$\lVert\Delta_k\rVert \ge |\partial\rho_{jk}/\partial\psi| = |\rho_{jk}|/\psi$,
while $\lVert E_k\rVert \lesssim \sqrt{n_s}\,\varepsilon|\rho_{jk}|/h$ over the
$n_s$ structural columns. Hence $\eta \lesssim \sqrt{n_s}\,\varepsilon\psi/h$
whatever the loadings. That is about $10^{-10}$ at $\psi = 1$: the order
Module 3 quoted for the unweighted Δ.

**What the weights do change is the signal.** $M$'s threshold columns have
singular values $w_t^{1/2}$ and its structural columns scale with the
correlation weights, so the genuine $\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}$ of $M$
includes the spread between the largest correlation weight and the smallest
threshold weight. That spread is a property of the design, not noise. The
chunk measures how far it pushes the genuine ratio toward $10^{-8}$.

**Scope.** Measurement models: loadings and $\psi$. A structural $\beta$ enters
$\Phi = (I-B)^{-1}\Psi(I-B)^{-\top}$ beyond quadratic order, so its column
carries an $O(h^2)$ truncation term too. The bound still holds, with that term
in $E$. **[Corrected 2026-09-28: it does not. For every $\beta$ row a
recursive model admits, $A$ is affine in that $\beta$ and every correlation
is quadratic in it, so its column carries no truncation term. The bound above
holds for it as stated, with rounding only. See @sec-delta's lemma, which
verifies this with a central difference at $h = 1/8$.]** Production's case E Δ, $\beta$ column included, matches lavaan's
analytic Jacobian at about $3\times10^{-12}$ (`test_delta.do` check 4). It is
not re-derived here.

### Verification

Population $\Gamma_0$ from @sec-gamma-pop's enumeration gives the weights at
the design points the Monte Carlo reference stresses. The control is d. The
extreme threshold weights come from b1 and b2 at an expected count of 1. The
largest correlation weights come from c at .998 and .999, and from B at .9975.
Δ's structural block is built two ways: exactly, from `pg_Delta()`'s closed
form, and by production's recipe, a central difference with production's $h$
on $\rho_{jk} = l_j\psi l_k$. **The second is a model of production's
arithmetic, not its bits.** The Stata test of `breaddiag` asserts the same
quantities on production's own Δ.

A deficient twin of every design frees the marker's loading too. $(l, \psi)
\to (cl, \psi/c^2)$ then leaves every $\rho$ unchanged, which gives Δ an exact
null direction. That is the case the criterion must catch.

The two-decade margin asserted on each side is **Module 3's own design claim**
("about two orders above the noise and seven below the signal",
`dwls_identify.mata`). It was not chosen from these results.

```{r bread-rank}
br_N <- 5000
br_b1 <- function(m) qnorm(cumsum(c(m / br_N, 0.50 - m / br_N, 0.30, 0.20))[-4])
br_b2 <- function(m) qnorm(cumsum(c(0.15, m / br_N, 0.65 - m / br_N, 0.20))[-4])
br_designs <- list(
  d      = list(lam = rep(0.7, 4),                           thr = thD),
  b1_m1  = list(lam = rep(0.7, 4),                           thr = c(list(br_b1(1)), thD[-1])),
  b2_m1  = list(lam = rep(0.7, 4),                           thr = c(list(br_b2(1)), thD[-1])),
  c_998  = list(lam = c(sqrt(.998), sqrt(.998), 0.7, 0.7),   thr = thD),
  c_999  = list(lam = c(sqrt(.999), sqrt(.999), 0.7, 0.7),   thr = thD),
  B_9975 = list(lam = rep(0.9975, 4),                        thr = thD))

# rho_jk = l_j psi l_k in combn order. marker: x = (l_2..l_p, psi), l_1 = 1;
# deficient twin: x = (l_1..l_p, psi), the marker's loading free as well.
br_rho <- function(x, p, marker) {
  if (marker) { l <- c(1, x[1:(p - 1)]); ps <- x[p] } else { l <- x[1:p]; ps <- x[p + 1] }
  pr <- combn(p, 2); l[pr[1, ]] * ps * l[pr[2, ]]
}
br_exact <- function(x, p, marker) {
  if (marker) { l <- c(1, x[1:(p - 1)]); ps <- x[p]; free <- 2:p } else { l <- x[1:p]; ps <- x[p + 1]; free <- 1:p }
  pr <- combn(p, 2)
  t(apply(pr, 2, function(v) { d <- numeric(length(x)); j <- v[1]; k <- v[2]
    if (j %in% free) d[match(j, free)] <- l[k] * ps
    if (k %in% free) d[match(k, free)] <- d[match(k, free)] + l[j] * ps
    d[length(x)] <- l[j] * l[k]; d }))
}
br_num <- function(x, p, marker)                     # production's step, dwlsmv_delta_cols
  sapply(seq_along(x), function(c) { h <- 1e-5 * max(1, abs(x[c]))
    e <- replace(numeric(length(x)), c, h)
    (br_rho(x + e, p, marker) - br_rho(x - e, p, marker)) / (2 * h) })
br_full <- function(Tn, Ds)                         # thresholds first: identity, then structural
  rbind(cbind(diag(Tn), matrix(0, Tn, ncol(Ds))), cbind(matrix(0, nrow(Ds), Tn), Ds))
br_ratio <- function(M) { s <- svd(M)$d; min(s) / max(s) }

br_one <- function(ds) {
  lam <- ds$lam; thr <- ds$thr; p <- length(lam); Tn <- sum(lengths(thr)); P <- choose(p, 2)
  Gam <- pg_point(lam, thr)$Gam; sw <- 1 / sqrt(diag(Gam))
  xm <- c(lam[-1] / lam[1], lam[1]^2)                # marker parameterization at the population
  xd <- c(lam, 1)                                    # deficient twin at an equivalent point
  Dx <- br_full(Tn, br_exact(xm, p, TRUE)); Dn <- br_full(Tn, br_num(xm, p, TRUE))
  E  <- Dn - Dx; ce <- (Tn + 1):(Tn + P)
  eta <- max(sqrt(rowSums(E[ce, , drop = FALSE]^2)) / sqrt(rowSums(Dx[ce, , drop = FALSE]^2)))
  Mn <- sw * Dn
  c(w_spread = max(sw) / min(sw),
    ratio_exact = br_ratio(sw * Dx), ratio_num = br_ratio(Mn),
    nu = svd(sw * E)$d[1] / svd(Mn)$d[1], bound = sqrt(P) * eta,
    nu_unweighted = svd(E)$d[1] / svd(Dn)$d[1],
    deficient_num = br_ratio(sw * br_full(Tn, br_num(xd, p, FALSE))))
}
br_tab <- t(sapply(br_designs, br_one))
signif(br_tab, 3)
stopifnot(br_tab[, "nu"] <= br_tab[, "bound"],          # the weight-free bound holds
          br_tab[, "nu"] < 1e-8 / 100,                  # noise two decades under the criterion
          br_tab[, "deficient_num"] < 1e-8 / 100,       # an exact deficiency reads there too
          br_tab[, "ratio_num"] > 1e-8 * 100,           # every identified design two decades over
          abs(br_tab[, "ratio_num"] / br_tab[, "ratio_exact"] - 1) < 1e-6)  # noise does not move the signal
```

### What the verification shows

Executed 2026-09-26 under R 4.6.0 and lavaan 0.7.2, with the whole file
extracted by `knitr::purl` and run in order (2.0 min); the document was not
re-rendered. **Every figure is a single run**, and none is asserted beyond
the chunk's inequalities.

| Design | Weight spread | Genuine ratio | $\nu$ | Bound $\sqrt P\eta$ | $\nu$, unweighted | Deficient twin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d | 1.7 | 0.120 | $9.4\times10^{-13}$ | $2.3\times10^{-12}$ | $9.4\times10^{-13}$ | $4.6\times10^{-17}$ |
| b1, $m = 1$ | 19.6 | 0.020 | $9.3\times10^{-13}$ | $2.3\times10^{-12}$ | $9.4\times10^{-13}$ | $3.1\times10^{-17}$ |
| b2, $m = 1$ | 1.6 | 0.119 | $9.3\times10^{-13}$ | $2.3\times10^{-12}$ | $9.4\times10^{-13}$ | $1.1\times10^{-17}$ |
| c .998 | 83 | 0.0085 | $3.5\times10^{-12}$ | $1.3\times10^{-11}$ | $5.3\times10^{-12}$ | $2.9\times10^{-15}$ |
| c .999 | 140 | 0.0051 | $4.3\times10^{-12}$ | $2.0\times10^{-11}$ | $6.3\times10^{-12}$ | $2.0\times10^{-14}$ |
| B .9975 | 42 | 0.0107 | $3.6\times10^{-12}$ | $8.3\times10^{-12}$ | $3.5\times10^{-12}$ | $4.2\times10^{-17}$ |

- **The weights do not raise the noise.** A spread of up to 140× in
  $w^{1/2}$ leaves $\nu$ within a factor 1.5 of the unweighted figure (it is
  lower on c), as the bound predicts.
- **Headroom on $M$:** noise three to four decades under $10^{-8}$, genuine
  ratios five to seven decades over it, exact deficiencies at
  $\le 2\times10^{-14}$. That is more than Module 3's stated two decades on
  the noise side, because the rounding term $\varepsilon/h$ at
  $h = 10^{-5}$ is $2\times10^{-11}$ per entry, and the per-row relative
  error is smaller still.
- **What the weights do move is the signal**, as the text said: the genuine
  ratio falls from 0.12 (d) to 0.005 (c .999), the spread between correlation
  and threshold weights. Five decades remain.
- **Not covered:** $\hat\theta$ rather than $\theta_0$ (the bound is
  pointwise, so it holds at either; the figures are at $\theta_0$), the
  structural $\beta$ column (Scope, above), and production's own bits. The
  Stata test of `breaddiag` is where production's Δ is held to the same
  inequalities.

## Theta and delta parameterizations: the conversion {#sec-theta-delta}

*Added 2026-09-28.* Drafted by a read-only agent; executed by the main session from this
file, alone and as part of the whole file run in order (lavaan 0.7.2, R 4.6.0).

Spec §7.5 (`gsem`, *Parameterization*) requires this note before any `gsem` number is
read. `gsem`'s ordinal probit, Mplus's and lavaan's theta parameterization all fix the
residual variance of each latent response, $\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_j)=1$.
dwlsmv uses delta: $\operatorname{Var}(y^*_j)=1$ (spec §4.2 compatibility matrix).

### Setup

For indicator $j$, $y^*_j = \lambda_j'\eta + \varepsilon_j$ and $y_j = k$ iff
$\tau_{j,k} < y^*_j \le \tau_{j,k+1}$. Factors follow $\eta = B\eta + \zeta$,
$\operatorname{Var}(\zeta)=\Psi$ (disturbance, `ptype 2`, spec §4.8), so
$\Phi = (I-B)^{-1}\Psi(I-B)^{-\top}$ is derived. The observed data identify only the
latent response up to a positive scale per indicator; the two parameterizations are two
choices of that scale. Write $y^{*\theta}_j = c_j\, y^{*\delta}_j$ with $c_j>0$.

**Delta to theta.** Delta has residual variance
$\theta^\delta_j = 1 - \lambda^{\delta\prime}_j \Phi^\delta \lambda^\delta_j$, so unit
residual variance requires
$$c_j = \bigl(\theta^\delta_j\bigr)^{-1/2} = \bigl(1-\lambda^{\delta\prime}_j\Phi^\delta\lambda^\delta_j\bigr)^{-1/2}.$$

**Theta to delta.** lavaan's *scaling factor* (`lavInspect(fit, "est")$delta`; not the
Jacobian of @sec-delta) is
$$\Delta_j = c_j^{-1} = \bigl(\lambda^{\theta\prime}_j\Phi^\theta\lambda^\theta_j + 1\bigr)^{-1/2}
= \operatorname{Var}\bigl(y^{*\theta}_j\bigr)^{-1/2}.$$
It is always in $(0,1]$; under delta it is identically 1.

Because the thresholds cut the same event,
$$\tau^\theta_{j,k} = c_j\,\tau^\delta_{j,k},\qquad \tau^\delta_{j,k} = \Delta_j\,\tau^\theta_{j,k}.$$
The scale is positive, so no sign changes; a negative $c_j$ would reverse the category
order and is excluded.

### Factor-level quantities depend on the metric

Rescaling $y^*$ rescales the factors only if the factor metric is tied to an indicator.
Let $D = \operatorname{diag}(d_f)$ be the factor rescaling, $\eta^\theta = D\eta^\delta$:

| Metric (same in both fits) | $d_f$ |
|---|---|
| unit variance (`unitvariance F`: $\psi_{ff}=1$, the disturbance variance) | $1$ |
| marker ($\lambda_{m(f),f}=1$) | $c_{m(f)}$, the marker indicator's scale |

Then, with $C=\operatorname{diag}(c_j)$,
$$\Lambda^\theta = C\Lambda^\delta D^{-1},\quad B^\theta = D B^\delta D^{-1},\quad
\Psi^\theta = D\Psi^\delta D,\quad \Phi^\theta = D\Phi^\delta D,$$
and inverses with $C^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(\Delta_j)$ and
$d_f = \Delta_{m(f)}^{-1}$ read from the theta side. $\Phi^\theta = D\Phi^\delta D$
follows from the other three because $(I-DBD^{-1})^{-1} = D(I-B)^{-1}D^{-1}$.

Consequences:

* **Unit variance.** $D=I$: $\Psi$, $B$ and $\Phi$ are **unchanged**; only $\lambda$
  and $\tau$ move, row by row. This holds for an **endogenous** factor too, *because*
  the unit is on $\psi_{ff}$ (disturbance), which is scale-free here: nothing in the
  factor block refers to an indicator. (Had a convention fixed total $\Phi_{ff}$ instead,
  it would also be unchanged; the two conventions give different fits, not different
  conversions.)
* **Marker.** $\psi_{ff}$ scales by $c_{m(f)}^2$, $\psi_{ff'}$ by $c_{m(f)}c_{m(f')}$,
  and $\beta_{ff'}$ by $c_{m(f)}/c_{m(f')}$ — $\beta$ is **not** invariant unless the two
  markers happen to share a scale. Non-marker loadings scale by $c_j/c_{m(f)}$.
* The conversion requires the two fits to share the **same metric choice and same
  markers**. Converting a marker theta fit to a unit-variance delta fit is two operations
  (conversion, then a factor rescaling) and must not be written as one.
* $\Delta_j$ and $c_j$ are functions of $\Phi$, so for indicators of an endogenous
  factor they depend on $B$ and on the exogenous $\Psi$, not only on the indicator's row.

The implied correlation of $y^*$ is identical under both, so the fit function,
$\chi^2$ and $T_3$ are invariant; it is a reparameterization, not a different model
(verified below: scaled $\chi^2$ agrees to $\le 1.9\times10^{-8}$).

### Verification

Two claims, tested separately. (i) The maps are exact identities: at any delta point,
delta $\to$ theta $\to$ delta returns the input, and the theta-implied $\Sigma^*$
standardised with $\Delta$ equals the delta-implied correlation. Asserted at
$10^{-12}$ (floating point; measured $\le 2.2\times10^{-16}$). (ii) Two separately
optimised lavaan fits, one per parameterization, agree after conversion. They are
separate optimisations, so they agree only to optimiser convergence. Measured once by
the drafting agent, in a scratch script not reproduced here: the
same theta fit moves by $9.0\times10^{-8}$ (E, unit variance) and
$2.2\times10^{-7}$ (E, marker) when `rel.tol` is tightened from the default to
$10^{-12}$ (nlminb then reports non-convergence: the default solution is already at the
attainable floor). The cross-parameterization gap is the same order
(max $2.6\times10^{-7}$). The tolerance $10^{-6}$ is **chosen after measuring**: about
4× the largest measured gap and 5× the measured convergence floor.

```{r theta-delta-maps}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lavaan))
root <- file.path("..", "..")
lav_version <- as.character(packageVersion("lavaan")); lav_version

rd <- function(f) { d <- read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "data", f)); d[] <- lapply(d, ordered); d }
datD <- rd("case_D.csv"); datE <- rd("case_E.csv")

fitp <- function(model, dat, par, ctrl = list(), ...)
  lavaan::sem(model, data = dat, ordered = names(dat), estimator = "WLSMV",
              parameterization = par, test = "scaled.shifted",
              zero.add = c(0.5, 0.0), zero.keep.margins = TRUE, control = ctrl, ...)

Bof  <- function(e) if (is.null(e$beta)) matrix(0, ncol(e$lambda), ncol(e$lambda)) else e$beta
PhiOf <- function(e) { IB <- solve(diag(ncol(e$lambda)) - Bof(e)); IB %*% e$psi %*% t(IB) }
marker_row <- function(L) apply(L != 0, 2, which.max)   # first indicator of each factor
row_of_tau <- function(e) match(sub("\\|.*", "", rownames(e$tau)), rownames(e$lambda))
rescale <- function(e, cj, d) {           # Lambda C . D^-1, tau C, B D.D^-1, Psi D.D
  Dd <- diag(d, length(d)); Di <- diag(1 / d, length(d))
  list(lambda = diag(cj) %*% e$lambda %*% Di, tau = cj[row_of_tau(e)] * e$tau[, 1],
       beta = Dd %*% Bof(e) %*% Di, psi = Dd %*% e$psi %*% Dd)
}

## delta -> theta; sgn and root exist only for the negative controls
to_theta <- function(e, marker, sgn = 1, root = sqrt) {
  cj <- sgn / root(1 - diag(e$lambda %*% PhiOf(e) %*% t(e$lambda)))
  d  <- if (marker) cj[marker_row(e$lambda)] else rep(1, ncol(e$lambda))
  out <- rescale(e, cj, d)
  L <- out$lambda; e2 <- list(lambda = L, beta = out$beta, psi = out$psi)
  out$scale <- 1 / sqrt(diag(L %*% PhiOf(e2) %*% t(L)) + 1)   # Delta_j, theta side
  out
}
## theta -> delta
to_delta <- function(e, marker) {
  Dj <- 1 / sqrt(diag(e$lambda %*% PhiOf(e) %*% t(e$lambda)) + diag(e$theta))
  d  <- if (marker) Dj[marker_row(e$lambda)] else rep(1, ncol(e$lambda))
  rescale(e, Dj, d)
}
gap <- function(a, e) c(lambda = max(abs(a$lambda - e$lambda)),
                        tau    = max(abs(a$tau - e$tau[, 1])),
                        beta   = max(abs(a$beta - Bof(e))),
                        psi    = max(abs(a$psi - e$psi)))
```

```{r theta-delta-verify}
M_E <- "f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3
        f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6
        f2 ~  f1"                       # case E: f2 endogenous
designs <- list(
  D_unit   = list(m = "f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", d = datD, std = TRUE),
  D_marker = list(m = "f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4", d = datD, std = FALSE),
  E_unit   = list(m = M_E, d = datE, std = TRUE),
  E_marker = list(m = M_E, d = datE, std = FALSE))

TOL_EXACT <- 1e-12
TOL_FIT   <- 1e-6   # chosen after measuring: see text
NEG_MIN   <- 1e-2   # a wrong map must miss by far more than TOL_FIT

tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(designs), function(nm) {
  z <- designs[[nm]]; mk <- !z$std
  fd <- fitp(z$m, z$d, "delta", std.lv = z$std)
  ft <- fitp(z$m, z$d, "theta", std.lv = z$std)
  stopifnot(lavInspect(fd, "converged"), lavInspect(ft, "converged"))
  ed <- lavInspect(fd, "est"); et <- lavInspect(ft, "est")

  ## (i) exact identities at the delta point
  t1 <- to_theta(ed, mk)
  et1 <- list(lambda = t1$lambda, beta = t1$beta, psi = t1$psi,
              tau = matrix(t1$tau, dimnames = list(rownames(ed$tau), NULL)),
              theta = diag(nrow(ed$lambda)))
  rownames(et1$lambda) <- rownames(ed$lambda)
  rt <- max(gap(to_delta(et1, mk), ed))
  S_d <- ed$lambda %*% PhiOf(ed) %*% t(ed$lambda)
  R_t <- cov2cor(t1$lambda %*% PhiOf(et1) %*% t(t1$lambda) + diag(nrow(S_d)))
  ir  <- max(abs((R_t - S_d)[lower.tri(S_d)]))

  ## (ii) cross-fit agreement, both directions, plus lavaan's own scaling factor
  d2t <- max(gap(t1, et)); sc <- max(abs(t1$scale - et$delta[, 1]))
  t2d <- max(gap(to_delta(et, mk), ed))
  x2  <- unname(abs(fitMeasures(fd, "chisq.scaled") - fitMeasures(ft, "chisq.scaled")))

  ## negative controls: wrong sign, missing sqrt
  ns <- max(gap(to_theta(ed, mk, sgn = -1), et))
  nq <- max(gap(to_theta(ed, mk, root = identity), et))

  stopifnot(rt < TOL_EXACT, ir < TOL_EXACT,
            d2t < TOL_FIT, sc < TOL_FIT, t2d < TOL_FIT,
            ns > NEG_MIN, nq > NEG_MIN)
  data.frame(design = nm, roundtrip = rt, impliedR = ir, d2t = d2t, scale = sc,
             t2d = t2d, chisq = x2, neg_sign = ns, neg_sqrt = nq)
}))
format(tab, digits = 3)
```

Measured by the main session from this file (lavaan 0.7.2, R 4.6.0, 2026-09-28): round
trip $\le 2.2\times10^{-16}$, implied $R$ $\le 1.7\times10^{-16}$; delta$\to$theta gap
$2.0\times10^{-8}$ (D unit; the drafting run's scratch copy had printed $9.0\times10^{-9}$),
$2.6\times10^{-8}$ (D marker), $1.5\times10^{-7}$ (E unit), $2.6\times10^{-7}$ (E
marker); theta$\to$delta $\le 1.4\times10^{-7}$; scaling factor vs lavaan's
$\le 6.3\times10^{-8}$. Negative controls miss by $1.9$–$3.0$ (sign) and $0.39$–$0.93$
(missing root). Under unit variance $\hat\beta$ is $0.529$ in both fits; under marker it
is $0.477$ (delta) vs $0.487$ (theta), and $\hat\psi_{11}$ is $0.491$ vs $0.964$ — the
marker non-invariance the algebra predicts.

### Open, not settled here

1. **`gsem`'s default factor metric.** `gsem` by default constrains the first loading
   of each latent to 1 (marker), and for an endogenous latent that makes $\psi$ a
   disturbance variance. Whether a §7.5 comparison fits dwlsmv with the same markers, or
   fits `gsem` with `var(F@1)`/`var(e.F@1)`, is a comparison-design choice the spec does
   not make. The algebra above covers both, provided both fits share it.
2. **Cutpoint sign.** `gsem`'s ordinal probit is documented as
   $P(y\le k) = \Phi(\kappa_k - x'\beta)$, which would make $\kappa = \tau^\theta$ with no
   sign flip. Not verified against `gsem` output here (agents do not run Stata); the
   negative control shows a sign slip would be caught, not which sign is right.
3. **Latent-response intercepts/means.** Everything above assumes zero factor means and
   no $y^*$ intercepts (single group). `gsem` estimates cutpoints with no ordinal
   intercept, consistent with this, but mean structures are outside §4.8's v1 grammar
   and are not covered.
4. **Standard errors.** Only point estimates are converted. SEs of converted quantities
   need the delta method through $c_j(\theta)$; lavaan's two fits' SEs will not equal a
   naive rescaling. Not derived here.
5. **Estimator.** `gsem` is ML, not WLSMV: after conversion its estimates differ from
   dwlsmv's by estimator, not by parameterization. This note removes only the
   parameterization difference; the §7.5 comparison tolerance is a separate question.

## Module 11 D7: the standardization map and its Jacobian {#sec-standardize}

*Added 2026-10-05.* Spec Module 11 *D7* orders the release work: (1) this map and its
Jacobian with executable verification, (2) a tier-2 fixture from lavaan's
`standardizedSolution()`, (3) implementation. This section is step (1).

**Notation.** @sec-gate5 already uses $G=\Gamma W\Delta$, so the standardization Jacobian is
$J_g$.

### The map

Under the delta parameterization $\operatorname{Var}(y^*_j)=1$ for every indicator (spec §4.3),
so standardizing with respect to $y^*$ (`std.all`) and with respect to the factors only
(`std.lv`) coincide: only the factor standard deviations enter. The oracle is `std.all`.
Factors follow $\eta = B\eta+\zeta$, $\operatorname{Var}(\zeta)=\Psi$ (`ptype 2`,
disturbances), and

$$\boxed{\;\Phi = (I-B)^{-1}\,\Psi\,(I-B)^{-\top}\;}\qquad A \equiv (I-B)^{-1},\quad
s_f = \sqrt{\Phi_{ff}} .$$

**$\Phi$ is derived, and `metric(unitvariance)` fixes the disturbance variance
$\psi_{ff}$, not the total variance $\Phi_{ff}$.** For an exogenous factor the two coincide;
for an endogenous one they do not. Case E, `F2 <- F1`, unit variance: $\psi_{F2F2}=1$ and
$\Phi_{F2F2} = \beta^2\psi_{F1F1}+\psi_{F2F2} = 1.280$ (@sec-theta-delta; asserted in
`fixtures/generate/20_lavaan_reference.R`). Its loadings therefore change on
standardization, by $\sqrt{1.280}$. A shortcut that rescales by $\sqrt{\psi_{ff}}$, or skips
rescaling under unit variance, is wrong for every endogenous factor; the verification
carries that shortcut as a negative control.

With $\theta = (\tau, \lambda, \beta, \psi)$ in the §4.2 order, $g(\theta)$ is

| Quantity | Standardized value |
|---|---|
| threshold $\tau_{jk}$ | $\tau_{jk}$ (unchanged; $\operatorname{sd}(y^*_j)=1$) |
| loading $\lambda_{jf}$ | $\lambda_{jf}\, s_f$ |
| path $\beta_{tf}$ ($f\to t$) | $\beta_{tf}\, s_f / s_t$ |
| disturbance (co)variance $\psi_{fg}$ | $\psi_{fg}/(s_f s_g)$ |
| factor correlation (derived) | $r_{fg} = \Phi_{fg}/(s_f s_g)$ |
| residual variance (derived) | $\Theta_{jj} = 1-(\Lambda\Phi\Lambda^\top)_{jj}$, already standardized |

The $\psi$ row follows lavaan's `std.all` convention: divide by the **total** factor
variances. Two cases of it carry the display decisions (2026-10-05):

* **Endogenous $f$, the `~~` row is $1-R^2_f$.** $\psi_{ff}/\Phi_{ff}$ is the share of
  $\Phi_{ff}$ not explained by the paths into $f$. With one predictor,
  $1-R^2_{F2} = 1-\beta_{\text{std}}^2$; asserted below.
* **Exogenous $f, g$ (the correlated case), the `~~` row is $r_{fg}$.** For exogenous
  factors $\Phi_{fg}=\psi_{fg}$, so $\psi_{fg}/(s_fs_g)=r_{fg}$ exactly; it is shown as the
  factor correlation. Where one factor of the pair is endogenous, $r_{fg}$ is not a row of
  $\theta$'s table and is not shown; the path is.

$\Theta$ and $r$ are not in $\theta$ or `e(b)` (D5); they are rows of $g$, reported from the
same machinery, nothing stored.

### The Jacobian

$J_g = \partial g/\partial\theta^\top$, one column per free parameter. For a perturbation
$(\mathrm d\Lambda, \mathrm dB, \mathrm d\Psi, \mathrm d\tau)$, using
$\mathrm dA = A\,\mathrm dB\,A$:

$$\mathrm d\Phi = A\,\mathrm dB\,\Phi + \Phi\,\mathrm dB^\top A^\top + A\,\mathrm d\Psi\,A^\top,
\qquad \mathrm ds_f = \frac{\mathrm d\Phi_{ff}}{2 s_f}.$$

Then

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm d(\lambda_{jf}s_f) &= s_f\,\mathrm d\lambda_{jf} + \lambda_{jf}\,\mathrm ds_f,\\
\mathrm d(\beta_{tf}s_f/s_t) &= \tfrac{s_f}{s_t}\mathrm d\beta_{tf}
  + \beta_{tf}\Bigl(\tfrac{\mathrm ds_f}{s_t} - \tfrac{s_f\,\mathrm ds_t}{s_t^2}\Bigr),\\
\mathrm d\bigl(\psi_{fg}/(s_fs_g)\bigr) &= \frac{\mathrm d\psi_{fg}}{s_fs_g}
  - \psi_{fg}\frac{s_g\,\mathrm ds_f + s_f\,\mathrm ds_g}{(s_fs_g)^2}
  \quad(\text{same form for } r_{fg} \text{ with } \Phi_{fg}, \mathrm d\Phi_{fg}),\\
\mathrm d\Theta_{jj} &= -2\,(\Lambda\Phi)_{j\cdot}\,\mathrm d\Lambda_{j\cdot}^\top
  - (\Lambda\,\mathrm d\Phi\,\Lambda^\top)_{jj},\\
\mathrm d\tau &= \mathrm d\tau .
\end{aligned}$$

Consequences for the implementation:

* The threshold block of $J_g$ is the identity on $\tau$ and zero elsewhere; thresholds enter
  no other row (the block structure of $\Delta$).
* A loading's column touches only its own standardized loading and its indicator's $\Theta$
  row; a $\beta$ or $\psi$ column touches every row through $\mathrm d\Phi$. For an endogenous
  $t$, $\Phi_{tt}$ depends on $\beta$ and on the exogenous $\psi$, so the $\beta$ and
  $\psi_{F1F1}$ columns are nonzero in the rows of F2's loadings.
* Fixed parameters have no column. A fixed marker loading still has a standardized value with
  a nonzero SE (through $s_f$); a fixed $\psi_{ff}=1$ of an **exogenous** factor standardizes
  to exactly 1 with SE 0.
* $\operatorname{ACOV}_{\text{std}} = J_g\,\operatorname{ACOV}(\hat\theta)\,J_g^\top$ over the
  free block of `e(V)` (D5 zero-embeds fixed rows, so the full-table form with zero columns
  for fixed parameters gives the same result).

### Verification

On Case E, delta, the fit options of `fixtures/generate/20_lavaan_reference.R`: the
structural model (`F2 <- F1`) and the equivalent correlated model (`F1 ~~ F2` free), each
under both metrics. Per fit:

1. **Point values equal lavaan's `standardizedSolution(type = "std.all")`.** Same
   $\hat\theta$, same arithmetic: $10^{-12}$, fixed before running.
2. **Analytic $J_g$ equals central differences**, $h=10^{-6}$. Budget fixed before running:
   truncation $O(h^2)\approx10^{-12}$, rounding $\approx\varepsilon/h\approx2\times10^{-10}$;
   tolerance $10^{-8}$.
3. **Delta-method SEs agree with lavaan's to lavaan's own Jacobian error.** lavaan tries a
   complex-step Jacobian of `lav_standardize_all_x`; for this model it fails and lavaan falls
   back to a **forward** difference with $h=\sqrt\varepsilon\max(1,|x|)$, error
   $O(\sqrt\varepsilon)\approx1.5\times10^{-8}$ per entry. Shown directly: lavaan's SEs equal
   $\sqrt{\operatorname{diag}(J_{\text{lav}} V J_{\text{lav}}^\top)}$, and $J_g$ and
   $J_{\text{lav}}$ differ by $O(\sqrt\varepsilon)$. The SE comparison is to lavaan's
   approximation. Tolerance $10^{-7}$ relative, **chosen after measuring** (the drafting
   run, 2026-10-04: max relative $1.7\times10^{-8}$), about $7\sqrt\varepsilon$. The analytic
   $J_g$ is the more accurate of the two (claim 2). This check uses lavaan internals
   (`lav_standardize_all_x`, `lav_func_jacobian_simple`), which may move between releases.
4. **The display rows.** Structural: the F2 `~~` row equals $1-\beta_{\text{std}}^2$ and
   $1-R^2$ computed from $\Phi$. Correlated: the F1–F2 `~~` row equals $r_{12}$. Both
   $10^{-12}$ (identities).

Across fits: **metric invariance** (marker vs unit variance on every row) and **model
equivalence** (correlated $r_{12}$ vs structural $\beta_{\text{std}}$, and every shared row).
These are separately converged fits, so they agree to optimizer convergence; tolerance
$10^{-6}$, as @sec-theta-delta's, **chosen after measuring** (scratch run of the fixture
generator draft, 2026-10-05: at most $7.0\times10^{-8}$).

Negative control, structural fits: rescaling F2's loadings by $\sqrt{\psi_{F2F2}}$ instead of
$\sqrt{\Phi_{F2F2}}$ must miss by more than $10^{-2}$.

```{r standardize-core}
## needs theta-delta-maps (lavaan, fitp, datE)
std_build <- function(x, est, fr) {     # fill free entries of the model matrices from x
  fill <- function(M, F) { i <- F != 0; M[i] <- x[F[i]]; M }
  fn <- colnames(est$lambda)
  B <- if (is.null(est$beta)) matrix(0, length(fn), length(fn), dimnames = list(fn, fn))
       else fill(est$beta, fr$beta)
  list(L = fill(est$lambda, fr$lambda), B = B, P = fill(est$psi, fr$psi),
       tau = fill(est$tau, fr$tau))
}
std_g <- function(m) {
  A <- solve(diag(nrow(m$B)) - m$B)
  Phi <- A %*% m$P %*% t(A); s <- sqrt(diag(Phi))
  list(Lstd = sweep(m$L, 2, s, `*`), Bstd = m$B * outer(1 / s, s),
       Pstd = m$P / outer(s, s), Rstd = Phi / outer(s, s),
       Th = 1 - rowSums((m$L %*% Phi) * m$L), tau = m$tau, Phi = Phi)
}
std_dg <- function(m, dm) {             # the differentials above
  A <- solve(diag(nrow(m$B)) - m$B)
  Phi <- A %*% m$P %*% t(A); s <- sqrt(diag(Phi))
  dPhi <- A %*% dm$B %*% Phi + Phi %*% t(dm$B) %*% t(A) + A %*% dm$P %*% t(A)
  ds <- diag(dPhi) / (2 * s); ss <- outer(s, s); dss <- outer(ds, s) + outer(s, ds)
  list(Lstd = sweep(dm$L, 2, s, `*`) + sweep(m$L, 2, ds, `*`),
       Bstd = dm$B * outer(1 / s, s) + m$B * (outer(1 / s, ds) - outer(ds / s^2, s)),
       Pstd = dm$P / ss - m$P * dss / ss^2, Rstd = dPhi / ss - Phi * dss / ss^2,
       Th = -2 * rowSums((m$L %*% Phi) * dm$L) - rowSums((m$L %*% dPhi) * m$L),
       tau = dm$tau)
}
std_flat <- function(gg, est) {         # keyed as lavaan labels rows: lhs op rhs
  fn <- colnames(est$lambda); yn <- rownames(est$lambda); out <- c()
  for (f in fn) for (j in yn) out[paste0(f, "=~", j)] <- gg$Lstd[j, f]
  for (t in fn) for (f in fn) out[paste0(t, "~", f)] <- gg$Bstd[t, f]
  for (a in seq_along(fn)) for (b in a:length(fn))
    out[paste0(fn[a], "~~", fn[b])] <- gg$Pstd[a, b]
  for (j in seq_along(yn)) out[paste0(yn[j], "~~", yn[j])] <- gg$Th[j]
  tn <- rownames(est$tau); for (k in seq_along(tn)) out[tn[k]] <- gg$tau[k]
  for (a in seq_along(fn)) for (b in seq_along(fn)) if (a < b)
    out[paste0("cor(", fn[a], ",", fn[b], ")")] <- gg$Rstd[a, b]
  out
}
```

```{r standardize-verify}
M_COR <- "f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3
          f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6
          f1 ~~ f2"
M_STR <- "f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3
          f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6
          f2 ~  f1"
std_fits <- list(cor_unitvar = fitp(M_COR, datE, "delta", std.lv = TRUE),
                 str_unitvar = fitp(M_STR, datE, "delta", std.lv = TRUE),
                 cor_marker  = fitp(M_COR, datE, "delta"),
                 str_marker  = fitp(M_STR, datE, "delta"))
TOL_PT <- 1e-12; TOL_J <- 1e-8
TOL_SE <- 1e-7   # relative; chosen after measuring: see text
TOL_FIT <- 1e-6  # optimizer convergence; chosen after measuring: see text
eps_rt <- sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)

std_g0 <- list()
std_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(std_fits), function(nm) {
  fit <- std_fits[[nm]]; stopifnot(lavInspect(fit, "converged"))
  est <- lavInspect(fit, "est"); fr <- lavInspect(fit, "free")
  x <- coef(fit); V <- vcov(fit); q <- length(x)
  m0 <- std_build(x, est, fr)
  stopifnot(max(abs(m0$P - t(m0$P))) == 0)
  g0 <- std_flat(std_g(m0), est); std_g0[[nm]] <<- g0
  zero <- lapply(est, function(M) M * 0)
  J <- sapply(seq_len(q), function(k) {
    e <- numeric(q); e[k] <- 1; std_flat(std_dg(m0, std_build(e, zero, fr)), est) })
  h <- 1e-6
  Jn <- sapply(seq_len(q), function(k) {
    e <- numeric(q); e[k] <- h
    (std_flat(std_g(std_build(x + e, est, fr)), est) -
     std_flat(std_g(std_build(x - e, est, fr)), est)) / (2 * h) })
  se0 <- sqrt(pmax(diag(J %*% V %*% t(J)), 0))

  ss <- standardizedSolution(fit, type = "std.all")
  ss <- ss[ss$op %in% c("=~", "~", "~~", "|"), ]
  key <- paste0(ss$lhs, ss$op, ss$rhs)
  i <- match(key, names(g0)); stopifnot(!anyNA(i))
  dpt <- max(abs(g0[i] - ss$est.std))
  free_se <- !(is.na(ss$se) | ss$se == 0)
  dse <- max(abs(se0[i] - ss$se)[free_se] / ss$se[free_se])
  dJ <- max(abs(J - Jn))

  ## lavaan's own forward-difference Jacobian (internals; diagnostic)
  fstd <- function(z, ...) lavaan:::lav_standardize_all_x(z, lavobject = fit)
  Jl <- lavaan:::lav_func_jacobian_simple(fstd, x)
  pt <- parTable(fit); il <- match(key, paste0(pt$lhs, pt$op, pt$rhs))
  dlav <- max(abs(sqrt(pmax(diag(Jl %*% V %*% t(Jl)), 0))[il] - ss$se)[free_se])
  dJl <- max(abs(J[i, ] - Jl[il, ]))

  gs <- std_g(m0)
  if (startsWith(nm, "str")) {          # endogenous F2: 1 - R^2, and the shortcut
    R2 <- m0$B[2, 1]^2 * gs$Phi[1, 1] / gs$Phi[2, 2]
    disp <- max(abs(g0["f2~~f2"] - (1 - g0["f2~f1"]^2)), abs(g0["f2~~f2"] - (1 - R2)))
    neg <- max(abs(m0$L[, 2] * sqrt(m0$P[2, 2]) - gs$Lstd[, 2]))
  } else {                              # exogenous pair: the ~~ row is r_12
    disp <- abs(g0["f1~~f2"] - g0["cor(f1,f2)"]); neg <- NA
  }
  stopifnot(dpt < TOL_PT, dJ < TOL_J, dlav < 1e-14, dJl < 10 * eps_rt,
            dse < TOL_SE, disp < TOL_PT, is.na(neg) || neg > 1e-2)
  data.frame(fit = nm, free = q, rows = length(i), point = dpt, J_cd = dJ,
             se_rel = dse, J_lav = dJl, display = disp, neg_sqrt_psi = neg,
             Phi22 = gs$Phi[2, 2], row.names = NULL)
}))
format(std_tab, digits = 3)

## across fits: metric invariance, model equivalence
inv <- sapply(c("cor", "str"), function(m) {
  u <- std_g0[[paste0(m, "_unitvar")]]; k <- std_g0[[paste0(m, "_marker")]]
  max(abs(u - k[names(u)])) })
cu <- std_g0$cor_unitvar; su <- std_g0$str_unitvar
shared <- c(grep("=~|\\|", names(cu), value = TRUE),
            paste0("y", 1:6, "~~y", 1:6), "f1~~f1")
equiv <- c(r_vs_beta = unname(abs(cu["f1~~f2"] - su["f2~f1"])),
           shared = max(abs(cu[shared] - su[shared])))
stopifnot(inv < TOL_FIT, equiv < TOL_FIT)
c(inv, equiv)
```

and run in order, 1.7 s; the document was not re-rendered). 19 free parameters and 27 rows
per fit. Points vs lavaan $\le 1.1\times10^{-16}$; $J_g$ vs central differences
$8.4\times10^{-11}$–$1.7\times10^{-10}$; SEs vs lavaan, max relative
$1.2\times10^{-8}$–$1.7\times10^{-8}$; $J_g$ vs lavaan's forward-difference Jacobian
$1.2\times10^{-8}$–$2.2\times10^{-8}$; display identities $\le 3.3\times10^{-16}$.
$\Phi_{F2F2}$ is 1.280 (structural, unit variance), 0.511 under marker, and 1 in the
correlated unit-variance fit, where F2 is exogenous. The $\sqrt\psi$ shortcut misses by
$8.3\times10^{-2}$ in both structural fits. Metric invariance $4.6\times10^{-8}$
(correlated), $7.0\times10^{-8}$ (structural); $r_{12}$ vs $\beta_{\text{std}}$

### What the fixture and Module 11 need

* The tier-2 fixture (`fixtures/generate/80_lavaan_standardized.R`) stores lavaan's point
  values and SEs for the four fits above. Stata compares points at the $10^{-12}$ class and
  SEs at the relative tier of claim 3, **not** at floating-point agreement, because lavaan's
  SE is a forward-difference approximation. $J_g$ itself is checked in Mata against central
  differences at the $10^{-8}$ tier of claim 2.
* Display (2026-10-05): the endogenous factor's `~~` row is $1-R^2$; in the correlated case
  the factor `~~` row is $r_{fg}$.

## Module 11 D7 at $G>1$: the per-group standardization map {#sec-standardize-mg}

*Drafted 2026-10-10 by cloud task Q (read-only, from `3a96fe5`; no R, no Stata), its hypotheses,
assertions and tolerances fixed in the verification table before any run. Executed 2026-10-10 by the
main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2). **Execution record.** `std-mg-g1` and `std-mg-jac` held as
preregistered. `std-mg-lavaan` halted at its first assertion (H-LV); every preregistered assertion
was then evaluated separately on the same fits (diagnostic, after the failure): of its 24 parts,
**eight failed and are kept as failures** (H-LV est, H-LV se, H-L-PT, H-P-PT on τ/ν/α/ψ jointly,
NC-1 on λ, NC-1 on Θ, H-SE, NC-2's no-ψ/β half), sixteen held; a 25th part, H-P-PT on α and ψ
alone (a split added after the run, to show which rows failed), held. The chunk now asserts that exactly this pattern reproduces; nothing
was loosened. One finding explains every failure: **lavaan 0.7.2's `std.all` is the own-scale
convention P, with ω·τ, ω·ν and a constant ω row**, not the convention L the draft read from
lavaan's `master` source. The user then froze P (O17 Q-A) and (b) for τ, ν, ω (Q-B), with the
measurements seen as prior information (decisions 2026-10-10, E-005). The chunk `std-mg-frozen` verifies
the frozen convention against lavaan; it was written after those measurements and is labelled so.
Q-C/Q-D (tie display, constant rows), Mplus STDYX at $g\ge2$, O15 and O16's display consequences
are not decided here.*

**Notation.** The group index is $g$. `@sec-standardize`'s map $g(\theta)$ and Jacobian $J_g$ are
here written $S_g(\theta)$ and $\mathcal J_g$, so that $g$ can index groups; at $G=1$ they are the
same objects (Result SG6). $\Phi_g=A_g\Psi_gA_g'$, $A_g=(I-B_g)^{-1}$, $s_{gf}=\sqrt{(\Phi_g)_{ff}}$,
$V_g=\Lambda_g\Phi_g\Lambda_g'$, $\kappa_g=A_g\alpha_g$, $\Theta^\circ_{g,jj}=\omega_{gj}^{-2}-(V_g)_{jj}$,
$\Theta^*_{g,jj}=1-\omega_{gj}^2(V_g)_{jj}$ (`@sec-mg-sigma-delta`).

### What "all" standardizes

Group $g$'s model (`@sec-mg-sigma-delta` MS1) is $y^\circ_g=\nu_g+\Lambda_g\eta_g+\varepsilon_g$ with
$\operatorname{Var}\varepsilon_g=\Theta^\circ_g$ diagonal, and the data identify only
$y^*_g=\Omega_g(y^\circ_g-\operatorname{E}y^\circ_g)$, $\Omega_g=\operatorname{diag}(\omega_g)$,
which has unit variance. The unscaled variable has

$$\operatorname{Var}(y^\circ_{gj})=(V_g)_{jj}+\Theta^\circ_{g,jj}=\omega_{gj}^{-2},\qquad
\operatorname{sd}(y^\circ_{gj})=1/\omega_{gj}.$$

**Result SG1 (the own-scale convention P).** Standardizing a coefficient of $y^\circ$ on $\eta$ by
the standard deviations of both sides gives the regression of the standardized response on the
standardized factor,

$$\lambda^\star_{gjf}=\frac{\lambda_{gjf}\,s_{gf}}{\operatorname{sd}(y^\circ_{gj})}=\omega_{gj}\lambda_{gjf}s_{gf},
\qquad
\Theta^\star_{gj}:=\frac{\Theta^\circ_{g,jj}}{\operatorname{Var}(y^\circ_{gj})}=\omega_{gj}^2\Theta^\circ_{g,jj}=\Theta^*_{g,jj}.$$

So **ω enters the standardized loading**, and the Θ row is the spec's $\Theta^*_g$. With one factor
and no cross-loading, $(\lambda^\star_{gjf})^2=\omega_{gj}^2\lambda_{gj}^2\Phi_g=\omega_{gj}^2(V_g)_{jj}$ and
so

$$(\lambda^\star_{gjf})^2+\Theta^*_{g,jj}=1\qquad(\text{identity ID-P}).$$

Group 1 has $\omega=1$, $\nu=0$, $\alpha=0$: its block is `@sec-standardize`'s map for group 1's
rows, exactly.

**Result SG2 (the frozen convention, and lavaan 0.7.2).** O17 (user, 2026-10-10) freezes P for
loadings and Θ, and for the rows SG1 does not cover: standardized $\tau_{gjk}$ is
$\omega_{gj}\tau_{gjk}$ and $\nu_{gj}$ is $\omega_{gj}\nu_{gj}$ (both divided by
$\operatorname{sd}(y^\circ_{gj})=1/\omega_{gj}$, uncentred), and the $\omega$ row is the constant 1
(ω is the standardizer; `(constrained)`). $\alpha_{gf}/s_{gf}$, $\beta$, $\psi$ and the factor
correlation are as SG1/`@sec-standardize`. Measured (`std-mg-frozen`): lavaan 0.7.2's
`standardizedSolution(type = "std.all")` is this map, row for row, in every cell of designs A–E at
the four levels, and its SEs are this map's delta-method SEs. At $G=1$ and in group 1 it is D7.

**The draft's reading L, refuted and kept.** The draft read lavaan's `master` source as follows,
and predicted lavaan = L; `std-mg-lavaan`'s record shows that prediction failing. Why the reading
was wrong is not established (`master` is not 0.7.2, and the draft did not run the code). L stays in
the chunks as the alternative that NC-5 and the failure record need. As read: `lav_standardize_lv()` multiplies each loading by
the factor's standard deviation taken from `lav_model_veta()`, which is $\Phi_g$ per block (a
variance, not a second moment, so $\alpha_g$ does not enter); `lav_standardize_all()` then divides
by $\sqrt{\mathrm{vy}}$, where `vy` is the diagonal of the *implied covariance*
(`lav_model_vy(diagonal_only = TRUE)`). Under the delta parameterization with free scaling factors
that diagonal is $\operatorname{Var}(y^*)=1$ (asserted by `mg2-lavaan`, $|\operatorname{diag}-1|<10^{-8}$). So:
loadings $\lambda_{gjf}s_{gf}$ (**no ω**); thresholds `|` and `~1` of an observed variable divided by 1
(unchanged); `~1` of a latent variable $\alpha_{gf}/s_{gf}$; `~*~` rows set to the constant 1;
`~~` on an observed variable divided by 1, i.e. lavaan's own residual variance, which the verified
$\operatorname{diag}(\text{implied})=1$ together with $\Sigma=\Delta(\Lambda\Phi\Lambda'+\Theta)\Delta$
(`lav_lisrel_sigma`) forces to be $\Theta^\circ_g$ (**not $\Theta^*_g$**). Hence lavaan's pair
satisfies $(\lambda s)^2+\Theta^\circ=\omega^{-2}$. The two conventions agree iff $\omega_{gj}=1$;
the loading gap is $|1-\omega_{gj}||\lambda s|$ and the Θ gap $|1-\omega_{gj}^2|\Theta^\circ_{g,jj}$.
Because $\operatorname{vy}=1$, `std.all` equals `std.lv` row for row under delta (`@sec-standardize`
verified this at $G=1$, SEs to $2.5\times10^{-12}$).

**The per-group map.** For group $g$, with $S_g$ the vector of output rows. The chunks were
drafted with τ, ν, ω open; their field `P` carries the stored τ, ν, ω, and the frozen rows are the
(b) alternates `tau_b`, `nu_b` and L's constant ω row (`stdmg_all_F`, `stdmg_jac_F`, defined in
`std-mg-frozen`).

| Output row | **Frozen (O17: Q-A P, Q-B (b)) = lavaan 0.7.2** | L (draft's reading, refuted) |
|---|---|---|
| loading $\lambda_{gjf}$ | $\omega_{gj}\lambda_{gjf}s_{gf}$ | $\lambda_{gjf}s_{gf}$ |
| path $\beta_{g,tf}$ | $\beta_{tf}s_{gf}/s_{gt}$ | same |
| $\psi_{g,fh}$ | $\psi_{fh}/(s_{gf}s_{gh})$ | same |
| factor correlation (derived) | $\Phi_{g,fh}/(s_{gf}s_{gh})$ | (no row) |
| $\alpha_{gf}$ | $\alpha_{gf}/s_{gf}$ | same |
| Θ row (derived) | $\Theta^*_{g,jj}=1-\omega_{gj}^2V_{g,jj}$ | $\Theta^\circ_{g,jj}=\omega_{gj}^{-2}-V_{g,jj}$ |
| $\tau_{gjk}$ | $\omega_{gj}\tau_{gjk}$ | $\tau_{gjk}$ |
| $\nu_{gj}$ | $\omega_{gj}\nu_{gj}$ | $\nu_{gj}$ |
| $\omega_{gj}$ | constant 1 | constant 1 |

Q-B's rejected options, kept so their Jacobians stay checked: τ and ν as stored, ω as stored, and
$\omega(\tau-\nu-\Lambda\kappa)$ (the model-implied standardized threshold, the threshold block of
$\sigma_g$), which missed lavaan by 0.288 (decisions 2026-10-10, E-005, Q-B measurement).

### The Jacobian

$S_g$ depends only on group $g$'s table rows. For a perturbation of group $g$'s rows
$(\mathrm d\tau,\mathrm d\Lambda,\mathrm dB,\mathrm d\Psi,\mathrm d\nu,\mathrm d\omega,\mathrm d\alpha)$,
with $\mathrm dA=A\,\mathrm dB\,A$ and `@sec-standardize`'s

$$\mathrm d\Phi=A\,\mathrm dB\,\Phi+\Phi\,\mathrm dB^\top A^\top+A\,\mathrm d\Psi\,A^\top,\quad
\mathrm ds_f=\frac{\mathrm d\Phi_{ff}}{2s_f},\quad
\mathrm dV_{jj}=2(\Lambda\Phi)_{j\cdot}\mathrm d\Lambda_{j\cdot}^\top+(\Lambda\,\mathrm d\Phi\,\Lambda^\top)_{jj},$$

**Result SG3.**

$$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm d\lambda^\star_{jf}&=s_f\big(\omega_j\,\mathrm d\lambda_{jf}+\lambda_{jf}\,\mathrm d\omega_j\big)+\omega_j\lambda_{jf}\,\mathrm ds_f
 &&(\text{L: } s_f\mathrm d\lambda_{jf}+\lambda_{jf}\mathrm ds_f),\\
\mathrm d\Theta^*_{jj}&=-2\omega_j V_{jj}\,\mathrm d\omega_j-\omega_j^2\,\mathrm dV_{jj},
 &&(\mathrm d\Theta^\circ_{jj}=-2\omega_j^{-3}\mathrm d\omega_j-\mathrm dV_{jj}),\\
\mathrm d\alpha^\star_f&=\mathrm d\alpha_f/s_f-\alpha_f\,\mathrm ds_f/s_f^2,\\
\mathrm d\tau^\star&=\mathrm d\tau,\ \mathrm d\nu^\star=\mathrm d\nu,\ \mathrm d\omega^\star=\mathrm d\omega,
\end{aligned}$$

and $\mathrm d\beta^\star$, $\mathrm d\psi^\star$, $\mathrm dr$ are `@sec-standardize`'s, unchanged. For the alternates, with $\mathrm d\kappa=A(\mathrm dB\,\kappa+\mathrm d\alpha)$,
$\mathrm d(\Lambda\kappa)=\mathrm d\Lambda\,\kappa+\Lambda\,\mathrm d\kappa$:
$\mathrm d(\omega\tau)=\tau\mathrm d\omega+\omega\mathrm d\tau$,
$\mathrm d(\omega\nu)=\nu\mathrm d\omega+\omega\mathrm d\nu$,
$\mathrm d[\omega(\tau-\nu-\Lambda\kappa)]=(\tau-\nu-\Lambda\kappa)\mathrm d\omega+\omega(\mathrm d\tau-\mathrm d\nu-\mathrm d(\Lambda\kappa))$.
At $\omega=1$, $\mathrm d\omega=0$ every line is `@sec-standardize`'s. The frozen rows (SG2) are the
P lines for λ and Θ*, $\mathrm d(\omega\tau)$ and $\mathrm d(\omega\nu)$ for τ and ν, and $0$ for the
constant ω row.

**Result SG4 (block structure and ties).** Let $v$ be the table-row values and $Z$ the 0/1
`fidx` matrix of `@sec-mg-sigma-delta` ($v=Z\theta+v_{\rm fixed}$). Then

$$\mathcal J_{\rm rows}=\frac{\partial S}{\partial v},\qquad \mathcal J=\mathcal J_{\rm rows}\,Z,$$

and **$\mathcal J_{\rm rows}$ is exactly block-structured**: the output rows of group $g$ have exact
zeros in every column of a row of another group. A tie therefore produces a shared column
(summing the members' columns, as $\Delta$ does) but no cross-group term in any one output row.
With $V_\theta$ the covariance of $\hat\theta$ (spec: `e(V)` = ACOV$/(N-G)$,
`@sec-multigroup-scaling`, which reproduces lavaan's `vcov()` at $G=2$) and $V_{\rm rows}=ZV_\theta Z'$
(lavaan's labelled-space `vcov()`: identical rows for tied copies, hypothesis H-V),

$$\operatorname{SE}(S_{g,r})=\sqrt{\big(\mathcal J V_\theta\mathcal J'\big)_{rr}}
=\sqrt{\big(\mathcal J_{\rm rows}V_{\rm rows}\mathcal J_{\rm rows}'\big)_{rr}}.$$

For a displayed (single-row) SE only the $\theta$ elements that group $g$ touches enter. The
covariance between standardized values of different groups (not displayed) is where cross-group
terms live.

**Result SG5 (what is constant).** A fixed $\psi_{ff}$ of an exogenous factor standardizes to 1,
SE 0. A *free* exogenous $\psi_{gff}$ in a group $g\ge2$ also standardizes to 1 (with $A=I$,
$\mathrm d(\psi/s^2)=\mathrm d\psi/\psi-\psi\,\mathrm d\psi/\psi^2$), so its Jacobian row is zero up to
cancellation error. Absent rows (O1) standardize to their reference value in every option.

**Result SG6 ($G=1$).** At $G=1$ the table has no ν, ω, α row, so $\omega=1$, $\nu=0$, $\alpha=0$ by the
absent-row default and $S_1$, $\mathcal J_1$ are `@sec-standardize`'s $g$ and $J_g$. The chunks
write each line in the same operation order as `std_g`/`std_dg` ($1\cdot x$ and $x+0$ are exact), so
the assertion is `identical`, not a tolerance.

**Result SG7 (reflection).** Under the reflection $\eta_f\to-\eta_f$ in the groups O16 decides,
$\lambda^\star$, $\beta^\star$, off-diagonal $\psi^\star$, $r$ and $\alpha^\star$ change sign and
$\tau^\star,\nu^\star,\omega^\star,\Theta^\ast$ and the unit factor-variance rows do not.
Standardization is equivariant, so it assumes nothing about O16; it assumes $\Phi_{g,ff}>0$ and,
for O15, accepts $\Theta^*_{g,jj}<0$ (shown as is). O12's $\hat\omega\le0$ flips $\lambda^\star$'s
sign under P and nothing under L. Under the frozen rows, ω̂ ≤ 0 also flips $\omega\tau$ and
$\omega\nu$; the ω row stays 1.

### Verification

Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2), every earlier chunk run first in
document order. The table is the draft's, frozen before any run; the **Outcome** column was added
after the run. Outcomes marked *diagnostic* come from evaluating each assertion separately after
the chunk halted at H-LV (a scratch script, discarded; recorded in decisions 2026-10-10, E-005).

Oracle: `inv_lav` (`@sec-invariance-id`), lavaan 0.7.2, delta, WLSMV, `group` = 2, `std.lv = TRUE`,
seed 20261008, designs A–E × four levels; **confirmatory set: A and E** (E has polytomous and
binary items); B, C, D are computed and printed, not asserted. `standardizedSolution(type =
"std.all")` is read as the oracle, `vcov(fit)` supplies $V$ in both our SEs and (implicitly) lavaan's, so
the divisor convention (`e(V)` = ACOV$/(N-G)$) does not enter.

| ID | Hypothesis / assertion (frozen before any run) | Tolerance and label |
|---|---|---|
| H-G1 | $G=1$: P and L map and every Jacobian entry equal `std_g`/`std_dg` | `identical`; four fits of `std_fits` |
| H-FD | analytic $\mathcal J$ = central differences, design E × 4 levels and the two-factor table `tabS` (β, α, ν, ω, ties), P and L, and the alternates | $10^{-8}$, $h=10^{-6}$; same budget as `@sec-standardize` claim 2 (truncation $\sim10^{-12}$, rounding $\sim2\times10^{-10}$; $\omega^{-3}\le2$ at the generic points), **set before the run** |
| H-BLK | $\mathcal J_{\rm rows}$ has exact zeros across groups | exact |
| H-LV | lavaan `std.all` = `std.lv`: estimates and SEs, every cell | est $10^{-12}$; SE $10^{-9}$ absolute, between $10^{-12}$ (single-group probe, `tools/probe_d7_stdall.R`) and the SE tolerance; **set before the run** |
| H-L-PT | L equals lavaan's `est.std` in every class (λ, τ, ν, α, ψ, ω, Θ°) | $10^{-12}$, as `@sec-standardize` TOL_PT |
| H-P-PT | P equals lavaan on τ, ν, α, ψ; on λ, Θ, ω it equals lavaan iff the cell has no free ω row ($<10^{-12}$) and misses by more than $10^{-3}$ when it has one | floor $10^{-3}$ set before the run from the recorded `mg2-lavaan` gaps (0.019–0.31) and the population $\omega_{2j}$ (1.043, 0.950, 0.875, 0.814, 0.762): the smallest expected loading gap is $\approx0.03$ (design D, where only item 1 has a free ω) |
| H-ID | ID-P: $(\lambda^\star)^2+\Theta^*=1$ under P at lavaan's estimates; the same pair with L's loading misses by $>10^{-3}$ when ω has a row | $10^{-12}$; floor as above |
| H-SE | SE from L's $\mathcal J_{\rm rows}$ and lavaan's $V$ equals lavaan's reported SE, per class, where lavaan's SE is finite and positive | relative $10^{-7}$, **carried from `@sec-standardize` claim 3, which was chosen after measuring at $G=1$** (max $1.7\times10^{-8}$; lavaan's forward-difference Jacobian). Not re-measured at $G=2$ before the run |
| H-V | lavaan's `vcov()` has identical rows for tied copies: $\lVert ZV_\theta Z'-V_{\rm rows}\rVert_{\max}/\lVert V_{\rm rows}\rVert_{\max}$ | $10^{-9}$, set before the run (orthonormal null-space basis rounding) |
| H-POOL | SE from $\mathcal J_{\rm rows}V_{\rm rows}$ equals SE from $(\mathcal J_{\rm rows}Z)V_\theta$ | $10^{-12}$ absolute (SEs $\lesssim0.3$) |
| H-TIE | tied λ, L convention: group values equal exactly at (A, loadings) ($\phi_2$ fixed 1, no ω); differ by more than $10^{-2}$ at (E, loadings) and (E, intercepts) and (A, intercepts) | exact; floor from $\phi_2$ population 1.44 ($s_2=1.2$; gap $\approx0.14$), set before the run |
| H-CONST | free exogenous $\psi_{gff}$, $g\ge2$: its $\mathcal J$ row is $\le10^{-14}$ in absolute value | set before the run (cancellation, $\sim10^{-16}$) |
| NC-1 | P vs lavaan λ, Θ, ω in a cell with a free ω row (part of H-P-PT) | $>10^{-3}$ |
| NC-2 | $\mathrm ds$ dropped from $\mathcal J$ (treating the factor sd as known): SE of λ rows misses lavaan's by more than $10^{-3}$ relative iff the cell has a free ψ (or β) row | floor set before the run |
| NC-3 | tie read as group 1's element only ($Z$ keeping the first member's column): SE misses by more than $10^{-3}$ relative iff the cell has a tie | floor set before the run |
| NC-4 | L's loading with P's Θ*: $\lvert(\lambda s)^2+\Theta^*-1\rvert>10^{-3}$ iff ω has a row (= H-ID's second half) | as H-ID |
| NC-5 | $\mathcal J$ under L vs central differences of P (and the reverse) misses by $>10^{3}\times10^{-8}$ iff ω has a row; $\mathrm ds$ dropped misses iff ψ/β is free | $10^{-5}$ = 1e3 × tol |

**Outcomes.**

| ID | Outcome | Note |
|---|---|---|
| H-G1 | held | |
| H-FD | held | max gap 1.95e-10 (P, L, alternates) |
| H-BLK | held | |
| H-LV | **FAILED**, kept | est to 0.307, SE to 0.18: lavaan's std.all applies ω, std.lv does not |
| H-L-PT | **FAILED**, kept (diagnostic) | L is not lavaan where ω has a row (λ to 0.31) |
| H-P-PT | τ, ν **FAILED**, kept (diagnostic); α, ψ held; λ, Θ, ω without an ω row held | lavaan's τ, ν are ω·τ, ω·ν (Q-B (b)) |
| H-ID | held | |
| H-SE | **FAILED**, kept (diagnostic) | L's Jacobian, rel. to 5.9; the frozen map's SEs match to 2.8e-8 (`std-mg-frozen`) |
| H-V, H-POOL | held | |
| H-TIE | held | |
| H-CONST | held | |
| NC-1 | λ, Θ **FAILED**, kept (diagnostic): P equals lavaan (≤ 3.3e-16) where ω has a row; ω held (stored ω vs lavaan's 1) | |
| NC-2 | free-ψ/β half held; no-ψ/β half **FAILED**, kept (diagnostic): it compares L's SEs, so it inherits H-SE's failure | |
| NC-3, NC-4, NC-5 | held | |

*What the chunks do not do:* compare any structural row with several factors at $G=2$ to lavaan
(task Q memo, 1.3); test Mata; decide Q-C or Q-D.

```{r std-mg-core}
# Depends on: mg2-core (mg2_tpos, mg2_pars). Base R otherwise. Every name is stdmg_*.
# Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2); outcomes in the verification table.
# Operation order in stdmg_g / stdmg_dg deliberately mirrors std_g / std_dg (@sec-standardize),
# so that at omega = 1, d omega = 0 the G = 1 comparison can be `identical`.

# Group g's output (Pg: list(tau, Lam, B, Psi, nu, om, al) as mg2_pars returns).
# P = own scale (omega enters the loading and Theta*), L = lavaan as read (no omega, Theta°, omega row 1).
stdmg_g <- function(Pg) {
  A <- solve(diag(nrow(Pg$B)) - Pg$B)
  Phi <- A %*% Pg$Psi %*% t(A); s <- sqrt(diag(Phi)); om <- Pg$om
  V <- rowSums((Pg$Lam %*% Phi) * Pg$Lam)                       # (Lam Phi Lam')_jj
  list(LstdP = sweep(om * Pg$Lam, 2, s, `*`), LstdL = sweep(Pg$Lam, 2, s, `*`),
       Bstd = Pg$B * outer(1 / s, s), Pstd = Pg$Psi / outer(s, s), Rstd = Phi / outer(s, s),
       ThP = 1 - om^2 * V, ThL = 1 / om^2 - V,
       tau = Pg$tau, nu = Pg$nu, omP = om, omL = rep(1, length(om)), al = Pg$al / s,
       Phi = Phi, s = s, V = V)
}
# The open alternates (memo Q-B): omega*tau, omega*nu, omega*(tau - nu - Lam kappa).
stdmg_alt <- function(Pg, Kg) {
  A <- solve(diag(nrow(Pg$B)) - Pg$B); kap <- drop(A %*% Pg$al); cc <- drop(Pg$Lam %*% kap)
  itm <- rep(seq_along(Kg), Kg - 1L)
  list(tau_b = Pg$om[itm] * Pg$tau, tau_c = Pg$om[itm] * (Pg$tau - Pg$nu[itm] - cc[itm]),
       nu_b = Pg$om * Pg$nu)
}
stdmg_zero <- function(Pg) lapply(Pg[c("tau", "Lam", "B", "Psi", "nu", "om", "al")], function(x) x * 0)
# The perturbation of one table row, in group g's matrices (Result SG3's inputs).
stdmg_dP <- function(Pg, Kg, type, i, j) {
  d <- stdmg_zero(Pg)
  switch(type,
    tau = { d$tau[mg2_tpos(Kg, i, j)] <- 1 }, lambda = { d$Lam[i, j] <- 1 }, beta = { d$B[i, j] <- 1 },
    psi = { d$Psi[i, j] <- 1; d$Psi[j, i] <- 1 }, nu = { d$nu[i] <- 1 },
    omega = { d$om[i] <- 1 }, alpha = { d$al[i] <- 1 }, stop("unknown row type"))
  d
}
# Result SG3. nods = TRUE drops d s (negative control NC-2): the factor sd treated as known.
stdmg_dg <- function(Pg, dP, nods = FALSE) {
  A <- solve(diag(nrow(Pg$B)) - Pg$B)
  Phi <- A %*% Pg$Psi %*% t(A); s <- sqrt(diag(Phi))
  dPhi <- A %*% dP$B %*% Phi + Phi %*% t(dP$B) %*% t(A) + A %*% dP$Psi %*% t(A)
  ds <- diag(dPhi) / (2 * s); ss <- outer(s, s); dss <- outer(ds, s) + outer(s, ds)
  if (nods) { ds <- 0 * ds; dss <- 0 * dss }
  om <- Pg$om; dom <- dP$om
  V <- rowSums((Pg$Lam %*% Phi) * Pg$Lam)
  dV1 <- rowSums((Pg$Lam %*% Phi) * dP$Lam); dV2 <- rowSums((Pg$Lam %*% dPhi) * Pg$Lam)
  list(LstdP = sweep(om * dP$Lam, 2, s, `*`) + sweep(om * Pg$Lam, 2, ds, `*`) +
               sweep(dom * Pg$Lam, 2, s, `*`),
       LstdL = sweep(dP$Lam, 2, s, `*`) + sweep(Pg$Lam, 2, ds, `*`),
       Bstd = dP$B * outer(1 / s, s) + Pg$B * (outer(1 / s, ds) - outer(ds / s^2, s)),
       Pstd = dP$Psi / ss - Pg$Psi * dss / ss^2, Rstd = dPhi / ss - Phi * dss / ss^2,
       ThP = -2 * om * dom * V - om^2 * (2 * dV1 + dV2),
       ThL = -2 * dom / om^3 - (2 * dV1 + dV2),
       tau = dP$tau, nu = dP$nu, omP = dom, omL = rep(0, length(om)),
       al = dP$al / s - Pg$al * ds / s^2)
}
stdmg_dalt <- function(Pg, dP, Kg) {
  A <- solve(diag(nrow(Pg$B)) - Pg$B); kap <- drop(A %*% Pg$al); cc <- drop(Pg$Lam %*% kap)
  dkap <- drop(A %*% (dP$B %*% kap + dP$al)); dcc <- drop(dP$Lam %*% kap + Pg$Lam %*% dkap)
  itm <- rep(seq_along(Kg), Kg - 1L); r <- Pg$tau - Pg$nu[itm] - cc[itm]
  list(tau_b = dP$om[itm] * Pg$tau + Pg$om[itm] * dP$tau,
       tau_c = dP$om[itm] * r + Pg$om[itm] * (dP$tau - dP$nu[itm] - dcc[itm]),
       nu_b = dP$om * Pg$nu + Pg$om * dP$nu)
}

# Keys follow lavaan's rows (lhs op rhs): f=~y1, f1~f2, f~~f, y1~~y1, y1|t1, y1~1, f~1, y1~*~y1,
# plus the derived cor(f1,f2). conv picks the P or L field (memo Q-A).
stdmg_flat <- function(o, conv = "P", Kg, fn, yn) {
  stopifnot(conv %in% c("P", "L"))
  p <- length(yn); m <- length(fn)
  itm <- rep(seq_len(p), Kg - 1L); kk <- unlist(lapply(Kg - 1L, seq_len))
  pick <- function(a, b) if (conv == "P") o[[a]] else o[[b]]
  ut <- which(upper.tri(diag(m)), arr.ind = TRUE)
  v <- c(setNames(as.numeric(pick("LstdP", "LstdL")), paste0(rep(fn, each = p), "=~", rep(yn, times = m))),
         setNames(as.numeric(o$Bstd), paste0(rep(fn, times = m), "~", rep(fn, each = m))),
         setNames(as.numeric(o$Pstd), paste0(rep(fn, times = m), "~~", rep(fn, each = m))),
         setNames(as.numeric(pick("ThP", "ThL")), paste0(yn, "~~", yn)),
         setNames(as.numeric(o$tau), paste0(yn[itm], "|t", kk)),
         setNames(as.numeric(o$nu), paste0(yn, "~1")),
         setNames(as.numeric(o$al), paste0(fn, "~1")),
         setNames(as.numeric(pick("omP", "omL")), paste0(yn, "~*~", yn)))
  if (nrow(ut) > 0L)
    v <- c(v, setNames(as.numeric(o$Rstd[ut]), paste0("cor(", fn[ut[, 1]], ",", fn[ut[, 2]], ")")))
  v
}
stdmg_flat_alt <- function(o, Kg, yn) {
  itm <- rep(seq_along(yn), Kg - 1L); kk <- unlist(lapply(Kg - 1L, seq_len)); tk <- paste0(yn[itm], "|t", kk)
  c(setNames(as.numeric(o$tau_b), paste0("tau_b:", tk)), setNames(as.numeric(o$tau_c), paste0("tau_c:", tk)),
    setNames(as.numeric(o$nu_b), paste0("nu_b:", yn)))
}
stdmg_one <- function(tab, Pg, g, conv, fn, yn, alt = FALSE) {
  v <- if (alt) stdmg_flat_alt(stdmg_alt(Pg, tab$K[[g]]), tab$K[[g]], yn)
       else stdmg_flat(stdmg_g(Pg), conv, tab$K[[g]], fn, yn)
  setNames(v, paste0(g, "/", names(v)))
}
stdmg_all <- function(tab, theta, conv = "P", fn = "f", yn = paste0("y", seq_len(tab$p)), alt = FALSE) {
  P <- mg2_pars(tab, theta)
  unlist(lapply(seq_len(tab$G), function(g) stdmg_one(tab, P[[g]], g, conv, fn, yn, alt)))
}
# d S / d (table row value): one column per free table row (the row-level object), then Z.
stdmg_jac_rows <- function(tab, theta, conv = "P", fn = "f", yn = paste0("y", seq_len(tab$p)),
                           alt = FALSE, nods = FALSE, rowidx = which(tab$rows$free)) {
  P <- mg2_pars(tab, theta)
  base <- lapply(seq_len(tab$G), function(g) stdmg_one(tab, P[[g]], g, conv, fn, yn, alt))
  ng <- lengths(base); off <- c(0, cumsum(ng))[seq_len(tab$G)]
  cols <- lapply(rowidx, function(r) {
    R <- tab$rows[r, ]; g <- R$g; Kg <- tab$K[[g]]
    d <- stdmg_dP(P[[g]], Kg, R$type, R$i, R$j)
    v <- if (alt) stdmg_flat_alt(stdmg_dalt(P[[g]], d, Kg), Kg, yn)
         else stdmg_flat(stdmg_dg(P[[g]], d, nods), conv, Kg, fn, yn)
    col <- numeric(sum(ng)); col[off[g] + seq_len(ng[g])] <- v; col })
  J <- do.call(cbind, cols); rownames(J) <- names(unlist(base)); J
}
stdmg_Z <- function(tab, rowidx = which(tab$rows$free)) {
  Z <- matrix(0, length(rowidx), tab$npar)
  Z[cbind(seq_along(rowidx), tab$rows$fidx[rowidx])] <- 1; Z
}
stdmg_se <- function(J, V) sqrt(pmax(rowSums((J %*% V) * J), 0))
```

```{r std-mg-g1}
# Depends on: std-mg-core; standardize-core (std_build, std_g, std_dg); standardize-verify (std_fits).
# Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2); outcomes in the verification table.
# H-G1 (Result SG6): at G = 1 (omega 1, nu 0, alpha 0 and their differentials 0) the map and every
# Jacobian column equal @sec-standardize's, bit for bit. identical() on as.vector (dimnames differ).
stdmg_g1 <- local({
  same <- function(a, b) identical(as.vector(a), as.vector(b))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(std_fits), function(nm) {
    fit <- std_fits[[nm]]; est <- lavInspect(fit, "est"); fr <- lavInspect(fit, "free")
    x <- coef(fit); q <- length(x); m0 <- std_build(x, est, fr); p <- nrow(m0$L); m <- ncol(m0$L)
    Pg <- list(tau = as.vector(m0$tau), Lam = m0$L, B = m0$B, Psi = m0$P,
               nu = numeric(p), om = rep(1, p), al = numeric(m))
    gs <- std_g(m0); hs <- stdmg_g(Pg)
    ok_map <- c(LstdP = same(hs$LstdP, gs$Lstd), LstdL = same(hs$LstdL, gs$Lstd),
                Bstd = same(hs$Bstd, gs$Bstd), Pstd = same(hs$Pstd, gs$Pstd), Rstd = same(hs$Rstd, gs$Rstd),
                ThP = same(hs$ThP, gs$Th), ThL = same(hs$ThL, gs$Th), tau = same(hs$tau, gs$tau))
    zero <- lapply(est, function(M) M * 0)
    ok_dg <- sapply(seq_len(q), function(k) {
      e <- numeric(q); e[k] <- 1; dm <- std_build(e, zero, fr)
      dP <- list(tau = as.vector(dm$tau), Lam = dm$L, B = dm$B, Psi = dm$P,
                 nu = numeric(p), om = numeric(p), al = numeric(m))
      a <- std_dg(m0, dm); b <- stdmg_dg(Pg, dP)
      c(LstdP = same(b$LstdP, a$Lstd), LstdL = same(b$LstdL, a$Lstd), Bstd = same(b$Bstd, a$Bstd),
        Pstd = same(b$Pstd, a$Pstd), Rstd = same(b$Rstd, a$Rstd), ThP = same(b$ThP, a$Th),
        tau = same(b$tau, a$tau)) })
    data.frame(fit = nm, free = q, map_all = all(ok_map), jac_all = all(ok_dg),
               map_fail = paste(names(ok_map)[!ok_map], collapse = ","), row.names = NULL)
  }))
})
print(stdmg_g1)
stopifnot(stdmg_g1$map_all, stdmg_g1$jac_all)
```

```{r std-mg-jac}
# Depends on: std-mg-core; mg2-core (mg2_pars); mg2-levels (mg2_level_table, mg2_point);
#   mg2-delta (tabS, thS: the two-factor, two-group table with every row type, ties across groups);
#   inv-setup (inv_designs, inv_levels, inv_jac).
# Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2); outcomes in the verification table.
# H-FD, H-BLK, NC-5. Tolerances fixed before the run: see the verification table.
STDMG_TOL_FD <- 1e-8
stdmg_cases <- c(
  lapply(inv_levels, function(l) { tb <- mg2_level_table(inv_designs$E, l)
    list(name = paste0("E/", l), tab = tb, th = mg2_point(tb), fn = "f", yn = paste0("y", 1:5)) }),
  list(list(name = "struct", tab = tabS, th = thS, fn = c("f1", "f2"), yn = paste0("y", 1:6))))

stdmg_fd <- do.call(rbind, lapply(stdmg_cases, function(cs) {
  tb <- cs$tab; Z <- stdmg_Z(tb); fr <- which(tb$rows$free)
  has_om  <- any(tb$rows$type == "omega")
  has_dsw <- any(tb$rows$free & tb$rows$type %in% c("psi", "beta"))     # a free psi/beta makes d s nonzero
  one <- function(cv) {
    Jr <- stdmg_jac_rows(tb, cs$th, cv, cs$fn, cs$yn); J <- unname(Jr %*% Z)
    Jn <- inv_jac(function(t) stdmg_all(tb, t, cv, cs$fn, cs$yn), cs$th, h = 1e-6)
    og <- as.integer(sub("/.*", "", rownames(Jr))); cg <- tb$rows$g[fr]
    list(J = J, Jn = Jn, gap = max(abs(J - Jn)), blk = all(Jr[outer(og, cg, "!=")] == 0))
  }
  P <- one("P"); L <- one("L")
  Ja <- unname(stdmg_jac_rows(tb, cs$th, "P", cs$fn, cs$yn, alt = TRUE) %*% Z)
  Jan <- inv_jac(function(t) stdmg_all(tb, t, "P", cs$fn, cs$yn, alt = TRUE), cs$th, h = 1e-6)
  nods <- unname(stdmg_jac_rows(tb, cs$th, "P", cs$fn, cs$yn, nods = TRUE) %*% Z)
  data.frame(case = cs$name, npar = tb$npar, has_om = has_om, has_dsw = has_dsw,
             gap_P = P$gap, gap_L = L$gap, gap_alt = max(abs(Ja - Jan)), blk = P$blk && L$blk,
             nc_L_vs_P = max(abs(L$J - P$Jn)), nc_nods = max(abs(nods - P$Jn)))
}))
print(stdmg_fd, digits = 3)
tolnc <- 1e3 * STDMG_TOL_FD
stopifnot(stdmg_fd$gap_P < STDMG_TOL_FD, stdmg_fd$gap_L < STDMG_TOL_FD, stdmg_fd$gap_alt < STDMG_TOL_FD,
          stdmg_fd$blk,
          stdmg_fd$nc_L_vs_P[stdmg_fd$has_om] > tolnc, stdmg_fd$nc_L_vs_P[!stdmg_fd$has_om] < STDMG_TOL_FD,
          stdmg_fd$nc_nods[stdmg_fd$has_dsw] > tolnc, stdmg_fd$nc_nods[!stdmg_fd$has_dsw] < STDMG_TOL_FD)
```

```{r std-mg-lavaan}
# Depends on: std-mg-core; mg2-core (mg2_pars); mg2-levels (mg2_level_table);
#   mg2-lavaan (mg2_from_lavaan); inv-setup (inv_designs, inv_levels);
#   inv-lavaan (inv_lav: lavaan 0.7.2 fits of designs A-E at four levels, group = 2, delta, WLSMV).
# Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2); outcomes in the verification table.
# Hypotheses, assertions and tolerances are the verification table's, fixed before the first run.
STDMG_TOL_PT <- 1e-12; STDMG_TOL_LVSE <- 1e-9; STDMG_TOL_SE <- 1e-7   # SE: carried from @sec-standardize claim 3
STDMG_TOL_V <- 1e-9; STDMG_TOL_POOL <- 1e-12; STDMG_TOL_CONST <- 1e-14
STDMG_FLOOR <- 1e-3; STDMG_TIE_FLOOR <- 1e-2; STDMG_CONF <- c("A", "E")
stdmg_cls <- c("lambda", "tau", "nu", "alpha", "psi", "omega", "theta")

# lavaan free index k -> position among the table's free rows (the keys of mg2-lavdelta)
stdmg_rowmap <- function(tab, fit) {
  pt <- parTable(fit); fr <- pt[pt$free > 0, ]; fr <- fr[order(fr$free), ]; ov <- lavNames(fit, "ov")
  key_l <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fr)), function(k) { x <- fr[k, ]; g <- as.integer(x$group)
    switch(x$op, "=~" = paste("lambda", g, match(x$rhs, ov), 1L),
           "|" = paste("tau", g, match(x$lhs, ov), as.integer(sub("t", "", x$rhs))),
           "~~" = paste("psi", g, 1L, 1L), "~*~" = paste("omega", g, match(x$lhs, ov), 1L),
           "~1" = if (x$lhs %in% ov) paste("nu", g, match(x$lhs, ov), 1L) else paste("alpha", g, 1L, 1L),
           NA_character_) }, "")
  fr_rows <- which(tab$rows$free); key_o <- with(tab$rows[fr_rows, ], paste(type, g, i, j))
  m <- match(key_l, key_o)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(m), anyDuplicated(m) == 0, length(m) == length(fr_rows)); m
}

stdmg_cell <- function(nm, l) {
  K <- inv_designs[[nm]]; r <- inv_lav[[nm]][[l]]; fit <- r$fit; tab <- mg2_level_table(K, l)
  fn <- "f"; yn <- paste0("y", seq_along(K)); p <- length(K); ov <- lavNames(fit, "ov")
  stopifnot(r$conv, identical(ov, yn))
  th <- mg2_from_lavaan(tab, fit, FALSE); fr <- which(tab$rows$free); Z <- stdmg_Z(tab)
  has_om <- any(tab$rows$type == "omega")
  has_dsw <- any(tab$rows$free & tab$rows$type %in% c("psi", "beta"))
  has_tie <- any(duplicated(tab$rows$fidx[fr]))
  # lavaan's rows
  ss <- standardizedSolution(fit, type = "std.all"); sl <- standardizedSolution(fit, type = "std.lv")
  kp <- ss$op %in% c("=~", "|", "~~", "~1", "~*~"); ss <- ss[kp, ]; sl <- sl[kp, ]
  stopifnot(all(ss$lhs == sl$lhs), all(ss$op == sl$op), all(ss$rhs == sl$rhs), all(ss$group == sl$group))
  key <- paste0(ss$group, "/", ss$lhs, ss$op, ss$rhs)
  cls <- ifelse(ss$op == "=~", "lambda", ifelse(ss$op == "|", "tau", ifelse(ss$op == "~*~", "omega",
         ifelse(ss$op == "~1", ifelse(ss$lhs %in% ov, "nu", "alpha"),
                ifelse(ss$lhs %in% ov, "theta", "psi")))))
  # ours
  sP <- stdmg_all(tab, th, "P", fn, yn); sL <- stdmg_all(tab, th, "L", fn, yn)
  i <- match(key, names(sL)); stopifnot(!anyNA(i))
  gap <- function(sv) vapply(stdmg_cls, function(k)
    if (any(cls == k)) max(abs(sv[i] - ss$est.std)[cls == k]) else NA_real_, 1)
  lv_est <- max(abs(ss$est.std - sl$est.std)); fin <- is.finite(ss$se) & is.finite(sl$se)
  lv_se <- if (any(fin)) max(abs(ss$se - sl$se)[fin]) else NA_real_
  # SEs: V in table-row space from lavaan's labelled-space vcov, and in theta space
  Vl <- unname(vcov(fit)); stopifnot(nrow(Vl) == length(fr), ncol(Vl) == length(fr))
  mp <- stdmg_rowmap(tab, fit); kl <- integer(length(mp)); kl[mp] <- seq_along(mp)
  Vr <- Vl[kl, kl]
  rep1 <- match(seq_len(tab$npar), tab$rows$fidx[fr])             # first member of each theta element
  Vt <- Vr[rep1, rep1]
  v_tie <- max(abs(Z %*% Vt %*% t(Z) - Vr)) / max(abs(Vr))
  JrL <- stdmg_jac_rows(tab, th, "L", fn, yn); JrP <- stdmg_jac_rows(tab, th, "P", fn, yn)
  seL <- stdmg_se(JrL, Vr); seP <- stdmg_se(JrP, Vr)
  pool <- max(abs(stdmg_se(JrL %*% Z, Vt) - seL))
  se_l <- ss$se; ok <- is.finite(se_l) & se_l > 0
  rel <- abs(seL[i] - se_l) / se_l
  se_rel <- vapply(stdmg_cls, function(k) if (any(ok & cls == k)) max(rel[ok & cls == k]) else NA_real_, 1)
  n_ours_only <- sum(!ok & seL[i] > 1e-10)                        # we have an SE where lavaan reports none/0
  # negative controls NC-2, NC-3
  seND <- stdmg_se(stdmg_jac_rows(tab, th, "L", fn, yn, nods = TRUE), Vr)
  Zf <- matrix(0, length(fr), tab$npar); Zf[cbind(rep1, seq_len(tab$npar))] <- 1
  seT1 <- stdmg_se(JrL %*% Zf, Vt)
  lamrow <- ok & cls == "lambda"
  nc_ds  <- max(abs(seND[i] - se_l)[lamrow] / se_l[lamrow])
  nc_tie <- max((abs(seT1[i] - se_l) / se_l)[ok])
  # H-ID and NC-4 (one factor, no cross-loading: designs A-E)
  lamk <- paste0(rep(seq_len(tab$G), each = p), "/f=~", yn); thk <- paste0(rep(seq_len(tab$G), each = p), "/", yn, "~~", yn)
  id_P  <- max(abs(sP[lamk]^2 + sP[thk] - 1))
  id_NC <- max(abs(sL[lamk]^2 + sP[thk] - 1))
  # H-TIE (L convention) and H-CONST
  tie_gap <- max(abs(sL[paste0("1/f=~", yn)] - sL[paste0("2/f=~", yn)]))
  pf <- unique(tab$rows$g[tab$rows$type == "psi" & tab$rows$free])
  const_dev <- if (length(pf)) max(abs(JrL[paste0(pf, "/f~~f"), , drop = FALSE])) else NA_real_
  row <- cbind(data.frame(design = nm, level = l, has_om = has_om, has_dsw = has_dsw, has_tie = has_tie,
                          lv_est = lv_est, lv_se = lv_se, v_tie = v_tie, pool = pool, nc_ds = nc_ds,
                          nc_tie = nc_tie, id_P = id_P, id_NC = id_NC, tie_gap = tie_gap,
                          const_dev = const_dev, n_ours_only = n_ours_only),
               as.data.frame(t(c(setNames(gap(sL), paste0("L_", stdmg_cls)), setNames(gap(sP), paste0("P_", stdmg_cls)),
                                 setNames(se_rel, paste0("se_", stdmg_cls))))))
  list(row = row, sP = sP, sL = sL, seL = seL, seP = seP, th = th)
}

stdmg_res <- lapply(names(inv_designs), function(nm) setNames(lapply(inv_levels, function(l) stdmg_cell(nm, l)), inv_levels))
names(stdmg_res) <- names(inv_designs)
stdmg_out <- do.call(rbind, unlist(lapply(stdmg_res, function(x) lapply(x, `[[`, "row")), recursive = FALSE))
rownames(stdmg_out) <- NULL
print(stdmg_out, digits = 3)

cf <- stdmg_out[stdmg_out$design %in% STDMG_CONF, ]
Lc <- grep("^L_", names(cf), value = TRUE)
seC <- grep("^se_", names(cf), value = TRUE)
# The preregistered assertions, each evaluated separately. The first run (2026-10-10) halted at H-LV; the

  `H-P-PT alpha,psi` = all(unlist(cf[paste0("P_", c("alpha", "psi"))]) < STDMG_TOL_PT, na.rm = TRUE),
```

```{r std-mg-frozen}
# Depends on: std-mg-core, std-mg-jac (stdmg_cases), std-mg-lavaan (stdmg_rowmap, stdmg_cls, STDMG_TOL_*),
#   inv-setup (inv_designs, inv_levels, inv_jac), inv-lavaan (inv_lav), mg2-lavaan (mg2_from_lavaan).
# Executed 2026-10-10 by the main session (R 4.6.0, lavaan 0.7.2). WRITTEN AFTER MEASURING: the frozen
# convention (O17 Q-A P, Q-B (b)) was chosen by the user after the Q run, the Q-B measurement and the SE
# diagnosis had shown lavaan 0.7.2's numbers (decisions 2026-10-10, E-005, prior information). This chunk is a
# verification of the frozen map, not preregistered evidence for it. Tolerances are carried, not re-chosen:
# points 1e-12 (@sec-standardize TOL_PT), SEs 1e-7 relative (@sec-standardize claim 3, chosen after
# measuring at G = 1; the SE diagnosis measured 2.8e-8 here), H-FD's 1e-8. All five designs are asserted.
# The frozen map: P's lambda, Theta*, alpha, beta, psi rows; tau -> omega*tau, nu -> omega*nu (the (b)
# alternates); the omega row is the constant 1 (Jacobian row 0).
stdmg_frz <- function(sP, sA) {
  k <- names(sP); f <- sP
  t <- grepl("\\|t[0-9]+$", k); f[t] <- sA[sub("^([0-9]+)/", "\\1/tau_b:", k[t])]
  n <- grepl("^[0-9]+/y[0-9]+~1$", k); f[n] <- sA[sub("^([0-9]+)/(y[0-9]+)~1$", "\\1/nu_b:\\2", k[n])]
  o <- grepl("~\\*~", k); f[o] <- if (is.matrix(f)) 0 else 1
  stopifnot(!anyNA(f)); f
}
stdmg_all_F <- function(tab, th, fn, yn)
  stdmg_frz(stdmg_all(tab, th, "P", fn, yn), stdmg_all(tab, th, "P", fn, yn, alt = TRUE))
stdmg_jac_F <- function(tab, th, fn, yn) {
  JP <- stdmg_jac_rows(tab, th, "P", fn, yn); JA <- stdmg_jac_rows(tab, th, "P", fn, yn, alt = TRUE)
  k <- rownames(JP); J <- JP
  t <- grepl("\\|t[0-9]+$", k); J[t, ] <- JA[sub("^([0-9]+)/", "\\1/tau_b:", k[t]), , drop = FALSE]
  n <- grepl("^[0-9]+/y[0-9]+~1$", k); J[n, ] <- JA[sub("^([0-9]+)/(y[0-9]+)~1$", "\\1/nu_b:\\2", k[n]), , drop = FALSE]
  J[grepl("~\\*~", k), ] <- 0; J
}
# (i) the frozen Jacobian against central differences (H-FD's cases and tolerance)
stdmg_fd_F <- vapply(stdmg_cases, function(cs) {
  tb <- cs$tab; J <- unname(stdmg_jac_F(tb, cs$th, cs$fn, cs$yn) %*% stdmg_Z(tb))
  max(abs(J - inv_jac(function(t) stdmg_all_F(tb, t, cs$fn, cs$yn), cs$th, h = 1e-6))) }, 0)
names(stdmg_fd_F) <- vapply(stdmg_cases, `[[`, "", "name"); print(stdmg_fd_F, digits = 3)
# (ii) points and SEs against lavaan 0.7.2 std.all, designs A-E x four levels
stdmg_frozen <- do.call(rbind, unlist(lapply(names(inv_designs), function(nm) lapply(inv_levels, function(l) {
  K <- inv_designs[[nm]]; fit <- inv_lav[[nm]][[l]]$fit; tab <- mg2_level_table(K, l)
  fn <- "f"; yn <- paste0("y", seq_along(K)); ov <- lavNames(fit, "ov")
  th <- mg2_from_lavaan(tab, fit, FALSE)
  ss <- standardizedSolution(fit, type = "std.all"); ss <- ss[ss$op %in% c("=~", "|", "~~", "~1", "~*~"), ]
  key <- paste0(ss$group, "/", ss$lhs, ss$op, ss$rhs)
  cls <- ifelse(ss$op == "=~", "lambda", ifelse(ss$op == "|", "tau", ifelse(ss$op == "~*~", "omega",
         ifelse(ss$op == "~1", ifelse(ss$lhs %in% ov, "nu", "alpha"), ifelse(ss$lhs %in% ov, "theta", "psi")))))
  sF <- stdmg_all_F(tab, th, fn, yn); i <- match(key, names(sF)); stopifnot(!anyNA(i))
  Vl <- unname(vcov(fit)); mp <- stdmg_rowmap(tab, fit); kl <- integer(length(mp)); kl[mp] <- seq_along(mp)
  seF <- stdmg_se(stdmg_jac_F(tab, th, fn, yn), Vl[kl, kl])[i]
  ok <- is.finite(ss$se) & ss$se > 0
  pt <- vapply(stdmg_cls, function(k) if (any(cls == k)) max(abs(sF[i] - ss$est.std)[cls == k]) else NA_real_, 1)
  se <- vapply(stdmg_cls, function(k) if (any(ok & cls == k)) max((abs(seF - ss$se) / ss$se)[ok & cls == k]) else NA_real_, 1)
  data.frame(design = nm, level = l, pt_max = max(pt, na.rm = TRUE), se_rel_max = max(se, na.rm = TRUE),
             se_zero_lav = sum(!ok), se_zero_ours = sum(!ok & seF > 1e-10), row.names = NULL)
})), recursive = FALSE))
print(stdmg_frozen, digits = 3)
stopifnot(stdmg_fd_F < STDMG_TOL_FD, stdmg_frozen$pt_max < STDMG_TOL_PT, stdmg_frozen$se_rel_max < STDMG_TOL_SE)
```
