```{r mr-thresholds}
# Result 5 on case E (needs mr-setup and mr-caseE: root, par_m, rec, s, w).
# Item 1 against lavaan 0.7.2 fits; items 2-3 as Gauss-Newton algebra on the
# marker model with Delta = blockdiag(I, d sigma_rho / d vartheta).
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lavaan))
dE <- read.csv(file.path(root, "fixtures", "data", "case_E.csv")); dE[] <- lapply(dE, ordered)
mE <- "f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3\n f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6\n f2 ~ f1"
th_gap <- function(est, model = mE) {
  f <- lavaan::sem(model, data = dE, ordered = names(dE), estimator = est,
                   parameterization = "delta")
  stopifnot(lavInspect(f, "converged"))
  pe <- parameterEstimates(f); pe <- pe[pe$op == "|", ]
  lab <- paste0(pe$lhs, "|", pe$rhs)
  mx(pe$est - lavInspect(f, "sampstat")$th[lab])
}
gaps <- c(DWLS = th_gap("DWLS"), ULS = th_gap("ULS"))
print(gaps)
stopifnot(all(gaps < tol_id))            # item 1; measured 0 exactly (2026-10-07)
# Negative control: one shared threshold (outside v1) leaves s_tau.
g_sh <- th_gap("DWLS", paste0(mE, "\n y1 | a*t1\n y2 | a*t1"))
cat(sprintf("shared-threshold control: max |tau-hat - s_tau| = %.3g\n", g_sh))
stopifnot(g_sh > tol_kill)               # measured 2.1e-2

# Items 2-3. s_tau: lavaan's sample thresholds; s_rho, w_rho: mr-caseE's s and w.
# The threshold weights are arbitrary positive numbers: Result 5 holds for any.
ftE <- lavaan::sem(mE, data = dE, ordered = names(dE), estimator = "DWLS")
s_tau <- unname(lavInspect(ftE, "sampstat")$th)
set.seed(20261007)
nT <- length(s_tau); w_tau <- runif(nT, .5, 2)
sig_rho <- function(v) Re(mr_sigma_theta(par_m, v, 6, 2)$s)
J_rho <- function(v, h = 1e-6) sapply(seq_along(v), function(j) {
  e <- replace(numeric(length(v)), j, h); (sig_rho(v + e) - sig_rho(v - e)) / (2 * h) })
gn_step <- function(tau, v) {
  Jr <- J_rho(v); P <- length(v); D <- length(s)
  Del <- rbind(cbind(diag(nT), matrix(0, nT, P)), cbind(matrix(0, D, nT), Jr))
  W <- c(w_tau, w); r <- c(s_tau - tau, s - sig_rho(v))
  g <- -2 * t(Del) %*% (W * r); H <- 2 * t(Del) %*% (W * Del)
  list(g = drop(g), step = drop(solve(H, -g)))
}
v0 <- rec$theta                                   # the transformed start
at_s <- gn_step(s_tau, v0)
stopifnot(all(at_s$g[1:nT] == 0),                  # item 2: exactly zero, not small
          mx(at_s$step[1:nT]) < tol_id)    # and no step moves tau (to rounding in solve)
tau0 <- rnorm(nT)                                  # anywhere
at_0 <- gn_step(tau0, v0)
stopifnot(mx(tau0 + at_0$step[1:nT] - s_tau) < tol_id,          # item 3: one step lands (1.1e-16)
          mx(at_0$step[-(1:nT)] - at_s$step[-(1:nT)]) < tol_id)  # and vartheta's step is unchanged: measured 0, 2026-10-07
cat(sprintf("one GN step from tau0: max |tau1 - s_tau| %.2g; vartheta step gap %.2g\n",
            mx(tau0 + at_0$step[1:nT] - s_tau), mx(at_0$step[-(1:nT)] - at_s$step[-(1:nT)])))
```

### What this section does not do

Open and not decided here (the development record is the place): the near-zero $c_f$ cutoff;
the **trigger** (the trap study found non-convergence on 200 of 200 trapped fits,
inadmissibility on only 153); what a failed recovery reports; the notes line and `e()`
flag; which version carries it; whether partial transformation could be useful;
production use of the stationarity check, and any tolerance for it; Stata-side tests
(Mata port: `mr_recover()` is table-in, table-out and keyed, as Module 3 owns each
$\theta$ order); and the spec patch (step 3).

## Fit indices, option A: scaled RMSEA, CFI and TLI with the c1 baseline {#sec-fit-indices}

*Added 2026-10-21, derivation first, for the scope decided 2026-10-10 (user, option A; spec Module 12
*Fit indices*).* Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` depends on this section yet. It derives the scaled
family **S** (lavaan's `*.scaled`): RMSEA, CFI and TLI computed from $T_3$ and its df; the **c1
baseline** (thresholds free in every group, every polychoric $\rho$ fixed at 0) in closed form from
Stage 1, with no additional fit; and ΔCFI/ΔRMSEA across generated invariance levels. It does
**not** derive the robust families R1 ($T_3/a$) or R2 (catML), any population-target or
finite-sample claim, any cutoff, or any Mplus-validation claim (all deferred to 0.4.0+). Every item
the derivation leaves open is listed in *Decisions this section leaves* with options and a
recommendation; none is resolved here. All new chunk names start with `fi-` and every new R name
with `fi_`; the chunks use base R only, except `fi-lavaan`, which follows `m9-lavaan`'s precedent of
calling lavaan directly on simulated data (no fixture is read or written).

### Notation

$G$ groups, $N=\sum_g N_g$, $\pi_g=N_g/N$. Per group, Stage 1 returns $s_g=(s_{\tau g}',
s_{\rho g}')'$, the $t_g$ thresholds and the $c=p(p-1)/2$ polychorics, and the empirical
$\hat\Gamma_g$; $W_g=\operatorname{diag}(\hat\Gamma_g)^{-1}$ (spec §4.9). The pooled objective is
weighting (a) of `@sec-multigroup-scaling`, $F=\sum_g\pi_gF_g$, with $T=(N-G)F$ (decided
2026-10-09), and $T_3=aT+b$, $a=\sqrt{D/\operatorname{Tr}(M^2)}$,
$b=D-\sqrt{D\operatorname{Tr}(M)^2/\operatorname{Tr}(M^2)}$, $M=U\hat\Omega$ (`@sec-gate5`,
Result MG4). $G=1$ is the special case $T=(N-1)F$. For a model $L$: $T_{3L}$, $D_L$; for the
baseline: $T_{3B}$, $D_B$. The *excess* of a model is $E_L=T_{3L}-D_L$.

### Result FI1: the scaled family

Exactly lavaan 0.7.2's `lav_fit_rmsea()`, `lav_fit_cfi()` and `lav_fit_tli()` with the scaled
statistic passed as `x2` and $\hat c=1$ (read from the 0.7.2 source; checked against `fitMeasures()`
in `fi-lavaan`):

$$
\mathrm{RMSEA}_S=\sqrt{\frac{\max(T_{3L}-D_L,\,0)}{n\,D_L}}\;\kappa_G,\qquad
\mathrm{CFI}_S=1-\frac{\max(E_L,0)}{\max(E_L,\,E_B,\,0)},\qquad
\mathrm{TLI}_S=1-\frac{E_L\,D_B}{E_B\,D_L}=\frac{T_{3B}/D_B-T_{3L}/D_L}{T_{3B}/D_B-1},
$$

with $n$ the sample-size divisor and $\kappa_G$ the multiple-group factor. **$n=N-G$** is not a new
choice: it is the divisor of the decided $T=(N-G)F$, so that $(T-D)/n$ estimates $F$ on the same
scale as $T$, and it is what lavaan's `rmsea.scaled` uses (`lav_inspect_ntotal`, measured in
`fi-lavaan`). **$\kappa_G$ is open** (item F1 below): lavaan uses $\sqrt G$. TLI is not clipped
in lavaan (item F2), and the $D_L=0$ and non-positive-excess cases are conventions (items F3, F4).

Since $T_3$ matches the first two moments of $\chi^2_{D}$ (`@sec-gate5`), $E_L$ is the
moment-matched excess over a central chi-square, which is all family S uses. Its population
limit is $(T_3-D)/n\to aF_0$, not $F_0$, which is why S's *target* is not claimed here (deferred
with R1, which divides by $a$).

### Result FI2: the c1 baseline in closed form

The c1 baseline frees every threshold in every group and fixes every $\rho$ at 0, so
$\sigma_g(\theta_B)=(\theta_{\tau g}',0')'$ and $\Delta_B=\operatorname{blockdiag}_g
\begin{pmatrix}I_{t_g}\\0\end{pmatrix}$: the threshold block is the identity (spec: Δ is block
diagonal, threshold block identity), and the correlation block has no free column. Because $W$ is
diagonal, the objective separates:

$$
F(\theta_B)=\sum_g\pi_g\Big[(s_{\tau g}-\theta_{\tau g})'W_{\tau g}(s_{\tau g}-\theta_{\tau g})
+s_{\rho g}'W_{\rho g}s_{\rho g}\Big],
$$

minimised at $\hat\theta_{\tau g}=s_{\tau g}$ exactly, so

$$
\boxed{T_B=(N-G)\sum_g\pi_g\sum_{k=1}^{c}\frac{\hat\rho_{gk}^2}{\hat\Gamma_{g,\rho_k\rho_k}},\qquad
D_B=G\,c=G\,\frac{p(p-1)}{2}.}
$$

**The traces.** With $W=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\pi_gW_g)$ diagonal and $\Delta_B$ selecting the
threshold coordinates, $U_B=W-W\Delta_B(\Delta_B'W\Delta_B)^{-1}\Delta_B'W$ is $W$ with the
threshold rows and columns zeroed. Then $M_B=U_B\hat\Omega$ has nonzero blocks only on the
correlation coordinates, and there $\pi_gW_{\rho g}\cdot\hat\Gamma_{\rho\rho,g}/\pi_g=
W_{\rho g}\hat\Gamma_{\rho\rho,g}=:Q_g$. With $S_g$ the diagonal of standard deviations of
$\hat\Gamma_{\rho\rho,g}$ and $R_g$ its correlation matrix, $Q_g=S_g^{-2}S_gR_gS_g=S_g^{-1}R_gS_g$, so
$Q_g$ is similar to $R_g$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(Q_g)=c$, $\operatorname{Tr}(Q_g^2)=\lVert R_g\rVert_F^2$.
Hence

$$
\boxed{\operatorname{Tr}(M_B)=D_B,\qquad \operatorname{Tr}(M_B^2)=\sum_g\lVert R_g\rVert_F^2,}\qquad
a_B=\sqrt{\frac{D_B}{\sum_g\lVert R_g\rVert_F^2}},\quad b_B=D_B\,(1-a_B).
$$

Both traces are free of $\pi_g$ and of the threshold block; $\operatorname{Tr}(M_B)=D_B$ holds
identically, so $T_{3B}=a_BT_B+D_B(1-a_B)$, i.e. $E_B=a_B(T_B-D_B)$. When every $R_g=I$ (no
correlation among the polychoric estimates), $a_B=1$, $b_B=0$ and $T_{3B}=T_B$. Everything above is
Stage 1 output ($\hat\rho$, $\hat\Gamma_{\rho\rho,g}$, $N_g$): **no baseline fit is run.**

**Why one baseline serves every generated level.** $T_{3B}$ and $D_B$ are functions of the Stage 1
output only, and spec Module 12 already requires every generated level (configural, thresholds,
metric, scalar, …) to share one Stage 1 (DIFFTEST's validation contract: same data, same sample).
Nothing in the c1 model depends on which equality constraints a level imposes, so the baseline is
the same pair $(T_{3B},D_B)$ for every level of a chain, and ΔCFI compares the levels against one
denominator. **What this does not give (finding, not a decision):** c1 is nested in the
configural model (fix every $\rho$ at zero by setting loadings and factor covariances to zero) but
**not** in a level that constrains thresholds across groups: c1 keeps every group's thresholds free,
so with $K\ge4$ categories (where Result I2's equivalence does not hold) it fits the threshold
block exactly while that level does not. The baseline is therefore a common reference point, not a
model nested in every level, and $E_L>E_B$ is not ruled out algebraically (CFI then sits at 0 by the
$\max$). lavaan's default categorical baseline (thresholds free per group) has the same property,
which is why c1 reproduces lavaan in `fi-lavaan`. This is recorded for the help text; it is not a
reason to reopen the decided c1.

### Result FI3: Δ across generated levels

For consecutive levels $L-1\to L$ in one chain, $\Delta\mathrm{CFI}=\mathrm{CFI}_L-\mathrm{CFI}_{L-1}$
and $\Delta\mathrm{RMSEA}=\mathrm{RMSEA}_L-\mathrm{RMSEA}_{L-1}$. Whenever
$E_B\ge\max(E_{L-1},E_L,0)$ (the usual case; then both denominators are $E_B$),

$$
\Delta\mathrm{CFI}=\frac{\max(E_{L-1},0)-\max(E_L,0)}{E_B}.
$$

ΔCFI is a difference of $T_3$ excesses on one scale, **not a test**: each level's $T_3$ carries its
own $a_L,b_L$, so $T_{3L}-T_{3,L-1}$ is not the DIFFTEST statistic (`@sec-difftest`), and $T_3$ need
not rise along a chain. ΔCFI can therefore be **positive** (demonstrated in `fi-delta`). ΔRMSEA
changes both through $E$ and through $D_L$ in the denominator. A level skipped because $d=0$ (spec
check 8, *Zero-df generated pairs*) has, by that rule, the previous level's $T_3$ and df, so its Δ
values would be 0 by construction; how the table shows it is open (item F6).

### Verification

```{r fi-setup}
#| cache: true
# Family S (Result FI1), written from the formulas, not copied from lavaan. kappa: TRUE = sqrt(G).
fi_rmsea <- function(T3, D, n, G = 1, kappa = TRUE)
  if (D > 0) sqrt(max(T3 - D, 0) / (n * D)) * (if (kappa) sqrt(G) else 1) else 0
fi_cfi <- function(T3, D, T3b, Db) {
  t1 <- max(T3 - D, 0); t2 <- max(T3 - D, T3b - Db, 0)
  if (isTRUE(all.equal(t1, 0)) && isTRUE(all.equal(t2, 0))) 1 else 1 - t1 / t2
}
fi_tli <- function(T3, D, T3b, Db) {               # lavaan's convention: unclipped, 1 when D = 0
  t1 <- (T3 - D) * Db; t2 <- (T3b - Db) * D
  if (D > 0 && abs(t2) > 0) 1 - t1 / t2 else 1
}
fi_ab <- function(D, tr1, tr2) c(a = sqrt(D / tr2), b = D - sqrt(D * tr1^2 / tr2))
# Result FI2: c1 baseline from Stage 1 output only. srho, Grr: per-group lists of the polychorics
# and their Gamma block; Ng: group sizes; Tdiv: the T convention (N - G by default).
fi_baseline <- function(srho, Grr, Ng, Tdiv = sum(Ng) - length(Ng)) {
  pig <- Ng / sum(Ng)
  F   <- sum(pig * mapply(function(s, Gm) sum(s^2 / diag(Gm)), srho, Grr))
  Db  <- sum(lengths(srho))
  tr2 <- sum(sapply(Grr, function(Gm) sum(cov2cor(Gm)^2)))
  ab  <- fi_ab(Db, Db, tr2)
  TB  <- Tdiv * F
  c(TB = TB, Db = Db, tr1 = Db, tr2 = tr2, ab, T3B = unname(ab["a"] * TB + ab["b"]))
}
fi_rpd <- function(m) { A <- matrix(rnorm(m^2), m); crossprod(A) / m + diag(m) * 0.3 }
```

**c1 closed form against the generic construction.** Two groups, $p=4$ items with three categories
($t_g=8$, $c=6$), random positive definite $\hat\Gamma_g$ with correlated polychorics. The generic
side minimises the pooled objective numerically and builds $U$, $\hat\Omega$ and $M$ from the
stacked matrices, as Module 9 does for any model; the closed form never sees $\Delta_B$.

```{r fi-c1}
#| cache: true
set.seed(20261021)
fi_G <- 2; fi_t <- 8; fi_c <- 6; fi_m <- fi_t + fi_c; fi_Ng <- c(350, 650); fi_N <- sum(fi_Ng)
fi_pi <- fi_Ng / fi_N
fi_s  <- lapply(1:fi_G, function(g) c(sort(rnorm(fi_t)), runif(fi_c, -0.6, 0.6)))
fi_Gm <- lapply(1:fi_G, function(g) fi_rpd(fi_m))
fi_idx_r <- (fi_t + 1):fi_m
cf <- fi_baseline(lapply(fi_s, `[`, fi_idx_r), lapply(fi_Gm, function(G) G[fi_idx_r, fi_idx_r]), fi_Ng)

# generic: stacked objective, numerical minimisation over the 16 thresholds
fi_W  <- lapply(fi_Gm, function(G) diag(1 / diag(G)))
fi_obj <- function(th) sum(sapply(1:fi_G, function(g) {
  r <- fi_s[[g]] - c(th[(g - 1) * fi_t + 1:fi_t], rep(0, fi_c)); fi_pi[g] * sum(r^2 * diag(fi_W[[g]])) }))
st  <- unlist(lapply(fi_s, `[`, 1:fi_t))
opt <- optim(st + rnorm(length(st), 0, 0.3), fi_obj, method = "BFGS",
             control = list(reltol = 1e-15, maxit = 1000))
bd  <- function(L) { out <- matrix(0, sum(sapply(L, nrow)), sum(sapply(L, ncol))); r <- 0; k <- 0
  for (B in L) { out[r + seq_len(nrow(B)), k + seq_len(ncol(B))] <- B; r <- r + nrow(B); k <- k + ncol(B) }; out }
Wst <- bd(lapply(1:fi_G, function(g) fi_pi[g] * fi_W[[g]]))
Om  <- bd(lapply(1:fi_G, function(g) fi_Gm[[g]] / fi_pi[g]))
DlB <- bd(lapply(1:fi_G, function(g) rbind(diag(fi_t), matrix(0, fi_c, fi_t))))
U   <- Wst - Wst %*% DlB %*% solve(t(DlB) %*% Wst %*% DlB) %*% t(DlB) %*% Wst
M   <- U %*% Om
gen <- c(TB = (fi_N - fi_G) * opt$value, tr1 = sum(diag(M)), tr2 = sum(diag(M %*% M)))
# pi-invariance of the traces: same Gamma_g, different group sizes
cf2 <- fi_baseline(lapply(fi_s, `[`, fi_idx_r), lapply(fi_Gm, function(G) G[fi_idx_r, fi_idx_r]), c(900, 100))
# R_g = I: the scaled baseline collapses to T_B
cfI <- fi_baseline(lapply(fi_s, `[`, fi_idx_r), lapply(1:fi_G, function(g) diag(diag(fi_Gm[[g]])[fi_idx_r])), fi_Ng)
fi_c1 <- data.frame(
  check = c("optimum thresholds = s_tau (max abs)", "T_B closed vs numerical min (rel)",
            "Tr(M_B) closed vs generic", "Tr(M_B) = D_B exactly", "Tr(M_B^2) closed vs generic (rel)",
            "traces free of pi (tr2 at N_g = 900/100)", "R_g = I: a_B - 1", "R_g = I: T3B - TB"),
  value = c(max(abs(opt$par - st)), abs(cf["TB"] - gen["TB"]) / gen["TB"],
            abs(cf["tr1"] - gen["tr1"]), unname(cf["tr1"] == cf["Db"]),
            abs(cf["tr2"] - gen["tr2"]) / gen["tr2"], abs(cf2["tr2"] - cf["tr2"]),
            unname(cfI["a"] - 1), unname(cfI["T3B"] - cfI["TB"])))
fi_c1
stopifnot(max(abs(opt$par - st)) < 1e-6, abs(cf["TB"] - gen["TB"]) / gen["TB"] < 1e-10,
          abs(cf["tr1"] - gen["tr1"]) < 1e-10, abs(cf["tr2"] - gen["tr2"]) / gen["tr2"] < 1e-12,
          cf["Db"] == fi_G * fi_c, abs(cf2["tr2"] - cf["tr2"]) < 1e-12,
          abs(cfI["a"] - 1) < 1e-15, abs(cfI["T3B"] - cfI["TB"]) < 1e-9)
```

**The $\sqrt G$ factor (item F1's evidence).** If every group has the same population RMSEA
$\varepsilon$ and its own df $D_g$ with $F_{0g}=D_g\varepsilon^2$, the pooled discrepancy is
$F_0=\sum_g\pi_gD_g\varepsilon^2$. With no cross-group ties ($D=\sum_gD_g$), $\sqrt{F_0/D}\,\sqrt G=\varepsilon$ exactly when
$\sum_g\pi_gD_g=D/G$, i.e. when the $D_g$ are equal (any $\pi_g$) or the groups are equal in size
(any $D_g$): $\sqrt G$ then makes the pooled index the common per-group value (Steiger, 1998).
Unequal $D_g$ together with unequal sizes, or ties ($D<\sum_g D_g$, every level
past configural) break the identity, and then neither $\kappa_G$ recovers $\varepsilon$.

```{r fi-sqrtG}
#| cache: true
fi_eps <- 0.05
fi_pool <- function(pig, Dg, D = sum(Dg)) { F0 <- sum(pig * Dg * fi_eps^2)
  c(kappa_sqrtG = sqrt(F0 / D) * sqrt(length(Dg)), kappa_1 = sqrt(F0 / D)) }
fi_sq <- rbind(
  "equal D_g, pi = (.5,.5)"         = fi_pool(c(.5, .5), c(20, 20)),
  "equal D_g, pi = (.1,.9)"         = fi_pool(c(.1, .9), c(20, 20)),
  "equal D_g, G = 4, unequal pi"    = fi_pool(c(.1, .2, .3, .4), rep(20, 4)),
  "unequal D_g (10, 30), pi = .5"   = fi_pool(c(.5, .5), c(10, 30)),
  "unequal D_g (10, 30), pi = (.2,.8)" = fi_pool(c(.2, .8), c(10, 30)),
  "ties: D = 34 < 40"               = fi_pool(c(.5, .5), c(20, 20), D = 34))
fi_sq
stopifnot(all(abs(fi_sq[1:4, "kappa_sqrtG"] - fi_eps) < 1e-15),
          all(abs(fi_sq[5:6,"kappa_sqrtG"] - fi_eps) > 1e-4))
```

**Edge cases under lavaan's conventions (items F2–F4).** These rows show what the formulas
give, not a decision: each is one of the conventions to be decided.

```{r fi-conventions}
#| cache: true
fi_case <- function(lbl, T3, D, T3b = 400, Db = 30, n = 998, G = 2)
  data.frame(case = lbl, T3 = T3, D = D, T3b = T3b, Db = Db,
             RMSEA = fi_rmsea(T3, D, n, G), CFI = fi_cfi(T3, D, T3b, Db), TLI = fi_tli(T3, D, T3b, Db))
fi_conv <- rbind(
  fi_case("ordinary", 60, 20),
  fi_case("negative excess T3 < D", 15, 20),
  fi_case("T3 = D exactly", 20, 20),
  fi_case("D = 0 (T3 undefined; 0 passed)", 0, 0),
  fi_case("baseline excess <= 0", 15, 20, T3b = 25),
  fi_case("model excess > baseline excess", 500, 20))
fi_conv
stopifnot(fi_conv$TLI[2] > 1,                  # lavaan's TLI is unclipped (F2)
          fi_conv$RMSEA[2] == 0, fi_conv$CFI[2] == 1,
          fi_conv$RMSEA[4] == 0, fi_conv$CFI[4] == 1, fi_conv$TLI[4] == 1,  # D = 0 (F3)
          fi_conv$CFI[6] == 0, fi_conv$TLI[6] < 0)
```

**The frozen conventions, F3 and F4 as amended (added 2026-10-21, after the freeze).** `fi_dw()` is
dwlsmv's production rule (the reference for the Mata routine `dwlsmv_fitidx`). The four sign
combinations of $(E_L,E_B)$ are each checked, and a mutant that merges the two conditions (lavaan's
form, in which $E_L\le0$ and $E_B\le0$ together give CFI $=1$) must disagree on the case where both
are non-positive, while RMSEA must not move with the baseline in any case.

```{r fi-frozen}
#| cache: true
fi_dw <- function(T3, D, n, G, T3b, Db) {
  out <- c(rmsea = NA_real_, cfi = NA_real_, tli = NA_real_)
  if (is.na(T3) || is.na(D) || D <= 0) return(out)                    # F3
  EL <- T3 - D
  out["rmsea"] <- sqrt(max(EL, 0) / (n * D)) * sqrt(G)                # model side only
  if (is.na(T3b) || is.na(Db) || Db <= 0) return(out)
  EB <- T3b - Db
  if (EB <= 0) return(out)                                            # baseline side only
  out["cfi"] <- 1 - max(EL, 0) / max(EL, EB)
  out["tli"] <- 1 - EL * Db / (EB * D)                                # raw E_L: unclipped (F2)
  out
}
fi_merged <- function(T3, D, n, G, T3b, Db)                           # mutant: lavaan's merged form
  c(rmsea = fi_rmsea(T3, D, n, G), cfi = fi_cfi(T3, D, T3b, Db), tli = fi_tli(T3, D, T3b, Db))
fi_four <- expand.grid(EL = c(15, -4), EB = c(300, -2))
fi_four$label <- sprintf("E_L %s 0, E_B %s 0", ifelse(fi_four$EL > 0, ">", "<="), ifelse(fi_four$EB > 0, ">", "<="))
fi_fz <- t(mapply(function(EL, EB) {
  D <- 20; Db <- 30; n <- 998; G <- 2
  d <- fi_dw(D + EL, D, n, G, Db + EB, Db); m <- fi_merged(D + EL, D, n, G, Db + EB, Db)
  r0 <- fi_dw(D + EL, D, n, G, NA, NA)["rmsea"]                       # no baseline at all
  c(d, merged_cfi = unname(m["cfi"]), rmsea_without_baseline = unname(r0))
}, fi_four$EL, fi_four$EB))
fi_fz <- data.frame(case = fi_four$label, fi_fz)
fi_fz
stopifnot(
  all(fi_fz$rmsea == fi_fz$rmsea_without_baseline),                   # baseline never moves RMSEA
  fi_fz$rmsea[1] > 0, fi_fz$rmsea[3] > 0, fi_fz$rmsea[2] == 0, fi_fz$rmsea[4] == 0,
  !is.na(fi_fz$cfi[1:2]), is.na(fi_fz$cfi[3:4]), is.na(fi_fz$tli[3:4]),  # E_B alone decides definedness
  fi_fz$cfi[2] == 1, fi_fz$tli[2] > 1,                                # model clamp; TLI unclipped
  fi_fz$merged_cfi[4] == 1, is.na(fi_fz$cfi[4]),                      # the merged mutant differs here
  all(is.na(fi_dw(0, 0, 998, 2, 330, 30))))                           # F3
```

**ΔCFI is not monotone (Result FI3).** A three-level chain with one baseline: the second level adds
restrictions ($D$ rises) but its $T_3$ falls, as it can because each level has its own $a,b$.

```{r fi-delta}
#| cache: true
fi_chain <- data.frame(level = c("configural", "thresholds", "metric"),
                       T3 = c(80, 78, 95), D = c(40, 46, 52))
fi_T3B <- 900; fi_DB <- 30
fi_chain$CFI   <- mapply(fi_cfi, fi_chain$T3, fi_chain$D, fi_T3B, fi_DB)
fi_chain$RMSEA <- mapply(fi_rmsea, fi_chain$T3, fi_chain$D, MoreArgs = list(n = 998, G = 2))
fi_chain$dCFI   <- c(NA, diff(fi_chain$CFI))
fi_chain$dRMSEA <- c(NA, diff(fi_chain$RMSEA))
E <- pmax(fi_chain$T3 - fi_chain$D, 0); EB <- fi_T3B - fi_DB
fi_chain
stopifnot(fi_chain$dCFI[2] > 0,
          max(abs(fi_chain$dCFI[-1] - (E[-3] - E[-1]) / EB)) < 1e-15)
```

**Against lavaan 0.7.2.** Simulated two-factor data (six items, four categories), single group and
two groups, configural, `estimator = "WLSMV"`, delta parameterization. From lavaan's own Stage 1
objects (`wls.obs`, `gamma`, `wls.v`), and **lavaan's** $T$ convention $\sum_g(N_g-1)F_g$ (not
ours; see `@sec-multigroup-scaling`), the c1 closed form must reproduce `baseline.chisq`,
`baseline.chisq.scaled` and `baseline.df`; and FI1 fed lavaan's `chisq.scaled`, `df` and baseline
must reproduce `rmsea.scaled` (with $n$ = `ntotal` − $G$ and $\kappa_G=\sqrt G$), `cfi.scaled` and
`tli.scaled`. Hypotheses and tolerances (1e-8 relative for the baseline, which is closed form against
lavaan's fitted baseline; 1e-12 for the indices, the same arithmetic) were written before the chunk
first ran. **Added after measuring:** that first run used only the well-fitting two-factor model,
whose $T_3<D$ left every RMSEA at 0, so it could not discriminate $n$ or $\kappa_G$; the misspecified
one-factor fits and the `fi_alt` comparison were added afterwards for that reason, with the
alternatives required to *miss* lavaan ($n=N$ by more than 1e-6; no $\kappa_G$ at $G=2$ by more than
1e-3). Result (2026-10-21, R 4.5.2, lavaan 0.7.2): every row agrees to $\le 2\times10^{-16}$
relative, including the $G=2$ baseline, which confirms that lavaan's scaled baseline traces are, like
FI2's, free of the group weights.

```{r fi-lavaan}
#| cache: true
library(lavaan)
set.seed(17)
fi_sim <- function(n, shift = 0) {
  f  <- MASS::mvrnorm(n, c(0, 0), matrix(c(1, .4, .4, 1), 2))
  ys <- cbind(f[, 1] %o% c(.8, .7, .6) , f[, 2] %o% c(.7, .6, .5))
  ys <- ys + matrix(rnorm(n * 6), n) %*% diag(sqrt(1 - c(.8, .7, .6, .7, .6, .5)^2))
  d  <- as.data.frame(apply(ys + shift, 2, cut, breaks = c(-Inf, -.8, 0, .7, Inf), labels = FALSE))
  names(d) <- paste0("y", 1:6); d }
fi_dat <- rbind(cbind(fi_sim(400), g = 1), cbind(fi_sim(600, .2), g = 2))
fi_mod <- "f1 =~ y1 + y2 + y3\n f2 =~ y4 + y5 + y6"
fi_fm  <- c("chisq.scaled", "df", "baseline.chisq", "baseline.chisq.scaled", "baseline.df",
            "rmsea.scaled", "cfi.scaled", "tli.scaled", "ntotal")
fi_one <- function(fit, G) {
  fm  <- fitMeasures(fit, fi_fm)
  as1 <- function(x) if (G == 1) list(x) else x
  obs <- as1(lavInspect(fit, "wls.obs")); gam <- as1(lavInspect(fit, "gamma"))
  wv  <- as1(lavInspect(fit, "wls.v"));   Ng  <- lavInspect(fit, "nobs")
  cc  <- 15; tail_idx <- function(k) (k - cc + 1):k
  srho <- lapply(obs, function(o) o[tail_idx(length(o))])
  Grr  <- lapply(gam, function(Gm) { k <- nrow(Gm); Gm[tail_idx(k), tail_idx(k)] })
  wchk <- max(mapply(function(w, Gm) max(abs(diag(w) * diag(Gm) - 1)), wv, gam))
  # lavaan's T: sum_g (N_g - 1) F_g, i.e. pooled weights (N_g - 1)
  bl  <- fi_baseline(srho, Grr, Ng - 1, Tdiv = sum(Ng - 1))
  n   <- unname(fm["ntotal"]) - G
  ours <- c(baseline.chisq = bl[["TB"]], baseline.chisq.scaled = bl[["T3B"]], baseline.df = bl[["Db"]],
            rmsea.scaled = fi_rmsea(fm[["chisq.scaled"]], fm[["df"]], n, G),
            cfi.scaled   = fi_cfi(fm[["chisq.scaled"]], fm[["df"]], fm[["baseline.chisq.scaled"]], fm[["baseline.df"]]),
            tli.scaled   = fi_tli(fm[["chisq.scaled"]], fm[["df"]], fm[["baseline.chisq.scaled"]], fm[["baseline.df"]]))
  data.frame(G = G, quantity = names(ours), ours = unname(ours), lavaan = unname(fm[names(ours)]),
             rel = abs(unname(ours) - unname(fm[names(ours)])) / pmax(1, abs(unname(fm[names(ours)]))),
             wv_is_inv_diag_gamma = wchk)
}
fi_fit1 <- sem(fi_mod, data = fi_dat[fi_dat$g == 1, 1:6], ordered = paste0("y", 1:6),
               estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta")
fi_fit2 <- sem(fi_mod, data = fi_dat, group = "g", ordered = paste0("y", 1:6),
               estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta")
fi_mod1 <- "f =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6"   # misspecified: added after the first run (below)
fi_fit1m <- sem(fi_mod1, data = fi_dat[fi_dat$g == 1, 1:6], ordered = paste0("y", 1:6),
                estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta")
fi_fit2m <- sem(fi_mod1, data = fi_dat, group = "g", ordered = paste0("y", 1:6),
                estimator = "WLSMV", parameterization = "delta")
fi_lav <- rbind(cbind(model = "2-factor", rbind(fi_one(fi_fit1, 1), fi_one(fi_fit2, 2))),
                cbind(model = "1-factor", rbind(fi_one(fi_fit1m, 1), fi_one(fi_fit2m, 2))))
fi_lav
# divisor and kappa_G alternatives on the misfitting fits, so F1's n and sqrt(G) are measured
fi_alt <- t(sapply(list(G1 = list(fi_fit1m, 1), G2 = list(fi_fit2m, 2)), function(z) {
  fm <- fitMeasures(z[[1]], c("chisq.scaled", "df", "ntotal", "rmsea.scaled")); G <- z[[2]]
  c(lavaan = fm[["rmsea.scaled"]],
    n_NminusG_sqrtG = fi_rmsea(fm[["chisq.scaled"]], fm[["df"]], fm[["ntotal"]] - G, G),
    n_N_sqrtG       = fi_rmsea(fm[["chisq.scaled"]], fm[["df"]], fm[["ntotal"]], G),
    n_NminusG_none  = fi_rmsea(fm[["chisq.scaled"]], fm[["df"]], fm[["ntotal"]] - G, G, kappa = FALSE)) }))
fi_alt
stopifnot(all(fi_lav$wv_is_inv_diag_gamma < 1e-12),
          all(fi_lav$rel[fi_lav$quantity %in% c("baseline.chisq", "baseline.chisq.scaled")] < 1e-8),
          all(fi_lav$rel[fi_lav$quantity == "baseline.df"] == 0),
          all(fi_lav$rel[grepl("scaled$", fi_lav$quantity) & fi_lav$quantity != "baseline.chisq.scaled"] < 1e-12),
          all(fi_lav$ours[fi_lav$model == "1-factor" & fi_lav$quantity == "rmsea.scaled"] > 0),
          all(abs(fi_alt[, "n_N_sqrtG"] - fi_alt[, "lavaan"]) > 1e-6),
          abs(fi_alt["G2", "n_NminusG_none"] - fi_alt["G2", "lavaan"]) > 1e-3)
cat("lavaan", as.character(packageVersion("lavaan")), "\n")
```

### Recorded failure: R2 against lavaan 0.7.2 (out of scope, kept as a failure)

Cloud draft P preregistered that its catML robust RMSEA (family R2) reproduces lavaan's
`rmsea.robust`. **On lavaan 0.7.2 that assertion FAILS** (main session, 2026-10-10, R 4.6.0:
gap 2.07e-5 against a 1e-9 criterion at $G=1$; 3.42e-6 at $G=2$ configural;
E-005 2026-10-10, *Cloud draft P*). The cause, verified in 0.7.2's source and by
arithmetic: `rmsea.robust` divides by `SampleStats@ntotal` $=N$, the draft by $N-G$, while
`rmsea.scaled` (family S, above) uses $N-G$. **This is recorded as a failure, not a passing check:**
no chunk here recomputes R2 with lavaan's divisor to make it agree, and no fixture, test or note may
present a divisor-matched R2 as the preregistered result. R2 itself is deferred to 0.4.0+, where it
starts from this failure. **NOT YET EXECUTED in this file** — the record above is the main session's
run, cited, not re-run here.

### Decisions, frozen 2026-10-21 (user)

**F1–F6 are decided as recommended below, F4 amended, and frozen** (user, 2026-10-21: "I approve
F1-F6 with one point about F4. It should distinguish model-side and baseline-side conditions
explicitly."). The production conventions (dwlsmv's, which differ from lavaan's only at F3 and
F4(ii)):

- **F1** $\kappa_G=\sqrt G$; $n=N-G$.
- **F2** TLI unclipped. TLI uses the raw $E_L$ (not $\max(E_L,0)$), which is what lets it exceed 1;
  clamping $E_L$ in TLI would clip it at 1, which F2 rejects.
- **F3** $D_L=0$ (or $T_{3L}$ missing): RMSEA, CFI and TLI all missing.
- **F4, as amended: two independent conditions.**
  *Model side,* $E_L=T_{3L}-D_L$: decides only the model's own clamp, RMSEA $=0$ when $E_L\le0$, and
  $E_L$ enters CFI as $\max(E_L,0)$. It never decides whether CFI or TLI is defined.
  *Baseline side,* $E_B=T_{3B}-D_B$: decides only whether CFI and TLI are defined ($E_B\le0$, or
  $T_{3B}$ missing, or $D_B=0$: both missing, with a note), from the baseline's own $T_3$ and df
  alone. It never affects RMSEA. When $E_B>0$, CFI $=1-\max(E_L,0)/\max(E_L,E_B)$ and TLI
  $=1-E_LD_B/(E_BD_L)$. In particular $E_L\le0$ does not give CFI $=1$ when the baseline is invalid,
  and an invalid baseline does not alter RMSEA. Exact comparisons, no `all.equal()` tolerance.
  `fi-frozen` checks all four sign combinations against a merged-condition mutant.
- **F5** `e(rmsea_s)`, `e(cfi_s)`, `e(tli_s)`, `e(T3_b)`, `e(df_T3_b)`.
- **F6** a skipped $d=0$ level's row is shown, marked "skipped (d = 0)", with Δ blank; the next
  level's Δ is against the last fitted level.

The options as they were presented for the decision follow, unchanged.

- **F1, the multiple-group factor $\kappa_G$.** (a) $\sqrt G$, as lavaan's `rmsea.scaled` (and
  Steiger, 1998): exact recovery of a common per-group RMSEA when nothing is tied and either the
  $D_g$ or the group sizes are equal (`fi-sqrtG`), matches the lavaan fixture without a conversion. (b) None: RMSEA as a single
  pooled discrepancy per df; at $G=1$ identical; at $G>1$ smaller by $\sqrt G$ and not comparable
  with lavaan or published multiple-group RMSEAs. Under ties (every level past configural) neither
  recovers a per-group value (`fi-sqrtG`, last row). **Recommend (a)**, with the help stating that
  multiple-group RMSEA includes $\sqrt G$.
- **F2, TLI clipping.** (a) Unclipped, as lavaan (TLI can exceed 1, `fi-conventions` row 2). (b)
  Clip to $[0,1]$ or at 1 only. Clipping hides information and makes ΔTLI zero across a range of
  well-fitting levels. **Recommend (a)**; TLI is not in the Δ table anyway.
- **F3, $D_L=0$.** $T_3$ is undefined at $D=0$ ($\operatorname{Tr}(M^2)=0$; spec already refuses
  `dwlsmv_sens_t3` there). (a) Report all three as missing with a note. (b) lavaan's values (RMSEA 0,
  CFI 1, TLI 1), which present a saturated model as perfect fit. **Recommend (a)**: post missing,
  print "not defined, df = 0".
- **F4, non-positive excesses.** (i) $E_L\le0$: RMSEA 0 and CFI 1 by the $\max$ (both families do
  this; recommend keeping lavaan's form). (ii) $E_B\le0$ (the baseline itself fits; $\hat\rho$ near
  zero): CFI is 1 or undefined, TLI's denominator changes sign. (a) lavaan's values; (b) post CFI/TLI
  missing with a note that the baseline does not fit worse than its df. **Recommend (b)** for
  $E_B\le0$ and lavaan's $\max$ for $E_L\le0$. lavaan's `all.equal()` test for "both zero" is
  tolerance-based; the implementation should use exact comparison after the $\max$, which differs
  from lavaan only when an excess is within $\sim10^{-8}$ of 0.
- **F5, `e()` names.** Existing names are project-specific (`e(T3)`, `e(df_T3)`); Stata's
  `estat gof` returns `r(rmsea)`, `r(cfi)`, `r(tli)`. (a) `e(rmsea)`, `e(cfi)`, `e(tli)`,
  `e(T3_b)`, `e(df_T3_b)` (baseline). (b) Suffix the family: `e(rmsea_s)`, `e(cfi_s)`,
  `e(tli_s)`, leaving room for R1/R2 in 0.4.0 without renaming. **Recommend (b)**, with
  `e(T3_b)`/`e(df_T3_b)` for the baseline. A generated chain's Δ table is display plus an `r()` or
  `e()` matrix whose name follows the same choice.
- **F6, skipped $d=0$ levels in the Δ table.** By check 8's rule a skipped level has the previous
  level's $T_3$ and df. (a) Show the row, marked "skipped (d = 0)", with Δ values blank. (b) Omit
  the row and footnote it. (c) Show Δ = 0. (c) states a comparison that was not made. **Recommend
  (a)**: the chain stays visible and the next level's Δ is computed against the last fitted level.
- **N1 (finding, no decision asked).** c1 is not nested in threshold-constraining levels (Result
  FI2); recommend one help sentence saying so.

## Gate: an ordinal observed variable in a structural path, as a single-indicator factor {#sec-single-indicator}

**Superseded in part (2026-10-24, E-006).** For an *exogenous* predictor,
Result 1's latent-response coefficient is not the 0/1 contrast users want. Observed exogenous
covariates go to a conditional-covariate mode (v0.4.0) instead. Results 2–4, for an
endogenous ordinal $z$, stand.

**Executed 2026-10-24** in the main session (R 4.5.2, base R, no fixtures). The figures
quoted below come from that run. This section is a **gate**: it establishes what the
single-indicator device can and cannot do, using v1's existing $\sigma(\theta)$, and
**decides nothing**. The open questions are listed at the end.

### The question

v1 has no observed variables in structural regressions (spec §3; Module 11). For a
*continuous* $x$ that needs polyserial statistics (spec Module 12). For an *ordinal* $z$,
everything $\sigma$ could need is already in $s$: $z$'s thresholds and its polychoric
correlations with every other item. So the question is whether a path to or from $z$ can
be written in v1's parameter table without new sample statistics. The standard device is a
factor $Z$ whose only indicator is $z$, with $\lambda_z=1$ and $\theta_{zz}=0$, so
$Z\equiv z^*$.

In the delta parameterization $\theta_{zz}$ is derived:
$\theta_{zz}=1-\lambda_z^2\Phi_{ZZ}$. With $\lambda_z=1$, **$\theta_{zz}=0$ iff
$\Phi_{ZZ}=1$**, which constrains the *total* variance. That is what separates the
exogenous case from the endogenous one.

### Result 1: exogenous $z$ fits the existing table

If $Z$ is exogenous then $\Phi_{ZZ}=\psi_{ZZ}$. Fixing $\lambda_z=1$ **and** $\psi_{ZZ}=1$,
both literal fixed values, gives $Z\equiv z^*$. On design X ($z\to F$, $F$ with three
indicators) this reproduces the population correlations exactly (gap 0). It gives
$\theta_{zz}=0$, and the Jacobian has full rank 4 of 4 ($\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}=0.31$).
Both fixed rows are needed. With $\lambda_z$ also free (X2) only $\lambda_z\beta$
enters $\sigma$, and the rank drops to 4 of 5 (ratio 2.4e-12).

The coefficient $\beta$ is the regression of $F$ on the **latent response** $z^*$, not on
the observed categories of $z$. That is a modeling choice, not a technicality; see the
open questions.

### Result 2: endogenous $z$ needs a total-variance constraint

Now let $z$ be predicted (design M: $F_1\to z\to F_2$). The unit-variance rule for latent
factors fixes the **disturbance** $\psi_{ZZ}$ (spec §4.8). Applied to $Z$ (M1, $\psi_{ZZ}=1$),
it gives $\Phi_{ZZ}=1+a^2$, so $\theta_{zz}=-a^2=-0.36$. That is inadmissible, and $\sigma$
misses the population by 0.135. The rule is right for latent factors and wrong here. It
is the same ψ-against-Φ distinction as for latent factors, but the other way round: for a
single-indicator factor it is the **total** variance that must be 1.

What works (M3) is the constraint $\Phi_{ZZ}=1$, i.e.
$$\psi_{ZZ}=1-\big[(I-B)^{-1}\Psi(I-B)^{-\top}\big]_{ZZ}^{\text{explained}},
\qquad\text{here } \psi_{ZZ}=1-a^2\Phi_{11}.$$
It reproduces the population to 1.1e-16, gives $\theta_{zz}=0$, and has full rank 8 of 8
(ratio 0.30). This is lavaan's handling of an ordinal endogenous $y^*$ under the delta
parameterization: the residual variance is $1-R^2$, not a free parameter. It is
**nonlinear in θ**, so the canonical form's literal fixed values cannot express it.

### Result 3: a free $\psi_{ZZ}$ is a different model, and identified only sometimes

Freeing $\psi_{ZZ}$ (M2) does not mean "$\theta_{zz}=0$ estimated". It lets
$\theta_{zz}=1-\Phi_{ZZ}$ float, which is a single-indicator factor *with measurement
error*. Under full mediation it is **identified**: rank 9 of 9, ratio 0.13. The indirect
covariance $\lambda_1 a c\lambda_2$ and the $z$–$F_2$ covariance $c\,\Phi_{ZZ}\lambda_2$
together pin $\Phi_{ZZ}$, which is $z^*$'s reliability. Add a direct path $F_1\to F_2$
(M2d) and it is not identified: rank 9 of 10, ratio 6.4e-12. So identification of a free
$\psi_{ZZ}$ depends on the structure. The Δ rank check would catch the deficient case, but
a user asking for "$z$ as an observed mediator" would silently get a reliability estimate
in the identified case. **This finding was not anticipated:** the first draft of the check
asserted M2 deficient and failed.

### Result 4: a pure outcome $z$

If $z$ has no outgoing path (design O), $\psi_{ZZ}$ never reaches $\sigma$. Its Δ column is
zero (rank 4 of 5, ratio 0), and $\sigma$ is identical at any fixed value (gap 0). Only the
reported $\theta_{zz}$ moves. The Result 2 constraint is then needed only so that
$\theta_{zz}$ and the standardized solution mean what they say.

### Verification

Tolerances: $10^{-12}$ for the identities (measured: at most 1.1e-16). For rank,
$\sigma_{\min}/\sigma_{\max}>10^{-8}$ on a central-difference Jacobian, $h=10^{-6}$. The
gaps between the two classes are about four orders of magnitude, so this rank
tolerance is not tuned (measured: full rank at ≥0.13, deficient at ≤2.4e-12). All
**chosen after measuring**. $10^{-4}$ is the threshold for M1's population gap counting
as a miss (measured 0.135).

```{r si-impl}
# Model-implied quantities in the delta parameterization, from (Lambda, B, Psi).
# Rows of Lambda are y*, columns are factors. Theta is derived, never free.
si_phi <- function(B, Psi) {
  A <- solve(diag(nrow(B)) - B)
  A %*% Psi %*% t(A)
}
si_sigma <- function(Lambda, B, Psi) {
  S <- Lambda %*% si_phi(B, Psi) %*% t(Lambda)
  S[lower.tri(S)]                    # the correlation block of sigma
}
si_theta <- function(Lambda, B, Psi) {
  1 - diag(Lambda %*% si_phi(B, Psi) %*% t(Lambda))
}
# Numerical rank of d sigma / d theta, judged on sigma_min / sigma_max
# (the project's rank convention), by central differences.
si_rank <- function(build, theta, h = 1e-6, tol = 1e-8) {
  J <- sapply(seq_along(theta), function(k) {
    e <- replace(numeric(length(theta)), k, h)
    m1 <- build(theta + e); m0 <- build(theta - e)
    (do.call(si_sigma, m1) - do.call(si_sigma, m0)) / (2 * h)
  })
  d <- svd(J)$d
  list(rank = sum(d / d[1] > tol), ratio = min(d) / max(d), p = length(theta))
}

```

```{r si-exog}
# Design X: ordinal z predicts factor F (indicators y1..y3).
# Population: z* ~ N(0,1), F = b z* + zeta, Var F = 1, so psi_F = 1 - b^2.
b <- 0.5; lam <- c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6)
pop_X <- {
  R <- diag(4)                       # order: z, y1, y2, y3
  R[1, 2:4] <- R[2:4, 1] <- b * lam
  R[2:4, 2:4] <- outer(lam, lam); diag(R) <- 1
  R[lower.tri(R)]
}
# X1: single-indicator factor Z, lambda_z = 1 and psi_ZZ = 1 both fixed.
# Free: lambda_y (3), beta. F metric: unit variance, psi_FF fixed. To match the
# population scale, psi_FF = 1 - b^2 here; it is a fixed value, not free.
build_X1 <- function(t, lz = 1, psiF = 1 - b^2) {
  L <- rbind(c(lz, 0), cbind(0, t[1:3]))
  B <- matrix(c(0, t[4], 0, 0), 2)   # F <- Z
  list(Lambda = L, B = B, Psi = diag(c(1, psiF)))
}
tX <- c(lam, b)
gap_X1   <- max(abs(do.call(si_sigma, build_X1(tX)) - pop_X))
theta_X1 <- do.call(si_theta, build_X1(tX))[1]
rank_X1  <- si_rank(build_X1, tX)
# X2 (negative control): lambda_z free as well. lambda_z * beta is confounded.
build_X2 <- function(t) build_X1(t[1:4], lz = t[5])
rank_X2  <- si_rank(build_X2, c(tX, 1))

```

```{r si-endog}
# Design M: F1 (y1..y3) -> z -> F2 (y4..y6); z is an ordinal mediator.
# Population: z* = a F1 + e with Var z* = 1, F2 = c z* + zeta with Var F2 = 1.
a <- 0.6; cc <- 0.5; l1 <- c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6); l2 <- c(0.75, 0.65, 0.7)
pop_M <- {
  # factors F1, Z, F2 with Z = z* exactly; total variances all 1
  P <- matrix(c(1, a, a * cc,  a, 1, cc,  a * cc, cc, 1), 3)
  L <- rbind(cbind(l1, 0, 0), c(0, 1, 0), cbind(0, 0, l2))
  S <- L %*% P %*% t(L); S[lower.tri(S)]
}
# Unit-variance metric on F2 fixes its disturbance, psi_F2 = 1 (spec 4.8), so
# the same population is reached at c' = c / sqrt(1 - c^2), l2' = l2 sqrt(1 - c^2).
# free: l1 (3), l2' (3), a, c'. psi_11 = 1 and psi_F2 = 1 fixed.
# psi_ZZ is given by `pz`, a function of the free vector.
build_M <- function(t, pz) {
  L <- rbind(cbind(t[1:3], 0, 0), c(0, 1, 0), cbind(0, 0, t[4:6]))
  B <- matrix(0, 3, 3); B[2, 1] <- t[7]; B[3, 2] <- t[8]
  list(Lambda = L, B = B, Psi = diag(c(1, pz(t), 1)))
}
tM <- c(l1, l2 * sqrt(1 - cc^2), a, cc / sqrt(1 - cc^2))
# M1 (the rule for latent factors, misapplied): psi_ZZ = 1 fixed, the disturbance.
M1 <- build_M(tM, function(t) 1)
gap_M1   <- max(abs(do.call(si_sigma, M1) - pop_M))
theta_M1 <- do.call(si_theta, M1)[4]         # z is the 4th y*
# M2: psi_ZZ free (appended to the free vector).
build_M2 <- function(t) build_M(t[1:8], function(.) t[9])
rank_M2  <- si_rank(build_M2, c(tM, 1 - a^2))
# M2d: the same, plus a direct path F2 <- F1 (free, evaluated at 0.3).
build_M2d <- function(t) {
  m <- build_M2(t[1:9]); m$B[3, 1] <- t[10]; m
}
rank_M2d <- si_rank(build_M2d, c(tM, 1 - a^2, 0.3))
# M3: the total-variance constraint Phi_ZZ = 1, i.e. psi_ZZ = 1 - a^2 Phi_11.
pz3 <- function(t) 1 - t[7]^2
M3 <- build_M(tM, pz3)
gap_M3   <- max(abs(do.call(si_sigma, M3) - pop_M))
theta_M3 <- do.call(si_theta, M3)[4]
rank_M3  <- si_rank(function(t) build_M(t, pz3), tM)

```

```{r si-outcome}
# Design O: F1 -> z only; z has no outgoing path. psi_ZZ never reaches sigma.
build_O <- function(t) {
  L <- rbind(cbind(t[1:3], 0), c(0, 1))
  B <- matrix(c(0, t[4], 0, 0), 2)
  list(Lambda = L, B = B, Psi = diag(c(1, t[5])))
}
rank_O <- si_rank(build_O, c(l1, a, 1 - a^2))
# sigma is the same at any fixed psi_ZZ; only the derived theta_z moves
sig_O_gap <- max(abs(do.call(si_sigma, build_O(c(l1, a, 0.2))) -
                     do.call(si_sigma, build_O(c(l1, a, 0.9)))))

```

```{r si-report}
stopifnot(gap_X1 < 1e-12, abs(theta_X1) < 1e-12,
          rank_X1$rank == rank_X1$p, rank_X2$rank < rank_X2$p,
          gap_M1 > 1e-4, theta_M1 < 0,
          rank_M2$rank == rank_M2$p, rank_M2d$rank < rank_M2d$p,
          gap_M3 < 1e-12, abs(theta_M3) < 1e-12, rank_M3$rank == rank_M3$p,
          rank_O$rank < rank_O$p, sig_O_gap < 1e-12)
print(rbind(
  X1 = c(gap = gap_X1, theta_z = theta_X1, rank = rank_X1$rank, p = rank_X1$p, ratio = rank_X1$ratio),
  X2 = c(NA, NA, rank_X2$rank, rank_X2$p, rank_X2$ratio),
  M1 = c(gap_M1, theta_M1, NA, NA, NA),
  M2 = c(NA, NA, rank_M2$rank, rank_M2$p, rank_M2$ratio),
  M2d = c(NA, NA, rank_M2d$rank, rank_M2d$p, rank_M2d$ratio),
  M3 = c(gap_M3, theta_M3, rank_M3$rank, rank_M3$p, rank_M3$ratio),
  O  = c(sig_O_gap, NA, rank_O$rank, rank_O$p, rank_O$ratio)), digits = 3)
```

### Open, and not decided here

1. **Semantics of an exogenous ordinal predictor.** Result 1 regresses on $z^*$. The
   alternative, conditioning on the observed $z$ (numeric or dummies), is the covariate
   route, with its own statistics (spec Module 12, `conditional.x`). Which one, or both,
   v1.x offers is the user's call.
2. **Canonical form.** Result 1 needs a factor with a fixed $\lambda$ *and* a fixed
   $\psi_{ff}$. That is one metric constraint plus one ordinary fixed row. Whether
   `dwls_identify()`'s "exactly one metric constraint per factor" invariant (spec §5.1)
   admits this unchanged has not been checked against the code.
3. **Endogenous $z$.** Result 2 needs a new constraint type ($\Phi_{ZZ}=1$, nonlinear),
   with its own Δ chain rule and an admissibility rule ($\psi_{ZZ}\ge0$, i.e.
   $R^2_z\le1$). That changes the locked API and the spec. Expanding it belongs in Module 3
   (like `metric`), since endogeneity is visible only there.
4. **Whether a free $\psi_{ZZ}$ (Result 3) is ever offered**, and if it isn't, how Module 11
   prevents a user from writing it by accident.
5. **$\theta_{zz}=0$ exactly, on the boundary.** Check every consumer: the admissibility
   check, D7 standardization, and `@sec-theta-delta`'s conversion, whose theta
   parameterization scales by $\theta_{jj}^{-1/2}$ and is undefined at zero.
6. **Sign canonicalization** (Module 5) for a factor with no free loading.
7. **A tier-2 reference.** How lavaan treats an `ordered` exogenous variable by default
   (conditioned on, or modeled jointly) must be checked, not assumed, before any fixture
   is generated. Endogenous ordinal $y^*$ in a lavaan path model is the natural reference
   for Result 2.
8. **Interaction with work already recorded.** Module 11 currently refuses observed
   exogenous variables and paths between observed variables at rc 198
   (E-061, 2026-10-04). Single-indicator factors are on the multigroup β
   "not established" list (2026-10-10), and a scalar step with single-indicator factors is
   an unverified $d=0$ pattern (2026-10-12). Opening this route must revisit all three.

## Conditional-covariate mode: one binary $x$, single group {#sec-condx}

**Executed 2026-10-24** in the main session (R 4.5.2, base R, no fixtures). The figures
below come from that run. Scope and obligations are the E-006 entry of
2026-10-24 (v0.4.0). This section is the narrow first deliverable: one group, ordinal
indicators, one binary $x$, items 1–5 of that entry and obligations (a)–(g). **It decides
nothing that entry leaves open:** not the conditional baseline or CFI/TLI, not DIFFTEST in
this mode, not the ordering of $s$ (lavaan's order is checked when the tier-2 fixture is
generated), not the $\theta$ order or `ptype` of $\gamma$ and $\kappa$, and not the
normaliser (see `@sec-normaliser`; the oracle here uses the observed information,
which is asymptotically equivalent). The simulation comparing the joint and conditional
approaches (item 6) is a separate preregistration. The lavaan reference (item 7) comes
later.

### Setting, and the data invariant (c)

Items $j=1,\dots,p$ with categories $0,\dots,K_j-1$. One observed $x\in\{0,1\}$. Stage 1
takes $(Y,K,X)$: $X$ is data, and nothing model-implied enters Stage 1. Rows with $x$
missing are deleted listwise **together with** the item listwise rule, (f). The rule is
the same as v1's: one complete-case sample, so that every Stage 1 statistic and Γ refer
to the same $N$. Under MCAR this is consistent; it is not a missing-data model for $x$.

Notation: π is already used for category probabilities, so the **reduced-form slopes are
$b_j$**. The E-006 decisions entry's $\Pi$ is the vector $b$.

### Model assumptions of Stage 1, stated as assumptions (a)

The conditional Stage 1 is a *model*, not a saturated summary:

* **(A1) Parallel shift.** $y_j^*\mid x\sim N(b_jx,1)$, with the same thresholds
  $\tau_j$ in both groups. For $K_j>2$ this fits $K_j-1+1$ parameters to $2(K_j-1)$ group
  proportions. It also assumes equal residual scale across groups.
* **(A2) Common residual correlation.** One $\rho_{ij}=\operatorname{Corr}(y_i^*,y_j^*\mid x)$,
  equal in both groups, with bivariate normality given $x$.

v1's univariate thresholds are saturated, and these are not. Their failure produces a
pseudo-true $s^*$, which the structural model is then fitted to.

### Stage 1, and its statistics

$s=(\tau,b,\rho)$: thresholds item-major, then slopes, then residual correlations in
lower-triangle order. Item $j$ maximises
$\sum_i\log\{\Phi(\tau_{j,y_{ij}+1}-b_jx_i)-\Phi(\tau_{j,y_{ij}}-b_jx_i)\}$ over
$\theta_j=(\tau_j,b_j)$. Pair $(i,j)$ maximises the bivariate rectangle log-likelihood in
$\rho_{ij}$ with $\theta_i,\theta_j$ held at their item estimates. All bounds are shifted
by $-b\,x$.

**Item 1: the probit-on-$x$ influence function.** With $g_j$ the per-observation score of
item $j$ and $H_j=-E\,\partial g_j/\partial\theta_j'$:
$$\psi_{\theta_j}=H_j^{-1}g_j.$$
The score is closed form. For an observation in category $c$, with
$u=\tau_{j,c+1}-b_jx$ and $l=\tau_{j,c}-b_jx$:
$\partial/\partial\tau_{j,c+1}=\phi(u)/P$, $\partial/\partial\tau_{j,c}=-\phi(l)/P$, and
$\partial/\partial b_j=-x\{\phi(u)-\phi(l)\}/P$.

**Item 2: the residual-polychoric influence function, with complete propagation.** The
pair score is $u_{ij}=P^{-1}\partial P/\partial\rho$, where $\partial\Phi_2/\partial\rho=\phi_2$
on each corner. The two-step expansion gives
$$\psi_{\rho_{ij}}=-U_\rho^{-1}\big(u_{ij}+U_{\theta}\,(\psi_{\theta_i}',\psi_{\theta_j}')'\big),
\qquad U_\rho=E\,\partial u/\partial\rho,\quad U_\theta=E\,\partial u/\partial(\theta_i',\theta_j').$$
$U_\theta$ has columns for the **slopes** as well as the thresholds. That slope part is new
relative to v1's `psi_rho`, and it is the term most easily dropped.

**Item 3: combined.** $\psi=(\psi_\tau,\psi_b,\psi_\rho)$, and
$\hat\Gamma=N^{-1}\sum_i\psi_i\psi_i'$, still empirical and still the production
estimator.

**Verification.** On a 36-pattern population ($K=(3,3,2)$, $\lambda=(0.8,0.7,0.6)$,
$\gamma=0.5$, $P(x=1)=0.4$), exact up to quadrature:

* the population Stage 1 returns the reduced form exactly (Fisher consistency, 3.3e-16);
* **the pointwise expansion test** compares ψ at each pattern with the Gateaux derivative
  of the population estimator toward that pattern. It agrees to 2.7e-8 on all 36. Drop
  the slope part of $U_\theta$ and it misses by 0.098; drop all of $U_\theta$ and it misses
  by 0.47. A centring test would not tell these apart (spec §4.5.5);
* centring $\sum w\psi$ = 3.7e-16;
* Monte Carlo, $R=400$, $N=2000$: the covariance of $\sqrt N(\hat s-s_0)$ against Γ, over
  all 66 elements, has max $|z|=2.31$ in Monte Carlo SEs. The threshold, $|z|<4$, was
  **fixed before the run** (P(max>4) ≈ 0.004 under the null).

### Item 4: reduced form, Δ, scale

Conditional delta parameterization: $\operatorname{Var}(y_j^*\mid x)=1$, so
$\theta_{jj}=1-\lambda_j^2\psi$ is derived, as in v1. The factor is endogenous on $x$, so
unit variance fixes the **disturbance** $\psi=1$, exactly spec §4.8's rule. With
$\eta=\Gamma_x x+B\eta+\zeta$ and direct effects $\kappa$:
$$\tau=\tau,\qquad b=\Lambda(I-B)^{-1}\Gamma_x+\kappa,\qquad
\rho=\operatorname{offdiag}\big(\Lambda(I-B)^{-1}\Psi(I-B)^{-\top}\Lambda'\big).$$
For one factor: $b_j=\lambda_j\gamma+\kappa_j$ and $\rho_{ij}=\lambda_i\lambda_j$.

**(d) The threshold block of Δ is the identity, with or without direct effects** (measured
2.9e-11, the FD error). No model parameter other than τ enters a τ row, and τ enters no
other row. This is a single-group result. It does not cover invariance-level fits
(@sec-marker-recovery; spec §4.8).

**(e) The slope block.** $\partial b_j/\partial\lambda_j=\gamma$, $\partial b_j/\partial\gamma=\lambda_j$,
$\partial b_j/\partial\kappa_j=1$: analytic against finite differences, 2.9e-11. Rank:
the model without κ, 9 of 9 (ratio 0.48, df 2); with one $\kappa$, 10 of 10 (0.25);
with κ on every item, 11 of 12. γ and the κ's are then confounded along one direction,
because $\rho$ fixes λ and $b$ has only $p$ rows. So **at least one item must carry no
direct effect**, the usual MIMIC anchor. γ and κ need a `ptype` and a place in θ's order,
which is spec §4.2 and §4.8's business. Not decided here.

### Item 5: recovery of the treatment contrast

DWLS with $W_D=\operatorname{diag}(\Gamma)^{-1}$ at the population statistics returns θ₀
exactly (3.3e-16), so $\hat\gamma=0.5$. The estimand is
$$\gamma=E[F\mid x=1]-E[F\mid x=0]\quad\text{in units of }\operatorname{SD}(F\mid x)=\sqrt\psi=1,$$
the within-group standardized mean difference, given the covariates in the model. The
total-SD version, $\gamma/\sqrt{1+\gamma^2q(1-q)}=0.486$ here, depends on the treatment
proportion $q$, so it is a different estimand. In the Monte Carlo: bias of $\hat\gamma$,
$z=1.41$. The empirical SD of $\hat\gamma$ is 0.0567 against the population sandwich SE
0.0577, $z=-0.50$. Both thresholds, $|z|<3$, were **fixed before the run**. That checks the
covariance calculation at the population Γ. Coverage with a per-replicate $\hat\Gamma$ is
the preregistered simulation's job.

### (a) What Stage 1 misfit does, and what sees it

T3 tests $\sigma(\hat\theta)$ against $\hat s$. It never sees the data beyond $s$, so
misfit absorbed by (A1)–(A2) into $s^*$ reaches T3 only if $s^*$ leaves the structural
model's manifold. Four exact population cases:

| Case | Stage 1 diagnostic (KL per obs) | T3 ($F_{\min}$) | $\gamma$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Correct model | 6e-17 | — | 0.5 |
| Threshold DIF, binary item, no κ | **0: untestable, $K=2$ is saturated** (margins reproduced to 1e-16) | 0.010 | 0.404 |
| same, $\kappa_3$ free | 0 | 5e-33 | 0.5000; $\kappa_3=-0.300$ |
| Non-parallel DIF, 3-category item, $\kappa_1$ free | 8.0e-3 | **1.8e-9** | 0.50003 |
| Non-parallel DIF on items 1 and 3, no κ | 8.0e-3 | 8.7e-3 | 0.284 |

Read across the rows:

* Threshold DIF on a binary item **is** a direct effect, exactly.
* Non-parallel DIF can be invisible to T3 while a Stage 1 diagnostic sees it. At
  $N=2000$ the noncentralities are about 4e-6 against 32. The diagnostic is the per-item
  likelihood ratio of group-saturated thresholds against the parallel shift, df $K_j-2$,
  so it **does not exist at $K_j=2$**. An analogous per-pair test of group-specific
  $\rho$ against (A2) is possible. It is not derived here.
* When misfit does reach T3 it can bias γ badly (0.284 against 0.5). These are
  population numbers on chosen designs, **chosen after measuring** in the sense that the
  first DIF design was kept and the κ-free cases were added once its result was seen.

### (b) Module 10 on $(y\text{ pattern},x)$

**Pattern lemma, re-established.** ψ depends on an observation only through its pattern
$(y,x)$, so $\hat\Gamma=\sum_k(n_k/N)\psi_k\psi_k'$ over observed patterns. When every
score equation is solved, $\sum_k n_k\psi_k=0$, and so
$\operatorname{rank}\hat\Gamma\le\min(D,n_{\text{pat}}-1)$, with
$n_{\text{pat}}\le2\prod_jK_j$. Checked on a 9-pattern sample: rank 8, centring 3.3e-16.
The bound needs $x$ discrete. A continuous $x$ makes the pattern set infinite, which is
the same reason `@sec-gamma-rank` limits its bounds to v1. The threshold-aliasing
statement is not re-derived here and stays open.

**Separation.** For a binary item, $\tau_j=\Phi^{-1}P(y_j=0\mid x=0)$ and
$\tau_j-b_j=\Phi^{-1}P(y_j=0\mid x=1)$, so **a finite estimate exists iff all four
(category, group) cells are non-empty**. With the cell $y_3=0,x=1$ empty, the profile
log-likelihood rises monotonically in $b_3$ (−0.510, −0.4988, −0.49881, −0.49881 at
$b_3=2,4,6,8$) and has no maximum. For $K_j>2$ the exact condition, and the pairwise
analogue (`@sec-emptycells`), are open.

### (g) Coding

Centring $x$ leaves $b$ and $\rho$ unchanged and shifts the thresholds by
$-b_j\bar x$ (all three to about 1e-15), so γ does not move. Coding $x$ as $\pm1$ halves
$b$, and hence γ (1.7e-16): **γ's meaning depends on the coding's unit**, and 0/1 is the
coding for which it is the treatment contrast. The reported thresholds are at $x=0$, so
they change with centring. Help text will need to say so.

### Verification

Tolerances. Identities: $10^{-12}$ (measured ≤ 3.3e-16). The pointwise expansion:
$10^{-6}$, set by the finite-difference error (measured 2.7e-8); a negative control is
killed above $10^{-3}$. Δ against FD: $10^{-8}$. The Monte Carlo thresholds were fixed
before the run, as stated above. $F_{\min}<10^{-7}$ and $|\gamma-0.5|<10^{-3}$ for the
non-parallel case were **chosen after measuring** (1.8e-9, 3e-5).

```{r cx-setup}
# Conditional-covariate Stage 1 for ordinal items and one binary x, in base R.
# Data are held as weighted patterns: Y (n_pat x p, categories 0..K-1), x
# (n_pat), w (n_pat, summing to 1). Population probabilities and sample
# proportions use the same code, so the influence function can be checked as
# a Gateaux derivative of the population estimator.
if (!exists("Phi2")) {
  Phi2 <- function(a, b, rho) {
    if (a == -Inf || b == -Inf) return(0)
    if (a ==  Inf && b ==  Inf) return(1)
    if (a ==  Inf) return(pnorm(b))
    if (b ==  Inf) return(pnorm(a))
    s <- sqrt(1 - rho^2)
    integrate(function(x) dnorm(x) * pnorm((b - rho * x) / s),
              -Inf, a, rel.tol = 1e-12)$value
  }
}
cx_phi2 <- function(a, b, rho) {
  if (!is.finite(a) || !is.finite(b)) return(0)
  exp(-(a^2 - 2 * rho * a * b + b^2) / (2 * (1 - rho^2))) /
    (2 * pi * sqrt(1 - rho^2))
}
cx_K <- c(3L, 3L, 2L)
cx_p <- length(cx_K)
cx_pairs <- t(combn(cx_p, 2))          # (1,2), (1,3), (2,3): lower-triangle order
cx_true <- list(tau = list(c(-0.5, 0.6), c(-0.2, 0.9), 0.3),
                lambda = c(0.8, 0.7, 0.6), gamma = 0.5, q = 0.4)

# Reduced form under the conditional delta parameterization, Var(y*|x) = 1,
# psi = 1 (F's disturbance; F is endogenous on x): b = lambda * gamma,
# rho_ij = lambda_i lambda_j. kappa (direct effects x -> y_j) optional.
cx_sigma <- function(tau, lambda, gamma, kappa = numeric(cx_p)) {
  rho <- apply(cx_pairs, 1, function(ij) lambda[ij[1]] * lambda[ij[2]])
  c(unlist(tau), lambda * gamma + kappa, rho)
}

# Population pattern probabilities, from the factor model by one-dimensional
# integration over F given x (y* = lambda F + e, F = gamma x + zeta). tau_x1,
# if given, replaces the thresholds in group x = 1 (threshold DIF).
cx_population <- function(par, tau_x1 = NULL) {
  grid <- expand.grid(lapply(cx_K, function(k) 0:(k - 1)))
  Y <- as.matrix(grid[rep(seq_len(nrow(grid)), 2), ]); dimnames(Y) <- NULL
  x <- rep(0:1, each = nrow(grid))
  s <- sqrt(1 - par$lambda^2)
  w <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(Y)), function(r) {
    tau <- if (x[r] == 1 && !is.null(tau_x1)) tau_x1 else par$tau
    f <- function(eta) {
      out <- dnorm(eta - par$gamma * x[r])
      for (j in seq_len(cx_p)) {
        tt <- c(-Inf, tau[[j]], Inf)
        out <- out * (pnorm((tt[Y[r, j] + 2] - par$lambda[j] * eta) / s[j]) -
                      pnorm((tt[Y[r, j] + 1] - par$lambda[j] * eta) / s[j]))
      }
      out
    }
    integrate(f, -Inf, Inf, rel.tol = 1e-13)$value
  }, 0)
  w <- w * ifelse(x == 1, par$q, 1 - par$q)
  list(Y = Y, x = x, w = w)
}

```

```{r cx-stage1}
# Item j: ordered probit on x with a parallel shift, y*_j = b_j x + e_j.
# theta_j = (tau_j1..tau_j,K-1, b_j). Score per pattern, n_pat x K.
cx_uni_score <- function(yj, x, th) {
  K <- length(th); tau <- th[-K]; b <- th[K]
  tt <- c(-Inf, tau, Inf)
  lo <- tt[yj + 1] - b * x; up <- tt[yj + 2] - b * x
  P  <- pnorm(up) - pnorm(lo)
  dl <- ifelse(is.finite(lo), dnorm(lo), 0)
  du <- ifelse(is.finite(up), dnorm(up), 0)
  G <- matrix(0, length(yj), K)
  for (k in seq_len(K - 1)) G[, k] <- (du * (yj + 1 == k) - dl * (yj == k)) / P
  G[, K] <- -x * (du - dl) / P
  G
}
cx_jac <- function(f, th, h = 1e-6) {
  sapply(seq_along(th), function(k) {
    e <- replace(numeric(length(th)), k, h)
    (f(th + e) - f(th - e)) / (2 * h)
  })
}
cx_uni_fit <- function(yj, x, w, K) {
  pm <- cumsum(tapply(w, factor(yj, 0:(K - 1)), sum))[-K]
  th <- c(qnorm(pm / sum(w)), 0)
  for (it in 1:50) {
    g <- colSums(w * cx_uni_score(yj, x, th))
    if (max(abs(g)) < 1e-14) break
    H <- cx_jac(function(t) colSums(w * cx_uni_score(yj, x, t)), th)
    th <- th - solve(H, g)
  }
  th
}

# Pair (i, j): residual polychoric given x, with the item fits held fixed.
# Cells are aggregated by (c_i, c_j, x) for speed.
cx_pair_cells <- function(yi, yj, x, w) {
  key <- paste(yi, yj, x)
  ag <- tapply(w, key, sum)
  parts <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(names(ag), " "))
  list(ci = as.integer(parts[, 1]), cj = as.integer(parts[, 2]),
       x = as.numeric(parts[, 3]), w = as.numeric(ag), key = key,
       ukey = names(ag))
}
cx_rect <- function(ci, cj, x, thi, thj, rho) {
  Ki <- length(thi); Kj <- length(thj)
  ti <- c(-Inf, thi[-Ki], Inf); tj <- c(-Inf, thj[-Kj], Inf)
  vapply(seq_along(ci), function(r) {
    a1 <- ti[ci[r] + 1] - thi[Ki] * x[r]; a2 <- ti[ci[r] + 2] - thi[Ki] * x[r]
    b1 <- tj[cj[r] + 1] - thj[Kj] * x[r]; b2 <- tj[cj[r] + 2] - thj[Kj] * x[r]
    P  <- Phi2(a2, b2, rho) - Phi2(a1, b2, rho) - Phi2(a2, b1, rho) + Phi2(a1, b1, rho)
    dP <- cx_phi2(a2, b2, rho) - cx_phi2(a1, b2, rho) - cx_phi2(a2, b1, rho) +
          cx_phi2(a1, b1, rho)
    c(P, dP)
  }, c(0, 0))
}
# score in rho per cell, u = (dP/drho) / P
cx_pair_u <- function(cells, thi, thj, rho) {
  r <- cx_rect(cells$ci, cells$cj, cells$x, thi, thj, rho)
  r[2, ] / r[1, ]
}
cx_pair_fit <- function(cells, thi, thj) {
  ll <- function(rho) sum(cells$w * log(cx_rect(cells$ci, cells$cj, cells$x,
                                                  thi, thj, rho)[1, ]))
  rho <- optimize(ll, c(-0.99, 0.99), maximum = TRUE, tol = 1e-10)$maximum
  for (it in 1:6) {
    g <- sum(cells$w * cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho))
    if (abs(g) < 1e-14) break
    h <- 1e-6
    H <- (sum(cells$w * cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho + h)) -
          sum(cells$w * cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho - h))) / (2 * h)
    rho <- rho - g / H
  }
  rho
}

# The full Stage 1: s = (tau, b, rho), thresholds item-major, then slopes,
# then correlations in lower-triangle order.
cx_stage1 <- function(d) {
  th <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) cx_uni_fit(d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w, cx_K[j]))
  rho <- apply(cx_pairs, 1, function(ij) {
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, ij[1]], d$Y[, ij[2]], d$x, d$w)
    cx_pair_fit(cells, th[[ij[1]]], th[[ij[2]]])
  })
  list(th = th, rho = rho,
       s = c(unlist(lapply(th, function(t) t[-length(t)])),
             vapply(th, function(t) t[length(t)], 0), rho))
}

```

```{r cx-psi}
# Influence function per pattern. Items: psi_j = H_j^{-1} g_j. Pairs: the
# two-step expansion psi_rho = -U_rho^{-1} (u + U_1 psi_1), where U_1 is the
# derivative of the mean pair score in the four first-stage parameters
# (tau_i, b_i, tau_j, b_j). `prop` selects the propagation term: "full",
# "tau" (slope part dropped), "none" (negative controls).
cx_psi <- function(d, fit, prop = "full") {
  n <- nrow(d$Y)
  psi1 <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
    th <- fit$th[[j]]
    H  <- -cx_jac(function(t) colSums(d$w * cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, t)), th)
    cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th) %*% t(solve(H))
  })
  psir <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]
    thi <- fit$th[[i]]; thj <- fit$th[[j]]; rho <- fit$rho[m]
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    ubar <- function(ti, tj, r) sum(cells$w * cx_pair_u(cells, ti, tj, r))
    h <- 1e-6
    Ur <- (ubar(thi, thj, rho + h) - ubar(thi, thj, rho - h)) / (2 * h)
    ni <- length(thi)
    U1 <- cx_jac(function(t) ubar(t[1:ni], t[-(1:ni)], rho), c(thi, thj))
    if (prop == "tau")  U1[c(ni, length(U1))] <- 0
    if (prop == "none") U1[] <- 0
    ucell <- cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho)
    u <- ucell[match(cells$key, cells$ukey)]
    -(u + cbind(psi1[[i]], psi1[[j]]) %*% U1) / Ur
  })
  tauc <- do.call(cbind, lapply(psi1, function(P) P[, -ncol(P), drop = FALSE]))
  bc   <- sapply(psi1, function(P) P[, ncol(P)])
  cbind(tauc, bc, psir)
}

```

```{r cx-gateaux}
#| cache: true
# Pointwise check: psi at pattern k equals the derivative of the population
# estimator in the direction of a point mass at k.
pop <- cx_population(cx_true)
fit0 <- cx_stage1(pop)
s0 <- cx_sigma(cx_true$tau, cx_true$lambda, cx_true$gamma)
gap_consistent <- max(abs(fit0$s - s0))           # Fisher consistency
psi_full <- cx_psi(pop, fit0)
psi_tau  <- cx_psi(pop, fit0, "tau")
psi_none <- cx_psi(pop, fit0, "none")
eps <- 1e-5
gat <- t(sapply(seq_len(nrow(pop$Y)), function(k) {
  dk <- function(e) {
    d <- pop; d$w <- (1 - e) * pop$w; d$w[k] <- d$w[k] + e
    cx_stage1(d)$s
  }
  (dk(eps) - dk(-eps)) / (2 * eps)
}))
gap_full <- max(abs(gat - psi_full))
gap_tau  <- max(abs(gat - psi_tau))
gap_none <- max(abs(gat - psi_none))
centre   <- max(abs(colSums(pop$w * psi_full)))
Gamma0   <- crossprod(psi_full * sqrt(pop$w))
```

```{r cx-model}
# theta = (tau, lambda, gamma) with psi = 1 fixed; optional kappa columns.
cx_unpack <- function(th, kap_idx = integer()) {
  nt <- sum(cx_K - 1)
  tau <- split(th[1:nt], rep(seq_len(cx_p), cx_K - 1))
  kappa <- numeric(cx_p); kappa[kap_idx] <- th[-(1:(nt + cx_p + 1))]
  list(tau = tau, lambda = th[nt + 1:cx_p], gamma = th[nt + cx_p + 1],
       kappa = kappa)
}
cx_sig_th <- function(th, kap_idx = integer()) {
  u <- cx_unpack(th, kap_idx); cx_sigma(u$tau, u$lambda, u$gamma, u$kappa)
}
cx_delta <- function(th) {               # analytic, no kappa
  u <- cx_unpack(th); nt <- sum(cx_K - 1)
  D <- matrix(0, nt + cx_p + nrow(cx_pairs), length(th))
  D[1:nt, 1:nt] <- diag(nt)
  for (j in seq_len(cx_p)) {
    D[nt + j, nt + j] <- u$gamma; D[nt + j, nt + cx_p + 1] <- u$lambda[j]
  }
  for (m in seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs))) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]; r <- nt + cx_p + m
    D[r, nt + i] <- u$lambda[j]; D[r, nt + j] <- u$lambda[i]
  }
  D
}
th0 <- c(unlist(cx_true$tau), cx_true$lambda, cx_true$gamma)
gap_delta <- max(abs(cx_delta(th0) - cx_jac(cx_sig_th, th0)))
nt <- sum(cx_K - 1)
tau_block_identity <- max(abs(cx_jac(cx_sig_th, th0)[1:nt, 1:nt] - diag(nt)))
# with a direct effect on item 1: are the threshold rows still untouched?
thk <- c(th0, 0.2)
Jk  <- cx_jac(function(t) cx_sig_th(t, 1L), thk)
tau_rows_k <- max(abs(Jk[1:nt, ] - cbind(diag(nt), matrix(0, nt, ncol(Jk) - nt))))
cx_rank <- function(J) { d <- svd(J)$d; c(rank = sum(d / d[1] > 1e-8),
                                           p = ncol(J), ratio = min(d) / max(d)) }
rank_A  <- cx_rank(cx_delta(th0))
rank_k1 <- cx_rank(Jk)
rank_kall <- cx_rank(cx_jac(function(t) cx_sig_th(t, 1:3), c(th0, 0.2, 0.1, 0)))

```

```{r cx-recover}
# DWLS at the population statistics, W_D = diag(Gamma)^{-1}: gamma recovered.
cx_dwls <- function(s, W, th) {
  for (it in 1:100) {
    r <- s - cx_sig_th(th); D <- cx_delta(th)
    step <- solve(t(D) %*% W %*% D, t(D) %*% W %*% r)
    th <- th + drop(step)
    if (max(abs(step)) < 1e-13) break
  }
  th
}
W0 <- diag(1 / diag(Gamma0))
start <- th0 + c(numeric(nt), -0.1, 0.1, -0.1, 0.2)
th_pop <- cx_dwls(fit0$s, W0, start)
gap_recover <- max(abs(th_pop - th0))
# the estimand: E[F|x=1] - E[F|x=0] in units of SD(F|x) = sqrt(psi) = 1
gamma_hat <- th_pop[nt + cx_p + 1]
d_total <- gamma_hat / sqrt(1 + gamma_hat^2 * cx_true$q * (1 - cx_true$q))
# sandwich ACOV per N at the population
D0 <- cx_delta(th0); B0 <- solve(t(D0) %*% W0 %*% D0)
acov0 <- B0 %*% t(D0) %*% W0 %*% Gamma0 %*% W0 %*% D0 %*% B0

```

```{r cx-mc}
#| cache: true
# Monte Carlo: covariance of sqrt(N)(s_hat - s0) against Gamma0, and the
# empirical SD of gamma_hat against the population sandwich SE. Judged in
# Monte Carlo standard errors, never by percentage.
set.seed(20261024)
cx_R <- 400; cx_N <- 2000
mc <- t(replicate(cx_R, {
  cnt <- tabulate(sample.int(length(pop$w), cx_N, TRUE, pop$w), length(pop$w))
  d <- pop; d$w <- cnt / cx_N
  f <- cx_stage1(d)
  c(f$s, cx_dwls(f$s, W0, th0)[nt + cx_p + 1])
}))
S_hat <- mc[, seq_along(s0)]
Z <- sqrt(cx_N) * sweep(S_hat, 2, s0)
C_mc <- crossprod(sweep(Z, 2, colMeans(Z))) / (cx_R - 1)
se_C <- sqrt((outer(diag(Gamma0), diag(Gamma0)) + Gamma0^2) / (cx_R - 1))
z_cov <- (C_mc - Gamma0) / se_C
z_cov_max <- max(abs(z_cov[upper.tri(z_cov, diag = TRUE)]))
gh <- mc[, ncol(mc)]
bias_z <- (mean(gh) - cx_true$gamma) / (sd(gh) / sqrt(cx_R))
se_pop <- sqrt(acov0[nt + cx_p + 1, nt + cx_p + 1] / cx_N)
sd_z <- (sd(gh) - se_pop) / (se_pop / sqrt(2 * (cx_R - 1)))

```

```{r cx-misspec}
# (a) Stage 1 misspecification. Threshold DIF in item 1 (its upper threshold
# is 0.4 higher in group x = 1) and in the binary item 3 (0.3 higher), on top
# of the parallel shift. Stage 1 then converges to a pseudo-true s*.
tau_dif <- list(cx_true$tau[[1]] + c(0, 0.4),
                cx_true$tau[[2]], cx_true$tau[[3]] + 0.3)
popD <- cx_population(cx_true, tau_x1 = tau_dif)
fitD <- cx_stage1(popD)
# K = 2: the parallel-shift probit reproduces both group margins exactly
m3 <- tapply(popD$w, list(popD$Y[, 3], popD$x), sum)
p3_fit <- sapply(0:1, function(x) pnorm(fitD$th[[3]][1] - fitD$th[[3]][2] * x))
gap_K2 <- max(abs(m3[1, ] / colSums(m3) - p3_fit))
# K = 3: the per-group saturated margins against the parallel fit (KL, per obs)
cx_uni_kl <- function(d, fit, j) {
  K <- cx_K[j]; tab <- tapply(d$w, list(factor(d$Y[, j], 0:(K - 1)), d$x), sum)
  th <- fit$th[[j]]; tt <- c(-Inf, th[-K], Inf)
  P <- sapply(0:1, function(x) diff(pnorm(tt - th[K] * x)))
  sum(tab * log(sweep(tab, 2, colSums(tab), "/") / P))
}
kl1_D <- cx_uni_kl(popD, fitD, 1); kl1_0 <- cx_uni_kl(pop, fit0, 1)
# what T3 sees: the population minimum of F at s*, with W_D from Gamma*
GammaD <- crossprod(cx_psi(popD, fitD) * sqrt(popD$w))
WD <- diag(1 / diag(GammaD))
thD <- cx_dwls(fitD$s, WD, th0)
FD_min <- drop(crossprod(fitD$s - cx_sig_th(thD), WD %*% (fitD$s - cx_sig_th(thD))))
gamma_D <- thD[nt + cx_p + 1]

```

```{r cx-module10}
# (b) The pattern lemma on (y pattern, x). psi is a function of the pattern
# alone, so Gamma_hat = sum_k (n_k / N) psi_k psi_k' and, with the scores
# solved (centring), rank Gamma_hat <= n_pat - 1. A sample on 9 patterns:
small <- pop; keep <- c(1, 3, 8, 13, 15, 22, 23, 29, 36)
small$w <- numeric(length(pop$w)); small$w[keep] <- c(3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2)
small$w <- small$w / sum(small$w)
fitS <- cx_stage1(small)
psiS <- cx_psi(small, fitS)
GS <- crossprod(psiS * sqrt(small$w))
dS <- svd(GS)$d
rank_small <- sum(dS / dS[1] > 1e-10)
centre_small <- max(abs(colSums(small$w * psiS)))
# Separation: binary item 3 with no y3 = 0 in group x = 1. The profile
# log-likelihood in b_3 has no maximum: it rises toward its supremum.
sep <- pop; sep$w[sep$Y[, 3] == 0 & sep$x == 1] <- 0; sep$w <- sep$w / sum(sep$w)
prof <- sapply(c(2, 4, 6, 8), function(b) {
  ll <- function(t) sum(sep$w * log(pmax(pnorm(c(-Inf, t, Inf)[sep$Y[, 3] + 2] - b * sep$x) -
                                         pnorm(c(-Inf, t, Inf)[sep$Y[, 3] + 1] - b * sep$x),
                                         1e-300)))
  optimize(ll, c(-5, 5), maximum = TRUE, tol = 1e-12)$objective
})

```

```{r cx-centre}
# (g) Coding. Centring x shifts thresholds by -b * xbar; b and rho do not
# move. Coding x as -1/+1 halves b, hence gamma.
xbar <- sum(pop$w * pop$x)
popC <- pop; popC$x <- pop$x - xbar
fitC <- cx_stage1(popC)
gap_centre_b   <- max(abs(fitC$s[nt + 1:cx_p] - fit0$s[nt + 1:cx_p]))
gap_centre_rho <- max(abs(tail(fitC$s, 3) - tail(fit0$s, 3)))
gap_centre_tau <- max(abs(fitC$s[1:nt] -
  (fit0$s[1:nt] - rep(fit0$s[nt + 1:cx_p], cx_K - 1) * xbar)))
popPM <- pop; popPM$x <- 2 * pop$x - 1
gap_pm_b <- max(abs(cx_stage1(popPM)$s[nt + 1:cx_p] - fit0$s[nt + 1:cx_p] / 2))
```

```{r cx-invisible}
# DIF on the binary item alone, absorbed exactly by Stage 1 (K = 2 is
# saturated). Fit the model with a direct effect kappa_3 free: does F reach 0,
# and is gamma still recovered? Gauss-Newton on a numerical Jacobian.
cx_dwls_k <- function(s, W, th, kap) {
  for (it in 1:200) {
    r <- s - cx_sig_th(th, kap); D <- cx_jac(function(t) cx_sig_th(t, kap), th)
    step <- drop(solve(t(D) %*% W %*% D, t(D) %*% W %*% r)); th <- th + step
    if (max(abs(step)) < 1e-12) break
  }
  th
}
popB <- cx_population(cx_true, tau_x1 = list(cx_true$tau[[1]], cx_true$tau[[2]],
                                              cx_true$tau[[3]] + 0.3))
fitB <- cx_stage1(popB)
GammaB <- crossprod(cx_psi(popB, fitB) * sqrt(popB$w)); WB <- diag(1 / diag(GammaB))
FB <- function(th, kap) { r <- fitB$s - cx_sig_th(th, kap); drop(crossprod(r, WB %*% r)) }
thB0 <- cx_dwls_k(fitB$s, WB, th0, integer())
thB3 <- cx_dwls_k(fitB$s, WB, c(th0, 0), 3L)
FB_nokappa <- FB(thB0, integer()); FB_kappa3 <- FB(thB3, 3L)
gamma_B0 <- thB0[nt + cx_p + 1]; gamma_B3 <- thB3[nt + cx_p + 1]
kappa_B3 <- thB3[length(thB3)]
# Non-parallel DIF on the 3-category item 1 alone, kappa_1 free (df 1).
popN <- cx_population(cx_true, tau_x1 = list(cx_true$tau[[1]] + c(0, 0.4),
                                              cx_true$tau[[2]], cx_true$tau[[3]]))
fitN <- cx_stage1(popN)
GammaN <- crossprod(cx_psi(popN, fitN) * sqrt(popN$w)); WN <- diag(1 / diag(GammaN))
thN1 <- cx_dwls_k(fitN$s, WN, c(th0, 0), 1L)
rN <- fitN$s - cx_sig_th(thN1, 1L)
FN_kappa1 <- drop(crossprod(rN, WN %*% rN)); gamma_N1 <- thN1[nt + cx_p + 1]
kl1_N <- cx_uni_kl(popN, fitN, 1)

```

## Conditional mode: the normaliser, the order of $s$, and lavaan's Stage 1 {#sec-condx-norm}

**Executed 2026-10-24** in the main session (R 4.5.2, base R; lavaan 0.7.2 only through
the committed fixtures of `fixtures/generate/99h_lavaan_condx.R`). This is item 1 and
item 4a of the work order in E-006 (2026-10-24). It builds on
`@sec-condx`'s oracle and populations. **It decides nothing:** the normaliser
choice it sets up is the user's, and so is θ's order.

### What lavaan does, read from its code

`lavaan:::muthen1984()` in 0.7.2 builds every block of $B$ from **outer products of
observed scores** (BHHH):

* the per-item block from the threshold-and-slope scores (`lav_m84_a11`);
* the cross block from the pair's ρ-score against the *pair's own* threshold and slope
  scores (`lav_m84_a21`, with `dx_sl_i` when `nexo > 0`);
* the ρ block as $\sum u^2$ (`lav_m84_a22`).

That is the v1 convention (`@sec-normaliser`, "v1 ships $W=\hat\pi$"), extended to
the slopes. Written as estimators of the two-step blocks:
$$H_j=\textstyle\sum_iw_ig_ig_i',\qquad U_\rho=-\sum_iw_iu_i^2,\qquad
U_\theta=-\sum_iw_iu_i\,s^{\text{pair}}_{\theta,i}.$$
The alternative is the M-estimator (Hessian) form `@sec-condx` used: the same blocks as
derivatives of the mean score.

### Result N1: the two agree only where the information identity holds

The two forms estimate the same matrices **iff** $E[gg']=-E[\partial g/\partial\theta']$,
the information identity. That holds when Stage 1 is correctly specified, i.e. (A1)–(A2)
hold. In the population:

* **Correct model:** both match the Gateaux derivative, at 2.70e-8 (Hessian) and 2.67e-8
  (BHHH). In finite samples their Γ̂'s differ by an $O(N^{-1/2})$ convention gap. The
  relative Frobenius gap is 0.029, 0.016 and 0.0070 at $N$ = 2000, 8000 and 32000, with
  $\sqrt N\times$gap of 1.30, 1.45 and 1.25: the same shape as v1's N-table.
* **Stage 1 misspecified** (`@sec-condx`'s two-item DIF population): the Hessian form
  still matches the Gateaux derivative (2.3e-8). That makes it the influence function of
  the estimator actually computed, whatever the data. **BHHH misses by 0.80**, and its Γ
  is off by 9% (relative Frobenius). The binary item's own block is unaffected (6e-10,
  the FD error), because its univariate model is saturated.

So the choice is not only a finite-sample convention, as it is under a correct model.
**Under Stage 1 misspecification, only the Hessian form gives a sandwich that is right
for the pseudo-true target.** The same holds in v1 for `psi_rho` under non-normal latent
responses. v1's thresholds are saturated, so there it touches only the ρ block.

### Result N2: lavaan's Stage 1 is ours, under BHHH

On the committed `condx_A` data ($N=1500$), against lavaan 0.7.2 with
`conditional.x = TRUE` and `do.fit = FALSE`:

* $s$ agrees to 3.0e-8. That is lavaan's optimiser tolerance; the thresholds agree to
  1.5e-12;
* **lavaan's thresholds are at $x=0$**, not at the mean of $x$ (the 1.5e-12 above).
  $\bar x$ is 0.39 here, so centring would have moved them by $b_j\bar x\approx0.1$;
* Γ̂ under BHHH agrees to **7.0e-9 relative** (largest element gap 1.0e-7). Under the
  Hessian form it is 3.3% away. That confirms the code reading from output.

### The order of $s$ (proved, not assumed)

lavaan's `wls.obs` is labelled, and the generator asserts it equal to its `sampstat`
pieces (gap 0). The order:
$$s=\big(\tau_{1,1},\dots,\tau_{p,K_p-1};\;b_{1,x_1},\dots,b_{p,x_1},\,b_{1,x_2},\dots;\;
\rho_{21},\rho_{31},\dots,\rho_{p,p-1}\big),$$
thresholds item-major, then slopes **covariate-major** (items within each covariate,
`lav_m84_layout`'s `seq(i, by = nvar)`), then the residual correlations in lower-triangle
column-major order. With one $x$, this is `@sec-condx`'s order. With several, the
covariate-major slope order follows lavaan's layout code; no multi-$x$ fixture exists yet.

### What is left to decide (item 1)

1. **The normaliser.** v1's criterion (compatibility with lavaan, Result N2) gives BHHH.
   Result N1 gives a reason against it that v1 did not record: BHHH's sandwich is wrong
   under the Stage 1 misspecification that the adequacy contract says T3 cannot see.
   Options: (i) BHHH, lavaan-compatible, with the contract stating that the SEs assume
   Stage 1 adequacy; (ii) the Hessian form, robust to (A1)–(A2), and not equal to
   lavaan's Γ̂ (3.3% here, $O(N^{-1/2})$ under a correct model); (iii) BHHH by default,
   with the Hessian as an option. Whether v1's `psi_rho` should follow is a separate
   question. Raising it here does not reopen v1's decision.
2. **θ's order and `ptype`s for γ (x → η) and κ (x → y\*).** Spec §4.2 and §4.8, and a
   locked-API change. Not settled here.

```{r cxn-psi}
# The influence function under either normaliser. "hessian": H and U are
# derivatives of the mean score (the M-estimator form, as in cx_psi).
# "bhhh": every block an outer product of observed scores, lavaan's form:
#   H_j = sum w g g',  U_rho = -sum w u^2,  U_theta = -sum w u s_theta,
# where s_theta is the pair log-likelihood's own score in (theta_i, theta_j).
# The two agree in expectation only where the information identity holds.
cx_psi_n <- function(d, fit, norm = "hessian") {
  psi1 <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
    th <- fit$th[[j]]; G <- cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th)
    H <- if (norm == "bhhh") crossprod(G * sqrt(d$w)) else
      -cx_jac(function(t) colSums(d$w * cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, t)), th)
    G %*% t(solve(H))
  })
  psir <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]
    thi <- fit$th[[i]]; thj <- fit$th[[j]]; rho <- fit$rho[m]; ni <- length(thi)
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    uc <- cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho)
    if (norm == "bhhh") {
      Sc <- cx_jac(function(t) log(cx_rect(cells$ci, cells$cj, cells$x,
                                           t[1:ni], t[-(1:ni)], rho)[1, ]), c(thi, thj))
      Ur <- -sum(cells$w * uc^2)
      U1 <- -colSums(cells$w * uc * Sc)
    } else {
      ubar <- function(ti, tj, r) sum(cells$w * cx_pair_u(cells, ti, tj, r))
      h <- 1e-6
      Ur <- (ubar(thi, thj, rho + h) - ubar(thi, thj, rho - h)) / (2 * h)
      U1 <- cx_jac(function(t) ubar(t[1:ni], t[-(1:ni)], rho), c(thi, thj))
    }
    u <- uc[match(cells$key, cells$ukey)]
    -(u + cbind(psi1[[i]], psi1[[j]]) %*% U1) / Ur
  })
  cbind(do.call(cbind, lapply(psi1, function(P) P[, -ncol(P), drop = FALSE])),
        sapply(psi1, function(P) P[, ncol(P)]), psir)
}
cx_gamma <- function(d, psi) crossprod(psi * sqrt(d$w))
# relative Frobenius gap between two Gammas
cx_relF <- function(A, B) sqrt(sum((A - B)^2) / sum(B^2))

```

```{r cxn-pop}
}))
```
