## Conditional mode: analytic second derivatives for the Hessian-form normaliser {#sec-condx-hess}

**Executed 2026-10-25** in a side session (R 4.5.2, base R; chunks extracted from this
file and run with `@sec-condx`'s and `@sec-condx-norm`'s chunks before them). The
normaliser is the Hessian (M-estimator) form, E-062 2026-10-25 decision
(1). Production needs the blocks of that form in closed form. Up to here the oracle took
them by finite differences (`cx_jac` in `cx_psi_n`). This section derives the closed
forms and checks them against that oracle. **It decides nothing:** θ's order, `ptype`s
and the Mata layout are not touched.

### The per-item block $H_j$

Item $j$, pattern with category $c$ and covariate $x$; $\theta_j=(\tau_{j1},\dots,
\tau_{j,K-1},b_j)$, $K=K_j$; $\tau_{j0}=-\infty$, $\tau_{jK}=+\infty$. The shifted bounds
and their gradients in $\theta_j$:
$$\ell=\tau_{jc}-b_jx,\quad \upsilon=\tau_{j,c+1}-b_jx,\qquad
a_\ell=e_c-x\,e_K,\quad a_\upsilon=e_{c+1}-x\,e_K,$$
where $e_0$ and $e_K$ inside $a$ for an *infinite* bound are never used (below). With
$P=\Phi(\upsilon)-\Phi(\ell)$, $\phi'(z)=-z\phi(z)$, and the convention that
$\phi(\pm\infty)=\phi'(\pm\infty)=0$:
$$g=\frac{\phi(\upsilon)a_\upsilon-\phi(\ell)a_\ell}{P},\qquad
\frac{\partial g}{\partial\theta_j'}=\frac{\phi'(\upsilon)\,a_\upsilon a_\upsilon'-
\phi'(\ell)\,a_\ell a_\ell'}{P}-gg'.$$
$P$ is linear in $\theta$ only through the bounds, so $\partial^2P$ has no cross term
between the two bounds. The slope enters through the $-x$ entries of $a$. They give the
$(\tau,b)$ cross entries $-x\,\phi'(\cdot)/P$ and the $(b,b)$ entry
$x^2[\phi'(\upsilon)-\phi'(\ell)]/P-g_b^2$. These are zero in group $x=0$. Then
$$H_j=-\sum_rw_r\,\frac{\partial g_r}{\partial\theta_j'}.$$

### The pair blocks $U_\rho$ and $U_\theta$

Pair $(i,j)$, cell $(c_i,c_j,x)$; bounds $a_k$ ($k=1,2$, lower and upper) on item $i$'s
shifted scale, $b_l$ on item $j$'s, gradients $A_k\in\mathbb R^{K_i}$ and
$B_l\in\mathbb R^{K_j}$ as for $a_\ell,a_\upsilon$ above. Corner sign
$\sigma_{kl}=(-1)^{k+l}$, $s=\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$, and $\phi_2$ the standard bivariate density.
$$P=\sum_{kl}\sigma_{kl}\Phi_2(a_k,b_l;\rho),\qquad
P_\rho=\sum_{kl}\sigma_{kl}\phi_2,\qquad u=P_\rho/P.$$
The ingredients:

* $\partial\phi_2/\partial\rho=\phi_2\,\big[\rho(1-Q)+ab\big]/(1-\rho^2)$, with
  $Q=(a^2-2\rho ab+b^2)/(1-\rho^2)$;
* $\partial\Phi_2/\partial a=\phi(a)\,\Phi\big((b-\rho a)/s\big)$, and symmetrically in
  $b$;
* $\partial\phi_2/\partial a=-\phi_2\,(a-\rho b)/(1-\rho^2)$, and symmetrically.

Corners with an infinite bound have $\phi_2=0$. A derivative in an infinite bound is
zero. $\Phi((b-\rho a)/s)$ with $a$ finite and $b=\pm\infty$ is 1 or 0, which base R's
`pnorm` returns. By the quotient rule:
$$\frac{\partial u}{\partial\rho}=\frac{P_{\rho\rho}}{P}-u^2,\qquad
\frac{\partial u}{\partial\theta'}=\frac{\partial_\theta P_\rho'}{P}-u\,
\frac{\partial_\theta P'}{P},$$
$$\partial_{\theta_i}P=\sum_{kl}\sigma_{kl}\,\phi(a_k)\Phi\Big(\frac{b_l-\rho a_k}{s}\Big)A_k,
\qquad
\partial_{\theta_i}P_\rho=-\sum_{kl}\sigma_{kl}\,\phi_2(a_k,b_l)\frac{a_k-\rho b_l}{1-\rho^2}A_k,$$
and the same in $\theta_j$ with the roles of $a$ and $b$ exchanged. The slope columns
($b_i$, $b_j$) are new relative to v1. They come only through the $-x$ entries of $A$ and
$B$, so they vanish in cells with $x=0$. Then, as weighted sums over observed cells:
$$U_\rho=\sum_cw_c\frac{\partial u_c}{\partial\rho},\qquad
U_\theta=\sum_cw_c\frac{\partial u_c}{\partial(\theta_i',\theta_j')}.$$
These enter $\psi_\rho=-U_\rho^{-1}(u+U_\theta\,[\psi_{\theta_i};\psi_{\theta_j}])$,
as in `cx_psi_n`. With $w$ the sample proportions, this is the sample Hessian. $\rho$ is
held at the pair's estimate and $\theta$ at the univariate estimates.

### Where the closed forms need care

* **Tails of $P$.** $\Phi(\upsilon)-\Phi(\ell)$ cancels catastrophically when both
  bounds are far in the upper tail. The upper-tail form $\Phi(-\ell)-\Phi(-\upsilon)$
  does not. The derivative terms are ratios $\phi/P$ (an inverse Mills ratio when one
  bound is infinite), so they inherit $P$'s error and add none of their own.
  `cxh_P` switches on $\ell>0$. Checked below at $\ell=8$, the top category of a
  binary item with $\tau=8$ at $x=0$.
* **Infinite bounds**: handled by the convention above, never by `Inf * 0`. Checked
  cell by cell on every cell of both datasets. Every cell has at least one infinite
  bound on some item, and the binary item 3 has one in every cell.
* **Bivariate tails.** $P$ for a pair inherits whatever accuracy the $\Phi_2$ routine
  has in the tails. This section uses the oracle's integrator. It does not test a
  production $\Phi_2$ in the tails. That is an open item, not settled here.

```{r cxh-forms}
# Closed forms for the Hessian-form blocks. `drop` selects negative controls:
# "slope" removes the slope terms: in U_theta the -x entries of the bound
# gradients; in H_j the (tau, b) cross entries (all of H_bb would be singular);
# "quot" removes the quotient-rule term -u dP/P from du/dtheta.
cxh_P <- function(lo, up) ifelse(lo > 0, pnorm(-lo) - pnorm(-up), pnorm(up) - pnorm(lo))
cxh_grad <- function(cat, K, x, drop = "none") {    # gradient of a bound in theta_j
  a <- numeric(K); if (cat >= 1 && cat <= K - 1) a[cat] <- 1
  if (drop != "slope") a[K] <- -x
  a
}
# Per-pattern dg/dtheta', n_pat x K x K; also returns g.
cxh_uni_dg <- function(yj, x, th, drop = "none") {
  K <- length(th); tt <- c(-Inf, th[-K], Inf)
  lo <- tt[yj + 1] - th[K] * x; up <- tt[yj + 2] - th[K] * x
  P <- cxh_P(lo, up)
  fl <- ifelse(is.finite(lo), dnorm(lo), 0); fu <- ifelse(is.finite(up), dnorm(up), 0)
  dl <- ifelse(is.finite(lo), -lo * fl, 0);  du <- ifelse(is.finite(up), -up * fu, 0)
  n <- length(yj); out <- array(0, c(n, K, K)); G <- matrix(0, n, K)
  for (r in seq_len(n)) {
    al <- cxh_grad(yj[r], K, x[r]); au <- cxh_grad(yj[r] + 1, K, x[r])
    g <- (fu[r] * au - fl[r] * al) / P[r]; G[r, ] <- g
    D <- (du[r] * tcrossprod(au) - dl[r] * tcrossprod(al)) / P[r] - tcrossprod(g)
    if (drop == "slope") D[K, -K] <- D[-K, K] <- 0
    out[r, , ] <- D
  }
  list(g = G, dg = out)
}
cxh_H <- function(yj, x, w, th, drop = "none") {
  -apply(w * cxh_uni_dg(yj, x, th, drop)$dg, c(2, 3), sum)
}
# Per-cell u, du/drho and du/dtheta' (theta = (theta_i, theta_j)).
cxh_pair_d <- function(cells, thi, thj, rho, drop = "none") {
  Ki <- length(thi); Kj <- length(thj); s2 <- 1 - rho^2; s <- sqrt(s2)
  ti <- c(-Inf, thi[-Ki], Inf); tj <- c(-Inf, thj[-Kj], Inf)
  n <- length(cells$ci); Ur <- numeric(n); Ut <- matrix(0, n, Ki + Kj); u <- numeric(n)
  for (r in seq_len(n)) {
    ci <- cells$ci[r]; cj <- cells$cj[r]; x <- cells$x[r]
    a <- ti[ci + 1:2] - thi[Ki] * x; b <- tj[cj + 1:2] - thj[Kj] * x
    A <- list(cxh_grad(ci, Ki, x, drop), cxh_grad(ci + 1, Ki, x, drop))
    B <- list(cxh_grad(cj, Kj, x, drop), cxh_grad(cj + 1, Kj, x, drop))
    P <- Pr <- Prr <- 0; dPi <- dPri <- numeric(Ki); dPj <- dPrj <- numeric(Kj)
    for (k in 1:2) for (l in 1:2) {
      sg <- (-1)^(k + l); ak <- a[k]; bl <- b[l]
      P <- P + sg * Phi2(ak, bl, rho)
      if (is.finite(ak) && is.finite(bl)) {
        f2 <- cx_phi2(ak, bl, rho); Q <- (ak^2 - 2 * rho * ak * bl + bl^2) / s2
        Pr  <- Pr + sg * f2
        Prr <- Prr + sg * f2 * (rho * (1 - Q) + ak * bl) / s2
        dPri <- dPri - sg * f2 * (ak - rho * bl) / s2 * A[[k]]
        dPrj <- dPrj - sg * f2 * (bl - rho * ak) / s2 * B[[l]]
      }
      if (is.finite(ak)) dPi <- dPi + sg * dnorm(ak) * pnorm((bl - rho * ak) / s) * A[[k]]
      if (is.finite(bl)) dPj <- dPj + sg * dnorm(bl) * pnorm((ak - rho * bl) / s) * B[[l]]
    }
    u[r] <- Pr / P; Ur[r] <- Prr / P - u[r]^2
    Ut[r, ] <- c(dPri, dPrj) / P - (drop != "quot") * u[r] * c(dPi, dPj) / P
  }
  list(u = u, Ur = Ur, Ut = Ut)
}
# psi from the analytic blocks, laid out as cx_psi_n.
cxh_psi <- function(d, fit, drop_h = "none", drop_u = "none") {
  psi1 <- lapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
    th <- fit$th[[j]]
    cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th) %*% t(solve(cxh_H(d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w, th, drop_h)))
  })
  psir <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w)
    pd <- cxh_pair_d(cells, fit$th[[i]], fit$th[[j]], fit$rho[m], drop_u)
    Ur <- sum(cells$w * pd$Ur); U1 <- colSums(cells$w * pd$Ut)
    u <- pd$u[match(cells$key, cells$ukey)]
    -(u + cbind(psi1[[i]], psi1[[j]]) %*% U1) / Ur
  })
  cbind(do.call(cbind, lapply(psi1, function(P) P[, -ncol(P), drop = FALSE])),
        sapply(psi1, function(P) P[, ncol(P)]), psir)
}

```

```{r cxh-check}
#| cache: true
# Each closed form against central differences of the oracle's own scores,
# pointwise (every pattern, every cell) and as weighted sums, on the
# population (pop, fit0) and on the committed condx_A data (dA, fitA).
cxh_gaps <- function(d, fit) {
  uni <- sapply(seq_len(cx_p), function(j) {
    th <- fit$th[[j]]; K <- length(th); h <- 1e-6
    fd <- array(0, c(nrow(d$Y), K, K))
    for (k in seq_len(K)) {
      e <- replace(numeric(K), k, h)
      fd[, , k] <- (cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th + e) -
                    cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th - e)) / (2 * h)
    }
    an <- cxh_uni_dg(d$Y[, j], d$x, th)
    Hfd <- -cx_jac(function(t) colSums(d$w * cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, t)), th)
    c(cell = max(abs(an$dg - fd)), H = max(abs(cxh_H(d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w, th) - Hfd)),
      g = max(abs(an$g - cx_uni_score(d$Y[, j], d$x, th))))
  })
  pair <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(cx_pairs)), function(m) {
    i <- cx_pairs[m, 1]; j <- cx_pairs[m, 2]
    thi <- fit$th[[i]]; thj <- fit$th[[j]]; rho <- fit$rho[m]; ni <- length(thi)
    cells <- cx_pair_cells(d$Y[, i], d$Y[, j], d$x, d$w); h <- 1e-6
    pd <- cxh_pair_d(cells, thi, thj, rho)
    fr <- (cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho + h) - cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho - h)) / (2 * h)
    ft <- cx_jac(function(t) cx_pair_u(cells, t[1:ni], t[-(1:ni)], rho), c(thi, thj))
    c(u = max(abs(pd$u - cx_pair_u(cells, thi, thj, rho))),
      Ur_cell = max(abs(pd$Ur - fr)), Ut_cell = max(abs(pd$Ut - ft)),
      Ur = abs(sum(cells$w * pd$Ur) - sum(cells$w * fr)),
      Ut = max(abs(colSums(cells$w * pd$Ut) - colSums(cells$w * ft))),
      Ut_slope_x0 = max(abs(pd$Ut[cells$x == 0, c(ni, ni + length(thj))])))
  })
  list(uni = uni, pair = pair)
}
gp <- cxh_gaps(pop, fit0)
gA <- cxh_gaps(dA, fitA)
# psi from the analytic blocks: against the FD-Hessian oracle and the Gateaux
# derivative (population), and against the oracle on condx_A
psi_an_pop <- cxh_psi(pop, fit0)
gap_an_oracle_pop <- max(abs(psi_an_pop - cx_psi_n(pop, fit0, "hessian")))
gap_an_gat <- max(abs(psi_an_pop - gat))
psi_an_A <- cxh_psi(dA, fitA)
gap_an_oracle_A <- max(abs(psi_an_A - cx_psi_n(dA, fitA, "hessian")))
relF_an_A <- cx_relF(cx_gamma(dA, psi_an_A), GA_h)
# misspecified population: the reason for the Hessian form
psi_an_D <- cxh_psi(popD, fitD)
gap_an_oracle_D <- max(abs(psi_an_D - cx_psi_n(popD, fitD, "hessian")))
gap_an_gatD <- max(abs(psi_an_D - gatD))      # gatD from @sec-condx-norm
# negative controls, each against the Gateaux derivative
ctl_h_slope <- max(abs(cxh_psi(pop, fit0, drop_h = "slope") - gat))
ctl_u_slope <- max(abs(cxh_psi(pop, fit0, drop_u = "slope") - gat))
ctl_u_quot  <- max(abs(cxh_psi(pop, fit0, drop_u = "quot") - gat))
ctl_A_u_slope <- max(abs(cxh_psi(dA, fitA, drop_u = "slope") - psi_an_A))
```

```{r cxh-tail}
# Tail cancellation: binary item, tau = 8, top category at x = 0, so
# lo = 8, up = Inf, P = 1 - Phi(8). The score in tau is -phi(8)/P exactly;
# the closed form's Hessian entry is phi'(8)/P... - g^2 = -8 g - g^2 (lo term).
tail_th <- c(8, 0.3)
tail_g_exact <- -dnorm(8) / pnorm(-8)
tail_stable <- cxh_uni_dg(1L, 0, tail_th)
tail_naive_P <- pnorm(Inf) - pnorm(8)
tail_rel_stable <- abs(tail_stable$g[1, 1] / tail_g_exact - 1)
tail_rel_naive  <- abs((-dnorm(8) / tail_naive_P) / tail_g_exact - 1)
tail_H_exact <- -8 * tail_g_exact - tail_g_exact^2     # -(phi'(lo)/P) - g^2, phi'(8) = -8 phi(8)
tail_rel_H <- abs(tail_stable$dg[1, 1, 1] / tail_H_exact - 1)

```
